src/ui.tsx::HeaderProps.text: What the top bar needs: the current screen, a way to change screens, the current exam's title, the unread alert count, the tracked exam count, and actions for alerts and the timeline.
src/ui.tsx::HeaderProps.tech: Interface {activeTab, setActiveTab(tab), selectedExamTitle?, unreadCount?, trackedCount?, onOpenNotifications?, onOpenTimeline?}.

src/ui.tsx::IBPSPracticeEngine.text: The practice area for IBPS PO 2026 only. Since GovOS has no checked IBPS questions, it says practice is not available yet rather than borrowing another exam's questions, and shows the real exam pattern, any official papers and answer keys, and past attempts.
src/ui.tsx::IBPSPracticeEngine.tech: Exported component {exam, scope='ALL', onOpenProvenanceModal}; returns null unless assertExamMatches(..., 'exam-ibps-po-2026', exam). Finds the first stage whose name matches /prelim/i for the PracticeShell patternSummary (else 'Objective CBT'). Renders FeatureUnavailable (with IBPS_PRACTICE_CONFIG.note), ExamPatternPanel, OfficialPapersPanel, OfficialPaperCatalogue, AnswerKeyPanel and ExamAttemptHistory.

src/ui.tsx::IBPS_PRACTICE_CONFIG.text: The fixed settings for IBPS PO practice: the exam it belongs to, a note that no question bank exists for it, and the reminder that each Preliminary section has its own separate timer.
src/ui.tsx::IBPS_PRACTICE_CONFIG.tech: Constant {examId: 'exam-ibps-po-2026', questionSource: null, note: '...separately timed...'}. The note is interpolated into the IBPSPracticeEngine's FeatureUnavailable reason.

src/ui.tsx::INK.text: The dark ink colour used for the line drawings on exam cards.
src/ui.tsx::INK.tech: '#14213d'; stroke and fill colour in AuthorityArt.

src/ui.tsx::ITEM_ROLE_RULES.text: Word patterns that identify what an official item is from its title: answer key, question paper, cut-off, calendar, result, admit card, corrigendum, syllabus, one-time registration, application portal or notification.
src/ui.tsx::ITEM_ROLE_RULES.tech: Ordered array of [ResourceRole, RegExp] checked first-match in that order (ANSWER_KEY, QUESTION_PAPER, CUTOFF, CALENDAR, RESULT, ADMIT_CARD, CORRIGENDUM, SYLLABUS, OTR_PORTAL, APPLICATION_PORTAL, NOTIFICATION). Index 0 and 1 are also used on their own by resourceRoleOf.

src/ui.tsx::JOURNEY_STAGES.text: The four milestone names in the home page animation: Discover, Apply, Exam, Result.

src/ui.tsx::JOURNEY_STOPS.text: Where along the road the walking candidate stops, a little before each milestone so he never covers its label.
src/ui.tsx::JOURNEY_STOPS.tech: [0.03, 0.355, 0.635, 0.935] as road fractions; journeyAt interpolates between them.

src/ui.tsx::JiggleLabel.text: A button label whose letters wiggle when you point at it, while still reading as one word.
src/ui.tsx::JiggleLabel.tech: Component {text}: .jiggle wrapper with an .sr-only copy and aria-hidden .jiggle-char spans per character, each with --ci = i/(n-1) (0 for one character).

src/ui.tsx::JourneyStep.text: One step of the 'How GovOS works' story: a verb, a title, a short text and an optional button.
src/ui.tsx::JourneyStep.tech: Interface {verb, title, text, action?: {label, run}}; consumed by JourneyStory.

src/ui.tsx::JourneyStory.text: The 'How GovOS works' section on the home page: numbered steps from discovering an exam to knowing what comes next, with a line beside them that fills as you scroll. Some steps have a button that takes you there.
src/ui.tsx::JourneyStory.tech: Component {steps}: section.journey with a sticky heading (chapter 02) and an <ol> of .journey-step[data-reveal] items (--si index, zero-padded number, verb, title, text, and a button calling action.run when present). ExamFinder passes seven steps.

src/ui.tsx::LEARNING_ROLES.text: The three categories that count as learning material and are listed in the Resource Library: study material, lessons and practice tools.

src/ui.tsx::LOOP_S.text: How long one full loop of the home page journey animation lasts: 17 seconds.
src/ui.tsx::LOOP_S.tech: 17 (seconds); journeyAt uses it for the closing camera settle and fade, and ClubSkyline takes elapsed time modulo it.

src/ui.tsx::MILESTONE_AT.text: How far along the road each of the four milestones stands.
src/ui.tsx::MILESTONE_AT.tech: [0.10, 0.40, 0.68, 0.98] as fractions of the road length; used to shrink farther milestones (scale 1.06 - at*0.3).

src/ui.tsx::MILESTONE_POSTS.text: The positions in the picture where the four milestone markers are drawn beside the road.
src/ui.tsx::MILESTONE_POSTS.tech: Four {x, y} SVG coordinates (offset from the path's left normal) at which each milestone group is translated; index 3 also anchors the sparks.

src/ui.tsx::MONTH_NAMES.text: The three-letter month abbreviations (JAN to DEC) used to label calendar dates.
src/ui.tsx::MONTH_NAMES.tech: Array indexed by month number 1-12; index 0 is an empty string so parseInt of the month can index it directly.

src/ui.tsx::MockChatMessage.text: One message in the practice test chat: who sent it, the text, the time, and the test it proposes if one was built.
src/ui.tsx::MockChatMessage.tech: Interface: id, sender 'user' | 'assistant', text, timestamp, optional proposedTest: MockPaper (the paper from a BUILT PracticePlan, offered with a start button).

src/ui.tsx::MyExams.text: The candidate's own shelf of exams: those they track, those they bookmarked and the one they last opened (shown first). Each card shows the exam's authority, name, next date with a day countdown where the exact day is known, and buttons to open the exam or track it. With nothing on the shelf, it explains how to add one.
src/ui.tsx::MyExams.tech: Reads storageService.getBookmarkedExams(); mine = exams that are tracked, bookmarked or equal to currentExamId, sorted with the current one first. PageStage shows shelf, tracking and bookmarked counts. Each .shelf-pass (tone from passToneOf) shows flags, examDisplayCode, title, the next non-superseded future date (formatted with shownWhen) and a countdown from nextMilestoneOf when days is not null. The Open button calls onSelectExam and Track calls onToggleTrackExam. Empty state has a Find-an-exam button that calls onFindExams.

src/ui.tsx::MyExamsProps.text: What the My Exams page needs: the list of exams, which are tracked, which was last opened, and actions to open, track or find exams.
src/ui.tsx::MyExamsProps.tech: Interface {exams? (default ALL_EXAMS), trackedExamIds, currentExamId, onSelectExam, onToggleTrackExam, onFindExams}.

src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_CONCEPTS.text: Common ways candidates describe a resource without naming it, each with what it means: 'the government's own paper' or 'PYQs' means previous-year question papers, 'bills explained simply' means PRS, 'the actual law' means the Constitution text, 'something to watch' means a video, 'which channel' means a YouTube channel, 'daily news' means PIB, 'this year's paper' means the 2026 question booklet.
src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_CONCEPTS.tech: Array of {pattern: RegExp, means: string}. readNavigatorQuery tests each pattern against the lower-cased query and appends every matching 'means' phrase to the query before scoring, so paraphrases reach entries whose words they share.

src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_FORMAT_WORDS.text: The words that tell the resource search what kind of thing is wanted, for example 'pdf' or 'notice' for a document, 'lecture' for a video, 'youtube' or 'sir' for a channel, 'website' for a portal, 'typing' for a tool.
src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_FORMAT_WORDS.tech: Array of {format, words[]} for PDF, VIDEO, CHANNEL, PORTAL and TOOL. readNavigatorQuery picks the format with the most matching words (ties go to the first listed) and strips all these words from the search terms, so a format word is treated as intent rather than as text to match.

src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_STOPWORDS.text: A list of filler words the resource search ignores, such as 'give me', 'please', 'official', 'ssc', and words like 'that' or 'it' that point back at the conversation.
src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_STOPWORDS.tech: Set of lower-case words removed from NavigatorReading.terms: request grammar (give, show, find, please...), generic library words (resource, material, study, official, link, download), 'ssc', 'cgl', '2026', 'exam', and deictic words (that, this, it, them, same, instead, again, more).

src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_SUBJECT_WORDS.text: The words that name a library subject directly, for example 'quant' or 'maths' for Quantitative Aptitude, 'polity' for General Awareness, 'rbi' for Banking, 'ncert' for foundation textbooks.
src/ui.tsx::NAVIGATOR_SUBJECT_WORDS.tech: Array of {subject: ResourceItem['subject'], words[]} covering nine library subjects (Quantitative Aptitude, English Comprehension, Reasoning, General Awareness & Static GK, Current Affairs & Governance, Banking & Financial Awareness, Foundation Textbooks & Open Courses, Computer & Typing, Official Gazette). Any matching word adds the subject to both subjects and directSubjects; some words appear under two subjects (e.g. 'science', 'class', 'typing', 'notice').

src/ui.tsx::NOT_READ_WORDS.text: Plain-English reasons why some pages or files on an authority's website were not read, such as the walk's file limit or a page built by a script.
src/ui.tsx::NOT_READ_WORDS.tech: Record mapping skipped_due_to_* coverage keys (file_budget, page_budget, item_budget, depth, script_rendering, fetch_failed, refused_address, not_opened, links_not_followed) to short phrases.

src/ui.tsx::NavigatorFormat.text: The five kinds of resource the search chat understands: a PDF, a video, a YouTube channel, a website, or a practice tool.
src/ui.tsx::NavigatorFormat.tech: Union type 'PDF' | 'VIDEO' | 'CHANNEL' | 'PORTAL' | 'TOOL', used by readNavigatorQuery, resourceFormatGroup and the format-adjustment table in scoreResourceForQuery.

src/ui.tsx::NavigatorReading.text: What the search chat understood from a request: the kind of resource asked for, the subjects it points at, any practice topics named, and the remaining search words.
src/ui.tsx::NavigatorReading.tech: Interface returned by readNavigatorQuery: format (NavigatorFormat | null), subjects (named or inferred from topics), directSubjects (named outright, scored higher), topicLabels (from parseTestRequest), terms (leftover words after stopwords and format words are removed).

src/ui.tsx::NotificationCenterModal.text: The slide-out panel that opens from the bell icon and lists the candidate's exam alerts. The candidate can filter to All, Unread or Urgent, mark alerts read, clear them all, open notification settings, or press 'Take Action' to jump to the part of the app an alert is about. When there is nothing to show it explains how to get alerts by tracking an exam.
src/ui.tsx::NotificationCenterModal.tech: Renders null unless isOpen; a right-hand fixed drawer (backdrop click closes, inner click stops propagation). Local state filterTab ALL | UNREAD | URGENT; urgent = priority 'CRITICAL' or eventType 'APPLICATION_DEADLINE'. Each card shows an icon by eventType, examCode badge, a CRITICAL DEADLINE badge, createdAt, title, message and the channelsDelivered pills; 'Mark Read' calls onMarkAsRead(id) and 'Take Action' calls onMarkAsRead(id) then onNotificationAction(notif). Header buttons: 'Read All' (onMarkAsRead('ALL'), only if unread > 0), Settings (onOpenPreferences), and clear (onClearAll, only if any). Stateless apart from the filter; all data changes go through the callbacks.

src/ui.tsx::NotificationCenterModalProps.text: The list of things the notifications panel needs to be given: whether it is open, the alerts to show, and what to do when the candidate closes it, marks alerts read, clears them, opens settings or acts on an alert.
src/ui.tsx::NotificationCenterModalProps.tech: Props interface for NotificationCenterModal: isOpen, onClose, notifications: CandidateNotification[], onMarkAsRead(id) (the component passes 'ALL' for mark-all), onClearAll, onOpenPreferences, onNotificationAction(notif).

src/ui.tsx::NotificationPreferencesModal.text: The settings window for alerts. The candidate chooses how to be told (inside the app, browser pop-ups, email, WhatsApp), which kinds of events to hear about (application opening and closing, corrections, admit cards, exam days, results) and how early to be reminded (7 days, 3 days, 1 day, closing day). The WhatsApp phone check is only a simulation: the app makes up a 4-digit code and shows it on screen, and nothing is actually sent. A 'test alert' button shows a sample alert through the chosen channels.
src/ui.tsx::NotificationPreferencesModal.tech: Copies preferences into local state on mount (it does not re-sync if the prop changes later); returns null unless isOpen. Browser push calls Notification.requestPermission() and sets channels.browserPush on 'granted'. WhatsApp verification is a stub: handleSendOtp needs a phone of 10+ characters and generates a random 4-digit code displayed on screen; handleVerifyOtp accepts that code or the hard-coded '1234' and sets channels.whatsapp and contactInfo.whatsappVerified. Toggles edit channels.inApp/browserPush/email/whatsapp, eventSubscriptions (applicationOpening, applicationDeadlines, correctionWindows, admitCards, examDates, results) and reminderSchedule (sevenDaysBefore, threeDaysBefore, oneDayBefore, lastDayHoursBefore). handleSave merges the email/phone inputs into contactInfo, calls onSavePreferences, shows a success message and closes after 1.2 s. handleTriggerTestAlert builds a CandidateNotification (examId 'exam-ssc-cgl-2026', examCode 'GOVOS_TEST', actionPayload {section: 2}, channels from the enabled ones), fires a real browser Notification if permission is granted, and passes it to onDispatchTestAlert.

src/ui.tsx::NotificationPreferencesModal.text: What the notification-settings window needs: whether it is open, the candidate's current settings, and what to do to close, save settings or send a test alert.
src/ui.tsx::NotificationPreferencesModal.tech: Props interface for NotificationPreferencesModal: isOpen, onClose, preferences: NotificationPreference, onSavePreferences(prefs), onDispatchTestAlert(testNotif: CandidateNotification).

src/ui.tsx::OFFICIAL_RESOURCE_SUBJECTS.text: Subject headings that mark a resource as one of the authority's own documents or portals rather than study material.
src/ui.tsx::OFFICIAL_RESOURCE_SUBJECTS.tech: Lower-case subjects: 'official gazette', 'official portal', 'official notices', 'previous year papers'; checked in resourceRoleOf.

src/ui.tsx::OfficialDocumentsPanel.text: Used in the Official Links part of the exam page. It lists the authority's own notices, pages and candidate services for this exam — official records that are not study material — from GovOS's list, reviewer additions and GovOS's walk of the authority's website, each with its source labelled.
src/ui.tsx::OfficialDocumentsPanel.tech: Uses useExamAdditions and useDiscoveredSources; docs = examResourcesFor(..., 'OFFICIAL_LINKS'); repos from discoveredForSection(..., 'OFFICIAL_LINKS'); portals = discovered.portals with role OFFICIAL_PORTAL not already in docs. Returns null only when all are empty and discovered is null. Renders SourceRows, per-listing groups with an 'Open the listing' link, a 'Candidate services' group and DiscoveryStatusLine.

src/ui.tsx::OfficialNoticeBoards.text: Shows the authority's live notice boards inside the exam page: SSC's own notice board for SSC exams (with a switch between CGL-only and all SSC notices) and UPSC's 'What's New' page for UPSC exams. Each says when it was last read, flags an old copy or a failed read, and opens every notice on the authority's own site. Since UPSC's page prints no dates, items are dated by when GovOS first saw them.
src/ui.tsx::OfficialNoticeBoards.tech: isSscExam / isUpscExam are substring checks on exam.id ('ssc' / 'upsc'); returns null for any other exam. Fetches resourceLiveService.upscNotices('cse', 8) and resourceLiveService.sscNotices(noticeScope, 8) (scope 'cgl' | 'all') in cancellable effects keyed on exam.id and scope. Renders headline, createdAt / 'first seen', file links with sizeKb, fetchedAt via formatFetched, stale and error states, and intervalHours.

src/ui.tsx::OfficialPaperCatalogue.text: The list of past question papers the exam's authority itself publishes, filtered to this exam only by each file's own naming. Candidates can filter by exam year and open each paper on the authority's site. Where a paper has not been turned into practice questions, the card says why.
src/ui.tsx::OfficialPaperCatalogue.tech: Component {exam, onOpenProvenanceModal}; returns null when exam.officialPapers filtered to identity.examId === exam.id is empty. Local `cycle` state ('ALL' or a cycle; missing cycles shown as 'undated', sorted descending) filters the list; shows at most 60 cards with a 'Showing 60 of N' note. Each card: OFFICIAL PAPER badge, identity.describe, contentsNote, 'Open the paper' link (paper.url) and EvidenceButton. Header notes when no paper has contentsStatus === 'VERIFIED'.

src/ui.tsx::OfficialPapersPanel.text: Shows the official past papers that are stored among this exam's own resources, each with a button to open the paper and its source. It never shows another exam's papers and shows nothing if there are none.
src/ui.tsx::OfficialPapersPanel.tech: Component {exam, onOpenProvenanceModal}. Filters exam.resources to subject === 'Previous Year Papers' && type === 'OFFICIAL_PDF'; returns null when none. Each card shows officialTag, title, recommendedFor, an 'Open the paper' link to directPdfUrl || url, and an EvidenceButton when provenance exists.

src/ui.tsx::PASS_TONES.text: The five colour themes GovOS uses for exam cards.
src/ui.tsx::PASS_TONES.tech: ['ink', 'saffron', 'jade', 'plum', 'tide'] as const; picked by passToneOf and applied as .pass-<tone> classes.

src/ui.tsx::PATTERN_FIELD_WORDS.text: Plain names for the exam-pattern figures GovOS can calculate, used on the 'how this was computed' buttons.
src/ui.tsx::PATTERN_FIELD_WORDS.tech: Record mapping marksPerQuestion, questions, marks, durationMinutes, negativeMarking, negativeMarkPerWrong to readable phrases; used for EvidenceButton labels in PatternNodeCard.

src/ui.tsx::PLAN_DAY_PRESETS.text: The plan lengths a candidate can pick: 60, 90, 120 or 180 days.
src/ui.tsx::PLAN_DAY_PRESETS.tech: [60, 90, 120, 180]; the days left to a firm exam date are added when there is one.

src/ui.tsx::PLAN_PHASE_SHARES.text: How GovOS splits the days of a plan: about 60% learning, 25% a second pass, and the rest full papers on the clock.
src/ui.tsx::PLAN_PHASE_SHARES.tech: {learn: 0.6, revise: 0.25}; practice takes the remainder. Stated on screen as GovOS’s guidance, not a rule of the exam.

src/ui.tsx::PLAN_STOP.text: Small words ignored when matching a syllabus subject to a part of the exam pattern.

src/ui.tsx::PLAN_THIN_SYLLABUS.text: The size below which an exam’s syllabus is too thin to plan from, so its plan is built from the exam pattern’s sections instead.
src/ui.tsx::PLAN_THIN_SYLLABUS.tech: 10 — studyPlanUnits uses the pattern path when exam.syllabus.length is below it.

src/ui.tsx::PLATFORM_MAP.text: The assistant’s map of where everything lives in GovOS: about 20 entries (eligibility, resources, practice, calendar, syllabus, application simulator, typing, past tests, saved items, target post, applying, admit card, cut-offs, roadmap, compare, trust and reporting, results, exam day, corrigenda, FAQs, posts), each with its keywords, a ready-made explanation and a button to that place.
src/ui.tsx::PLATFORM_MAP.tech: Array of {keys, answer, action}. Answers use placeholders filled by fillCounts ({exam}, {posts}, …); an answer that counts {posts} is replaced by noPostsReply for an exam with no posts. The admit-card and results answers no longer name one authority’s process ("regional website", "final posting").

src/ui.tsx::PORTAL_WORDS.text: Recognises wording that describes a general website or portal ('portal', 'official website').
src/ui.tsx::PORTAL_WORDS.tech: Case-insensitive RegExp for the word 'portal' or 'official site/website'; used with ITEM_ROLE_RULES in resourceRoleOf.

src/ui.tsx::POST_SHAPED_FACTS.text: The questions only a recruitment can answer — age, vacancies, pay, physical standards, target post, study plan by post and post-by-post eligibility — which an exam with no posts answers differently.
src/ui.tsx::POST_SHAPED_FACTS.tech: Set of FACT_INTENTS ids; answerCorrectedQuery routes them to noPostsReply when exam.posts is empty.

src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_CONCEPTS.text: Common ways candidates describe practice without naming a topic, each with what it means: 'money problems' means percentage, profit and loss and interest; 'odd one out' means classification; 'the whole thing' means a full mock test; 'the law of the land' means polity; 'sums' means questions. Phrases like 'help me with' are recognised but add nothing.
src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_CONCEPTS.tech: Array of {pattern, means} used by understandPracticeRequest to append the meaning to the query before parseTestRequest reads it; the full-mock entry is special-cased, and the 'struggle with / weak in' entry has an empty meaning (no change).

src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_ENGINES.text: The registry that says which practice screen each exam gets: SSC CGL, UPSC CSE, IBPS PO, APPSC Group-I and APPSC Group-II each have their own. It is looked up by the exam's fixed id, and there is deliberately no default, so an exam without an entry is never given another exam's engine.
src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_ENGINES.tech: Record<string, PracticeEngineEntry> keyed by SSC_CGL_EXAM.id, UPSC_CSE_EXAM.id, IBPS_PO_EXAM.id, APPSC_GROUP1_EXAM.id and APPSC_GROUP2_EXAM.id. SSC's patternSummary reads the TIER_1 stage (name before ':', totalMarks, durationMinutes) and renders PracticeEngine; the others use fixed summaries and render UPSCPracticeEngine, IBPSPracticeEngine, APPSCGroup1PracticeEngine, APPSCGroup2PracticeEngine. supportedModes lists each engine's features as strings.

src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_MODIFIER.text: Recognises words that only make sense as a follow-up to the last test, such as 'harder', 'easier', 'more', 'again' or 'longer'.
src/ui.tsx::PRACTICE_MODIFIER.tech: RegExp /\b(harder|tougher|difficult|advanced|easier|simpler|basic|more|another|again|same|repeat|longer|shorter)\b/ tested against the normalised query in planPracticeRequest when no topic or subject is named.

src/ui.tsx::PageStage.text: The coloured opening banner at the top of pages like My Exams, Compare and the Trust Panel: a small label, a big title, a short introduction, the page's buttons and a few key numbers, over a wavy background.
src/ui.tsx::PageStage.tech: Component {eyebrow, title, lede?, icon?, actions?, stats?, children?, colour='yellow' (yellow|pink|cyan|periwinkle|green)}: section.page-stage.stage-<colour> with ClubWaves, an eyebrow (icon or .cine-dot), h1 title, optional lede, actions, a <dl> of stats and a footer for children. Presentation only.

src/ui.tsx::PageWipe.text: A coloured ribbon that sweeps across the screen whenever the main screen changes, hiding the moment of swapping. It is off for people who prefer less motion.
src/ui.tsx::PageWipe.tech: Component {token}: a useLayoutEffect compares token with a ref and bumps a run counter (skipped under reduced motion), so the overlay is present before paint; an effect resets run to 0 after 950 ms. Renders .page-wipe keyed by run with an SVG ribbon path.

src/ui.tsx::PatternNodeCard.text: Shows one part of an exam’s structure — a stage, a paper or a section — with its questions, marks, time and marks per question as the authority stated them, then the parts inside it. Figures GovOS worked out itself are marked ‘computed’, unclear rows are flagged ‘needs review’ with their original text, and rules such as negative marking, qualifying marks, language and mode are listed.
src/ui.tsx::PatternNodeCard.tech: Recursive component { node: ExamPatternNode, depth, onOpenProvenanceModal }. Figures only for defined questions / marks / durationMinutes / marksPerQuestion (labelled 'Mark / question' when it is 1); node.derived marks '(computed)', underReview adds '*'. Shows levelLabel, code, NEEDS_REVIEW, negativeMarking, qualifying, languages, mode, questionType, sectionalTiming, durationVariants, an EvidenceButton per provenance and derivedEvidence, and recurses into children.

src/ui.tsx::PlanMarkNode.text: One part of an exam’s pattern that states its marks, with what sits above it.
src/ui.tsx::PlanMarkNode.tech: Type {name, path (ancestor words), marks, depth, key, qualifying, stage}.

src/ui.tsx::PostStudyPathEngine.text: The 'Post Study Plan' view of the syllabus (used for SSC CGL). The candidate picks the post they are aiming for and sees exactly what to study for it: the common modules for each stage, extra modules that post needs, any physical or medical standards, and the modules they can skip because that post does not need them. Modules can be ticked off as done, and a button copies the candidate's progress to the server database.
src/ui.tsx::PostStudyPathEngine.tech: State: selectedPostId from storageService.getTargetPost() (handleSelectPost also calls setTargetPost), selectedStage ALL | TIER_1 | TIER_2, completedModules from getCompletedModules() (toggled via toggleCompletedModule). currentPath = getPostStudyPath(selectedPostId); post pills come from ALL_POST_STUDY_PATHS. Renders tier1/tier2 commonModules (with provenance-type badges and EvidenceButton when onOpenProvenanceModal is given), tier2.additionalModules, physicalMedical when required, and tier2.excludedModules (empty case shows a fixed sentence about Junior Statistical Officer). 'Sync to SQLite' awaits storageService.syncAllToSQLite() and shows its message on failure. Not exam-parameterised: it reads SSC's study paths directly.

src/ui.tsx::PostStudyPathEngineProps.text: What the post-wise study plan needs: an optional way to open a fact's evidence, and an optional link to practice.
src/ui.tsx::PostStudyPathEngineProps.tech: Props for PostStudyPathEngine: optional onOpenProvenanceModal(prov) and optional onNavigatePractice() (accepted but not used by the component).

src/ui.tsx::PracticeApplicationSimulator.text: A practice version of SSC's online application form, so a candidate can rehearse filling it in and learn the common mistakes before doing it for real. It walks through six steps: personal details, education, category, post preferences, photo and signature, and a final review with a declaration tick-box; it starts pre-filled with a sample candidate. The candidate can upload their own photo and signature and the form checks the file type (JPEG), the size in kilobytes and the shape on the spot, or they can pick example 'trap' cases such as a photo with glasses or a signature in capital letters. On submit it lists each mistake that would get an application rejected, with why it matters and the clause it comes from, plus the checks that passed. The result (checks passed out of checks run, and time taken) is saved to the candidate's practice history under SSC CGL; files are only inspected in the browser and are not sent anywhere.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeApplicationSimulator.tech: No props are used; state is `currentStep` (1-6, freely clickable tabs plus Back / 'Save & Next'), `form: FormState` seeded from `initialFormState`, `isSubmitted` and `startedAt`. File handlers build `UploadedFileMeta` with an `Image` load: photo JPEG and 20-50 KB with aspect 0.65-0.90 and height at least 250 px; signature JPEG and 10-20 KB with aspect at least 1.4 and width at least 80 px; marksheet/certificate at most 500 KB (the certificate upload appears only for a non-UR category). `evaluateApplication()` (recomputed every render) returns `{mistakes, passedChecks}`: a 12th-maths percentage outside 0-100, JSO among the preferences without 60%+ maths or statistics, missing/oversized/misshapen uploads in REAL_UPLOAD mode or WITH_GLASSES/WITH_CAP photo and CAPITAL_LETTERS signature in PRESET_TRAPS mode (BLURRY_SELFIE and BLURRY_SIGN raise nothing), and a graduation status after 01-08-2026. Submit (disabled until `declarationAgreed`) calls `storageService.saveMockAttempt` with `exam_id: SSC_CGL_EXAM.id`, subject 'Application Practice Simulator', score = round(passed / (passed + mistakes) x 100) of 100, and the elapsed seconds since `startedAt`. The post list is a hard-coded seven SSC posts, and Reset restores the seed form and restarts the clock; `ApplicationGuide` renders this only when an `ssc.gov.in` guide has no `simulator` spec.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeApplicationSimulator.text: The settings handed to SSC's practice application form. It has one optional slot for opening the evidence panel, which the form does not currently use.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeApplicationSimulator.tech: Interface with a single optional `onOpenProvenanceModal?: (prov: any) => void`. `PracticeApplicationSimulator` declares it but destructures nothing from its props, so the callback is never called.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngine.text: This is SSC CGL's practice screen, where a candidate sits timed practice tests and then studies the answers. It has tabs for full-length GovOS practice papers, 25-question subject tests, 15-question topic drills, a chat where you describe the test you want and it builds one, the test in progress, and a history of past attempts. During a test there is a countdown clock (it submits automatically at zero), a numbered grid of questions to jump around, and buttons to clear an answer or mark it for review. After submitting you see your score, accuracy, topics sorted into weak, moderate and strong, an optional split of your own daily study hours across subjects, and a worked solution for every question with where it came from. Every attempt is saved in the browser and sent to the GovOS server, and any past attempt can be reopened for review or retaken. For exams other than SSC CGL the paper shelves are empty and a note says these questions are written to SSC's pattern and would mislead. On a phone the test creator's header wraps (the target badge drops below the title) and its replies use the full width beside the bot icon.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngine.tech: Props: `exam`, `onOpenProvenanceModal`, `scope` ('ALL' | 'PRACTICE' | 'MOCKS'; MOCKS hides papers/sectionals/drills and opens on the creator, PRACTICE hides the creator); `activePracticeTab` switches PAPERS_LIST, SUBJECT_TESTS, TOPIC_DRILLS, AI_CHAT_ASSISTANT, ACTIVE_TEST, PAST_ANALYTICS. The bank (`OFFICIAL_10_MOCK_PAPERS`, `SUBJECT_MOCK_TESTS`, `TOPIC_DRILL_TESTS`) is shown only when `exam.id === PRACTICE_BANK_EXAM_ID`; 'Show More Practice Papers' adds `NEW_DISCOVERED_PAPERS` after a 1.2 s timeout, and PAPERS_LIST also mounts `OfficialPaperCatalogue` and `AnswerKeyPanel`. Test state is `userAnswers`, `markedForReview`, `currentIdx`, `timerSeconds` (1 s interval, pause toggle, auto `handleSubmitTest` at 0), and a `sittingIdRef` id fixed at start so a double submit replaces one record; scoring uses `selectedPaper.marking` (correct/wrong), topics under 50% / under 75% / 75%+ become weak/medium/strong, and weak cards cite `exam.syllabus` weightage and offer a `TOPIC_DRILL_TESTS` drill matched by subject. Submit builds a `MockAttemptRecord` (exam_id, scores, time, userAnswers, paperData) and calls `storageService.saveMockAttempt`, showing a `saveWarning` when `kept.local` is false; history comes from `storageService.getMockAttempts(exam.id)` and on mount `loadMockAttemptsFromSQLite(exam.id)`, and `handleReviewPastAttempt` rebuilds a paper through a 7-step fallback (stored paperData, id, title, fuzzy match, regenerated quant drill, a built-in 4-question application drill, `OFFICIAL_10_MOCK_PAPERS[0]`), defaulting missing marking to `SSC_TIER1_MARKING`. The chat calls `planPracticeRequest(query, pastAttempts, buildChatContext(exam, 'PRACTICE'))` after a 400 ms delay, appends both turns to `conversationService`, and offers the returned paper as a start button; daily hours are read and written via `storageService.getDailyStudyHours`/`setDailyStudyHours` (0.5-16) and split by Tier-1 section marks from `exam.stages`, boosted by each section's share of weak topics, with a Statistics slice when the target post (`storageService.getTargetPost()`, `getPostStudyPath`) names statistics. Solutions can be filtered by result and subject and show the five-part `detailedExplanation`, an 'Open source' link and an `EvidenceButton`; the section jump tabs assume four 25-question blocks for papers of 50+ questions.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngineEntry.text: The shape of one entry in GovOS's list of practice engines: a short description of the exam's pattern, the practice modes it supports, and how to draw that exam's practice screen.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngineEntry.tech: Interface {config: {patternSummary: (exam: Exam) => string; supportedModes: string[]}; render: (props: {exam, scope: PracticeScope, onOpenProvenanceModal}) => React.ReactElement}. The value type of PRACTICE_ENGINES.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngineProps.text: What the SSC practice engine needs: the exam, a way to open a fact's evidence, and which set of tabs to show.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeEngineProps.tech: Props interface for PracticeEngine: exam: Exam, onOpenProvenanceModal(provenance: DataProvenance), optional scope?: PracticeScope (defaults to 'ALL').

src/ui.tsx::PracticePlan.text: The decision the practice test chat makes for one message: whether it built a test, refused because the topic is off the syllabus, or found no match, plus the reply text and the test itself when one was built.
src/ui.tsx::PracticePlan.tech: Interface: kind 'BUILT' | 'OFF_SYLLABUS' | 'NO_MATCH', text, optional paper: MockPaper, and topics/count/difficulty recorded on the turn so follow-ups like 'make it harder' can rebuild the same request. Returned by planPracticeRequest.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeScope.text: Which set of tabs the practice engine shows: everything, the practice tabs (past papers, section tests, topic drills), or the mock-test tabs (the custom test builder).
src/ui.tsx::PracticeScope.tech: Union type 'ALL' | 'PRACTICE' | 'MOCKS' passed as PracticeEngine's scope prop; the engine itself is the same, only the tab row differs, and the active-test and past-attempt views are always reachable.

src/ui.tsx::PracticeShell.text: The common frame around every exam's practice area: a heading ('09 — Practice & PYQs' or '17 — Mock Tests'), an introduction, the exam's code and a one-line summary of its pattern, with the engine's own content underneath.
src/ui.tsx::PracticeShell.tech: Component { exam, scope, patternSummary, intro, children }; heading chosen by scope === 'MOCKS'; badge uses examDisplayCode(exam). Pure renderer holding no exam-specific data.

src/ui.tsx::PreparationPlanner.text: The Study Roadmap section of an exam. If the exam has authored study tracks (for example a 90-day plan), the candidate picks one and sees its suggested daily timetable and week-by-week goals to tick off, with overall progress; these are clearly called GovOS suggestions, not official rules. If the exam has only a machine-read syllabus study order, it shows the syllabus roadmap instead, and if it has neither it says plainly that no study guidance exists yet rather than borrowing another exam's plan. It now shows only an authored track that has phases; for every other exam the generated study plan above it is the roadmap.
src/ui.tsx::PreparationPlanner.tech: State: selectedTrackId (first of exam.roadmapTracks, else 'TRACK_90_DAYS'), expandedPhase (1), completedGoals from storageService.getRoadmapGoals(exam.id); toggleGoal uses storageService.toggleRoadmapGoal(exam.id, key). On an exam switch it resets goals, track and phase during render (plannerExamId). No track + studyGuidance.steps -> SyllabusRoadmap; no track at all -> 'not yet generated' card naming the syllabus and pattern sections. Otherwise renders track cards, the dailyTimetable (or a note when empty), and phases with weekly goals keyed '<trackId>-p<phase>-w<week>-g<idx>'; completion counts stored keys starting with the track id over total goals, and shows 'Not tracked yet' when the track has no goals. Returns null when no track has authored phases (the old “not yet generated” card and the empty-phase panels are gone).

src/ui.tsx::PreparationPlannerProps.text: What the study planner needs: the exam it is planning for.
src/ui.tsx::PreparationPlannerProps.tech: Props interface for PreparationPlanner: exam: Exam. The JSDoc that follows it describes SyllabusRoadmap, not this interface.

src/ui.tsx::PublishedSyllabusPanel.text: Shows the syllabus exactly as the exam's authority published it, at whatever depth its document uses. If GovOS has not read an official syllabus for this exam, it says so plainly and explains that it will not borrow another exam's syllabus, pointing to the Exam Pattern section instead.
src/ui.tsx::PublishedSyllabusPanel.tech: Exported component {exam, onOpenProvenanceModal}. Reads exam.syllabusTree; counts every node recursively (useMemo). Empty tree renders an explanatory card naming the authority (authorityName before ' ('); otherwise a line with the entry count followed by one depth-0 SyllabusNodeCard per root, keyed by syllabusNodeKeys(tree).

src/ui.tsx::QUALIFICATION_WORDS.text: Plain names for the minimum education an exam needs (Class 10, Class 12, Graduation, Post-graduation), used on exam cards.
src/ui.tsx::QUALIFICATION_WORDS.tech: Record<ExamQualificationLevel, string> mapping CLASS_10, CLASS_12, GRADUATION, POST_GRADUATION to display words; used by ExamFinder's exam cards.

src/ui.tsx::QuestionPaperSourcesPanel.text: Shown next to the practice area. It lists where this exam's past question papers and answer keys are published: links from GovOS's list (third-party copies are labelled as such), the authority's own paper and key listings, and a plain statement of whether GovOS found them, could not find them, or could not finish looking.
src/ui.tsx::QuestionPaperSourcesPanel.tech: items = examResourcesFor(..., 'PRACTICE') minus official PDFs with subject 'Previous Year Papers' (already shown by the engine). repos = discovered repositories with role QUESTION_PAPER or ANSWER_KEY (shown even with no matching items) plus other repos holding PRACTICE items. states = discovered.searchStates for QUESTION_PAPER and ANSWER_KEY, rendered with SEARCH_STATE_WORDS (or the reason) and notReadWords(notRead). Returns null when all three are empty.

src/ui.tsx::REFERENCE_SECTIONS.text: The four reference sections on every exam page (FAQs, Corrigenda Log, Official Portals & Links, Cutoff History). Each names the main part it supports, so the page can lead back to it.
src/ui.tsx::REFERENCE_SECTIONS.tech: Constant array of {num, label, icon, under}: 11 FAQs & Official Clauses (under Overview), 13 Corrigenda Log (Dates & Timeline), 12 Official Portals & Links (Application & Documents), 10 Cutoff History (Results & Next Steps). ExamDetailView uses `under` for the 'backs' label and the back-to-part pager button.

src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_ROLES.text: The full list of 'what is this link for' categories GovOS uses (notification, syllabus, question paper, admit card, study material, lecture video and so on).
src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_ROLES.tech: Array of the 22 ResourceRole values; used by resourceRoleOf to accept a role already stated on the item. Mirrors the Python vocabulary in tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py.

src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_ROLE_LABEL.text: Plain names for each resource role (for example 'Answer keys', 'One-time registration', 'Lessons', 'Lead'), shown as a small heading on cards.
src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_ROLE_LABEL.tech: Record<ResourceRole, string> of display labels; also used by AuthoritySourceDiscoveryCard for search-state tiles.

src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_SECTION.text: The one table that says which section of the exam page each kind of resource goes to: question papers and answer keys to Practice, portals to Application, notices to Official Links, study material to Resources, and so on. News leads and unknown links are shown nowhere.
src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_SECTION.tech: Exported Record<ResourceRole, ResourceSection | null>; DISCOVERY_SIGNAL and UNKNOWN map to null. Mirrors SECTION_FOR_ROLE in tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py; both pinned to resource_role_cases.json 'sectionForRole'.

src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_SUBJECT_ORDER.text: The order in which subject groups appear in the Resource Library: official material first, then foundation textbooks, then the individual subjects.
src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_SUBJECT_ORDER.tech: Ordered list of ResourceItem subjects (Official Gazette, Foundation Textbooks & Open Courses, General Awareness & Static GK, Current Affairs & Governance, Banking & Financial Awareness, Quantitative Aptitude, Reasoning, English Comprehension, Computer & Typing). Subjects not listed are appended after these.

src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_TYPE_GROUPS.text: Defines the Resource Library's type filters and which kinds of entry each one covers, for example 'Official Documents & Portals' or 'Third-party (not official)'.
src/ui.tsx::RESOURCE_TYPE_GROUPS.tech: Array of { key, label, types }: OFFICIAL -> OFFICIAL_PDF, OFFICIAL_PORTAL; BOOKS -> RECOMMENDED_BOOK, SIMPLIFIED_GUIDE; VIDEO -> VIDEO_LECTURE; TOOLS -> ONLINE_TOOL; THIRD_PARTY -> THIRD_PARTY. Only groups with at least one matching resource are shown.

src/ui.tsx::RESULT_SCHEMES.text: A short list of the two exams that have their own special result screens: UPSC Civil Services and IBPS PO. Every other exam uses the general result screen.
src/ui.tsx::RESULT_SCHEMES.tech: Readonly map keyed by exact exam id: UPSC_CSE_EXAM.id -> 'UPSC_CSE', IBPS_PO_EXAM.id -> 'IBPS_PO'. Deliberately matched by stable id, never by code/title substrings. Not exported.

src/ui.tsx::REVEAL_EXEMPT.text: Parts of the page that must never wait for the fade-in: pop-up windows, the top bar and anything marked to skip it.
src/ui.tsx::REVEAL_EXEMPT.tech: Selector '.modal-overlay, .topbar, [data-no-reveal]'; elements inside a match are not bound by installRevealObserver.

src/ui.tsx::REVEAL_SELECTOR.text: Which parts of the page get the gentle fade-in when they first scroll into view: cards, tiles and anything marked for it.

src/ui.tsx::ROAD_D.text: The shape of the road the animated candidate walks along in the home page picture.
src/ui.tsx::ROAD_D.tech: SVG path data 'M40 548 C ... 330 414' used for the faint road, the travelled road and the dashed centre line, and sampled with getPointAtLength to place the walker.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceAIAssistant.text: The resource search chat inside the Resource Library. The candidate types what they want ('geometry video', 'constitution pdf') or taps a suggestion, and it replies with what it understood, the matching library items as cards with open buttons, or an honest 'nothing in the library matches' instead of a guess. A short follow-up such as 'any video on that?' is understood as being about the previous subject for the same exam. It is a word-matching search, not an AI model.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceAIAssistant.tech: Local messages state seeded with a greeting naming exam.title; eight fixed quickPrompts. handleSendMessage runs rankResourcesForQuery(text, resources, 6); if there are no results or the reading names no subject, topic or term, it tries resolveWithHistory over conversationService.history('RESOURCES') filtered to this exam's examId and keeps the expansion only if it yields results (prefixing 'Reading that as a follow-up about ...'). The reply states the reading, notes when the requested format is missing, or explains the miss with a count of entries in the named subjects. Appends user and assistant turns (with subject and examId) via conversationService.append('RESOURCES', ...). Replies render as React text via renderAssistantText (no raw HTML); matched resources render as cards whose buttons open the link or call onOpenResourceModal. The thread is not reset by an effect; it starts fresh only when the component remounts.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceAIAssistantProps.text: What the resource search chat needs: the exam's list of library items, a way to open one in the reader window, and the current exam.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceAIAssistantProps.tech: Props for ResourceAIAssistant: resources: ResourceItem[], onOpenResourceModal(resource), optional exam?: Exam (used in the greeting and to scope conversation history by examId).

src/ui.tsx::ResourceChatMessage.text: One message in the resource search chat: who sent it, the text, the time, and any library items it suggests.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceChatMessage.tech: Interface: id, sender 'USER' | 'AI', text, optional matchedResources: ResourceItem[] (rendered as action cards under an AI reply), timestamp string.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceLibrary.text: The Resource Library for an exam: study material only (official texts, books, videos and practice tools), with a 'Start here' shelf of essentials, a search box, filters by type and subject, a saved-items shelf, and results grouped by subject. Each card has one main button suited to its kind (watch, open PDF, open portal, launch tool), a save button, and a badge saying whether the link opened when last checked. It also points out how many official documents live in other sections instead, shows learning links found on the authority's own website, and includes a collapsible search helper. Everything links to the publisher's own site; nothing is stored by GovOS.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceLibrary.tech: Merges exam.resources with additions (resourceLiveService.additions, mapped by additionToResource) and keeps isLearningResource; counts others by resourcePlacementOf for a 'placed elsewhere' note. State: query, typeGroup, subjectFilter, savedOnly, bookmarkIds (storageService.getBookmarkedResourceIds, then loadBookmarksFromSQLite; toggleResourceBookmark), linkChecks, healthMeta, channelFeeds; filters reset on exam.id. On exam change: loads additions, then resourceLiveService.healthSync(urls) and channelUploads(channel ids), re-polling healthSync once after 15 s if pending > 0. 'Verify all links now' calls resourceLiveService.recheck and summarises HEALTHY/REDIRECT/BLOCKED counts. linkBadge prefers a live check, then linkVerifiedDate, then 'Link check pending' for UNDER_VERIFICATION. primaryAction is chosen by resourceFormat (YOUTUBE_COURSE / INTERACTIVE_HANDBOOK open onOpenResource). Shows discovered.learning not already listed, the essentials shelf (isEssential) and ResourceAIAssistant collapsed; showSectionNumber toggles the '08 —' heading.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceLibraryProps.text: The inputs the Resource Library needs: the exam, ways to open a resource or its evidence, and whether to show the section number in the heading.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceLibraryProps.tech: Interface { showSectionNumber?: boolean (false when used as its own top-level tab); exam; onOpenResource(resource); onOpenProvenanceModal(provenance) }.

src/ui.tsx::ResourcePlacement.text: The list of places on an exam page where a resource can appear (Resources, Practice, Application, Official Links and so on), plus 'nowhere'.
src/ui.tsx::ResourcePlacement.tech: Exported union of section keys RESOURCES, PRACTICE, APPLICATION, OFFICIAL_LINKS, CORRIGENDA, ADMIT_CARD, RESULTS, SYLLABUS, CUTOFFS, EXAM_DAY, DATES, PATTERN, OVERVIEW, NONE.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceReaderModal.text: The full-screen window that opens when a candidate opens a study resource. A PDF is shown inside the window straight from the publisher's own site, with buttons to open or download it; a single video lesson plays inside the window; a YouTube channel or an official website gets a description card and a button that opens it on its own site. GovOS stores no copy of the material.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceReaderModal.tech: Returns null when resource is null. Uses isPdfResource/getDirectPdfUrl and resourceFormat (YOUTUBE_CHANNEL, YOUTUBE_COURSE, ONLINE_TOOL) to pick the header action and body: PDF -> <iframe src='{pdfUrl}#toolbar=1&navpanes=0'> plus open/download links (download name from downloadFileName or the sanitised title); YOUTUBE_COURSE with a youtubeEmbedId -> youtube-nocookie.com embed iframe with autoplay (no embed is rendered without a real id); YOUTUBE_CHANNEL -> channel card linking youtubeUrl || url; anything else -> official-source card linking url ('Launch Tool' for ONLINE_TOOL). Shows subject, officialTag, author, description and recommendedFor; hostname is parsed from the URL, falling back to author. Close button calls onClose.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceReaderModalProps.text: What the resource reader window needs: the item to show and what to do when it is closed.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceReaderModalProps.tech: Props for ResourceReaderModal: resource: ResourceItem | null (null renders nothing), onClose().

src/ui.tsx::ResourceSection.text: The same list of places, without 'nowhere'.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceTypeGroup.text: The names of the filter groups in the Resource Library: all, official, books, videos, tools and third-party.

src/ui.tsx::ResourceTypeIcon.text: Shows a small icon matching a resource's type: a globe for websites, a play button for videos, a lightning bolt for tools, a book for books, and a document otherwise.
src/ui.tsx::ResourceTypeIcon.tech: Component { type, size = 14 } rendering a lucide icon (Globe, PlayCircle, Zap, BookOpen, FileText) coloured by resourceTypeColor(type).

src/ui.tsx::ResultNextStepsSection.text: The Results & Next Steps part of an exam page. At the top it shows the results the authority has officially declared (or says GovOS has not read any yet), and the authority's own rules for moving between stages. Below that is a self-assessment: you type your marks or upload your scorecard, pick your category and a past year, and GovOS compares your marks with that year's recorded cut-off for your category, saying clearly that this is not a result. It then suggests one of several 'what next' guides; UPSC Civil Services has its own three-stage version, and every other exam gets guides built from its own record. Your marks are remembered per exam in the browser. An exam with only one stage (an eligibility or admission test) is not asked for second-stage marks and is not offered the second-stage guides; with no category chosen the guides say ‘your category’.
src/ui.tsx::ResultNextStepsSection.tech: scheme = RESULT_SCHEMES[exam.id] for authored exams (isUPSC / isIBPS). State per exam loaded from storageService.getResultEntry(exam.id) and reset in a useEffect on exam.id (inputs, year, category via startingResultCategory, selectedStatus). Cut-off = matchCutoffRow(verdictCutoffRows(exam, selectedYear), activeCategory); no row shows a data-cutoff-state notice instead of borrowing another row. applyUpscEntry / applyMultiTierEntry build a MultiTierResultEntry and save via storageService.setResultEntry (a false return sets entryNotKept and shows a 'not kept' alert). handleScorecard calls storageService.parseResultDocument(file, exam.id), discards stale reads via isCurrentScorecardRequest and a ref counter, maps fields per scheme (keeping only this exam's skill metric keys) and saves. A verdict object (badge, headline, conclusion, recommendedTab) is computed from margins (UPSC also checks CSAT >= 66.66); a useEffect moves selectedStatus to recommendedTab unless chosen manually. Also renders exam.resultDeclarations (declared / scheduled / superseded fold), exam.resultNextSteps (official vs guidance), SkillTestCards from evaluateSkillTest, the tab row, and for non-UPSC exams a ResultPathwayPanel from resultPathway(resultPathwayOf(selectedStatus)); UPSC renders its own bespoke pathway panels. hasStageTwo = !!exam.stages[1]: the second marks box and the TIER2_PREP / BOTH_PASSED_SELECTION / TIER2_MISSED_RECOVERY tabs render only then, and selectedStatus starts (and resets on an exam switch) on TIER1_FAILED_RECOVERY otherwise.

src/ui.tsx::ResultNextStepsSectionProps.text: The inputs the Results & Next Steps part of the page needs: the exam, ways to jump to another section or to practice, and a way to open evidence.
src/ui.tsx::ResultNextStepsSectionProps.tech: Props interface: { exam; onNavigateSection(sectionNum); onNavigatePractice?; onSelectAlternativeExam?(examCode); onOpenProvenanceModal?(provenance) }. onSelectAlternativeExam is accepted but not used inside the component.

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathway.text: A complete 'what next' guide: its title, a summary, its boxes and its main buttons.
src/ui.tsx::ResultPathway.tech: Interface { id: ResultPathwayId; title; summary; blocks: ResultPathwayBlock[]; actions: ResultPathwayAction[] }, produced by resultPathway().

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayAction.text: A button inside a 'what next' guide, which can open a section of the exam page, open practice, or switch to another guide.
src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayAction.tech: Interface { label: string; section?: number; practice?: true; pathway?: ResultPathwayId }; ResultPathwayPanel runs pathway first, then practice, then section.

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayBlock.text: One box inside a 'what next' guide: a heading, its lines, a sentence to show if the exam's record has nothing for it, and an optional button.
src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayBlock.tech: Interface { key; heading; items: ResultPathwayItem[]; missing: string (shown when items is empty; never filled from another exam); action?: ResultPathwayAction }.

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayId.text: The names of the five 'what next' guides offered after a result: preparing for stage two, after passing both stages, closing a stage-two gap, a comeback after stage one, and the skill test.

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayItem.text: One line inside a 'what next' guide: a title, optional detail, and optionally the source it came from.
src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayItem.tech: Interface { title: string; body?: string; provenance?: DataProvenance }.

src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayPanel.text: Draws one 'what next' guide on screen: a summary card with its main buttons, then each box with its lines and source buttons, or the 'missing' sentence when the box is empty. Extra content such as skill-test cards can be slotted in under the summary.
src/ui.tsx::ResultPathwayPanel.tech: Props: pathway, onNavigateSection, onNavigatePractice?, onSelectPathway, onOpenProvenanceModal?, children. Action buttons dispatch to onSelectPathway / onNavigatePractice / onNavigateSection; a practice action is hidden when onNavigatePractice is absent. Renders EvidenceButton per item provenance; sets data-result-pathway, data-pathway-block and data-pathway-block-empty attributes. Holds no exam-specific text.

src/ui.tsx::ResultStanding.text: Where you stand on one stage: your score, the recorded cut-off, and the difference between them.
src/ui.tsx::ResultStanding.tech: Interface { score: number | null; cutoff: number | null; margin: number | null }.

src/ui.tsx::SEARCH_STATE_WORDS.text: Plain-English sentences for the result of GovOS looking for something on an authority's website, so that 'not found after reading everything' never reads the same as 'could not look'.
src/ui.tsx::SEARCH_STATE_WORDS.tech: Record mapping FOUND_VERIFIED, FOUND_AMBIGUOUS, FOUND_UNREADABLE, NOT_FOUND_AFTER_DISCOVERY, SEARCH_INCOMPLETE and NOT_SEARCHED to explanatory phrases; used by QuestionPaperSourcesPanel.

src/ui.tsx::SECTION_EVIDENCE_ROLES.text: For each section that an authority's own document can prove, the kind of document that counts as proof, for example a question paper for Practice & PYQs or a result notice for Results. Sections without an entry have nothing a site search can confirm or rule out.
src/ui.tsx::SECTION_EVIDENCE_ROLES.tech: Exported readonly Record keyed by section id (not exam): pyqs → QUESTION_PAPER, cutoffs → CUTOFF, results → RESULT, 'admit-card' → ADMIT_CARD, syllabus → SYLLABUS, corrigenda → CORRIGENDUM, application → APPLICATION_PORTAL, 'official-links' → NOTIFICATION. Used by resolveSectionState as the fallback when sectionStates[id].evidenceRoles is absent.

src/ui.tsx::SECTION_OF_PLACEMENT.text: For each of those sections, its fixed section number and the name the exam page shows (for example 'Practice & PYQs' is section 9).
src/ui.tsx::SECTION_OF_PLACEMENT.tech: Exported Record<ResourceSection, {num, label}> using the stable deep-link ids (1 Overview, 2 Dates, 4 Application, 5 Pattern, 6 Syllabus, 8 Resources, 9 Practice, 10 Cutoffs, 12 Official Links, 13 Corrigenda, 14 Admit Card, 15 Exam Day, 16 Results).

src/ui.tsx::SECTION_PANEL_COPY.text: The heading and short introduction shown above the official documents in sections such as Corrigenda, Admit Card, Results, Syllabus, Cut-offs, Exam Day, Dates, Pattern and Overview.
src/ui.tsx::SECTION_PANEL_COPY.tech: Partial<Record<ResourceSection, { title, intro }>> for CORRIGENDA, ADMIT_CARD, RESULTS, SYLLABUS, CUTOFFS, EXAM_DAY, DATES, PATTERN, OVERVIEW; a section without an entry gets no generic panel.

src/ui.tsx::SECTION_PANEL_FOR.text: Links each exam-page section number to the kind of documents its document panel shows.
src/ui.tsx::SECTION_PANEL_FOR.tech: Record<number, ResourceSection> built from SECTION_PANEL_COPY's keys via SECTION_OF_PLACEMENT[section].num.

src/ui.tsx::SECTION_STATE_WORDING.text: The plain-language wording for each possible status of a section on a machine-read exam, such as 'Not published yet', 'Not found', 'Source unreadable' or 'GovOS guidance'. Each status has a short label, an explanation and a colour tone, so very different situations never look the same to a candidate.
src/ui.tsx::SECTION_STATE_WORDING.tech: Record<string, {tone: 'info' | 'warn' | 'guide', label, text}> for SUPPORTED_AND_PROJECTED, RUNTIME_DERIVED, NOT_YET_GENERATED, NOT_YET_PUBLISHED, NOT_APPLICABLE, SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH, SOURCE_UNREADABLE, EXTRACTION_FAILED, NEEDS_REVIEW, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, plus the walk-derived SEARCH_INCOMPLETE, LISTED_NOT_CONFIRMED and FOUND_AFTER_BUILD. Read by SectionStateNote.

src/ui.tsx::SHOW_DEV_FIXTURES.text: A switch that is on only while developers run GovOS locally. It lets the Trust Panel show sample (made-up) monitoring data that never appears in the real app.
src/ui.tsx::SHOW_DEV_FIXTURES.tech: Boolean from import.meta.env.DEV (Vite). Gates the Trust Panel's fixture-driven HEALTH and EXTRACTION tabs (and their default tab) and DevFixtureNote; false in production builds.

src/ui.tsx::SKETCH_LINE.text: The shared pen style for the card drawings: dark ink, thick rounded lines, no fill.
src/ui.tsx::SKETCH_LINE.tech: SVG props object {fill: 'none', stroke: INK, strokeWidth: 3, strokeLinecap: 'round', strokeLinejoin: 'round'} spread onto AuthorityArt shapes.

src/ui.tsx::SKILL_TEST_WORDS.text: Recognises wording any authority uses for a keyboard skill test: typing, data entry, skill test or keyboard skill.
src/ui.tsx::SKILL_TEST_WORDS.tech: Exported case-insensitive RegExp; deliberately contains no authority's acronym. Used by skillTestInRecord.

src/ui.tsx::SOURCE_TONE_STYLE.text: The text and background colours used for each kind of source label.
src/ui.tsx::SOURCE_TONE_STYLE.tech: Record<SourceTone, { color, bg }>: OFFICIAL green, TRUSTED blue, THIRD_PARTY amber, LEAD neutral (var(--text-secondary) on var(--surface-3)).

src/ui.tsx::STAGE_WORDS.text: Patterns that recognise which exam stage a heading or paper belongs to: Preliminary, Main, Interview or Skill test.
src/ui.tsx::STAGE_WORDS.tech: Array of [RegExp, label]: /prelim/ -> 'Preliminary', /mains?|main examination|written examination/ -> 'Main', /interview|personality/ -> 'Interview', /skill|typing|computer proficiency/ -> 'Skill test'. First match wins (via stageOf).

src/ui.tsx::STUDY_REFERENCE.text: Recognises reference texts, like the Constitution, laws and NCERT textbooks, that stay study material even when filed under an official heading.
src/ui.tsx::STUDY_REFERENCE.tech: Case-insensitive RegExp matching constitution, india code, central act(s), statute(s), bare act(s), textbook(s), ncert.

src/ui.tsx::SUBJECT_TO_CANONICAL.text: Translates a readable topic name back into the phrase the assistant matches on (for example 'the pay by post' to 'salary').
src/ui.tsx::SUBJECT_TO_CANONICAL.tech: Built from FACT_SUBJECTS: label -> FACT_CANONICAL[id] (or the label itself). Used by resolveWithHistory.

src/ui.tsx::SectionSourcesPanel.text: A general document panel for one section of the exam page (for example Results or Syllabus). It shows that section's official documents from GovOS's list and from GovOS's walk of the authority's website, each appearing in only one section.
src/ui.tsx::SectionSourcesPanel.tech: Props { exam, section, onOpenProvenanceModal }; docs = examResourcesFor(..., section); groups = discoveredForSection(discovered, section) minus URLs already in docs. Returns null when SECTION_PANEL_COPY has no entry for the section or there is nothing to show; heading uses copy.title and the authority name.

src/ui.tsx::SectionStateNote.text: The coloured note at the top of a section on a machine-read exam that tells the candidate, in words, what GovOS knows about that section, for example 'Not published yet' or 'Source unreadable'. Nothing is shown for exams written by hand or for sections already verified.
src/ui.tsx::SectionStateNote.tech: Component {exam, sectionNum, discovered=null}. Returns null unless exam.origin === 'MACHINE_ACQUIRED' and exam.sectionStates exists; state from resolveSectionState; hidden for VERIFIED_AVAILABLE or unknown states. Palette by SECTION_STATE_WORDING tone (warn amber, guide primary-soft, info surface). For NEEDS_REVIEW and NOT_YET_GENERATED it prefers entry.studentStatusSummary over the generic text.

src/ui.tsx::SkillMetricResult.text: The outcome for one measure of a skill test: the measure, your figure, the standard that applies, and whether you met it.
src/ui.tsx::SkillMetricResult.tech: Interface { metric: SkillTestMetric; score: number | null; standard: { value; computed } | null; passed: boolean | null }; null means unknown (missing figure or standard).

src/ui.tsx::SkillTestCard.text: A small card for one skill test (such as a typing test) as the exam's own record describes it. It shows the test's name, duration and requirements, your entered figures against the published standard for your category, and a badge such as 'standards met' or 'below a standard'. Anything the record does not state is named as missing rather than guessed.
src/ui.tsx::SkillTestCard.tech: Props: result (SkillTestResult), position, category, onOpenProvenanceModal?. Badge from result.allPassed (true/false), else test.qualifying (QUALIFYING / COUNTED FOR MERIT), else NOT STATED. Each metric shows the score formatted with unit and outOf, or 'not entered', plus the standard ('At least'/'At most' value for the category, flagged '(computed from the printed percentage)' when standard.computed) and metric.standard.asPrinted. Lists result.notStated; EvidenceButton for test.provenance. Sets data-skill-test={test.name}.

src/ui.tsx::SkillTestInRecord.text: Describes where an exam's record mentions a typing or data-entry test: as a section of a stage, as a whole stage, only in a stage's mode description, or not at all.
src/ui.tsx::SkillTestInRecord.tech: Exported union: {where: 'SECTION', stage, section} | {where: 'STAGE', stage} | {where: 'MODE', stage} | null.

src/ui.tsx::SkillTestResult.text: The full outcome for one skill test: which stage it belongs to, each measure's result, whether all standards were met, and a list of things the record does not state.
src/ui.tsx::SkillTestResult.tech: Interface { stage; test: SkillTestSpec; metrics: SkillMetricResult[]; allPassed: boolean | null (true only when every metric has a score and a standard and meets it); notStated: string[] (phrases naming missing facts) }.

src/ui.tsx::SkyWalker.text: The drawing of the candidate in the home page animation: a boy with a backpack holding a notice, with legs that can swing.
src/ui.tsx::SkyWalker.tech: Static SVG <g className='boy'> with a shadow, two .boy-leg groups (animated by CSS while data-walking), and a .boy-body with backpack, torso, arm, notice and head; feet at origin (0, 0).

src/ui.tsx::SourceChip.text: A small coloured pill that states where a link comes from, such as 'Official source'.
src/ui.tsx::SourceChip.tech: Component { text, tone } rendering a span styled from SOURCE_TONE_STYLE[tone].

src/ui.tsx::SourceRow.text: One row in a list of documents or links: a small heading, the title, optional extra lines, a source label, an Open button and, where available, an Evidence button. The source label and buttons wrap inside the row on a narrow screen instead of pushing past its edge.
src/ui.tsx::SourceRow.tech: Component { kicker, title, url, sub?, source, note?, provenance?, onOpenProvenanceModal? }; Open is an external link (target _blank); EvidenceButton only when both provenance and onOpenProvenanceModal are given. The action group is flex '0 1 auto' with minWidth 0 and maxWidth 100% (it used to be flexShrink 0, which overflowed at 375 px).

src/ui.tsx::SourceTone.text: The four kinds of source label colouring: official, trusted, third-party and lead.

src/ui.tsx::SplitWords.text: Shows a line of text word by word so each word can spring in separately, while screen readers still read the whole line normally.
src/ui.tsx::SplitWords.tech: Component {text, start=0, className}: a .sr-only copy of the full text plus aria-hidden .split-word spans per space-separated word with --wi = start + index for CSS staggering.

src/ui.tsx::StageOf.text: Shorthand for 'one stage of an exam' in the code.

src/ui.tsx::StudyPlan.text: The whole generated plan: its days and hours, the phases, the subjects and their shares, every week, the reasons, and how many topics are left or done.
src/ui.tsx::StudyPlan.tech: Interface {days, hoursPerDay, learnDays, reviseDays, practiceDays, tracks, track, subjects, weeks, basis, unitsLeft, unitsDone, hoursPerUnit, tight}.

src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanItem.text: One line of a week: a unit and the hours given to it that week.

src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanSubject.text: A subject in the plan with its share of the time, the marks it came from, its units and its hours.
src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanSubject.tech: Interface {name, share (0–1), marks?, units, hours, included}.

src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanUnit.text: One piece of study in the plan — a syllabus topic or a part of a pattern section — with its weight and its source.
src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanUnit.tech: Interface {id, subject, name, subtopics, weight, topicId?, provenance?}.

src/ui.tsx::StudyPlanWeek.text: One week of the plan: its days, its phase (learn, second pass or full papers) and what to do.

src/ui.tsx::SyllabusNodeCard.text: One box in the official syllabus as the authority published it: a heading or topic, with its own sub-entries nested inside. Top levels start opened and deeper ones can be opened with a plus button. Where GovOS knows which document the entry was read from, an Evidence button shows that source.
src/ui.tsx::SyllabusNodeCard.tech: Recursive React component taking {node: ExamSyllabusNode, depth, onOpenProvenanceModal}. Local `open` state defaults to depth < 2; shows node.levelLabel (upper-cased), a NEEDS REVIEW badge when node.status === 'NEEDS_REVIEW', the child count, title, note, and 'Applies to:' from node.scope labels (depth <= 1 only), plus an EvidenceButton when node.provenance exists. Children render through syllabusNodeKeys(kids) so repeated ids get unique React keys; styling (padding, background, border) varies by depth.

src/ui.tsx::SyllabusRoadmap.text: A study roadmap for exams whose syllabus was read by machine from the authority's notice. It groups the syllabus into the exam's own stages and papers, shows each stage's official schedule in the authority's words, and lets the candidate tick off topics, with progress shown for the whole syllabus, each stage and each paper. It is labelled as GovOS guidance and suggests no durations or hours, because none are published.
src/ui.tsx::SyllabusRoadmap.tech: Internal component (exam, completed, onToggle). Walks exam.syllabusTree to map each node title to a stage (a 'Stage'-level node sets it, else stageOf(title)); then groups exam.studyGuidance.steps (by topicId into exam.syllabus) into phases by stage and papers by subject (subject matched by exact key, prefix, or stageOf). Progress keys are 'syllabus::<topicId>' in the completed map. A stage's schedule is non-superseded EXAM_TIER1/EXAM_TIER2/INTERVIEW dates whose stageLabel+label resolve to that stage, showing one (preferring a label containing 'schedule'). One paper open at a time (openPaper state, first paper by default). Assumes exam.studyGuidance is present (non-null assertion).

src/ui.tsx::SyllabusTreeMap.text: The 'Tree Map' view of the Syllabus section: it draws the same syllabus topics as the list, as a branching diagram from the exam, to its subjects, to topics, to subtopics. Candidates can drag to move around, zoom with buttons, a pinch or ctrl plus the scroll wheel, fit the whole tree, or open it full screen. Clicking a topic's name jumps to that topic in the official syllabus list, while the arrow beside it just opens its branch. Topics marked done show in green, and topics a verifier added or changed carry a small NEW or REV tag.
src/ui.tsx::SyllabusTreeMap.tech: Component {exam, completedTopics, onOpenTopic}. Builds the tree (useMemo) from exam.syllabus grouped by subject in register order; topic meta shows T1/T2/T1+T2 only when a stage name contains 'tier'; root label uses examDisplayCode(exam) (+ ' Syllabus' unless narrow). Resets expanded/selected on exam.id change. Layout places leaves at TREE_ROW_H + TREE_ROW_GAP pitch with parents centred on children; columns from TREE_COLS_WIDE/NARROW chosen by a ResizeObserver (narrow < 560 px); SVG bezier connectors, highlighted for the selected branch. Zoom clamped 0.3–1.8; fitZoom capped at 1 and floored at 0.5; the opening fit runs only on box size/narrow/exam change and is skipped once adjustedRef is set by manual pan/zoom (reset by Fit and the full-screen toggle). Pointer handlers do one-pointer drag and two-pointer pinch (linear to finger span) via zoomAbout; a non-passive wheel listener zooms by 1.08 per notch only with ctrl/meta. Full screen renders through createPortal into a modal overlay, locks body scroll and closes on Escape or outside click; touchAction is 'none' full screen, 'pan-y' inline. Clicking a TOPIC label closes full screen and calls onOpenTopic(topicId).

src/ui.tsx::SyllabusTreeNode.text: The shape of one box on the syllabus tree map: the whole syllabus, a subject, a topic or a subtopic, with its label, an optional small tag (like a topic count), any verifier revision, and the boxes under it.
src/ui.tsx::SyllabusTreeNode.tech: Interface {id, label, kind: 'ROOT' | 'SUBJECT' | 'TOPIC' | 'SUBTOPIC', topicId?, meta?, revision?: SyllabusTopic['revision'], children: SyllabusTreeNode[]}. Built by SyllabusTreeMap from exam.syllabus.

src/ui.tsx::SyllabusWatchState.text: The six honest situations the syllabus watch can be in: still loading, server unreachable, no notice board for this exam, board never read, nothing new, or new notices found.
src/ui.tsx::SyllabusWatchState.tech: String union type 'LOADING' | 'UNREACHABLE' | 'NO_BOARD' | 'NOT_READ' | 'NOTHING_NEW' | 'NOTICES', produced by syllabusWatchState(). Exists so a failed or never-made read is never shown as 'nothing published'.

src/ui.tsx::TREE_COLS_NARROW.text: Narrower column positions and widths for the syllabus tree map on a phone, so the text stays readable instead of the whole map shrinking.
src/ui.tsx::TREE_COLS_NARROW.tech: Constant {x: [0, 140, 310, 530], w: [124, 154, 204, 210]}, used when the tree viewport is narrower than 560 px.

src/ui.tsx::TREE_COLS_WIDE.text: The column positions and widths used for the four levels of the syllabus tree map on a wide screen.
src/ui.tsx::TREE_COLS_WIDE.tech: Constant {x: [0, 236, 500, 838], w: [200, 232, 306, 300]}: left offset and width per depth (root, subject, topic, subtopic), used when the viewport is 560 px or wider.

src/ui.tsx::TREE_OPEN_ALL_UP_TO.text: The largest syllabus size (24 topics) for which the tree map opens every subject at once. A bigger syllabus opens only its first subject so the map starts readable.
src/ui.tsx::TREE_OPEN_ALL_UP_TO.tech: Constant 24. SyllabusTreeMap opens all SUBJECT nodes by default when exam.syllabus.length <= this value; otherwise only the first subject is open by default.

src/ui.tsx::TREE_PAD.text: The margin, in pixels, between the edge of the tree map's frame and the drawn tree (16).
src/ui.tsx::TREE_PAD.tech: Constant 16 (px): inset of the drawn layer inside the viewport. Part of every screen-to-content conversion in SyllabusTreeMap (transform translate, fitZoom, centredPan, zoomAbout).

src/ui.tsx::TREE_ROW_GAP.text: The vertical gap, in pixels, between boxes on the syllabus tree map (6).
src/ui.tsx::TREE_ROW_GAP.tech: Constant 6 (px) added to TREE_ROW_H for each leaf row placed by SyllabusTreeMap's layout pass.

src/ui.tsx::TREE_ROW_H.text: The height, in pixels, of each box on the syllabus tree map (30). Kept small so a long syllabus still fits on screen at a readable size.
src/ui.tsx::TREE_ROW_H.tech: Constant 30 (px): node height in the tree's unscaled coordinates, used in layout, connector midpoints and node styles of SyllabusTreeMap.

src/ui.tsx::UPSCPracticeEngine.text: The practice area for UPSC Civil Services 2026 only. It switches between Preliminary and Main papers, shows each paper's marks, time and negative marking from UPSC's own record, and links to the real 2026 paper. On the Mains side it offers the essay-writing practice; it explains why Prelims tests cannot be scored yet, and also shows the pattern, official papers, answer keys and past attempts.
src/ui.tsx::UPSCPracticeEngine.tech: Exported component {exam, scope='ALL', onOpenProvenanceModal}. Its one hook (state `group`, 'Prelims' | 'Mains') is called first, then it returns null unless assertExamMatches('UPSCPracticeEngine', 'exam-upsc-cse-2026', exam), so React sees the same hooks on every render. `group` filters UPSC_PRACTICE_CONFIG.papers; sectionFor(regex) finds the first stage section matching sectionMatch, paperFor(regex) finds a 'Previous Year Papers' OFFICIAL_PDF resource whose title matches paperMatch. Renders inside PracticeShell: paper cards, UpscEssayPractice (Mains only), a FeatureUnavailable note per group, then ExamPatternPanel, OfficialPapersPanel, OfficialPaperCatalogue, AnswerKeyPanel and ExamAttemptHistory.

src/ui.tsx::UPSC_PRACTICE_CONFIG.text: The fixed settings for UPSC Civil Services practice: which exam it belongs to and the list of its seven papers (two Prelims, five Mains) in the order a candidate meets them, with patterns used to find each paper's details in UPSC's own record.
src/ui.tsx::UPSC_PRACTICE_CONFIG.tech: Constant {examId: 'exam-upsc-cse-2026', papers: [...], questionSource: null}. Each paper has group ('Prelims' | 'Mains'), key, label, sectionMatch (regex against stage section names), paperMatch (regex against resource titles) and objective flag; papers are GS-I, CSAT, Essay, GS-I to GS-IV (Mains). questionSource null records that no attemptable CSE item bank exists.

src/ui.tsx::UnavailablePracticeEngine.text: What a candidate sees in Practice or Mock Tests for an exam that has no practice engine built yet. It says plainly that practice is not available instead of running the exam through another exam's questions, points to the exam's pattern and syllabus, and, in Mock Tests, lists the rules any mock for this exam would have to follow. Official papers and answer keys are still shown if the authority published any. The authority’s own question-paper PDFs (such as NTA’s nine JEE shift papers) are listed too.
src/ui.tsx::UnavailablePracticeEngine.tech: Component {exam, scope, onOpenProvenanceModal}. Heading is '17 — Mock Tests' when scope === 'MOCKS', else '09 — Practice & PYQs'. Mentions exam.stages[0].stageName only when that stage is not derivedFrom; hasOfficial checks officialPapers or answerKeys length. In MOCKS scope, when any stage has sections, lists each stage (with qualifyingNature) and section (questions, marks, durationMinutes, negative marking from section or stage, else 'not stated in the notice'). Ends with OfficialPaperCatalogue and AnswerKeyPanel. Also renders OfficialPapersPanel, and hasOfficial counts resources with subject 'Previous Year Papers' and type OFFICIAL_PDF.

src/ui.tsx::UploadedFileMeta.text: A record of one file the candidate picked in the practice application form, such as a photo, signature, marksheet or certificate. It keeps the file, a preview, its name and size, its width and height for images, whether the size and shape passed the checks, and the message shown about it.
src/ui.tsx::UploadedFileMeta.tech: Interface: `file: File | null`, `previewUrl` (an object URL from `URL.createObjectURL`), `name`, `sizeKb`, optional `width`, `height`, `aspectRatio`, plus `isSizeValid`, `isDimensionValid` and `validationMessage`. Filled by `handlePhotoFileChange`, `handleSignFileChange` and `handleDocFileChange`; documents always set `isDimensionValid: true` and carry no dimensions.

src/ui.tsx::UpscEssayPractice.text: Lets a candidate practise writing an essay on one of the real topics UPSC printed in its 2026 Essay paper. It runs a timer and a word counter while they write, then saves the attempt with the time taken; it does not give a score, because essays have no official answer key. If the browser cannot store it, it warns the candidate and keeps their text on screen.
src/ui.tsx::UpscEssayPractice.tech: Component {exam, onOpenProvenanceModal}. Loads officialQuestionsForExam(exam.id) filtered to paperName containing 'Essay'; returns null if none. State: active question, answer, startedAt, elapsed (1-second setInterval while active), saved message. submit() calls storageService.saveMockAttempt with id `upsc-essay-<qid>-<startedAt>`, exam_id from the question record, score 0, total_marks = marks, time_taken_seconds and details {words, answer, questionId, notScored: true}; dispatches 'govos:attempt-saved'; shows a 'Saved' or 'Not saved' message based on kept.local, and only clears the essay when kept.local is true. List view groups questions by section with a 'Write this one' button and an OCR/under-verification note.

src/ui.tsx::WALKS.text: The timetable for the walking candidate: when each walk between milestones starts and ends during the loop.
src/ui.tsx::WALKS.tech: [[1.6, 4.8, 0, 1], [6.0, 9.2, 1, 2], [10.4, 13.6, 2, 3]] as [start s, end s, from stop, to stop]; reaching a walk's end lights the next stage.

src/ui.tsx::_CARRIABLE.text: A word list of things a person could physically carry into an exam hall, such as phones, calculators, bags, watches or jewellery. Used to tell a banned object apart from a rule of behaviour.
src/ui.tsx::_CARRIABLE.tech: Case-insensitive word-boundary regex over carry/possess verbs and object nouns (gadgets, devices, phones, calculators, watches, electronic, bags, books, notes, chits, pen drives, bluetooth, earphones, wallets, ornaments, jewellery, log tables, instruments, items, articles). Used by examDayDisplayCategory.

src/ui.tsx::_MONTHS.text: The twelve month names, used to recognise dates written in words inside quoted notice text.
src/ui.tsx::_MONTHS.tech: Lower-case array 'january'..'december'; _dateForms uses the full name and its first three letters.

src/ui.tsx::_STOP.text: Small filler words (the, and, for...) that are ignored when checking whether a name appears in a quotation.
src/ui.tsx::_STOP.tech: Set {'the','and','for','with','from','into','cum'}; _oneInQuote drops these (and words of 2 letters or fewer) before its every-word check.

src/ui.tsx::_alternatives.text: Turns the shown value into a clean list of non-empty alternatives to look for.
src/ui.tsx::_alternatives.tech: Wraps a non-array in an array, drops null, undefined and blank-after-trim entries, and stringifies the rest.
