src/ui.tsx::_bareUrl.text: Tidies a web address for comparison by dropping anything after a '#' and extra spaces.
src/ui.tsx::_bareUrl.tech: (u?: string) => string: (u || '').split('#')[0].trim(). Used by supersessionOf to compare document URLs.

src/ui.tsx::_dateForms.text: Builds the different ways a notice might print one date (21.05.2026, 21/5/2026, 21st May 2026, May 21, 2026, 2026-05-21) so GovOS can tell whether a quoted passage really contains it.
src/ui.tsx::_dateForms.tech: (y, mo, d) => RegExp[] of four patterns: dd sep mm sep yyyy (separators . / -), day with optional ordinal and optional 'of' before full or 3-letter month and year, month day[ordinal], year, and yyyy-mo-d. Leading zeros optional; digit lookarounds avoid partial matches.

src/ui.tsx::_figure.text: Builds a pattern that finds a particular number in text, with or without its commas.
src/ui.tsx::_figure.tech: (n) => RegExp matching n with optional commas, not preceded by a digit, '.' or ',' and not followed by a digit.

src/ui.tsx::_norm.text: Tidies a piece of text for comparison: lower case, single spaces, no spaces at the ends.
src/ui.tsx::_norm.tech: (s?: string) => string: lower-cases, collapses whitespace to one space and trims. Used by supersessionOf to compare notice numbers with document titles.

src/ui.tsx::_oneInQuote.text: Does the real checking for one value: a date is looked for in any printed form, a number with or without commas, and a name by making sure each of its words appears in the quote.
src/ui.tsx::_oneInQuote.tech: Normalises p.excerptText with _quoteText (empty quote returns false). ISO dates (optionally with time) go through _dateForms. Pure numbers (optionally followed by a parenthetical) are matched digit-by-digit with optional commas and no adjacent digits. Otherwise a plain substring match, then a fallback: words outside ()/[] of 3+ letters not in _STOP must all appear as tokens in the quote (no words left means false).

src/ui.tsx::_quoteText.text: Tidies up text before comparing it with a quotation: lower case, one kind of dash, single spaces.
src/ui.tsx::_quoteText.tech: (s) => lower-cases, replaces Unicode dashes and the minus sign (U+2010-U+2015, U+2212) with '-', and collapses whitespace runs to one space.

src/ui.tsx::_words.text: Simplifies text to plain lower-case words and single spaces, for loose comparison.
src/ui.tsx::_words.tech: Lower-cases, replaces runs of anything other than a-z, 0-9 and space with a space, collapses spaces and trims.

src/ui.tsx::actionForExam.text: Stamps an assistant button with the exam it was created for, but only when the button leads to a screen that shows a single exam.
src/ui.tsx::actionForExam.tech: Exported. Returns {...action, examId} when action.tab is in EXAM_BOUND_TABS; returns the action unchanged otherwise, and undefined for an undefined action.

src/ui.tsx::additionToResource.text: Turns a link that a GovOS reviewer added into a Resource Library card. If the server judged the link to be on the exam authority's own site, it is shown as official, but still marked as not verified and quoting nothing. Anything else is shown as a third-party link with a clear warning that GovOS has not fact-checked it and that the official notice wins where they disagree; a government site that is not this authority's own is labelled as such.
src/ui.tsx::additionToResource.tech: Input ResourceAddition; kind = a.sourceKind (server-derived) or 'THIRD_PARTY'. OFFICIAL -> type OFFICIAL_PDF (DIRECT_PDF), VIDEO_LECTURE (YOUTUBE_COURSE/CHANNEL) or OFFICIAL_PORTAL, officialTag 'ADDED <date> · VERIFIER-APPROVED FROM LIVE SOURCE RESEARCH' only when findingId is set, provenance EXPLANATION / UNDER_VERIFICATION with no excerpt and empty publishedDate. Otherwise type THIRD_PARTY with recommendedFor/officialTag varying for GOVERNMENT_SITE and TRUSTED_PUBLIC, provenance RECOMMENDATION / UNDER_VERIFICATION with a disclaimer excerptText. verifiedDate = addedAt's date.

src/ui.tsx::answerCandidateQuery.text: The main entry point of the GovOS assistant. It replies to greetings and thanks, keeps track of which exam the conversation is about (switching if another is named), repairs typos, adds the meaning of common phrasings, treats short follow-ups ('when is it?', 'and for OBC?') as continuing the earlier topic, then gets the answer. The reply begins by saying what it corrected or switched, and remembers its topic and exam so the next question can build on it.
src/ui.tsx::answerCandidateQuery.tech: Exported answerCandidateQuery(query, context?) -> AssistantReply; warns and uses defaultChatContext() if no context. Steps: greeting/thanks regexes; base = threadExam(ctx), switched = examNamedIn; correctAssistantQuery then expandParaphrases; if needsInheritedSubject, answers resolveWithHistory text first; a short refinement (starts with and/for/what about..., <= 3 content words) is kept only if it lands on the previous subject; otherwise answerCorrectedQuery; an unresolved reply retries with history. Sets subject from the best FACT_INTENTS/PLATFORM_MAP match if missing, stamps the action via actionForExam(activeExam.id), sets switchedExamId when the exam changed, and prefixes '(I read ... as ...)' and '(Switching to ...)' notes.

src/ui.tsx::answerCorrectedQuery.text: Produces the actual answer once the question has been cleaned up. It decides whether the candidate wants to know where something is (and points there) or wants a fact, then reads that fact from the current exam's own record: age limits and relaxations, attempts, physical standards, which dates are final, target post, what to do next, study plan, eligibility from the saved profile, dates by stage, marking and pattern, vacancies, pay, syllabus, fee, resources, admit card, cut-offs, how to apply or practice. Each fact answer cites its source; if nothing fits, it says plainly that the question is not in the verified record rather than guessing. For an exam with no posts, questions about age, vacancies, pay, physical standards or posts are answered from what its record states instead; questions its own FAQs answer are answered from them before it gives up. A question one of the exam’s own FAQs answers word for word is answered by that FAQ first; an admit-card question with no date on record is answered with the authority’s release rule; cut-offs say what kind they are and whether they are this cycle’s; after a declared result the next step names it. Age relaxations are read from the exam’s own list: SC and ST separately where an authority prints them apart, EWS where stated, a category with nothing read said to be unread (never "no relaxation"), and "a PwBD candidate who is also OBC or SC/ST gets both" only where the record carries such a combined relaxation. Asked whether there is an interview, it reads the exam's own stages: if one is an interview it gives its marks and rule, otherwise it says none is on record and lists the stages.
src/ui.tsx::answerCorrectedQuery.tech: answerCorrectedQuery(q, ctx). Orientation phrases (via has) get a platform overview. Scores PLATFORM_MAP and FACT_INTENTS with bestMatch (exact then loose); questionFocus can override the fact match. If no intent scores >= 6, namedResourceAnswer(q, 10) may answer first. Navigation wins when asksLocation(q) or nav score >= 6 and beats the fact score (adding a resourceLink when it points at section 8); a best score < 3 with 2+ content words tries namedResourceAnswer(q, 6). Then one branch per factId reading exam fields (posts, ageRelaxations/eligibilityHighlights, dates with displayWhen via shownWhen, stages, factEvidence.vacanciesTotal, cutoffsHistory by year/category, admitCardEvents, applicationGuide), ctx.profile (evaluateCandidateEligibility), ctx.targetPost, ctx.stage and ctx.daysToApplicationClose, with citeFrom citations. Falls back to nav, then namedResourceAnswer, then a full map for location questions, else {verified: false, sourceKind: UNVERIFIED, unresolved: true}. Quirks: the general age answer prints '+null years' for a relaxation the record lacks; the fee fallback (verified: false) states a generic exemption list; the location map text contains a literal '{exam}' because fillCounts is not applied to it. Exams with no posts route POST_SHAPED_FACTS (and {posts} navigation answers) to noPostsReply. Fee reads applicationGuide.fee first and no longer asserts exemptions; the admit-card answer lists the event's own instructions instead of a photo-ID rule; attempts says GovOS holds no limit rather than that the notice sets none; cut-off answers pass marks for an ELIGIBILITY_TEST and 'No cut-off is on record' when there is none; a 'documents' branch reads requiredDocuments; nextStep says 'notified, applications not yet open' once the notification date has passed; faqAnswerFor runs before the refusal. Early wholeFaq = faqAnswerFor(withoutParaphrases(q), exam, true) unless asksLocation or a fact intent scores 6+; the dates branch answers ADMIT_CARD from admitCardEvents' releaseRule / releaseNote; cut-off lines add cutoffType, say 'published for this cycle' when the year is the record's own exam year, 'no pass mark' when asked for one the record lacks, and drop 'vacancies' for an exam with no posts; nextStep POST_EXAM names the last firm RESULT date that has passed.

src/ui.tsx::answerVerification.text: Labels a whole AI answer: fully verified only if the server says so and every fact it cites checks out; partly verified if some do; otherwise not verified.
src/ui.tsx::answerVerification.tech: Maps citations through citationVerification; returns VERIFIED when a.verification === 'VERIFIED', there is at least one citation and all are VERIFIED; PARTLY_VERIFIED when any is VERIFIED; else NOT_VERIFIED.

src/ui.tsx::applicationAnswerFor.text: Writes the assistant's answer to 'how do I apply?' for a specific exam, from its own application guide: the authority's own portal (or that GovOS has not recorded one), how many registration steps there are, and which topics section 04 actually covers. It reminds the candidate that GovOS submits nothing for them.
src/ui.tsx::applicationAnswerFor.tech: Reads exam.applicationGuide: officialPortal, otrSteps length, rejectionPitfalls length, photoRules/signatureRules (counted only if they carry rules, dimensions, fileFormat or fileSize), requiredDocuments, fee, certificateRules. Lists only the covered items, or says section 04 has no guide on record. Returns paragraphs joined by blank lines.

src/ui.tsx::asksLocation.text: Detects when the candidate is asking where something is or how to get to it ('where', 'which tab', 'how do I', 'take me', 'in this platform').
src/ui.tsx::asksLocation.tech: Single RegExp test on q covering where, which tab/section/page/part, how do/can/should i, how to, what should i, navigate, find, locate, go to, open, show me, take me, 'check ... in this platform/app/site' and 'in this platform'.

src/ui.tsx::assertExamMatches.text: A guard used by each practice engine: it refuses to show anything if the engine was given a different exam from the one it was built for, so one exam's practice content can never appear under another exam's name.
src/ui.tsx::assertExamMatches.tech: Returns true when exam.id === expectedId; otherwise logs console.error('[GovOS] <engine> was handed ... Refusing to render.') and returns false.

src/ui.tsx::assistantDestination.text: Works out where an assistant button should actually go. If the button names an exam, it opens that exam even if another is open now; if GovOS does not hold that exam, it goes nowhere instead of quietly opening a different one.
src/ui.tsx::assistantDestination.tech: Exported. If action has no examId or its tab is not exam-bound, returns {exam: currentExam, tab, section}. Otherwise resolves examId against currentExam or exams; returns {exam, tab, section} or null when the exam is not found.

src/ui.tsx::assistantVocab.text: Builds the list of every word the assistant knows, used to repair typos: words from its navigation and fact keywords, common question words, resource titles and subjects, the ordinary-word list and the paraphrase meanings. It also learns the words of every exam’s FAQ questions, so ‘percentile’ is not corrected to ‘percentage’.
src/ui.tsx::assistantVocab.tech: Returns the cached set if built; otherwise adds words of length >= 4 from PLATFORM_MAP and FACT_INTENTS keys, a fixed list of whole words, every ALL_EXAMS resource's title and subject, COMMON_WORDS and ASSISTANT_PARAPHRASES 'means', then caches it in assistantVocabulary. Also adds every ALL_EXAMS FAQ question's words.

src/ui.tsx::assistantVocabulary.text: A remembered copy of the assistant's word list, so it is only built once.

src/ui.tsx::authoritySketchOf.text: Picks which drawing an exam’s card shows on the home page from the exam’s own category and career fields, so a new exam gets the right card without any code change.
src/ui.tsx::authoritySketchOf.tech: (exam) → AuthoritySketch | undefined: BANKING → banking, RAILWAYS → railway, STATE_PSC → state, CIVIL_SERVICES → civil, STAFF_SELECTION → selection, then careerFields Teaching & Education → teaching, Engineering & Technology → engineering, Civil Services & Governance → civil.

src/ui.tsx::bestMatch.text: Finds the entry in a keyword table that best fits the question, by score, rather than the first one that happens to match.
src/ui.tsx::bestMatch.tech: Generic over {keys: string[]}; computes scoreKeys(query, entry.keys, loose) for every entry and returns the highest-scoring {entry, score} (first wins ties), or null when all score 0.

src/ui.tsx::channelIdOf.text: Pulls the YouTube channel id out of a channel web address, if there is one.
src/ui.tsx::channelIdOf.tech: Matches /\/channel\/(UC[\w-]+)/ and returns the captured id, or null.

src/ui.tsx::citationVerification.text: For a fact cited in an AI answer, the page checks the evidence itself and only shows 'verified' when both its own check and the server agree.
src/ui.tsx::citationVerification.tech: (c: ClaudeAnswerCitation): own = factVerification(c.provenance, c.claim if non-empty else c.text); if own is not VERIFIED returns own; else returns 'VERIFIED' when c.verification is VERIFIED, otherwise c.verification or 'UNVERIFIED'.

src/ui.tsx::citeFrom.text: Turns a fact's source record into the short citation shown under an assistant answer (document title, page and clause).
src/ui.tsx::citeFrom.tech: Returns undefined without provenance; otherwise {documentTitle: provenance.documentTitle || fallbackTitle, pageNumber: provenance.pageNumber || 1, clauseNumber: provenance.clauseNumber || 'See source document', provenance}. Note it fills page 1 when no page is recorded.

src/ui.tsx::claimInQuote.text: Checks whether the words a source quotes actually contain the value GovOS shows beside it. If there is no value to check, it counts as fine.
src/ui.tsx::claimInQuote.tech: (p, value): returns true when _alternatives(value) is empty, else true if any alternative passes _oneInQuote(p, v). Only p.excerptText is consulted; URLs, authority names and confidence are never evidence.

src/ui.tsx::classificationIsConfirmed.text: Says whether GovOS has an official document that states a post's group classification; if not, the assistant presents the classification as the record's reading, not the authority's word.
src/ui.tsx::classificationIsConfirmed.tech: True when post.id is an own key of CLASSIFICATION_CONFIRMED.

src/ui.tsx::claudeAnswerAction.text: Builds the 'take me there' button under a Claude answer, opening the section Claude named in the exam the answer was about.
src/ui.tsx::claudeAnswerAction.tech: Exported. Looks up CLAUDE_NAV_SECTIONS[navigateTo]; if found returns actionForExam({label, tab: 'EXAM_DETAIL', section}, examId), otherwise undefined (an unknown destination gets no button).

src/ui.tsx::claudeAnswerBadgeText.text: Decides the label on an answer written by Claude. It says 'from GovOS verified data' only when every fact it cites is officially verified; otherwise it says partly verified, not verified, not in the verified record, or that Claude needs the candidate's details.
src/ui.tsx::claudeAnswerBadgeText.tech: Exported. basis NEEDS_CLARIFICATION -> 'NEEDS YOUR DETAILS'; any basis other than VERIFIED_DATA -> 'NOT IN THE VERIFIED RECORD'; for VERIFIED_DATA it uses answerVerification(answer): VERIFIED, PARTLY_VERIFIED, or else 'FROM THE EXAM RECORD - NOT VERIFIED'. All prefixed 'CLAUDE-ASSISTED'. Claude's own basis alone never earns the verified label.

src/ui.tsx::claudeJobColor.text: Chooses the text colour for a job's status: green when it succeeded, red when it failed, grey when cancelled, and gold while it is still waiting or running.
src/ui.tsx::claudeJobColor.tech: Maps status string: SUCCEEDED #137638, FAILED #b71f1f, CANCELLED var(--text-muted), anything else #8a6d00.

src/ui.tsx::claudeStateLabel.text: Turns the server's Claude status into a short label for a status tile, such as 'Ready', 'Not installed' or 'Not signed in'.
src/ui.tsx::claudeStateLabel.tech: Returns {label, ok}: no health -> 'Checking...' (not ok); health.ready -> 'Ready' or 'Ready (busy)' (ok); otherwise maps CLAUDE_DISABLED, CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_INSTALLED, CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED to readable labels, defaulting to 'Unavailable'.

src/ui.tsx::contentWordsOf.text: Picks out the meaningful words of a question, dropping filler words, very short words and plain numbers.
src/ui.tsx::contentWordsOf.tech: normaliseQuery then keeps words longer than 2 characters, not in ASSISTANT_FILLER, and not all digits.

src/ui.tsx::correctAssistantQuery.text: Fixes obvious typos in a question before the assistant tries to understand it ('whree' becomes 'where') and records each correction so the reply can say what it read.
src/ui.tsx::correctAssistantQuery.tech: Normalises the query; for each word of 4+ letters not in assistantVocab (and not a plural of a known word), finds a known word with the same first letter that fuzzyWordEq accepts, or for 4-letter words a candidate of <= 5 letters within editDistanceShort 1; prefers the candidate closest in length. Returns {text: corrected normalised words, corrections: [{typed, readAs}]}.

src/ui.tsx::cutoffFigure.text: Gives a cut-off's mark: the first-stage figure where the record labels it, otherwise its own value, or 'not stated'.

src/ui.tsx::cutoffItems.text: Lists past cut-offs for one stage for your own category, newest year first. It never shows another category's figure in place of yours.
src/ui.tsx::cutoffItems.tech: For each distinct year in exam.cutoffsHistory (descending), runs matchCutoffRow over that year's rows where c[which] (tier1Cutoff or tier2Cutoff) is non-null; keeps only MATCHED rows and maps to { title: 'year · category', body: 'N marks (postsEligible)', provenance }.

src/ui.tsx::dateClaim.text: Gives the ways a date should appear in its source: as printed (for example 'May/June 2024') and as the plain day.
src/ui.tsx::dateClaim.tech: (d) => [d.displayWhen || '', first space-separated part of d.dateTimeStr] with empty strings removed.

src/ui.tsx::dateOfType.text: Finds an exam's date of a given kind (for example the last date to apply), preferring the current one over a superseded one.
src/ui.tsx::dateOfType.tech: Returns the first date of that type with status !== SUPERSEDED, else the first of that type at all, else undefined. exam defaults to SSC_CGL_EXAM.

src/ui.tsx::defaultChatContext.text: A fallback conversation context for when none was supplied: the reference exam (SSC CGL by default), before-notification stage, and an empty history.

src/ui.tsx::discoveredForSection.text: Picks the links found on the authority's website that belong in one section of the exam page, grouped by the listing they were found on. Each link appears only once.
src/ui.tsx::discoveredForSection.tech: Over discovered.repositories, keeps items whose role is not DISCOVERY_SIGNAL and whose (item.section || repo.section || 'OFFICIAL_LINKS') equals section, de-duplicated by URL across repositories (first wins); drops empty groups. Returns { repo, items }[].

src/ui.tsx::discoveredItems.text: Collects every document or link that GovOS's walk of the authority's website listed for this exam into one list, wherever it was filed.
src/ui.tsx::discoveredItems.tech: (d: DiscoveredSources) => DiscoveredSourceItem[]: flattens d.repositories[].items with d.portals, d.practicalGuidance and d.learning (each defaulting to []).

src/ui.tsx::discoveredRow.text: Draws one link GovOS found on the authority's website as a source row, with its kind, where it was listed, its source label and any warning.
src/ui.tsx::discoveredRow.tech: Returns a SourceRow keyed by url: kicker = given kicker or RESOURCE_ROLE_LABEL[item.role] or 'Link'; sub 'Listed on: foundOnTitle'; source text item.label || sourceLabel || 'Official source' with toneOfClass(sourceClass); note = relationNote(item).

src/ui.tsx::distinctCategories.text: Builds the list of reservation categories a candidate can choose from a cut-off table, each listed once. A row that names several categories sharing one figure is split, and short and long forms of the same disability category are treated as one.
src/ui.tsx::distinctCategories.tech: Exported (rows: {category}[]) => string[]: splits each row.category on commas, trims, and de-duplicates by a key that lower-cases, strips a leading 'pwd'/'pwbd' prefix and removes non-alphanumerics (so 'OH' and 'PwBD-OH' collide); keeps the first spelling seen.

src/ui.tsx::distinctStageNames.text: Gives the short names of an exam's stages, each listed once. For example, SSC's three Tier-II papers all become one 'Tier-II'.
src/ui.tsx::distinctStageNames.tech: Exported (stages: {stageName}[]) => string[]: takes each stageName up to the first ':', '—' or '(' and trims, drops empties, de-duplicates preserving order.

src/ui.tsx::easeInOut.text: A smoothing curve that makes movements start and end gently instead of abruptly.

src/ui.tsx::editDistanceShort.text: Counts how many single-letter edits turn one short word into another, treating two swapped letters as a single edit ('crad' to 'card').
src/ui.tsx::editDistanceShort.tech: Dynamic-programming edit distance (insert, delete, substitute) with adjacent transposition counted as one (optimal string alignment). Returns the distance between a and b.

src/ui.tsx::evaluateSkillTest.text: Checks your skill-test figures against the standards in the exam's own record for your category. It reports pass or fail per measure, an overall result only when everything needed is known, and lists what the record leaves unstated.
src/ui.tsx::evaluateSkillTest.tech: For each test.metrics entry: score = skillScoreOf(entry, key), standard = skillStandardFor(metric, category), passed = null if either missing, else score >= value (AT_LEAST) or <= value (otherwise). notStated adds 'whether it is qualifying' (qualifying undefined), 'its duration or what it involves' (no duration and no requirements), and 'how it is scored' (no metrics) or 'the standard that qualifies' (a metric without standard). allPassed is set only when metrics exist and all have non-null passed. Returns SkillTestResult.

src/ui.tsx::evidenceKind.text: Decides what kind of evidence a source is: quoted directly, reconciled between two notices, calculated by GovOS, GovOS's own interpretation, or unsupported. It never assumes something is a quotation without reason.
src/ui.tsx::evidenceKind.tech: (p) => 'UNSUPPORTED' if claimNotInQuote; else p.evidenceType if set; 'DERIVED' if p.derivation; 'RECONCILED' if supersedes is non-empty or supersededBy is set; otherwise 'DIRECT' when taxonomyType === 'FACT', else 'INTERPRETATION'.

src/ui.tsx::examChecklistKey.text: Builds the name under which the browser remembers which exam-day checklist items you ticked, separately for each exam.

src/ui.tsx::examDayDisplayCategory.text: Decides which heading an exam-day instruction is shown under. An item filed as a prohibited item that does not name anything you could carry (for example a rule about which language to write in) is shown under exam rules instead; the item's words and source are unchanged.
src/ui.tsx::examDayDisplayCategory.tech: Exported (item: {category, title, description}) => category | 'CONDUCT': returns 'CONDUCT' when item.category === 'ITEMS_PROHIBITED' and _CARRIABLE does not match `${title} ${description}`; otherwise item.category.

src/ui.tsx::examDisplayCode.text: The short name to show for an exam where space is tight. Exams written into GovOS use their short code (like 'SSC CGL 2026'); exams read by machine use their full title, because their code is an internal label.
src/ui.tsx::examDisplayCode.tech: (exam) => exam.title when exam.origin === 'MACHINE_ACQUIRED' or exam.code is empty, else exam.code with underscores replaced by spaces.

src/ui.tsx::examFactStates.text: Lists the verification state of every date and post an exam shows, so the badge can say how many are officially verified.
src/ui.tsx::examFactStates.tech: Returns FactVerification[]: factVerification(d.provenance, dateClaim(d)) for each non-SUPERSEDED date, then factVerification(p.provenance, p.postName) for each post.

src/ui.tsx::examHeaderWindowTiles.text: Builds the first two date tiles under an exam's name: when applications open and when they close. If no opening date is published but a notification date is, the first tile is labelled 'Notification Date' rather than pretending it is the application start. Missing dates show 'TBA', and tentative ones are marked.
src/ui.tsx::examHeaderWindowTiles.tech: Exported (liveDates: ImportantDate[]) => {label, value}[] of length 2. First tile: APPLICATION_OPEN as 'Application Starts', else NOTIFICATION as 'Notification Date', else 'Application Starts' / 'TBA'. Second: APPLICATION_CLOSE as 'Application Closes'. Values via shownWhen; ' (Tentative)' appended when isTentative.

src/ui.tsx::examInitials.text: A very short label for an exam, such as 'TGPSC' or 'SSC CGL', used in small tiles.
src/ui.tsx::examInitials.tech: Splits examDisplayCode(exam) on whitespace; returns the first word if it has 4+ characters, otherwise the first two words joined by a space.

src/ui.tsx::examNamedIn.text: Spots when the candidate names a different exam in their message (for example 'and for UPSC?'), so the assistant can switch to it.
src/ui.tsx::examNamedIn.tech: Returns the first ALL_EXAMS entry other than current whose identifying words appear as whole words in the normalised query: code tokens of 3+ letters and title words of 4+ letters, excluding digits and GENERIC_EXAM_WORDS. Else null.

src/ui.tsx::examResourcesFor.text: Collects an exam's resources, including reviewer-added links, that belong in one particular section of the exam page.
src/ui.tsx::examResourcesFor.tech: Concatenates exam.resources with additions mapped through additionToResource, filtered to resourcePlacementOf(r) === placement.

src/ui.tsx::expandParaphrases.text: Adds the meaning of any recognised phrasing to the end of the question, so the keyword tables can find it even if the candidate never used a listed keyword.
src/ui.tsx::expandParaphrases.tech: Tests every ASSISTANT_PARAPHRASES pattern against q and appends each distinct matching 'means' string (space-separated); returns q unchanged if none match.

src/ui.tsx::factVerification.text: Works out the one honest label for a fact: officially verified, not in the quoted words, verification pending, superseded by a later notice, or no official source. Only a fact whose own quote contains the value can be 'verified'. It mirrors the server's rule, and both follow one shared list of test cases.
src/ui.tsx::factVerification.tech: (p, claim) => FactVerification: UNVERIFIED if !provenanceHasEvidence; UNSUPPORTED if claimNotInQuote; SUPERSEDED if verificationLevel is SUPERSEDED or supersededBy is set; UNDER_VERIFICATION if not OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED; UNVERIFIED if no http(s) URL plus page or excerpt; else VERIFIED when claimInQuote(p, claim), otherwise UNSUPPORTED. Pinned to tools/claude_cli/fact_verification_cases.json alongside the Python context.fact_verification.

src/ui.tsx::faqAnswerFor.text: Lets the assistant answer from the exam’s own FAQs when no other topic fits — for example “can I use this pass for DSC?” — with the FAQ’s clause and source, instead of saying it does not know. It can also be asked to answer only when one FAQ carries every word of the question, which lets a FAQ answer ahead of a general section.
src/ui.tsx::faqAnswerFor.tech: (q, exam) → AssistantReply | null: distinctive words (3+ letters, stop words removed) shared with a FAQ's question and first sentence; needs at least 2 shared and half of the question's words; returns the best FAQ's answer, officialClause and provenance, with a button to section 11. Optional third argument whole: requires every content word to be shared; a one-word question matches only a 7+ letter word in the FAQ's own question.

src/ui.tsx::fillCounts.text: Fills placeholders in the assistant's ready-made answers with live figures and text for the current exam (number of posts, resources and syllabus topics, the exam's name, and the practice, application, typing and syllabus answers), so the wording never goes out of date.
src/ui.tsx::fillCounts.tech: Replaces {practice}, {apply}, {typing}, {syllabusWhere} with practiceAnswerFor/applicationAnswerFor/typingAnswerFor/syllabusAnswerFor(exam), and {posts}, {resources} (learning resources only, via isLearningResource), {syllabus}, {exam} with counts/title.

src/ui.tsx::formatFetched.text: Writes when something was last fetched as a short date and time, or 'not yet' if it never was.
src/ui.tsx::formatFetched.tech: Returns toLocaleString('en-IN', { day, month: 'short', hour, minute }) of the ISO string, or 'not yet' for null/undefined/empty.

src/ui.tsx::formatVerifiedDate.text: Writes a date like '2026-09-09' in a friendly Indian format such as '09 Sept 2026'. If the date cannot be read, it shows it as given.
src/ui.tsx::formatVerifiedDate.tech: Parses iso + 'T00:00:00'; returns the input unchanged if invalid, else toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day: '2-digit', month: 'short', year: 'numeric' }).

src/ui.tsx::generateStudyPlan.text: Builds the study plan: splits the days into learning, a second pass and full papers; shares the learning hours between subjects and topics; moves every subject forward together week by week; leaves out ticked topics and subjects the candidate turned off; and warns when the time per topic is tight.
src/ui.tsx::generateStudyPlan.tech: (exam, {days, hoursPerDay, done?, track?, excludedSubjects?}) → StudyPlan. Learning: per-subject queues of unticked units in syllabus order, hours = learnHours × share × weight/Σweight, each week spending days/learnDays of a subject’s hours (the last week takes the rest). Revision weeks: per-subject second pass over its heaviest units. Practice weeks: one full paper every two days on the first stage’s stated questions/marks/minutes, the authority’s own papers first. tight when under 2 learning hours per unit. Pure.

src/ui.tsx::getDirectPdfUrl.text: Finds the web address of the actual PDF file for a library item, if there is one.
src/ui.tsx::getDirectPdfUrl.tech: Returns '' for null; otherwise directPdfUrl, else url when it contains '.pdf' (case-insensitive), else ''. The trailing OFFICIAL_PDF branch is redundant with the previous check.

src/ui.tsx::has.text: A quick check of whether a question contains any of a given set of phrases.
src/ui.tsx::has.tech: has(q, ...words) returns true if q.includes(any word) - plain substring matching, not whole-word. Used for the orientation check in answerCorrectedQuery.

src/ui.tsx::installRevealObserver.text: Makes cards fade and rise into place the first time they appear on screen, with a small stagger when several appear together. It does nothing for people who prefer less motion, and it never leaves content hidden.
src/ui.tsx::installRevealObserver.tech: (root) => cleanup. No-op under reduced motion or without IntersectionObserver/MutationObserver. Adds html.motion-ok; a MutationObserver (rAF-batched) scans root for REVEAL_SELECTOR elements, skipping exempt ones and nested cards (only the outermost reveals), adds .rv-wait and observes them. On intersection (rootMargin bottom -6%, threshold 0.01) it sets --rv-i (batch index capped at 8, reset after 120 ms), swaps .rv-wait for .rv-in/.rv-seen and removes .rv-in on the element's own animationend. Cleanup disconnects both observers, removes every .rv-wait and the motion-ok class.

src/ui.tsx::installSmoothWheel.text: Smooths out scrolling with a mouse wheel so the page glides instead of jumping. It leaves touchpads, touch screens, keyboard scrolling, zoom gestures, pop-ups and inner scrolling boxes alone, and it slows scrolling in sections marked for that.
src/ui.tsx::installSmoothWheel.tech: Returns cleanup; no-op under reduced motion or without a fine hover pointer. A passive:false wheel listener eases the document, or a [data-smooth-scroll] pane, towards a target at LERP 0.22 per 16.7 ms frame (frame-rate independent). It returns early for ctrl/meta, horizontal-dominant wheels, modals and nested scrollers that can still move. Pixel deltas under 40 px mark a fine (touchpad) stream for 300 ms, which stays native but is scaled by a [data-scroll-rate] zone filling the viewport (rate clamped 0.2-1). A run stops if something else moves the scroller by more than 2 px.

src/ui.tsx::isCurrentScorecardRequest.text: A safety check for scorecard uploads: a finished reading is only used if it is the latest upload and you are still on the same exam it was started for.

src/ui.tsx::isExternalUrl.text: Checks whether a value is a web address starting with http or https.
src/ui.tsx::isExternalUrl.tech: Type guard: true when value is non-empty and matches /^https?:\/\//i.

src/ui.tsx::isLearningResource.text: Says whether a resource is learning material that belongs in the Resource Library.
src/ui.tsx::isLearningResource.tech: Exported; true when resourceRoleOf(r) is in LEARNING_ROLES.

src/ui.tsx::isPdfResource.text: Checks whether a library item is a PDF document, so the reader window knows to show it as a document.
src/ui.tsx::isPdfResource.tech: Returns false for null/undefined; true if the item has a directPdfUrl, its url ends in '.pdf' or contains '.pdf?' or '.pdf#', or its resourceFormat is 'DIRECT_PDF' / type is 'OFFICIAL_PDF' and a PDF url is present. Case-insensitive on the URL.

src/ui.tsx::jobSeconds.text: Shows how long a background job has taken, in seconds.
src/ui.tsx::jobSeconds.tech: Parses startedAt (or createdAt) and finishedAt (or Date.now() if unfinished); returns 'Ns' rounded, or '' if either time is invalid or end is before start.

src/ui.tsx::journeyAt.text: Given a moment in the animation loop, works out where the candidate is on the road, which milestones are lit, whether he is walking, how far the view has zoomed in, and how visible he is.
src/ui.tsx::journeyAt.tech: (t) => {f, stage, walking, camera, fade}. For t < 0.5: first stop, stage -1, fading in. Otherwise walks WALKS: past a walk's end sets f and stage to its target; inside a walk eases f between stops and sets walking. camera = 1 + 0.045*stage (+0.015 while walking), easing back to 1 over the last 1.2 s; fade eases to 0 over the last 0.9 s.

src/ui.tsx::linkFor.text: Packages one resource as a direct link (title, address and button text) for an answer that is about that resource.
src/ui.tsx::linkFor.tech: Returns {title: r.title, url: r.url, label: resourceActionLabel(r)}; used as AssistantReply.resourceLink.

src/ui.tsx::matchesWord.text: Checks whether a question contains a given word as a whole word, also accepting simple plurals and, for longer stems, words that start with it (so 'eligib' matches 'eligible').
src/ui.tsx::matchesWord.tech: True if any query word equals word, word+'s', word+'es', the singular of a word ending in 's', or (word length >= 5) starts with word.

src/ui.tsx::matchesWordLoose.text: Like matchesWord but also forgives a small typo (such as 'negetive' for 'negative'); used only as a second attempt.
src/ui.tsx::matchesWordLoose.tech: matchesWord OR any query word (or that word minus a trailing 's'/'es') satisfies fuzzyWordEq(w, word).

src/ui.tsx::meritMaxOf.text: Gives the maximum marks a stage's merit is counted on, if the record states it. Zero means it is not stated.
src/ui.tsx::meritMaxOf.tech: Returns 0 for no stage; else stage.meritMarks if set, else 0 when unstatedFields includes 'totalMarks', else stage.totalMarks.

src/ui.tsx::meritSectionsOf.text: Lists the sections of an exam stage that count towards the merit list, leaving out any sections that make up its skill test.
src/ui.tsx::meritSectionsOf.tech: Returns stage.sections' sectionName values excluding those in stage.skillTest.sectionNames; [] for an undefined stage.

src/ui.tsx::milestoneTime.text: Turns a milestone's date text into a moment in time the computer can compare and count down from.
src/ui.tsx::milestoneTime.tech: Parses dateTimeStr (space replaced with 'T') via new Date(...).getTime(); returns NaN when the string is not a valid date.

src/ui.tsx::minutesText.text: Writes a number of minutes in a readable way, such as '2 h 30 min' or '45 min'.
src/ui.tsx::minutesText.tech: m >= 60 -> `${floor(m/60)} h` plus ` ${m%60} min` when non-zero; otherwise `${m} min`.

src/ui.tsx::moneyFigureEvidence.text: For a summary card that lists several money amounts (such as an application fee and an exam fee), finds the source for each amount separately. If no official quote prints an amount, it is returned without a source so the card can say so.
src/ui.tsx::moneyFigureEvidence.tech: (body, own, record) => [{label, figure, provenance?}]. Splits body on ';' or em dash and parses 'Label: Rs./₹ 1,234'. Uses own when its excerpt prints the figure (_figure); otherwise searches quotedProvenances(record) for one whose excerpt prints the figure and contains the label's words (_words), restricted to own.officialUrl when that is set. Used by the eligibility highlights cards.

src/ui.tsx::namedResourceAnswer.text: When the candidate names a specific resource ('typing test tool', 'constitution pdf'), answers with that item and a direct link, and says which section of the exam page holds it. It only searches the current exam's own library, and does nothing for very small libraries where a match would mean little. Words that only name the exam itself (its code or its authority’s initials) are ignored, because every entry in that exam’s library carries them.
src/ui.tsx::namedResourceAnswer.tech: Exported namedResourceAnswer(q, minScore = 6, exam = SSC_CGL_EXAM). Returns null if the library has < 5 entries, if rankResourcesForQuery(q, library, 3) has no result at minScore, or if the top item's placement is NONE. Otherwise returns {reply, score}: sourceKind OFFICIAL when the provenance is OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED else GUIDANCE, resourceLink via linkFor, up to two other hits in the same placement, and an action to EXAM_DETAIL at SECTION_OF_PLACEMENT[placement].num. Drops the exam’s code tokens and authority acronym from q before ranking; a question with nothing else left names no entry.

src/ui.tsx::navigatorFormatLabel.text: The plain wording the search chat uses for each kind of resource, such as 'a video lesson' or 'an official portal'.
src/ui.tsx::navigatorFormatLabel.tech: Record<NavigatorFormat, string>: PDF 'a PDF or official document', VIDEO 'a video lesson', CHANNEL 'a YouTube channel', PORTAL 'an official portal', TOOL 'a practice tool'. Used in ResourceAIAssistant's 'I read that as' line and the missing-format note.

src/ui.tsx::needsInheritedSubject.text: Decides whether a message names nothing of its own (like 'when is it?') and so has to borrow its topic from the conversation.
src/ui.tsx::needsInheritedSubject.tech: True when contentWordsOf(q) contains no word other than DEICTIC_WORDS.

src/ui.tsx::nextMilestoneOf.text: Finds an exam's next upcoming date and how many days away it is. A date printed without an exact day (like 'May/June') is shown as printed with no countdown.
src/ui.tsx::nextMilestoneOf.tech: (exam, now=Date.now()) => {label, when, days} | null: the earliest non-SUPERSEDED date whose parsed dateTimeStr is at or after now. when = statedWhen(d); days = ceil((at - now)/86400000), floored at 0, only when displayWhen is empty, else null.

src/ui.tsx::noPostsReply.text: The assistant’s answer for an exam that fills no post. For an eligibility test such as a TET it says there are no vacancies, pay or age band, and gives the rules its notice states instead (who may appear, what the pass is for); for any other exam with no posts on record it says the record holds none yet. An admission test such as JEE is described the same way, as an admission test.
src/ui.tsx::noPostsReply.tech: (exam, factId) → AssistantReply: examNature ELIGIBILITY_TEST → 'is an eligibility test, not a recruitment'; otherwise 'The record holds no posts … yet'. Lists eligibilityHighlights (all for eligibility/age, the first two otherwise), cites the first; study-plan and target-post questions point at the syllabus. examNature ADMISSION_TEST → 'is an admission test, not a recruitment'.

src/ui.tsx::normaliseQuery.text: Tidies a question before matching: lowercase, punctuation turned into spaces, extra spaces removed.
src/ui.tsx::normaliseQuery.tech: Lowercases, replaces every character outside a-z, 0-9 and whitespace with a space, collapses whitespace and trims.

src/ui.tsx::notReadWords.text: Turns counts of unread places into one readable sentence part, like '12 not fetched (the walk's file limit), 2 built by script'.
src/ui.tsx::notReadWords.tech: Maps each [key, n] of counts to `${n} ${NOT_READ_WORDS[key] || key}` and joins with ', '; '' for no counts.

src/ui.tsx::notificationDestination.text: Works out what an alert opens when tapped: the exam it is about and the right section (for example Admit Card or Results). If GovOS does not hold that exam, it opens nothing rather than a default exam.
src/ui.tsx::notificationDestination.tech: Exported. Finds notif.examId in exams (null if absent or missing). Section = actionPayload.section, else by actionType (EXAM_DETAIL 1, APPLICATION_GUIDE 4, CALENDAR 2, TIMELINE 2, ADMIT_CARD 14, RESULT 16), else 1.

src/ui.tsx::passToneOf.text: Picks a colour theme for an exam based on the authority that runs it, so the same authority always gets the same colour.
src/ui.tsx::passToneOf.tech: (seed: authority name): returns PASS_TONES[index mod 5] where index is the name's position among the unique authorityName values of ALL_EXAMS; for names not in ALL_EXAMS, a 31-multiplier string hash mod 5.

src/ui.tsx::patternMarkNodes.text: Lists every part of the exam pattern that has marks, noting which stage it belongs to and whether it is only qualifying (a minimum to pass, not counted for rank).
src/ui.tsx::patternMarkNodes.tech: (exam) → PlanMarkNode[] from patternTree (or stages’ sections): qualifying when the node’s own name says qualifying, qualifyingOnly, or a non-STAGE node not counted for merit — a screening stage that is not counted for merit is still competitive and does not make its parts qualifying.

src/ui.tsx::patternNodesFor.text: Finds the parts of the exam pattern that name a syllabus subject (inside the right paper), deepest first.
src/ui.tsx::patternNodesFor.tech: (subject, nodes) → PlanMarkNode[]: own words within the subject’s words or the reverse, and the paper’s words within the node’s path; sorted by depth.

src/ui.tsx::planHours.text: How the plan shows hours: to the nearest half hour, never less than half an hour.
src/ui.tsx::planHours.tech: (h) → max(0.5, round(h×2)/2); used only for display — the plan keeps exact hours.

src/ui.tsx::planPracticeRequest.text: The brain of the practice test chat. It reads the candidate's message, works out the topics, number of questions and difficulty, and either builds a matching practice test with a summary of what it understood, or explains honestly why it did not: the topic is outside the syllabus, GovOS has no questions on it yet, or the words matched nothing. It handles follow-ups like 'make it harder' or '20 more', and 'test my weak areas' by finding topics the candidate scored under 60% on.
src/ui.tsx::planPracticeRequest.tech: planPracticeRequest(rawQuery, pastAttempts, ctx?): PracticePlan. Applies understandPracticeRequest; if the query names no topic/subject, matches PRACTICE_MODIFIER and ctx.history has an assistant turn with topics, it rebuilds '<count> <difficulty> questions on <labels>' (stepDifficulty for harder/easier; count kept unless a non-default number was given). For focusGoal WEAK_AREAS with no topics, tallies answered questions per matchTopicByName topic across pastAttempts (paperData/userAnswers or details.*) and drills up to four below 60%. Returns OFF_SYLLABUS when every named topic is !inSyllabus with no generator (with nearest in-syllabus topics), NO_MATCH when all named topics lack supply (topicHasSupply) or nothing was recognised, else calls generateCustomMockTest and returns BUILT with a summary (topic scope, count, difficulty, time, typo corrections, request and generation notes) plus topics/count/difficulty. The syllabus is named from ctx.exam.title; topics come from SSC's TOPIC_CATALOG. Pure; exported for headless tests.

src/ui.tsx::planTokens.text: Breaks a name into lower-case words, so “Paper-I · Language-II (English)” and “Language II (English)” can be compared.
src/ui.tsx::planTokens.tech: (s) → string[]: lower-cases, turns brackets, punctuation, “·” and hyphens into spaces, drops PLAN_STOP words.

src/ui.tsx::practiceAnswerFor.text: Writes the assistant's answer to 'what practice is there?' for a specific exam, from that exam's own record: official paper and key links, catalogued papers, answer keys that actually contain answers, answer-key notices whose answers GovOS does not have, the authority's own questions GovOS holds, and GovOS-written practice only for the exam it was written for. It never borrows another exam's papers or marking.
src/ui.tsx::practiceAnswerFor.tech: Builds paragraphs from: resources placed in PRACTICE with an OFFICIAL source (sourceOfResource), exam.officialPapers count, exam.answerKeys split into keys with entries vs notices with none (naming other cycles via getExamCycle and noting login-only access), officialQuestionsForExam(exam.id) with counts lacking officialAnswerKey and UNDER_VERIFICATION. For exam.id === PRACTICE_BANK_EXAM_ID it describes the GovOS-authored papers, sectionals, drills and the first stage's negativeMarking; otherwise says no practice is written and notes when PRACTICE_ENGINES has no engine. Returns text joined by blank lines.

src/ui.tsx::prefersReducedMotion.text: Checks whether the person has asked their device for less animation, so GovOS can switch its motion off.
src/ui.tsx::prefersReducedMotion.tech: Returns true when window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') matches; false outside a browser or without matchMedia.

src/ui.tsx::provenanceHasEvidence.text: Checks whether a source gives the candidate something to look at: either a web link or the quoted words.
src/ui.tsx::provenanceHasEvidence.tech: Type guard: true when p exists and has an http(s) officialUrl or a non-blank excerptText. EvidenceButton renders nothing when it is false.

src/ui.tsx::provenanceIsVerified.text: Decides whether a source may be called officially verified: it must be marked verified, have a link, point to a page or quote the words, and not have been flagged as missing the value.
src/ui.tsx::provenanceIsVerified.tech: True only when claimNotInQuote is unset, verificationLevel === 'OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED', officialUrl is http(s), and pageNumber or a non-blank excerptText is present.

src/ui.tsx::provesSection.text: Decides whether one found document is enough, on its own, to prove that a section's information exists: it must be the right kind of document, from the authority itself, clearly for this exam and year, and actually openable. A classification that only Claude suggested does not count.
src/ui.tsx::provesSection.tech: (item, roles) => boolean: true when roles includes item.role, item.relation === 'THIS_EXAM', item.sourceClass === 'PRIMARY_OFFICIAL', item.obtainable, item.url is set, item.duplicateOf is not set, and item.roleFrom !== 'CLAUDE'.

src/ui.tsx::questionFocus.text: Finds the part of a question that actually asks something. In 'my resources are limited, what is the fee', the part that matters is 'what is the fee'.
src/ui.tsx::questionFocus.tech: Splits q on question words/phrases (what, when, how much, how many, how, which, where, who, why, is there, are there, do i, can i, tell me, give me), keeps the last question word plus what follows; returns it if it has at least one content word and is shorter than q, else null (also null if no question word).

src/ui.tsx::quotedProvenances.text: Searches an exam's whole record for every source that quotes official words, so a figure can be matched to the passage that prints it.
src/ui.tsx::quotedProvenances.tech: Depth-first walk over any object or array graph (cycle-safe via a Set), collecting objects with string excerptText and documentTitle that pass provenanceHasEvidence. Used lazily by moneyFigureEvidence.

src/ui.tsx::rankResourcesForQuery.text: Searches an exam's resource library for a request and returns the best-fitting items, best first, together with what it understood from the request. If nothing exists in the kind requested, it tries again without that requirement, and it drops weak matches so a strong answer is not padded out.
src/ui.tsx::rankResourcesForQuery.tech: rankResourcesForQuery(query, resources, limit = 6): {reading, results: {resource, score}[]}. Builds the reading (readNavigatorQuery) and rarity map, scores every resource, keeps score > 0 sorted descending; if empty and a format was named, re-ranks with format null. Keeps results scoring at least max(2, 45% of the top score), up to limit. Pure; exported for headless tests.

src/ui.tsx::readExamChecklist.text: Reads back the ticks you saved for an exam's checklist from the browser's storage. If nothing is saved or the data cannot be read, it starts empty.
src/ui.tsx::readExamChecklist.tech: localStorage.getItem(key) parsed as JSON into Record<string, boolean>; returns {} when absent or on any error (logs a console warning).

src/ui.tsx::readNavigatorQuery.text: Reads a resource search request and works out what the candidate wants: what kind of resource, which subjects, which practice topics, and which other words to search for.
src/ui.tsx::readNavigatorQuery.tech: readNavigatorQuery(rawQuery): NavigatorReading. Appends NAVIGATOR_CONCEPTS expansions, normalises (normaliseQuery) and splits the query; picks the format with the most matchesWord hits in NAVIGATOR_FORMAT_WORDS; collects directSubjects from NAVIGATOR_SUBJECT_WORDS; runs parseTestRequest for topicLabels and adds their library subjects via CATALOG_SUBJECT_TO_LIBRARY; terms are words longer than one letter that are not stopwords or format words. Pure.

src/ui.tsx::relationNote.text: Writes a short warning for a link GovOS found on an authority's website when needed: for example that it belongs to another year of the exam, does not state its year, could not be opened, was only classified by Claude, or is run by another site that the authority merely links to.
src/ui.tsx::relationNote.tech: Joins non-empty notes from DiscoveredSourceItem: relation THIS_EXAM_OTHER_CYCLE (with identity.cycle) or THIS_EXAM_CYCLE_UNSTATED, else !obtainable; roleFrom === 'CLAUDE'; relationship === 'LINKED_FROM_OFFICIAL' (names item.owner). Returns '' when none apply.

src/ui.tsx::relativeWhen.text: Says how far away a date is in everyday words: 'today', 'tomorrow', 'yesterday', 'in 16 days' or '3 days ago', and whether it has passed.
src/ui.tsx::relativeWhen.tech: relativeWhen(dateTimeStr, now) returns {text, isPast, days}: days = round((time - now) / 86400000). Special-cases 0 (today; isPast if time < now), 1 and -1; otherwise 'in N days' / 'N days ago'. An unparseable date returns empty text, isPast false, days NaN.

src/ui.tsx::renderAssistantText.text: Displays the assistant's text with any words wrapped in double asterisks shown in bold.
src/ui.tsx::renderAssistantText.tech: Splits text on **...** runs and returns React nodes: matched runs longer than 4 chars become <strong> (indigo #4f46e5), everything else plain fragments.

src/ui.tsx::researchHost.text: Shortens a web address to just the website name (for example 'ssc.gov.in'), for display.
src/ui.tsx::researchHost.tech: Returns new URL(url).hostname with a leading 'www.' stripped; if the URL cannot be parsed, returns the input unchanged.

src/ui.tsx::researchTrustMeta.text: Picks the label and colours for a research finding's trust level in the Trust Panel: green 'Official domain', blue 'Academic / public body', or amber 'Unverified source'.
src/ui.tsx::researchTrustMeta.tech: Maps ResearchFinding['trustLevel'] to {label, color, bg, border}: OFFICIAL -> 'OFFICIAL DOMAIN' (green), TRUSTED_PUBLIC -> 'ACADEMIC / PUBLIC BODY' (blue), anything else -> 'UNVERIFIED SOURCE' (amber).

src/ui.tsx::resolveSectionState.text: Works out which status banner a section of a machine-read exam should show. It normally uses the status recorded when the exam was built, but if that said 'not found', it checks GovOS's later walk of the authority's website: if that walk found a proper document, the banner says it was found; if the walk did not read everything, it says the search is incomplete instead of claiming the item does not exist.
src/ui.tsx::resolveSectionState.tech: Exported (exam, sectionNum, discovered) => string | null. Finds the exam.sectionStates entry with that sectionNum (null if none). Returns entry.state unless it is SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH and discovered is a DISCOVERED projection for this exam.id. Roles come from entry.evidenceRoles, else SECTION_EVIDENCE_ROLES[sectionId]. Returns FOUND_AFTER_BUILD if any item of those roles passes provesSection; keeps the build state if every tracked role search state is NOT_FOUND_AFTER_DISCOVERY (or none tracked); returns LISTED_NOT_CONFIRMED when FOUND_AMBIGUOUS and an official UNIDENTIFIABLE item of the role exists; otherwise SEARCH_INCOMPLETE.

src/ui.tsx::resolveWithHistory.text: Helps the assistant understand a follow-up like 'when is it?' by adding the topic the conversation was already about. If there is nothing to borrow, it gives up rather than inventing a topic.
src/ui.tsx::resolveWithHistory.tech: Exported. Takes the last assistant turn's subject, else the content words of the most recent user turn that has any; returns null if neither exists. Maps a subject label to its matching phrase via SUBJECT_TO_CANONICAL and returns {text: message + ' ' + phrase, inherited: the label or words}.

src/ui.tsx::resourceActionLabel.text: Chooses the button text for a resource link according to what it is: 'Open the PDF', 'Launch the tool', 'Watch the video', 'Open the channel' or 'Open the official page'.
src/ui.tsx::resourceActionLabel.tech: Switch on resourceFormat: DIRECT_PDF, ONLINE_TOOL, YOUTUBE_COURSE, YOUTUBE_CHANNEL, default 'Open the official page'.

src/ui.tsx::resourceFormatGroup.text: Sorts a library item into one of the five kinds (PDF, video, channel, tool, or website) so it can be compared with what the candidate asked for.
src/ui.tsx::resourceFormatGroup.tech: Maps a ResourceItem to NavigatorFormat: DIRECT_PDF or type OFFICIAL_PDF -> PDF, YOUTUBE_COURSE -> VIDEO, YOUTUBE_CHANNEL -> CHANNEL, ONLINE_TOOL -> TOOL, anything else -> PORTAL.

src/ui.tsx::resourcePlacementOf.text: Tells which section of the exam page a given resource should appear in, or 'nowhere'.

src/ui.tsx::resourceRoleOf.text: Decides what any resource card is for (its role), so it is shown in the right part of the exam page. Only learning material goes in the Resource Library; notices, papers, portals and the like go to their own sections. This must match GovOS's Python version of the same rules.
src/ui.tsx::resourceRoleOf.tech: Exported. Order: a valid stated r.role wins; third-party items (type THIRD_PARTY or EXTERNAL_PAGE) take the first ITEM_ROLE_RULES hit on title+officialTag, else QUESTION_PAPER for subject 'previous year papers', else STUDY_MATERIAL; videos/YouTube formats use videoRoleOf; ONLINE_TOOL -> PRACTICE_TOOL; subject 'previous year papers' -> ANSWER_KEY or QUESTION_PAPER; official subjects -> STUDY_MATERIAL for STUDY_REFERENCE, APPLICATION_PORTAL for APPLICATION_PORTAL_WORDS, OFFICIAL_PORTAL when 3+ roles are named or a portal names only notifications or it is an archive, else the first rule hit or OFFICIAL_PORTAL; any other subject -> ANSWER_KEY/QUESTION_PAPER if named, else STUDY_MATERIAL. Held to tools/exam_builder/resource_role_cases.json with the Python classify_resource_item.

src/ui.tsx::resourceTypeColor.text: Picks the accent colour for a resource card based on its type: green for official, red for videos, amber for tools and third-party links, indigo otherwise.
src/ui.tsx::resourceTypeColor.tech: Returns '#137638' for OFFICIAL_PDF/OFFICIAL_PORTAL, '#b71f1f' for VIDEO_LECTURE, '#af5109' for ONLINE_TOOL/THIRD_PARTY, '#4f46e5' by default.

src/ui.tsx::resourceTypeLabel.text: Turns a resource's internal type into a readable label such as 'Official Document', 'Video Course' or 'Third-party link'.
src/ui.tsx::resourceTypeLabel.tech: Switch over ResourceItem['type'] returning a display string; default 'Resource'.

src/ui.tsx::resourceWords.text: Collects all the searchable words of a library item (its title, author, tag, subject and descriptions) into one list.
src/ui.tsx::resourceWords.tech: Returns normaliseQuery of title, author, officialTag, subject, recommendedFor and description joined, split into words. Used by termRarityMap to count how many entries carry each search term.

src/ui.tsx::resultPathway.text: Builds one of the five 'what next' guides for an exam after a result, using only that exam's own record. Depending on the guide, it describes how the next stage is marked, past cut-offs for your category, linked syllabus topics, skill tests, later stages, declared next steps, certificate and document rules, physical standards, eligibility notes and the next cycle's dates. Whenever the record lacks something, the guide says what is missing instead of filling it in. With no category chosen it says ‘your category’ rather than leaving a gap.
src/ui.tsx::resultPathway.tech: resultPathway(exam, id, { category, year?, stageOne, stageTwo, now? }) -> ResultPathway. Uses the first two exam.stages (names via stageShortName) and helper builders howStage (stageFactItems, action section 5), topics (stageTopicItems, section 6), cutoffs (cutoffItems, section 10) and skillTestsAt (skillTestsOf). standingLine phrases the ResultStanding (no cut-off on record / enter marks / +margin above / below). Cases: TIER2_PREP (stage two pattern, tier2 cut-offs, skill tests, topics, stages 3+); BOTH_PASSED_SELECTION (later stages, non-superseded resultDeclarations with nextStep, applicationGuide.certificateRules and requiredDocuments, posts' physicalNote grouped); TIER2_MISSED_RECOVERY; TIER1_FAILED_RECOVERY (stage one, tier1 cut-offs, topics, eligibilityHighlights, future non-superseded NOTIFICATION/APPLICATION_OPEN dates after now); SKILL_TEST. Pure function. forCategory = ctx.category || 'your category' in the cut-off blocks and standing lines.

src/ui.tsx::resultPathwayOf.text: Translates a result verdict into the 'what next' guide that fits it.
src/ui.tsx::resultPathwayOf.tech: Maps status strings to a ResultPathwayId: TIER2_PREP/QUALIFIED_TIER2 -> TIER2_PREP; BOTH_PASSED_SELECTION/DOC_VERIFICATION -> BOTH_PASSED_SELECTION; TIER2_MISSED_RECOVERY; TIER1_FAILED_RECOVERY/NOT_QUALIFIED -> TIER1_FAILED_RECOVERY; SKILL_TEST; anything else (e.g. UPSC_* statuses) -> null.

src/ui.tsx::scoreKey.text: Scores how well one keyword or phrase describes the question. A phrase of several words scores far more than a single word because it is a more specific statement of what the candidate wants, and scores highest when its words appear together.
src/ui.tsx::scoreKey.tech: scoreKey(qWords, qNorm, key, loose). Single-word key: 1 + min(length, 12) x 0.12 if it matches, else 0. Multi-word key: 0 unless every part matches; then 6 if the joined phrase appears contiguously in qNorm else 4, plus 1.5 per word. Uses matchesWord or matchesWordLoose.

src/ui.tsx::scoreKeys.text: Gives a total score for how well a list of keywords fits the question, counting each word of the question only once so near-duplicate keywords cannot inflate a weak match.
src/ui.tsx::scoreKeys.tech: Scores every key with scoreKey, keeps those > 0, sorts descending, then adds each key's score only if it covers at least one query word not already credited (via wordsCoveredByKey). Returns the total.

src/ui.tsx::scoreResourceForQuery.text: Gives one library item a score for how well it fits the candidate's request, based on the words it shares (rarer words count more), the subject and topic asked for, and the kind of resource asked for. A score of zero means it does not fit, for example a YouTube channel when the candidate asked for a PDF.
src/ui.tsx::scoreResourceForQuery.tech: Per term, takes the best field weight it matches (title 3, author 2, officialTag 2, subject 2, recommendedFor 1, description 1) times a rarity factor (seen in <=2 entries x2, <=5 x1.4, else x1); +4 if 2+ terms appear together in the title; +3 per topic label whose first word (4+ letters) is in title/blurb. Subject: +4.25 if a direct subject, +2 if inferred, return 0 if a subject was named and it neither matches nor shares a term, and cap at 3.5 for a weak outsider when a subject was named directly. Format: adds from a requested-vs-actual table (match +5) and returns 0 when the adjustment is -3 or worse. +0.5 for isEssential. The qNorm parameter is unused.

src/ui.tsx::shownWhen.text: Formats an exam date the way the authority printed it: its own words when it gave only a month or a range, otherwise the day, with the time only if one was actually read.
src/ui.tsx::shownWhen.tech: Exported (d: ImportantDate, withTime = false) => string; a thin wrapper around statedWhen(d, withTime) from services.ts.

src/ui.tsx::skillScoreOf.text: Looks up the figure you entered for one skill-test measure (for example, typing speed). It also understands entries saved by older versions of GovOS.
src/ui.tsx::skillScoreOf.tech: Returns entry.skillScores[key] if a number; otherwise falls back to a numeric top-level property entry[key] (legacy storage); else null. Returns null for a null entry.

src/ui.tsx::skillStandardFor.text: Works out the qualifying standard of a skill-test measure for your category, exactly as the notice prints it. If the notice gives the standard as a percentage, it converts it to marks and notes that it was computed.
src/ui.tsx::skillStandardFor.tech: Returns null if metric.standard is missing or category is blank. Splits category into uppercase words and picks the first byCategory row whose categories include one; otherwise uses standard.otherwise (null if undefined). If percentOfOutOf is set, converts to (printed/100)*metric.outOf rounded to 2 decimals with computed: true (null if no outOf); else { value: printed, computed: false }.

src/ui.tsx::skillTestInRecord.text: Looks through an exam's stages to find where, if anywhere, its record mentions a typing or data-entry test, picking the most specific mention first.
src/ui.tsx::skillTestInRecord.tech: Exported. First a stage section whose sectionName or any module matches SKILL_TEST_WORDS (SECTION), then a stage whose stageName matches (STAGE), then a stage whose mode matches (MODE), else null. Reads only record fields, so new exams need no code.

src/ui.tsx::skillTestsOf.text: Finds the stages of an exam whose record says they include a skill test, such as a typing or data-entry test. Nothing else counts as a skill test.
src/ui.tsx::skillTestsOf.tech: Returns exam.stages filtered to those with st.skillTest, mapped to { stage, test: st.skillTest }. Pure; no name or mode heuristics.

src/ui.tsx::sourceOfResource.text: Decides how to label a resource from GovOS's own list: 'Official source', unless it is marked as third-party or as a recommendation, in which case it says 'Third-party source — not verified'.
src/ui.tsx::sourceOfResource.tech: Returns { text, tone }: THIRD_PARTY tone when r.type === 'THIRD_PARTY' or provenance.taxonomyType === 'RECOMMENDATION', else OFFICIAL.

src/ui.tsx::splitPaper.text: Splits a syllabus subject like “Paper 1 · Physics” into its paper and its subject.

src/ui.tsx::stageBadge.text: Chooses the short label for a stage badge using the authority's own wording ('TIER-I', 'PHASE II', 'PAPER 1'), or the stage's position ('STAGE 2') rather than GovOS's internal 'tier' term, which many exams do not use.
src/ui.tsx::stageBadge.tech: If stageName contains tier/phase/stage/paper/session/round followed by a Roman numeral, 1-2 digits or a letter A-H, returns that uppercased. Else, if stage.tier (underscores to spaces) is 'TIER n', returns 'STAGE ' + stageNumber; otherwise returns the tier text (e.g. INTERVIEW).

src/ui.tsx::stageFactItems.text: Lists the key facts about a stage as its notice states them: marks, time, the penalty for wrong answers, how the stage counts, and which sections count towards merit. Only facts the record actually has are listed.
src/ui.tsx::stageFactItems.tech: Builds ResultPathwayItems from a stage, each citing stage.provenance: 'Marks' (only if meritMaxOf > 0; shows meritMarks of totalMarks when meritMarks is set), 'Time' (durationMinutes > 0 and not in unstatedFields, via minutesText), 'Wrong answers' (negativeMarking), 'How it counts' (qualifyingNature), and 'Sections its merit is counted on' (meritSectionsOf, with question and mark counts).

src/ui.tsx::stageOf.text: Looks at a piece of text and says which exam stage it names, or nothing if it names none.
src/ui.tsx::stageOf.tech: stageOf(text): string | null; returns the label of the first STAGE_WORDS pattern matching text (empty string safe), else null.

src/ui.tsx::stageShortName.text: Gives a short name for an exam stage by cutting its full name at the first colon, dash or bracket, with a fallback name if there is no stage.
src/ui.tsx::stageShortName.tech: Returns stageName split on /[:—(]/ first part, trimmed; uses fallback when the stage is undefined or the result is empty. Not exported.

src/ui.tsx::stageTopicItems.text: Picks up to eight syllabus topics the exam's record links to a stage, putting high-yield and heavily weighted topics first.
src/ui.tsx::stageTopicItems.tech: Filters exam.syllabus to topics with tier equal to the stage's tier or 'BOTH', sorts by isHighYield then weightagePercentage descending, takes 8, maps to items { title: topicName, body: subject (+ high-yield note), provenance: officialProvenance }.

src/ui.tsx::startingResultCategory.text: Decides which category the result screen starts on: the one you saved, otherwise your profile's category if the record has a cut-off for it, otherwise none.
src/ui.tsx::startingResultCategory.tech: Returns saved.category if set; else matchCutoffRow(verdictCutoffRows(exam, year), profileCategory) and its row.category when MATCHED; else ''. Replaces an old fallback to the first row's category.

src/ui.tsx::stepDifficulty.text: Moves a test's difficulty one step up or down between Easy, Medium and Hard, never past either end.
src/ui.tsx::stepDifficulty.tech: stepDifficulty(current, up): returns the next level on ['EASY','MEDIUM','HARD'] from current (unknown/undefined treated as MEDIUM), clamped to the ladder.

src/ui.tsx::studyPlanDefaultDays.text: Chooses the plan’s starting length: the days left to the next firm exam date on record, otherwise 90 days. A tentative date or one printed without a day is never counted down to.
src/ui.tsx::studyPlanDefaultDays.tech: (exam, now) → {days (clamped 30–365), reason | null} from future, non-superseded, non-tentative EXAM_TIER1/EXAM_TIER2 dates without displayWhen.

src/ui.tsx::studyPlanTracks.text: The papers a candidate chooses between when an exam’s syllabus is organised by alternative papers (JEE’s Paper 1 / 2A / 2B, TG TET’s Paper-I / II).
src/ui.tsx::studyPlanTracks.tech: (exam) → the distinct “Paper X” prefixes of syllabus subjects, when there are two or more; else [].

src/ui.tsx::studyPlanUnits.text: Decides what the plan is made of and how much each part weighs: for a full syllabus, its topics, with each subject’s share from the marks the exam pattern gives it and each topic’s share from its weightage or breadth; for a thin syllabus, the exam pattern’s own sections and what they name. Returns the reasons in words too.
src/ui.tsx::studyPlanUnits.tech: (exam, track) → {subjects: {name, share, marks?, units}[], basis}: subject marks are read from the stage that names the most subjects; qualifying parts and unnamed subjects take the average; topic weight = weightagePercentage when every topic in the subject has one, else sub-topic count; thin path = stages’ sections (marks) and their modules (printed question counts, else 1), with each syllabus topic placed in the section it shares most words with.

src/ui.tsx::supersessionOf.text: Explains why an old date was replaced, but only as far as the record proves it. If the new date came from a numbered corrigendum (correction notice) the record holds, it names that notice; if it came from another later official statement, it names that document; otherwise it just says 'Superseded'.
src/ui.tsx::supersessionOf.tech: Exported (d, exam: {dates, corrigendums}) => {label, source}. Finds the replacing date via d.supersededBy; none → {label: 'Superseded', source: ''}. Looks for a corrigendum whose pdfUrl or provenance.officialUrl (via _bareUrl) equals the replacing date's provenance URL and whose noticeNumber is set and differs (via _norm) from both document titles → 'Superseded by corrigendum' with the notice number; else 'Superseded by a later official statement' with the replacing date's documentTitle or label.

src/ui.tsx::syllabusAnswerFor.text: Writes the assistant's answer about where an exam's syllabus is and what it contains (how many topics and subjects), mentioning weightage only if the record has it, and that topics can be ticked off.
src/ui.tsx::syllabusAnswerFor.tech: Counts exam.syllabus topics and distinct subjects; mentions GovOS's weight estimate only if some weightagePercentage > 0. With no topics, says none is on record and points to sections 06 and 05.

src/ui.tsx::syllabusNodeKeys.text: Gives each item at one level of a syllabus tree a unique label for the screen to keep track of it, because some older syllabus records repeat the same id for several items. Repeats get '~2', '~3' and so on added.
src/ui.tsx::syllabusNodeKeys.tech: Returns one React key per node: the node's id (or 'node' if empty); a repeat takes the first `${id}~${i}` (i from 2) that is neither already used nor some sibling's own id. Keys are unique only among siblings.

src/ui.tsx::syllabusWatchMessage.text: Gives the plain-English sentence to show when the syllabus watch cannot vouch that nothing changed, such as 'GovOS could not reach its server', always adding that the syllabus shown is the last verified version.
src/ui.tsx::syllabusWatchMessage.tech: Switches on syllabusWatchState(watch): UNREACHABLE and NOT_READ (appending watch.error in brackets if present) and NO_BOARD (using watch.note or a default 'No live notice board is wired...') return fixed explanatory text; every other state returns an empty string.

src/ui.tsx::syllabusWatchState.text: Works out which of the six syllabus-watch situations applies, from what the server returned about the exam's notice board.
src/ui.tsx::syllabusWatchState.tech: Pure function of SyllabusWatch | null | undefined: undefined -> LOADING, null -> UNREACHABLE, watch.source === null -> NO_BOARD, items.length > 0 -> NOTICES, otherwise NOTHING_NEW if fetchedAt is set, else NOT_READ.

src/ui.tsx::termRarityMap.text: Counts how many library items mention each search word. A word that only one or two items use is a strong clue to what the candidate means; a word half the library uses tells very little.
src/ui.tsx::termRarityMap.tech: termRarityMap(terms, resources): Map<term, count> where count is the number of resources whose resourceWords matchesWord the term. Consumed by scoreResourceForQuery's rarity multiplier.

src/ui.tsx::threadExam.text: Works out which exam the conversation is currently about, in case an earlier message switched to another exam.
src/ui.tsx::threadExam.tech: Takes the examId of the most recent assistant turn in ctx.history; returns that exam from ALL_EXAMS if it differs from ctx.exam and exists, otherwise ctx.exam.

src/ui.tsx::tokensWithin.text: Whether every word of one name appears in another.
src/ui.tsx::tokensWithin.tech: (a, b) → a non-empty and every word of a in b.

src/ui.tsx::toneOfClass.text: Chooses the label colour for a source found on the web, based on how GovOS classified it.
src/ui.tsx::toneOfClass.tech: PRIMARY_OFFICIAL -> OFFICIAL, TRUSTED_SECONDARY -> TRUSTED, DISCOVERY_ONLY -> LEAD, anything else -> THIRD_PARTY.

src/ui.tsx::typingAnswerFor.text: Writes the assistant's answer about typing practice for a specific exam: whether its Resource Library has a typing tool, and where its own record places a typing test, quoting the record and adding nothing it does not say.
src/ui.tsx::typingAnswerFor.tech: Finds a learning resource whose title/description mentions typing, data entry or keyboard; uses skillTestInRecord(exam) to describe a SECTION (with its negativeMarking), a STAGE (with qualifyingNature) or a MODE (quotes stage.mode and points to Exam Pattern), or states the record has no such test. Returns paragraphs joined by blank lines.

src/ui.tsx::understandPracticeRequest.text: Rewrites a practice request into words the topic reader understands, for example turning 'give me the whole thing' into 'full mock test'.
src/ui.tsx::understandPracticeRequest.tech: If the full-mock pattern matches, returns '<n> questions full mock test' (n = first 1-3 digit number, if any) or 'full mock test'; otherwise appends each matching PRACTICE_CONCEPTS meaning to the query and returns it.

src/ui.tsx::unsupportedClaims.text: Counts how many of an exam's current dates and posts are shown with a source whose quoted words do not contain them.
src/ui.tsx::unsupportedClaims.tech: Counts non-SUPERSEDED dates where withClaim(d.provenance, dateClaim(d)).claimNotInQuote is set, plus posts where withClaim(p.provenance, p.postName) sets it. Used by ExamVerifiedBadge.

src/ui.tsx::useDiscoveredSources.text: Fetches what GovOS found the last time it explored the exam authority's own website, as it applies to this exam. It is empty while loading or when the server cannot be reached.
src/ui.tsx::useDiscoveredSources.tech: Hook: state null reset on examId change, then sourceDiscoveryService.forExam(examId) (backed by GET /api/sources/exam/<id>), with a cancelled guard. Returns DiscoveredSources | null.

src/ui.tsx::useExamAdditions.text: Fetches the extra links reviewers have added for one exam from the GovOS server, and refetches when you switch exam.
src/ui.tsx::useExamAdditions.tech: Hook: state [] reset on examId change, then resourceLiveService.additions(examId); ignores results after unmount or a newer examId (cancelled flag). Returns ResourceAddition[].

src/ui.tsx::usePointerDepth.text: Tracks where the mouse is over a decorative area so the picture can tilt slightly towards it. It is off for touch screens and for people who prefer less motion.
src/ui.tsx::usePointerDepth.tech: Hook (ref): with a fine hover pointer and no reduced motion, listens for pointermove and pointerleave and writes --mx and --my (-1 to 1, reset to 0 on leave) to the element once per animation frame. Used by ClubHero.

src/ui.tsx::useReplayOnChange.text: Replays a short entrance animation on part of the page whenever something changes (such as the screen or section), without rebuilding what is inside it.
src/ui.tsx::useReplayOnChange.tech: Hook (ref, key, className): skips the first run and reduced motion; otherwise removes the class, forces a reflow (offsetWidth) and re-adds it, removing it again on the element's own animationend. Effect depends only on key.

src/ui.tsx::verdictCutoffRows.text: Picks the cut-off rows for a given year that can be used to judge a stage result, ignoring rows that only give a post-level or section-level figure.
src/ui.tsx::verdictCutoffRows.tech: Returns exam.cutoffsHistory rows with year === year and a non-null tier1Cutoff or tier2Cutoff.

src/ui.tsx::videoRoleOf.text: Decides what a video is for from its title: a how-to-apply walkthrough, a news-style update (treated only as a lead), or otherwise a lesson.
src/ui.tsx::videoRoleOf.tech: Returns APPLICATION_GUIDE for titles about applying/registering/filling the form/OTR/step-by-step; DISCOVERY_SIGNAL for news words (released, out now, declared, breaking, update, announced, news); otherwise LECTURE_VIDEO.

src/ui.tsx::withClaim.text: Prepares a fact's source for display. If the source claims to quote or verify the value but its quote does not contain it, GovOS marks it so it is shown as 'not in the quoted words' rather than as verified. A source that has neither a link nor quoted words is left as it is: it is simply unverified, not 'not in the quoted words'.
src/ui.tsx::withClaim.tech: (p, value): returns p unchanged when p is missing, the value list is empty, the provenance neither has evidenceKind 'DIRECT' nor passes provenanceIsVerified, or claimInQuote passes. Otherwise returns a copy with claimNotInQuote set to the first alternative. Also returns p unchanged when !provenanceHasEvidence(p).

src/ui.tsx::withoutParaphrases.text: Gives back the question exactly as the candidate typed it, without the meanings the assistant added to it, so an FAQ is matched on the candidate’s own words.
src/ui.tsx::withoutParaphrases.tech: Recomputes which ASSISTANT_PARAPHRASES patterns match and strips their joined means-suffix when q ends with it; otherwise returns q unchanged.

src/ui.tsx::wordsCoveredByKey.text: Lists which words of the question a keyword or phrase accounts for, so the same word is not counted twice.
src/ui.tsx::wordsCoveredByKey.tech: Returns [] unless every part of the normalised key matches; otherwise the query words that match at least one part (exact or loose matcher).

src/ui.tsx::writeExamChecklist.text: Saves the current checklist ticks for one exam into the browser's storage.
src/ui.tsx::writeExamChecklist.tech: localStorage.setItem(key, JSON.stringify(ids)) inside try/catch; failures only log a console warning. Not exported.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::AuditSink.text: The basic definition of a place where Claude call records are sent. On its own it simply discards them.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::AuditSink.tech: Base class with a no-op record(event). Subclassed by MemoryAuditSink and SqliteAuditSink; the gateway's default audit target.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::AuditSink.rec.text: Receives one call record; the basic version does nothing with it.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::AuditSink.rec.tech: record(event: dict) -> None; no-op interface method.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.text: A memory of Claude answers that already passed GovOS's checks, so an identical question with the same instructions can be answered without calling Claude again. It is kept in memory and, optionally, in the database. Failures are never remembered.
