tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.tech: In-process LRU (OrderedDict, max_entries default 4000, thread-locked) of valid output dicts keyed by input fingerprint, optionally mirrored to claude_decision_cache. Values are deep-copied via JSON round-trip.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.text: Sets up an empty answer memory, optionally linked to a database file, with a maximum size.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.tech: __init__(db_path=None, max_entries=4000): stores settings, a threading.Lock and an empty OrderedDict.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.text: Forgets every answer held in memory (the database copy is untouched).
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.tech: Clears the in-memory OrderedDict under the lock only.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.text: Looks up a remembered answer, first in memory and then in the database; returns nothing if there is none or the lookup fails.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.tech: get(key) -> dict | None: memory hit moves the key to the end and returns a deep copy; else, if db_path, SELECT output_json from claude_decision_cache, load it into memory and return it; exceptions -> None.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.text: Remembers a valid answer in memory (dropping the oldest when full) and in the database if one is set; a database failure is ignored.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::DecisionCache.tech: put(key, operation, template_version, output): stores a deep copy in the LRU and trims to max_entries; with db_path, INSERT OR REPLACE into claude_decision_cache with created_at=now_iso(). Exceptions swallowed.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::INVOCATION_CO.text: The list of details recorded for every Claude call in the audit log: when, which operation, which job, how it ended, how long it took, fingerprints of the input and output, whether a cached answer was used, the tool version and usage counts. No prompt text or Claude output is recorded.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::INVOCATION_CO.tech: Tuple of claude_invocations column names: ts, operation, job_id, status, exit_category, duration_ms, template_version, input_fingerprint, output_fingerprint, cache_hit, cli_version, turns, input_tokens, output_tokens, web_search_requests, web_fetch_requests, message. Drives SqliteAuditSink's INSERT.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::MemoryAuditSi.text: A record keeper that holds Claude call records in memory, mainly so tests can inspect them.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::MemoryAuditSi.tech: AuditSink subclass storing copies of events in self.events (a list).

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::MemoryAuditSi.text: Starts with an empty list of records.
Adds a copy of one call record to the in-memory list.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::SqliteAuditSi.text: A record keeper that writes each Claude call record into the database's audit table.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::SqliteAuditSi.tech: AuditSink writing rows to claude_invocations in the SQLite file at db_path. Used by app.py's gateway.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::SqliteAuditSi.text: Remembers which database file to write to.
Writes one call record into the audit table. If writing fails for any reason, it is silently skipped, so auditing can never break the call it describes.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::SqliteAuditSi.tech: Opens sqlite3 (timeout 10), init_audit_tables, INSERTs INVOCATION_COLUMNS values (missing -> '', cache_hit as 0/1), commits, closes. All exceptions swallowed.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::init_audit_ta.text: Creates the two database tables for Claude: the audit log of calls and the cache of valid answers, if they do not exist yet.
tools/claude_cli/audit.py::init_audit_ta.tech: init_audit_tables(conn): CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claude_invocations (+ index on job_id) and claude_decision_cache (cache_key PK, operation, template_version, output_json, created_at). Idempotent; does not commit. Called by app.init_database and on each sink/cache DB access.

tools/claude_cli/audit.py::now_iso.text: The current time in UTC as standard text, to the millisecond, used to stamp audit records.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::Capabilities.text: What GovOS learned about the installed Claude program: its version, which options it supports, which required ones are missing, and whether it is usable.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::Capabilities.tech: Dataclass {version: str = '', flags: frozenset, missing_required: tuple, ok: bool = False}; produced by _probe_capabilities.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: The single doorway through which GovOS talks to the Claude program installed on the server. It accepts only operations from a fixed list, fills in GovOS's own fixed instructions, runs Claude in a locked-down way, and checks every reply against a strict format before anyone sees it. Failures come back as clear server states, never as facts, and every call is logged without its content.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: ClaudeGateway(config=None, *, runner=None, audit=None, cache=None, clock=time.monotonic). Locates the CLI (_resolve), detects flags from --help (capabilities), probes login (_auth_state), reports health(), and run(operation, payload) builds a hardened argv (_argv), renders the PromptTemplate to stdin, enforces concurrency via _Slots, interprets output (_interpret: JSON envelope, structured_output, strip_reasoning, schema validate) and audits via _finish. Uses SingleFlight for probes and an optional DecisionCache for cacheable templates.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Sets up the doorway: its settings (fixed, or read from the environment each time), the part that starts the program, the audit log, the optional answer memory, and the call limit.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Stores config (fixed or None), runner (default SubprocessRunner), audit (default no-op AuditSink), cache, clock; _Slots from the config's max_concurrency; empty capability and auth caches; a lock; a SingleFlight for probes.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Builds the exact locked-down command used to run Claude: print mode, a JSON reply in the operation's required format, GovOS's fixed system instructions, only the allowed tools, no saved session, no permission prompts, no local settings, plugins or slash commands, plus optional extras and a chosen model when supported.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _argv(cfg, path, op, template, caps): base argv + ['-p', '--output-format', 'json', '--json-schema', compact to_cli_schema(OPERATION_SCHEMAS[op]), '--system-prompt', template.system, '--tools', ','.join(template.tools), '--no-session-persistence', '--permission-mode', 'dontAsk', '--setting-sources', 'local', '--strict-mcp-config', '--disable-slash-commands']; adds --allowedTools (when tools and supported), --no-chrome, --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections, --model cfg.model when the flags exist.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Says whether the Claude program is signed in: yes, no, or cannot tell. The answer is remembered briefly, and simultaneous checks share one probe.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _auth_state(cfg, path) -> True | False | None. Cache key (path, cli_args_prefix) with expiry from self._clock; on miss _probes.do(('auth', key), ...) -> _probe_auth.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: The start of the command used to run Claude: the program itself, plus a test-only prefix when one is configured.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Returns [path, *cfg.cli_args_prefix].

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Checks the data for a Claude call before anything starts: it must be a set of named fields, include every required field, be no larger than allowed, and fit the shape the operation's instructions expect. A wrong shape is a bad input, not a Claude failure.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Static _check_payload(template, payload) -> list of errors: non-dict; 'missing input: k' for required keys None/''; not JSON-serialisable; larger than template.max_input_chars; else template.render(payload, '0'*16) raising -> shape error.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Turns a failure message from the Claude program into a clear state: not signed in, busy or over its usage limit, or a general failure.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Static: matches body+stdout against _AUTH_PATTERNS -> CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_AUTHENTICATED, _BUSY_PATTERNS (rate limit, 429/529, overloaded) -> CLAUDE_CLI_BUSY, else CLAUDE_CLI_FAILED. returncode is unused.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Completes a Claude result: stamps start and end times and duration, adds a safe message and a fingerprint of the output, and writes one audit record (with no prompt or output text). An audit failure never affects the result.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _finish(result, started, t0, job_id): sets started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, job_id, default message from SAFE_MESSAGES, output_fingerprint when output is present; audit.record({...INVOCATION_COLUMNS fields, stats counters...}) inside try/except. Returns result.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Reads what the Claude program returned and decides the outcome: could not start, cancelled, timed out, reply too big, error, not signed in, busy, a discovery that was blocked, no proper structured answer, or an answer that breaks the required format. Only an answer that passes every check is accepted, after any 'reasoning' fields are removed.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _interpret(op, template, outcome, result): start_error -> NOT_INSTALLED ('not_found') or CLI_FAILED; sets exit_category (timeout/cancelled/ok/nonzero); CANCELLED; CLAUDE_CLI_TIMEOUT; output_truncated -> CLAUDE_INVALID_OUTPUT. stdout parsed as one JSON envelope; non-dict -> _failure_status (or INVALID_OUTPUT when exit 0). stats from _stats; is_error / non-success subtype / nonzero exit -> _failure_status. DISCOVER_SOURCES with permission_denials -> CLAUDE_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE. Takes structured_output, else `result` parsed as a single JSON object (no prose search); non-dict -> INVALID_OUTPUT. strip_reasoning (count into stats), validate against OPERATION_SCHEMAS[op] -> CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED (first 12 errors) or OK with output.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Runs Claude's login-status command and reads whether it is signed in. A 'signed in' or 'cannot tell' answer is remembered for a minute; 'not signed in' for only 10 seconds so a fresh login is noticed quickly.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Runs `auth status` via _quick (20 s), parses stdout JSON; state = data['loggedIn'] when a bool, else None (any exception -> None). TTL _AUTH_TTL_SECONDS (60) unless state is False (_UNAUTH_TTL_SECONDS, 10). Stores (state, expiry) in self._auth.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Actually asks the Claude program for its help text and version, works out which options it has and whether all required ones are present. An unreadable help text is not remembered, so it is tried again next time.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Runs --help and --version via _quick; flags = lower-cased '--name' tokens from help; version = first x.y.z; missing = REQUIRED_FLAGS not in flags; ok = flags non-empty and none missing. Caches in self._caps only when flags were read.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Runs a short helper command of the Claude program (such as asking for its help text, version or login status), with no input, a time limit and a restricted environment.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _quick(cfg, path, args, timeout=20.0): runner.run(base argv + args, stdin_text='', env=build_child_env(), cwd=_workdir(cfg), timeout, max_output_bytes=262144).

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Finds the Claude program: the configured path if one is set, otherwise 'claude' on the system path. It refuses script wrappers (.cmd, .bat, .ps1) because they could re-interpret the arguments unsafely.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _resolve(cfg) -> _Resolved. Configured cli_path is expanded (~, env vars); not a file -> CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_INSTALLED. Else shutil.which('claude'), preferring claude.exe on Windows; none -> NOT_INSTALLED. .cmd/.bat/.ps1 -> CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED. Otherwise path and basename label.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Does the work of one Claude call in order: stop if switched off or cancelled; check the input; reuse a remembered valid answer if one exists; find and check the program, its options, its allowed tools and its sign-in; wait for a free slot; run Claude with GovOS's fixed instructions; then check the reply and remember it if valid.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _run(op, template, payload, result, cancel_event): CLAUDE_DISABLED / CANCELLED early; _check_payload errors -> CLAUDE_INPUT_REJECTED; input_fingerprint over {op, v, payload}; cacheable + cache hit that validates -> OK, cache_hit. _resolve status; caps not ok -> UNSUPPORTED; template tools other than websearch/webfetch -> UNSUPPORTED; auth False -> NOT_AUTHENTICATED. argv via _argv, prompt via template.render(payload, new_nonce()), timeout = max(10, cfg.timeout * template.timeout_factor); _slots.acquire(slot_wait) fails -> CLAUDE_CLI_BUSY; runner.run with build_child_env, workdir, max_output_bytes, cancel_event; _interpret; caches OK cacheable output.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Pulls usage numbers out of Claude's reply for the audit log: turns taken, tokens in and out, and how many web searches and page fetches it made.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Static _stats(envelope) -> {turns: num_turns, inputTokens: input + cache_creation + cache_read tokens, outputTokens, webSearchRequests: usage.server_tool_use.web_search_requests + sum of modelUsage[*].webSearchRequests, webFetchRequests: server_tool_use.web_fetch_requests}; non-int (or bool) values count as 0.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Picks the empty folder Claude runs in, creating it if needed. It never falls back to the project folder (which holds GovOS's own instructions and settings); if the chosen folder cannot be used it uses one in the system's temporary area.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: _workdir(cfg): makedirs(cfg.effective_workdir); on OSError falls back to <tempdir>/govos-claude-work, then to tempfile.gettempdir(). Returns the path.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Finds out what the installed Claude program supports, remembering the answer until the program file changes. If several requests ask at once, only one check runs.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: capabilities(cfg=None, path='') -> Capabilities. Resolves the CLI unless path is given (unresolvable -> empty Capabilities); cache key (path, mtime_ns, size, cli_args_prefix); cached hit returned; otherwise _probes.do(('capabilities', key), ...) calling _probe_capabilities.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: The current Claude settings, re-read from the environment unless fixed; it also keeps the call limit in step with them.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Property: self._config_fixed or load_config(); calls _slots.set_limit(cfg.max_concurrency) as a side effect.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Forgets the remembered sign-in state so the next check asks again.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Clears self._auth under the lock.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Reports whether Claude is ready to use: switched on, installed, a supported version, signed in, and whether all call slots are busy. It reveals no file paths, commands, accounts or secrets, only the program's short name and version.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: health() -> {enabled, installed, authenticated, ready, executable, version, busy, status, message}. Early returns: CLAUDE_DISABLED; _resolve failure (installed true only for UNSUPPORTED); caps not ok -> CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED; auth False -> CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_AUTHENTICATED. ready True when auth is True or None. busy = slots in use >= limit. Messages from SAFE_MESSAGES.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: Says whether the Claude integration is switched on.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: Returns self.config.enabled.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.text: The one function every part of GovOS uses to ask Claude something. It takes an operation name from a fixed list and the data for it, and always returns a typed result: either a checked answer or a clear failure state. An unknown operation is refused, and any unexpected error becomes a plain 'Claude failed' state rather than leaking details.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::ClaudeGatewa.tech: run(operation, payload, *, job_id='', cancel_event=None) -> ClaudeResult. job_id/cancel_event default from the job_scope ContextVar. Unknown Operation -> CLAUDE_INPUT_REJECTED ('operation is not on the allowlist'). Builds a result with TEMPLATES[op].version and calls _run; any exception -> CLAUDE_CLI_FAILED with output None. Always passes through _finish (timings, fingerprint, audit).

tools/claude_cli/client.py::JobScope.text: A small record of which background job the current work belongs to and the switch that can cancel it.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::JobScope.tech: Dataclass {job_id: str = '', cancel_event: Optional[threading.Event] = None}; held in the _SCOPE ContextVar.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::OPTIONAL_FLA.text: Extra Claude program options GovOS uses when available; without them things still work, just with a little more overhead.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::OPTIONAL_FLA.tech: ('--no-chrome', '--exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections', '--model', '--allowedtools'); documentation constant. _argv checks caps.flags for these names directly.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::REQUIRED_FLA.text: The command-line options the installed Claude program must support for GovOS to call it safely. If any is missing, GovOS refuses to use that version rather than call it with weaker protection.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::REQUIRED_FLA.tech: ('--print', '--output-format', '--json-schema', '--system-prompt', '--tools', '--no-session-persistence', '--permission-mode', '--setting-sources', '--strict-mcp-config', '--disable-slash-commands'); checked against flags parsed from `--help` in _probe_capabilities; any missing -> CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Resolved.text: The result of looking for the Claude program: its location and short name, or the reason it cannot be used.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Resolved.tech: Dataclass {path: str = '', status: Optional[InfraStatus] = None, label: str = ''} returned by ClaudeGateway._resolve; status set means unusable.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.text: A turnstile limiting how many Claude calls can run at once; the limit can be changed between calls.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.tech: Counting semaphore on a threading.Condition with mutable limit (minimum 1); methods set_limit, acquire(wait), release and properties in_use, limit.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.__ini.text: Sets up the turnstile with a starting limit and no calls running.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.acqui.text: Waits for a free slot for up to a given time; says yes and takes the slot, or says no if time runs out.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.acqui.tech: acquire(wait) -> bool: waits on the condition while _in_use >= _limit until the monotonic deadline; False on timeout, else increments _in_use and returns True.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.in_us.text: How many slots are currently taken.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.in_us.tech: Property returning _in_use under the condition lock.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.limit.text: The current maximum number of slots.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.relea.text: Gives a slot back and lets one waiting caller through.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.set_l.text: Changes how many calls may run at once and wakes any waiting callers.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::_Slots.set_l.tech: Under the condition sets _limit = max(1, limit) and notify_all().

tools/claude_cli/client.py::get_gateway.text: Gives every part of the server the same shared Claude doorway, creating a plain one if none has been set yet.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::get_gateway.tech: Returns module-global _DEFAULT under _DEFAULT_LOCK, creating ClaudeGateway() on first use.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::job_scope.text: Marks a stretch of work as belonging to one job, so every Claude call made inside it is recorded under that job and can be cancelled with it, without passing the job along by hand.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::job_scope.tech: Context manager job_scope(job_id='', cancel_event=None): sets _SCOPE to JobScope(job_id, cancel_event) and resets the token on exit. ClaudeGateway.run falls back to these values when not passed explicitly.

tools/claude_cli/client.py::set_gateway.text: Installs the shared Claude doorway (or clears it). The app uses it to attach its audit log and answer memory; tests use it to put in a fake.
tools/claude_cli/client.py::set_gateway.tech: set_gateway(gateway: Optional[ClaudeGateway]): sets _DEFAULT under _DEFAULT_LOCK; None resets so get_gateway creates a fresh default.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ClaudeConfig.text: The fixed set of Claude settings in use: whether it is on, where the program is, time limit, how many calls at once, largest reply, the empty folder it runs in, an optional model, and how long to wait for a free slot. It cannot be changed once made.
tools/claude_cli/config.py::ClaudeConfig.tech: Frozen dataclass: enabled=False, cli_path='', timeout_seconds=120, max_concurrency=2, max_output_bytes=262144, workdir='', model='', slot_wait_seconds=30, cli_args_prefix=() (test-only, never read from env or a request, lets tests run a fake CLI script).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ClaudeConfig.text: The folder Claude actually runs in: the configured one, or a 'govos-claude-work' folder in the system's temporary directory.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_CONC.text: By default, at most two Claude calls run at the same time.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_MAX_.text: By default, a Claude reply larger than 256 KB is not accepted.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_SLOT.text: How long a request waits for a free Claude slot before being told the service is busy: 30 seconds.
tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_SLOT.tech: 30.0; default slot_wait_seconds used by the gateway's _Slots.acquire.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_TIME.text: The standard time limit for one Claude call: 120 seconds.
tools/claude_cli/config.py::DEFAULT_TIME.tech: 120.0; base per-call timeout, scaled per operation by the gateway.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_ADMIN_TO.text: The name of the setting holding the optional administrator password-like token (GOVOS_CLAUDE_ADMIN_TOKEN).
tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_ADMIN_TO.tech: 'GOVOS_CLAUDE_ADMIN_TOKEN'; declared here but not read by load_config (the security module handles it).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_CLI_PATH.text: The name of the setting that can point to a specific Claude program file (GOVOS_CLAUDE_CLI_PATH).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_CONCURRE.text: The name of the setting for how many Claude calls may run at once (GOVOS_CLAUDE_MAX_CONCURRENCY).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_ENABLED.text: The name of the setting that switches the Claude integration on (GOVOS_CLAUDE_ENABLED).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_MAX_OUTP.text: The name of the setting for the largest reply GovOS accepts from Claude (GOVOS_CLAUDE_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_MODEL.text: The name of the setting that can choose a particular Claude model (GOVOS_CLAUDE_MODEL).
tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_MODEL.tech: 'GOVOS_CLAUDE_MODEL'; empty means the CLI's own default.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_TIMEOUT.text: The name of the setting for how long one Claude call may take (GOVOS_CLAUDE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::ENV_WORKDIR.text: The name of the setting for the empty folder Claude runs in (GOVOS_CLAUDE_JOB_WORKDIR).

tools/claude_cli/config.py::_number.text: Reads a setting as a number within a safe range, using a default if it is not a number.
tools/claude_cli/config.py::_number.tech: _number(value, default, low, high): float(value.strip()) clamped to [low, high]; TypeError/ValueError -> default.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::_truthy.text: Reads a setting as on or off: '1', 'true', 'yes' or 'on' mean on.

tools/claude_cli/config.py::load_config.text: Builds the Claude settings from the current environment each time it is called, applying defaults and safe ranges. Settings never come from a web request, and there is no API key setting.
tools/claude_cli/config.py::load_config.tech: load_config(env=None) -> ClaudeConfig from os.environ (or a given mapping): enabled via _truthy(ENV_ENABLED), cli_path, timeout clamped 10-900, concurrency 1-4, max output 4096-4,194,304, workdir, model. slot_wait_seconds and cli_args_prefix keep their defaults.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::DEFAULT_AUT.text: Where the exported copy of the hand-written exams is kept (exam_data/authored_exams.json), which the assistant reads its facts from.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::DEFAULT_AUT.tech: os.path.join(REPO_ROOT, 'exam_data', 'authored_exams.json'); generated by `npm run export:authored`; ExamStore's default authored_path.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.text: Looks up an exam's full record by its id, first among the exams GovOS built automatically and published, then among the hand-written exams. It can also list the names of all other exams, so an answer can be checked for mentioning the wrong exam.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.tech: ExamStore(db_path, authored_path=None). get(exam_id) tries _registry_exam (read-only SQLite exam_registry) then _authored_exams (authored_exams.json, reloaded when its mtime changes). other_exam_names(exam_id) returns titles and codes (space-separated, at least 6 chars) of every other exam. Used by AppHooks and app.py's sources routes.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.text: Sets up the exam lookup with the database file and the hand-written exams file.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.tech: Stores db_path, authored_path (default DEFAULT_AUTHORED_PATH), a lock, an empty authored cache and _authored_mtime = -1.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.text: Reads the hand-written exams file, re-reading it only when the file has changed. If the file is missing or broken it returns no exams.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.tech: Returns {id: exam} from authored_path; reloads under lock when os.path.getmtime differs from the cached mtime; OSError on stat -> {}; read/parse error -> {} (and caches that mtime).

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.text: Reads the newest published, non-retired version of an automatically built exam from the database without changing anything.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore._.tech: _registry_exam(exam_id): read-only URI connection; SELECT exam_json FROM exam_registry WHERE exam_id=? AND published=1 AND retired=0 ORDER BY version DESC LIMIT 1; returns parsed JSON or None on any sqlite or JSON error.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.g.text: Looks up one exam's full record by its id so the AI assistant can answer from it. It checks the live exam registry first and, if the exam is not there, the exam list exported from the app's own data.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.g.tech: Strips `exam_id`; returns None for an empty id. Otherwise returns `_registry_exam(exam_id)` (latest published, non-retired row of `exam_registry`, opened read-only) or, failing that, the entry from `_authored_exams()` (the mtime-cached `exam_data/authored_exams.json`), else None.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.o.text: Collects the names of every exam GovOS knows except the one being asked about. These are used to catch an AI answer that wrongly talks about a different exam.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::ExamStore.o.tech: Builds a pool from the authored exams overlaid with every published, non-retired `exam_registry` row (read-only connection; sqlite and JSON errors are skipped). For each exam other than `exam_id`, appends its `title` and its `code` with underscores turned to spaces, keeping only strings of 6+ characters. Returns the list (may contain duplicates).

tools/claude_cli/context.py::FAQ_ANSWER_.text: How much of each FAQ answer (500 characters) is included in the facts given to Claude.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::FAQ_ANSWER_.tech: 500; truncation length for FAQ answers in the fact context.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::Fact.text: One numbered fact about an exam that the AI is allowed to use, such as a date, a post or a fee rule, together with the source it came from and exactly what it claims.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::Fact.tech: Dataclass: `id` (F1, F2...), `section`, `label`, `text`, optional `provenance` dict, and `claim` (list of printed forms the evidence must contain). Exposes the `verification` property and `as_prompt()`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::Fact.as_pro.text: The short version of the fact that is actually sent to the AI: its number, section, label and text, without the source details.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::Fact.as_pro.tech: Returns `{'id', 'section', 'label', 'text'}`; provenance and claim are deliberately left out of the prompt.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::Fact.verifi.text: The trust state of this fact, worked out from its source and its claim.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.text: The full list of numbered facts about one exam that the AI may draw on when answering a candidate, plus the exam's title and authority, and a note if some facts had to be left out for length.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.tech: Dataclass with `exam_id`, `title`, `authority`, `facts` (list of `Fact`) and `truncated` (True when the character budget dropped candidates). Provides `by_id` and `corpus()`; built by `build_fact_sheet`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.b.text: A quick lookup from a fact's number (like F3) to the fact itself.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.b.tech: Property returning `{fact.id: fact}` over `self.facts`, rebuilt on each access.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.c.text: All the words the AI answer is allowed to rely on, joined into one block of text: the exam title, the authority and every fact.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::FactSheet.c.tech: Returns a space-joined string of title, authority and each fact's 'label text'. Used by `validate_answer` as the trusted text for URLs, figures and own-exam names.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::MAX_FACT_CH.text: The most text (20,000 characters) of exam facts that may be sent to Claude for one answer.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::MAX_FACT_CH.tech: 20_000; cap on the fact sheet built for the assistant.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::MAX_QUESTIO.text: The longest question (600 characters) a candidate's message is cut to before it is used.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::MAX_QUESTIO.tech: 600; limit applied with clean_text to candidate questions.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::REPO_ROOT.text: The project's top folder, worked out from where this file sits.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::REPO_ROOT.tech: Three dirname()s up from context.py's absolute path.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_candidates.text: Walks through an exam's record and lists every fact it can offer the AI, in a fixed order: overview, dates, eligibility, posts, fees, stages, syllabus, FAQs, corrections, admit card, results, exam-day items, links and cut-offs. Each fact carries its source and what its source must say for it to count as verified.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_candidates.tech: Returns tuples (section, label, text, provenance, claim). `add` skips blank text and defaults the claim to [text]. Covers title/authority, cycle, vacanciesTotal and crucialEligibilityDate (with `factEvidence`), overview (500 chars), each date (via `_when`, tagged tentative/superseded, claim = displayWhen + day), eligibility highlights, posts (name, age band, pay, classification, qualification), fee rules and modes, application portal, stages (marks, minutes, negative marking), syllabus grouped by subject (first topic's provenance), FAQs, corrigenda, admit-card events, result declarations, exam-day checklist, official links and a count of cut-off rows. Text is clipped with `_short`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_clock_form.text: For each 24-hour time in the facts (like 18:00), works out the 12-hour hour (6) so an answer that says '6 PM' is accepted.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_clock_form.tech: For every HH:MM in `text` (`_CLOCK`), adds str(h-12) when h > 12 and '12' when h == 0; hours 1-12 add nothing (they already appear as digits). Returns a set of strings.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_date_forms.text: Given one calendar date, lists all the usual ways an Indian notice might print it (21.05.2026, 21st May 2026, May 21, 2026, 2026-05-21 and so on), so GovOS can check whether a quote really contains that date.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_date_forms.tech: Takes year, month and day strings and returns four compiled ASCII regexes: dd[./-]mm[./-]yyyy with optional leading zeros, 'dd(st|nd|rd|th)? (of)? Month|Mon. ,? yyyy', 'Month|Mon. dd(st..)? ,? yyyy', and 'yyyy-m-d'. Digit look-arounds stop partial number matches.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_figure_gro.text: Pulls out every number in a piece of text (without leading zeros), so an answer's numbers can be checked against the allowed ones. A date like 2024-03-16 gives 2024, 3 and 16.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_figure_gro.tech: Returns the set of `_norm_group` of every `\d+` run in `text`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_norm_group.text: Removes leading zeros from a number written as text, so '07' and '7' count as the same figure.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_norm_group.tech: Returns `group.lstrip('0')`, or '0' if that leaves nothing.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_norm_url.text: Tidies a web address for comparison: trailing punctuation and slash removed, lower case.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_norm_url.tech: Strips trailing '.,;:!?\'"', then a trailing '/', and lower-cases.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_one_in_quo.text: Checks whether one value (a date, a number or a phrase) actually appears in the words an official source is quoted as saying. This is how GovOS decides a quote really backs up a fact.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_one_in_quo.tech: Normalises the provenance's `excerptText`; empty quote -> False. ISO dates (optionally with a time) match any `_date_forms` pattern; a pure number (optionally followed by a parenthetical) matches its digits with optional commas between them; otherwise the normalised value as a substring, or failing that every word of 3+ letters (brackets removed, small stop words dropped) must appear among the quote's words. No qualifying words -> False.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_quote_text.text: Tidies a piece of quoted text so two versions of the same words can be compared fairly: lower case, all kinds of dashes turned into a plain hyphen, and extra spaces squeezed out.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_quote_text.tech: Lower-cases `s`, maps U+2010-U+2015 and U+2212 to '-', and collapses whitespace runs to one space. Used by `_one_in_quote`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_score.text: Gives a fact a relevance score for a candidate's question: one point for each meaningful word they share, plus a bonus if the question uses words typical of that fact's section (like 'fee' for application facts).
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_score.tech: Counts the overlap between `question_words` and the fact's label+text words (3+ alphanumeric chars, minus `_STOP`), and adds 3 if any `_SECTION_CUES[section]` substring occurs in the lower-cased question.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_short.text: Shortens a long piece of text to a set length and adds a note that the rest is on the exam page.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_short.tech: Collapses whitespace; if longer than `limit`, cuts to `limit`, right-strips and appends ' […continues in the exam page]'.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_url_in.text: Checks that a link in an AI answer is one of the links GovOS supplied, or the site or parent folder of one of them. It compares whole address parts, so a look-alike address such as ssc.gov instead of ssc.gov.in is refused.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_url_in.tech: Normalises `url` with `_norm_url`; returns True if some trusted URL equals it or starts with it followed by '/', '?' or '#'. `trusted` must already be normalised.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_when.text: Turns a recorded date into the text to show the AI: the date exactly as printed if there is one, otherwise the day, plus the time only when a real time was given.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_when.tech: Returns `displayWhen` if set; otherwise splits `dateTimeStr` on the first space and returns the day alone when there is no time or it starts with '00:00', else 'day HH:MM'.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::_without_li.text: Blanks out the 1., 2., 3. numbering of numbered lists in an AI answer so it is not mistaken for a figure that needs checking. A number at the start of a line that does not continue the count (like '32. Relaxations apply') is kept and checked.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::_without_li.tech: Scans `_LINE_NUMBER` matches (line-start 1-3 digits followed by '.' or ')' and a space); a match is a marker only if it equals the expected next number or 1 (restart). Markers are replaced by spaces of equal length; everything else is untouched. Returns the new string.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::answer_veri.text: Gives an AI answer an overall trust label from the facts it cites: fully verified only if every cited fact is verified, partly verified if some are, otherwise not verified.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::answer_veri.tech: Reads each cited dict's `verification`. Returns 'VERIFIED' if the list is non-empty and all are VERIFIED, 'PARTLY_VERIFIED' if any is VERIFIED, else 'NOT_VERIFIED' (including an empty list).

tools/claude_cli/context.py::build_fact_.text: Builds the list of numbered facts the AI may use to answer a question about one exam. The exam's core overview facts always go in; the rest are picked by how relevant they are to the question until a size limit is reached. The same exam and question always give the same list.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::build_fact_.tech: Gets candidates via `_candidates`, keeps the first 6 OVERVIEW ones as core, ranks the rest by -`_score` then original index, and greedily adds while label+text+24 fits in `max_chars` (default 20,000), setting `truncated` when something is skipped. Chosen facts are re-sorted into record order and numbered F1..Fn; non-dict provenance becomes None. Returns a `FactSheet`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::citations.text: Turns the fact numbers an AI answer cites into full entries the page can show as Evidence, each with its source, what it claims and its own trust state.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::citations.tech: For each id in `output['cited_fact_ids']` present in `sheet.by_id`, returns {id, section, label, text, provenance, claim, verification}; unknown ids are skipped.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::claim_in_qu.text: Asks whether the quoted words of a source state a fact's claim in any of the accepted forms (for example a date as printed, or its plain day). If the fact makes no specific claim, the answer is yes.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::claim_in_qu.tech: Filters `claim` to non-empty strings; returns True when none remain, else True if `_one_in_quote(p, v)` holds for any alternative. Mirrors `claimInQuote` in ui.tsx and is held to `fact_verification_cases.json`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::clean_text.text: Cleans text a candidate typed: removes invisible control characters, collapses runs of spaces, and cuts it to a length limit.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::clean_text.tech: clean_text(text, limit): replaces control chars (excluding tab and newline) with spaces, collapses spaces/tabs, strips, slices to limit.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::fact_verifi.text: Decides how trustworthy one fact is, using only its recorded source: Verified, Unsupported (official source but the quote does not say it), Under verification, Superseded, or Unverified (no checkable source). The AI's opinion plays no part in it.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::fact_verifi.tech: Returns UNVERIFIED if `p` is not a dict or has neither an http(s) `officialUrl` nor an excerpt; UNSUPPORTED if `claimNotInQuote` is set; SUPERSEDED if level is SUPERSEDED or `supersededBy` is set; UNDER_VERIFICATION for any level other than OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED; UNVERIFIED if it lacks an http(s) URL plus a page number or excerpt; else VERIFIED when `claim_in_quote(p, claim)` holds, otherwise UNSUPPORTED. Same rule as the frontend's `provenanceIsVerified`/`withClaim`.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::syllabus_to.text: Lists the syllabus topic names an exam has, each once, in order. Used to limit AI-written practice to topics on the real syllabus.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::syllabus_to.tech: Iterates `exam['syllabus']`, whitespace-normalises `topicName`, and returns unique non-empty names in first-seen order; empty list when there is no syllabus.

tools/claude_cli/context.py::validate_an.text: The safety check every AI answer must pass before a candidate sees it. It refuses an answer that cites facts it was not given, claims to be verified without citing anything, points to a section that does not exist, is empty, contains a link or a number or time not found in GovOS's own facts, or mentions another exam. The candidate's own question never counts as proof of anything.
tools/claude_cli/context.py::validate_an.tech: Returns a list of problem strings ([] = accept). Checks: unknown or duplicate `cited_fact_ids`; VERIFIED_DATA with no citations; NOT_IN_RECORD with uncertainty NONE; `navigate_to` not in NAVIGATION_TARGETS; empty answer. Answer+follow_up are then checked: every URL must pass `_url_in` against URLs in `sheet.corpus()`; figures (URLs removed, list numbering blanked) must appear among digit groups of the cited facts + title + authority (any length) for VERIFIED_DATA, or of the whole corpus (2+ digits) otherwise; 12-hour times must match allowed hours incl. `_clock_forms`; any `other_exam_names` entry present in the answer but not in the corpus fails. `question` is unused as evidence.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Candidate.text: One web page the AI suggested as a possible source, together with everything GovOS's own checks found out about it: its trust level, whether it opens, where it ends up, and whether it seems to match the search.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Candidate.tech: Dataclass with Claude's fields (title, url, snippet, authority_name, document_kind, why_relevant) and the checks' fields (trust, syntax_ok, reachable, http_status, final_url, final_trust, identity, reasons). Has `host` and `as_dict()`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Candidate.text: The suggested link and its check results in the format the app stores and shows.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Candidate.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of all fields (authorityName, documentKind, whyRelevant, syntaxOk, httpStatus, finalUrl, finalTrust...), with a copy of `reasons`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Candidate.text: The site name of the suggested link, in lower case and without 'www.'.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.text: The complete record of one AI source search: what was asked, what the AI returned word for word, which links passed GovOS's checks, which were rejected and why, and how much web searching the AI did. It exists so every search can be audited.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.tech: Dataclass: query, started_at, ended_at, status (InfraStatus value), message, template_version, job_id, raw_candidates (redacted), candidates (Candidate list), rejected, searched_queries, notes, web_activity. Serialised by `as_dict()`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.text: The search record in the format the app saves, with a note that no link is official just because the AI suggested it.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.tech: Returns camelCase dict of all fields with candidates expanded via `Candidate.as_dict()`, plus a fixed 'note' string.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.text: An error meaning the AI source search could not run at all (AI switched off, not installed, not signed in and so on). It is never taken to mean anything about the exam authority.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.tech: RuntimeError subclass carrying an `InfraStatus` in `.status`; raised by `discover` for any non-OK, non-CANCELLED gateway result.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.text: Creates the 'search could not run' error with the reason code and an optional message.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::Discovery.tech: Stores `status`; the exception message is `message` or `status.value`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FETCH_MAX.text: The most data (about 1.5 MB) GovOS will download from one page when checking it.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FETCH_MAX.tech: Int 1,500,000; default `max_bytes` for `fetch_checked`; bodies beyond it are cut and flagged `truncated`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FETCH_TIM.text: How long (12 seconds) GovOS waits on a website at each step when checking a link.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FETCH_TIM.tech: Float 12.0; default per-socket-operation timeout in `fetch_checked`; the whole-download budget defaults to four times it.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FetchResu.text: The outcome of GovOS downloading one link: whether it worked, the status code, the final address after any forwarding, the type of file, its text, a fingerprint of its contents and, if it failed, why.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::FetchResu.tech: Dataclass: ok, status, final_url, content_type, text (only for html/text), hops, error, content_hash (first 24 hex of SHA-256 of bytes read), truncated, body (only with keep_body), error_kind (BLOCKED/TLS/TIMEOUT/NETWORK/HTTP/REDIRECTS).

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::MAX_REDIR.text: How many times a link may forward to another address (4) before GovOS gives up on it.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::MAX_REDIR.tech: Int 4; `fetch_checked` loops MAX_REDIRECTS+1 times and reports REDIRECTS beyond that.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::MAX_URL_L.text: The longest web address (2,048 characters) GovOS will accept from an AI suggestion.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::MEMO_TTL_.text: How long (10 minutes) a remembered short-term result stays valid.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::OFFICIAL_.text: The website endings GovOS treats as government sites when checking AI-suggested links: .gov.in and .nic.in.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::OFFICIAL_.tech: Tuple ('.gov.in', '.nic.in') used by `classify_host` for OFFICIAL and passed as domain hints to DISCOVER_SOURCES when `official_only`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::TRUSTED_S.text: Website endings for academic and research institutions (.ac.in, .edu, .edu.in, .res.in), treated as trusted public sources but not official.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::TRUSTED_S.tech: Tuple used by `classify_host` to return TRUSTED_PUBLIC.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_NoRedire.text: A small helper that stops the download library from following forwarding links by itself, so GovOS can check each step on its own.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_NoRedire.tech: urllib `HTTPRedirectHandler` subclass whose `redirect_request` returns None, so 3xx responses surface as HTTPError for `fetch_checked` to handle.
Returns None for any arguments, disabling urllib's built-in redirect following.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_check.text: Runs the checks on one suggested link: downloads it, records whether it opens and where it ends up, lowers its trust if it forwards to a less trusted site, and checks whether the page's words match the search. A file that is not a web page is marked as not read rather than as not matching.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_check.tech: Calls `fetch(url)`; sets reachable, http_status, final_url, final_trust=`classify(final_url)`. On failure adds a reason and returns. If final trust differs it adds a reason and lowers `trust` when the final rank is lower (never raises it). Empty text -> identity 'UNREAD' with a reason; else `identity_hint`. Mutates and returns the candidate.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_error_ki.text: Sorts a download failure into a simple category: a security certificate problem, a timeout, or a general network problem.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_error_ki.tech: Inspects the exception and its `.reason`: SSL/CertificateError -> 'TLS'; socket.timeout/TimeoutError -> 'TIMEOUT'; else 'NETWORK'.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_words.text: Picks out the distinctive words of a text, ignoring common ones like 'exam', 'notice' or 'official'.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::_words.tech: Returns the set of lower-case 3+ char alphanumeric tokens not in `_GENERIC`.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::classify_.text: Labels a website's host name by its ending: OFFICIAL for .gov.in / .nic.in, TRUSTED_PUBLIC for academic and research endings, and UNVERIFIED for everything else.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::classify_.tech: Lower-cases and strips a trailing dot, then checks `OFFICIAL_SUFFIXES`, then `TRUSTED_SUFFIXES`; returns 'OFFICIAL' | 'TRUSTED_PUBLIC' | 'UNVERIFIED'.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::classify_.text: Labels a whole web address by its host's ending, using the rule above.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::discover.text: Runs one AI source search for the Trust Panel. The AI proposes candidate pages; GovOS then throws out malformed, duplicate or (in official-only mode) non-government links, visits the rest itself, and keeps only those that open and stay on an allowed site. If the AI could not run, it raises an error rather than pretending nothing was found.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::discover.tech: Calls `gateway.run(Operation.DISCOVER_SOURCES, {query, max_results, domain_hints})`. Non-OK result: returns the manifest if CANCELLED, else raises `DiscoveryUnavailable`. Otherwise stores searched queries, notes and redacted raw candidates, then for up to `max_results` candidates rejects bad syntax, duplicates (ignoring '#fragment') and non-OFFICIAL trust when `official_only`. If `verify`, runs `_check` on 4 threads and rejects unreachable ones or ones that redirected off OFFICIAL. Returns the `DiscoveryManifest`. `fetch` and `classify` are injectable.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::fetch_che.text: Safely downloads a web page or file for GovOS. Before each step, including every forwarding hop, it re-checks that the address is well formed and public; it verifies security certificates, limits the time and the size of the download, and records a fingerprint of what it got. It never trusts a redirect without checking it.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::fetch_che.tech: Loops up to MAX_REDIRECTS+1 hops: `validate_url_syntax` and `resolves_public` per hop (else BLOCKED), GET with a GovOS User-Agent plus optional `headers`, using `_NoRedirect` and a default SSL context. Reads with read1 in 64 KB chunks up to max_bytes+1, aborting with TIMEOUT past `max_seconds` (default 4x timeout). Sets status, final_url, content_type, truncated, ok (2xx), content_hash, body (if keep_body) and text (decoded only for html/text/*). 301/302/303/307/308 with Location are followed via urljoin (spaces -> %20); other HTTP errors -> HTTP; other exceptions -> `_error_kind`; too many hops -> REDIRECTS.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::identity_.text: Gives a rough sign of whether a found page is about what was searched for, by checking how many of the search's distinctive words appear on the page. It is only advice; the exam builder makes the real decision later.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::identity_.tech: Compares `_words(query)` with `_words(title + tag-stripped, unescaped page_text[:40000])`. Returns 'UNCHECKED' if there are no query words or no text/title; else 'MATCHED' (share >= 0.6), 'WEAK' (>= 0.3) or 'NOT_MATCHED'.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::memo_clea.tech: Clears `_MEMO` under the lock (used by tests).

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::memo_get.text: Fetches a recently remembered result, if it has not expired yet.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::memo_get.tech: Under `_MEMO_LOCK`, returns the stored value if its monotonic expiry is in the future; otherwise removes the key and returns None.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::memo_put.text: Remembers a result for ten minutes. If more than 200 are held, the oldest is forgotten.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::memo_put.tech: Stores (now + MEMO_TTL_SECONDS, value) under the lock; when the dict exceeds 200 entries pops the first-inserted key.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::redact_ur.text: Hides any username and password embedded in a web address before it is saved in the record of a search.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::redact_ur.tech: Replaces a `user:pass@` segment after '//' with '***@' via regex; None-safe.

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::resolves_.text: Looks up where a site name points and makes sure every address is on the public internet, so a link can never trick the GovOS server into reaching its own private network.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::resolves_.tech: Resolves via `resolver` or `socket.getaddrinfo`; returns (False, reason) on resolution failure, no addresses, unparsable address, or any address that is not `ip.is_global` (zone suffix stripped). Else (True, '').

tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::validate_.text: Checks that a suggested web address is well formed and safe to visit: only http or https, no passwords in it, a real public site name (not a bare IP number or a local machine name), a normal port, and no odd characters. It says nothing about whether the page exists or is official.
tools/claude_cli/discovery.py::validate_.tech: Returns (ok, reason). Rejects empty, >2048 chars, whitespace/control chars, unparsable or bad port, non-http(s), userinfo, hosts without a dot, IP literals and legacy numeric IPv4 forms (last label all digits or 0x...), localhost/.localhost/.local/.internal/.lan, ports other than 80/443, and hosts with characters outside [a-z0-9.-].

tools/claude_cli/fake_cli.py::main.text: Test support: a pretend Claude program that GovOS's tests run as a real separate process. A scenario file decides how it behaves: answer normally, hang, crash, print broken output, leak a secret in its error text, report not-logged-in or rate-limited, and so on. It also logs how it was called so tests can check what GovOS sent it.
tools/claude_cli/fake_cli.py::main.tech: Reads optional '--scenario <path>' JSON. Answers '--version', '--help' (HELP_FLAGS minus help_omit) and 'auth status' (loggedIn + auth_extra). Otherwise reads stdin, appends {argv, stdin, cwd, pid, env_keys} to `log`, picks `mode` (with 'sequence' using a counter file and `steps`), and emits: timeout (sleep 600), tree (spawns a hanging child, writes its pid), exit1, bad_json, wrong_schema, huge, stderr_secret, stderr_flood, auth_error, rate_limit, text_json, prose_json, cot (adds 'thinking'), denied_tools, or a normal envelope. Returns the exit code.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_fail.tech: Returns JobOutcome('FAILED', error_category=status.value, error_message=message or SAFE_MESSAGES[status], retryable=status.retryable unless overridden, **kw).

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_failed_re.text: Turns an unsuccessful AI call into the right job result: 'cancelled' if it was cancelled, otherwise a failure with the reason.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_failed_re.tech: CANCELLED status -> JobOutcome('CANCELLED', error_category 'CANCELLED', safe message); else `_fail(res.status, template_version, audit={'inputFingerprint'})`.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_need_id.text: Reads a required identifier (such as an exam id) from a request and rejects it unless it is a plain id made of letters, numbers and a few safe symbols.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_need_id.tech: Strips `inp[key]`; raises ValueError unless it matches ^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,120}$; returns the value.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_norm.text: Squeezes extra spaces out of a piece of text.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::_norm.tech: Collapses whitespace runs and strips; None-safe.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::answer_que.text: The background job behind Ask GovOS AI's Claude fallback. It builds a list of numbered facts from the chosen exam's record, asks Claude to answer the candidate's question from those facts only, and then runs strict checks. If the answer fails any check it is thrown away. A passing answer is marked verified only if every fact it cites is officially verified, whatever Claude claims.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::answer_que.tech: EXAM_NOT_FOUND if missing. `build_fact_sheet(exam, question)` -> Operation.ANSWER_QUESTION with title, authority, facts (as_prompt), question, history. Non-OK -> `_failed_result`. `validate_answer` with `other_exam_names`; any problem -> FAILED ANSWER_REJECTED (up to 6 problems in audit). Citations only for basis VERIFIED_DATA; `verification = answer_verification(cited)`. Returns answer, basis, uncertainty, verification, navigateTo, followUp, citations, label, engine, examId, factsSupplied, factsTruncated.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::build_exam.text: The background job that builds an exam record from an authority's documents using the exam builder. A build that the safety gate blocks still counts as finished (nothing was published); only an unavailable source or service makes the job fail, and then it may be retried.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::build_exam.tech: Calls `build_exam(query, year, registry=ExamRegistry(db_path), use_claude, gateway, should_continue, authority_discovery=_authority_run_for(ctx) if requested)`. CANCELLED state -> CANCELLED; INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE/SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE -> FAILED retryable; otherwise SUCCEEDED with `result.to_dict()`, a REGISTRY evidence link when registered, and audit state.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::default_sp.text: The fixed list of background AI jobs GovOS allows: source search, reading facts, building an exam, exploring an authority's site, ordering a roadmap, answering a question and writing practice. Anything not on this list cannot be queued.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::default_sp.tech: Returns {name: JobSpec(name, handler, normaliser, ...)}: DISCOVER_SOURCES (retries 2), EXTRACT_FIELDS (1), BUILD_EXAM (1, exclusive `_build_exclusive`), DISCOVER_AUTHORITY (1, exclusive 'authority:<examId>'), ORDER_ROADMAP (1), ANSWER_QUESTION and GENERATE_PRACTICE (candidate=True, retries 0).

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::discover_a.text: The background job that explores an exam authority's official website, starting from the address in that exam's record. It reads links from the pages themselves, uses Claude only if asked and only to label unclear links, saves the whole exploration for audit, and reports what it found for this exam.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::discover_a.tech: Loads the exam (EXAM_NOT_FOUND), validates `officialDomain` with `validate_url_syntax` (NO_OFFICIAL_ADDRESS). Runs `discover_authority([root], authority_name, gateway if useClaude else None, should_continue)`; cancelled -> CANCELLED. Projects with `project_for_exam` (cycle from the record or a -20xx suffix of the id), saves via `SourceGraphStore.save(run, job_id, coverage=coverage_report(run))`, and returns runId, estate, coverage, searchStates, repository summaries and Claude usage, with a SOURCE_RUN evidence link.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::discover_s.text: The background job behind the Trust Panel's AI source search. It runs the search, records the full result, saves it as a research run if the app supports that, and reports how many links were kept or rejected.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::discover_s.tech: Stage DISCOVERING: calls `discover(query, max_results, official_only=mode=='OFFICIAL', gateway=hooks.claude(), job_id, classify=hooks.classify_trust)`; DiscoveryUnavailable -> `_fail(status)`; cancellation -> CANCELLED. Stage RECORDING: `persist_discovery` if set; returns SUCCEEDED with {runId, manifest}, a RESEARCH_RUN evidence link and audit counts.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::extract_fi.text: The background job behind 'Read with Claude' in the Trust Panel. It loads a saved finding's page text, asks Claude to pull out requested facts with exact quotes, keeps only the ones whose quote GovOS finds in the page, and stores those as facts waiting for human review. Nothing is published.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::extract_fi.tech: Fails (non-retryable) without `load_finding`; FINDING_NOT_FOUND / NO_SOURCE_TEXT when missing. Runs Operation.EXTRACT_FIELDS on the first 40,000 chars with the requested fields; non-OK -> `_failed_result`. `verify_proposals` then filters; accepted ones go to `ingest_facts` when present. Returns SUCCEEDED with proposed/verified counts, rejected reasons, ingest summary and a RESEARCH_FINDING evidence link.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::generate_p.text: The background job that has Claude write a few practice questions on one topic from the exam's verified syllabus. Questions go through the checks above, then a second, separate Claude call solves each one without seeing the answer; only questions where both agree are served, labelled as GovOS practice and not official. If the second check cannot run, nothing is served.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::generate_p.tech: Requires the exam (EXAM_NOT_FOUND), a syllabus (NO_VERIFIED_SYLLABUS) and topic in `syllabus_topics` (TOPIC_NOT_IN_SYLLABUS). Runs GENERATE_PRACTICE with a pattern note from the first stage's name/mode, filters with `validate_practice` (none -> PRACTICE_REJECTED), then SOLVE_PRACTICE on stems+options; non-OK -> `_failed_result`. Keeps questions whose solved choice equals `correct_index`, adds reasons for the rest; none kept -> PRACTICE_REJECTED. Returns labelled questions (source GOVOS_AUTHORED, generatedBy CLAUDE_CLI, officialSource False, label, answerCheck) and dropped reasons.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_answe.text: Cleans a candidate's question for the AI assistant: the question is required and length-limited, and only the last six turns of the conversation are kept, each trimmed and limited to user or assistant messages.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_answe.tech: Returns {examId, question (clean_text, MAX_QUESTION_CHARS=600, required), history}. `history` must be a list; the last 6 dict turns with role user/assistant and non-empty text (500 chars) are kept.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_autho.text: Cleans a request to explore an exam authority's website. It only accepts an exam GovOS already holds; the starting address comes from that exam's record, never from the request.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_autho.tech: Returns {examId (via `_need_id`)} plus useClaude: True only when the flag is truthy.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_build.text: Cleans and checks a request to build an exam record: an exam name is required, the year must look like 2026 or 2026-27, and the 'use Claude' and 'walk the authority's site' options are read as yes/no.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_build.tech: Returns {query (from query or exam, 160 chars), year (from year or cycle, must match `_YEAR`, may be empty), useClaude bool (strings '1/true/yes/on')}, adding authorityDiscovery: True only when requested, so plain builds keep the same input and dedupe key.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_disco.text: Cleans and checks a request to run an AI source search: a search text is required, the scope is official-only unless 'any' is asked for, and the number of results is kept between 1 and 12.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_disco.tech: Returns {query (clean_text, 300 chars, required), mode 'OFFICIAL'|'ANY', maxResults clamped 1-12 (default 8, also reads max_results)} plus `examId` via `_need_id` when examId/exam_id is given.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_extra.text: Cleans and checks a request to have Claude read facts from a saved research finding: the finding number must be a positive number, and only known field names are kept (all of them if none are named).
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_extra.tech: Parses findingId/finding_id as positive int (else ValueError); `fields` must be a list, filtered to EXTRACTABLE_FIELDS, defaulting to all. Returns {findingId, fields}.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_pract.text: Cleans a request for Claude-written practice questions: a topic is required, between 1 and 5 questions (3 by default), and difficulty easy, medium or hard (medium if anything else).
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_pract.tech: Returns {examId, topic (300 chars, required), count clamped 1-5 (default 3), difficulty in EASY/MEDIUM/HARD else MEDIUM}.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::norm_roadm.text: Cleans a request to order an exam's study roadmap; only the exam id is accepted.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::order_road.text: The background job that suggests a study order for an exam's syllabus topics, using the roadmap guidance tool.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::order_road.tech: Loads the exam (EXAM_NOT_FOUND), maps syllabus to {id, topicName, subject, weightagePercentage (0 default), isHighYield}, calls `roadmap_guidance.generate(exam id, topics, authority, exam_label, gateway)`, and returns SUCCEEDED with `g.as_dict()` and audit generatedBy.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::validate_p.text: Checks each Claude-written practice question and drops any that is not on the requested syllabus topic, does not have four different options and one correct answer, pretends to be from a real past paper or contains a link, is missing its text or explanation, has an explanation that corrects itself, or repeats an earlier question.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::validate_p.tech: Over the first `count` questions: rejects topic != `topic` or topic not in `allowed`; options not 4 distinct non-empty; `correct_index` not an int 0-3 (bools refused); `_OFFICIAL_CLAIM` matches in stem/explanation/options; empty stem or explanation; `_SELF_CORRECTION` in the explanation; duplicate stem (case-insensitive). Returns (accepted, ['question N: reason']).

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::value_supp.text: Checks whether a value Claude proposed is actually stated in the quote it gave. Every number and every word of three or more letters in the value must appear in the quote; a date may be written differently, but nothing may be added.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::value_supp.tech: Lower-cased, whitespace-normalised. True if the value appears as a whole token-bounded substring. Otherwise every digit group of the value (leading zeros stripped) must be among the quote's, and every 3+ letter word must be among the quote's words; False if the value has neither digits nor words, or either string is empty.

tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::verify_pro.text: Checks each value Claude proposed while reading a page. A value is accepted only if it was asked for, its quote is long enough, the quote appears word for word in the page text GovOS fetched itself, and the quote states the value. Each proposal comes back marked accepted or not, with reasons.
tools/claude_cli/handlers.py::verify_pro.tech: For each proposal: rejects if `field` not in `wanted` (when given), quote < 8 chars, or quote not in normalised `source_text`; then requires `value_supported_by_quote`. Returns copies with normalised `quote`, `verified` bool and `reasons`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::CANDIDATE_RETE.text: How long (one day) a candidate's question and the AI's answer are kept before being wiped.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::FINALISE_RETRY.text: Pauses (half a second, then two seconds) before trying again to save a job's result when the database is busy.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::FINALISE_RETRY.tech: Tuple (0.5, 2.0) consumed by `_finalise_safely` on sqlite errors; afterwards the job is left to `recover_stale`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::HEARTBEAT_SECO.text: How often (every 15 seconds) the job system's housekeeping runs to mark running jobs as alive and tidy up.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::Job.text: One background AI job as stored: what it is, who asked, its cleaned input, its state and stage, its result or error, timings, retries and audit details.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::Job.tech: Dataclass mirroring a `claude_jobs` row (input/result/evidence_links/audit/access_hashes decoded). `as_dict()` is the public view.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::Job.as_dict.text: The safe view of a job shown to the app, which never includes the secret access codes or which worker ran it.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::Job.as_dict.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of id, operation, exam, cycle, status, stage, result, errors, template version, timings, retries, cancelRequested, evidenceLinks, audit, inputFingerprint, requestedBy, role; adds `input` unless `include_input=False`. Omits access_hashes, worker_id, heartbeat.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.text: What a running job handler is given: the job itself, the database location, the app's connections, a way to report its current stage, and a way to see if it has been cancelled.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.tech: Holds job, db_path, cancel_event, hooks and the store; `stage(name)` writes the stage, `cancelled` reads the event.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.__i.text: Sets up the job's working context.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.__i.tech: Stores job, db_path, cancel_event, hooks and `_store`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.can.text: Whether someone has asked to cancel this job.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.sta.text: Records which step the job is on (for example 'ASKING' or 'VERIFYING_QUOTES') so the screen can show progress.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobContext.sta.tech: Calls `store.set_stage(job.id, name)`, which also refreshes the heartbeat.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobOutcome.text: What a job handler hands back when it finishes: succeeded, failed or cancelled, with its result or error, whether it is worth retrying, links to evidence and audit details.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobOutcome.tech: Dataclass: status ('SUCCEEDED'|'FAILED'|'CANCELLED'), result, error_category, error_message, retryable, evidence_links, template_version, audit.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.text: The engine that runs background AI jobs. It accepts new jobs, runs a small number of worker threads that pick jobs up one by one, keeps them alive, recovers stuck ones, retries temporary failures, handles cancellation, and makes sure nothing a job does can crash the workers.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.tech: Wraps a `JobStore` and a dict of `JobSpec`s; worker threads run `_loop`, a housekeeping thread runs `_housekeeping`. Tracks active attempts in a Counter, cancel events per job, and the last 50 contained `incidents`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.__ini.text: Sets up the job engine with its database, the allowed job kinds and the app's connections. Workers do not start yet.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.__ini.tech: Creates the store, events, lock, a random worker id 'w-xxxxxxxxxx', `_active` Counter, `incidents` deque(maxlen=50) and an injectable `_sleep`; `workers` overrides the configured concurrency.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._exec.text: Runs one job: gives its handler a working context, catches any crash and turns it into a plain failure, then saves the outcome. It keeps track of which jobs are active so their heartbeat stays correct.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._exec.tech: Creates a cancel Event (pre-set if cancel_requested), increments `_active[job.id]`, registers the event. Unknown spec -> FAILED UNKNOWN_OPERATION; else runs `spec.handler(JobContext(...))` inside `job_scope(job.id, cancel)`. A non-JobOutcome or bad status, or any exception -> FAILED INTERNAL. Removes the cancel event, calls `_finalise_safely`, then decrements/deletes the active count.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._fina.text: Decides a job's final state: cancelled if a cancel was requested at any point; back in the queue after a pause if it failed for a temporary reason and has retries left; otherwise succeeded or failed.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._fina.tech: Re-reads the job. Cancel event, stored cancel_requested or CANCELLED outcome -> `finish` as CANCELLED (coercing the outcome). FAILED + retryable + retry_count < max_retries -> `requeue` with RETRY_BACKOFF_SECONDS[retry_count] and wake. Else `finish` SUCCEEDED or FAILED.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._fina.text: Saves a job's outcome while containing every problem: a result that cannot be saved becomes a failure, a busy database is retried a couple of times, and any other bug becomes a plain failure. If nothing can be saved, the job is left for stuck-job recovery. It never crashes.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._fina.tech: Loops on `_finalise`: ResultNotPersistable -> incident, outcome FAILED RESULT_NOT_SAVED; sqlite3.Error -> sleep through FINALISE_RETRY_SECONDS then incident and return False; other exceptions -> incident and FAILED INTERNAL (return False if already that). Returns True once written.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._hous.text: The background loop that runs the housekeeping step every 15 seconds until the engine stops.
One housekeeping round: mark the running jobs as alive and pass on any cancel requests, recover stuck jobs, and every ten minutes wipe old candidate data. Each step runs even if another fails.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._hous.tech: Heartbeats active job ids and sets their cancel events for ids returned; then `recover_stale`; then `purge_candidate_data` if >600 s since `last_purge`. Each wrapped separately with `_incident`. Returns the updated last_purge.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._inci.text: Records a problem the workers caught and contained: logs it, keeps it in a short list for diagnosis, and notes it on the job's history. It never fails itself.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._inci.tech: Appends {at, where, error type, jobId} to `incidents`, logs at error with exc_info, and calls `store.note(job_id, 'WORKER_ERROR', ...)` when a job id is given; never includes job input/output.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._loop.text: What each worker does over and over: take the next job and run it, or wait a moment if there is none. Nothing that goes wrong may stop the worker.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._loop.tech: Until stop: `claim_next`; exceptions (non-sqlite ones recorded as incidents) sleep 1 s. None -> waits on `_wake` up to 1 s. Otherwise `_execute(job)`, recording any exception as an 'execute' incident.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._work.text: Decides how many workers to run: the number asked for, or the configured limit.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue._work.tech: Returns max(1, workers) when set, else `load_config().max_concurrency`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.cance.text: Cancels a job immediately: a waiting job is cancelled in the database, and a job running in this process is told to stop at once without waiting for housekeeping.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.cance.tech: Calls `store.request_cancel(job_id)` and sets the in-process cancel event if present; returns the Job or None.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.ensur.text: Starts the worker threads and the housekeeping thread the first time it is called, after recovering any jobs a previous run left stuck.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.ensur.tech: Under the lock, once: clears stop, runs `store.recover_stale()`, starts `_worker_count()` daemon `_loop` threads and one `_housekeeping` daemon thread.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.run_p.text: Runs waiting jobs one after another in the current thread, for tests and one-off tools.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.run_p.tech: Claims and `_execute`s up to `max_jobs` (50) jobs, recording exceptions as incidents; returns how many ran.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.stop.text: Stops the workers and waits briefly for them to end.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.stop.tech: Sets stop and wake, joins each thread with `timeout`, clears the thread list and the started flag.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.submi.text: Accepts a new job request: checks the job kind is allowed (and allowed for candidates if a candidate asked), cleans the input, stores the job, and wakes the workers.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobQueue.submi.tech: Unknown operation -> ValueError; candidate role on a non-candidate spec -> PermissionError. Normalises the payload ({} if not a dict), calls `store.create`, `ensure_started()`, sets `_wake`. Returns (job, deduplicated, token).

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobSpec.text: The definition of one allowed kind of background job: its name, the code that runs it, the code that cleans its input, whether candidates may start it, how many retries it gets, and an optional rule that only one such job may run at a time for the same thing.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobSpec.tech: Dataclass: name, handler(JobContext)->JobOutcome, normalize(dict)->dict (raises ValueError), candidate=False, max_retries=2, exclusive(normalised, exam_id, cycle)->key or None.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStatus.text: The possible states of a background AI job: waiting, running, succeeded, failed or cancelled.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStatus.tech: str Enum QUEUED, RUNNING, SUCCEEDED, FAILED, CANCELLED with a `terminal` property.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStatus.term.text: Whether the job is finished for good (succeeded, failed or cancelled).

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.text: The part that keeps background AI jobs in the database: creating them (without duplicates), reading them, handing the next one to a worker, recording progress, finishing, retrying, cancelling, recovering stuck jobs and wiping old candidate data.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.tech: SQLite-backed store over `claude_jobs`/`claude_job_events`; autocommit connections with explicit BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions; injectable clock. Creates its tables on construction.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.__ini.text: Connects the job store to its database and makes sure the job tables exist.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.__ini.tech: Stores db_path and clock, runs `init_job_tables` and commits.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore._conn.text: Opens a database connection for the job store.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore._even.text: Adds an entry to a job's event history.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore._even.tech: INSERT into claude_job_events with now_iso() and detail truncated to 300 chars, on the given connection.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore._seri.text: Converts a job's result, evidence links and audit details into saveable text before saving, and reports clearly if that is impossible.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore._seri.tech: Static; returns (result JSON or None, links JSON, audit JSON); TypeError/ValueError/RecursionError -> ResultNotPersistable.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.can_r.text: Decides whether someone may see a job: an administrator always can; anyone else needs the secret code issued when the job was created.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.can_r.tech: True if `admin`; else True if `token_matches(token, h)` for any stored access hash.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.claim.text: Hands the oldest waiting job to a worker and marks it running, skipping any job whose 'one at a time' slot is already taken and any job scheduled for a later retry.
