tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.claim.tech: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; collects exclusive keys of RUNNING jobs, scans up to 50 QUEUED rows with not_before <= now by created_epoch, picks the first whose exclusive key is free, sets RUNNING/started_at/worker_id/heartbeat/stage 'STARTING', logs STARTED with attempt number, commits and returns the Job (or None).

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.count.tech: Returns {status: count} from a GROUP BY.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.creat.text: Creates a new background job, unless the same requester already has an identical job waiting or running, in which case that one is returned. Candidate jobs get a one-off secret code to read their result later; only a scrambled copy of the code is stored. Refuses when the queue is full.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.creat.tech: Computes `fingerprint` over op/exam/cycle/input and a dedupe key adding requester and role, plus `exclusive` key. In a BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction: an active (QUEUED/RUNNING) duplicate returns (job, True, token), appending the new token's hash for candidates; otherwise enforces MAX_QUEUED_JOBS and MAX_QUEUED_CANDIDATE_JOBS (QueueFull), inserts a uuid4 row and a CREATED event. Returns (job, deduplicated, token) — token '' for non-candidates. Rolls back and re-raises on sqlite errors.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.event.text: Gives a job's history of events in order (created, started, retried, finished and so on).
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.event.tech: Returns dicts {ts, event, detail} for the job ordered by id.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.finis.text: Saves a job's final state and result. It only does so if this run still owns the job, so an older run cannot overwrite a newer retry's result.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.finis.tech: Serialises first, then BEGIN IMMEDIATE UPDATE of status, result, errors (message 300 chars), template version, finished_at, links, audit and stage, guarded by `_OWNER` (id, RUNNING, worker_id, retry_count). Logs an event when a row changed; returns whether it did.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.get.text: Fetches one job by its id, or nothing if there is no such job.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.get.tech: SELECT by id; returns `_row_to_job` or None.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.heart.text: Marks the jobs this worker is actually running as still alive, and reports which of them someone has asked to cancel. A job whose worker thread has died is no longer marked alive, so it can be recovered.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.heart.tech: Updates heartbeat_at for RUNNING rows of `worker_id`, limited to `job_ids` when given ([] returns [] without touching anything). Returns ids among them with cancel_requested=1.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.list.text: Lists recent jobs, newest first, optionally only those with a given state or kind.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.list.tech: Optional status/operation filters; ORDER BY created_epoch DESC with limit clamped to 1-100 (default 30). Returns Job list.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.note.text: Adds a note to a job's history on a best-effort basis; it never causes an error itself.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.note.tech: Opens a connection and calls `_event`; all exceptions swallowed.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.purge.text: Wipes candidates' questions and the AI's answers from finished jobs older than a day. The job's record of timing and status is kept for auditing.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.purge.tech: UPDATE candidate-role terminal rows with created_epoch < now - older_than that still hold data: input_json='{}', result_json=NULL. Returns rowcount.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.recov.text: Finds running jobs that have stopped showing signs of life (for example after a crash) and either puts them back in the queue, if they have retries left and were not cancelled, or marks them failed or cancelled as interrupted. No job is silently lost.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.recov.tech: For RUNNING rows with heartbeat_at < now - stale_after: if retry_count < max_retries and not cancel_requested, re-queue (retry_count+1, clear worker/stage, not_before=0, RECOVERED event); else set CANCELLED (if cancel requested) or FAILED with error INTERRUPTED. Returns how many rows were handled.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.reque.text: Cancels a job. A waiting job is cancelled straight away; a running one is flagged so its worker stops the Claude program.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.reque.tech: BEGIN IMMEDIATE; missing id -> None. QUEUED -> CANCELLED with cancel_requested, finished_at, error/stage CANCELLED and an event; RUNNING -> cancel_requested=1 and CANCEL_REQUESTED event; terminal jobs unchanged. Returns the refreshed Job.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.reque.text: Puts a failed job back in the queue for another try after a delay, if this run still owns it.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.reque.tech: Guarded by `_OWNER`: sets QUEUED, retry_count+1, not_before=now+delay, clears stage and worker; logs RETRY_SCHEDULED with reason. Returns whether a row changed.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.set_s.text: Records the step a running job is on and notes it is still alive.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::JobStore.set_s.tech: UPDATE stage (60 chars) and heartbeat_at for a RUNNING job id.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::MAX_QUEUED_CAN.text: The most candidate requests (20) that may wait in the AI queue at once.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::MAX_QUEUED_CAN.tech: Int 20; `JobStore.create` raises QueueFull for a candidate job when this many candidate jobs are QUEUED.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::MAX_QUEUED_JOB.text: The most jobs of any kind (200) that may wait in the AI queue at once.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::MAX_QUEUED_JOB.tech: Int 200; `JobStore.create` raises QueueFull when this many jobs are QUEUED.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::QueueFull.text: The error raised when the AI job queue is too full to accept another request.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::RETRY_BACKOFF_.text: How long to wait before retrying a job that failed for a temporary reason: 5 seconds, then 20, then 60.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::RETRY_BACKOFF_.tech: Tuple (5.0, 20.0, 60.0) indexed by retry_count (capped at the last) in `_finalise`.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::ResultNotPersi.text: The error raised when a job's result cannot be saved. Such a job is marked failed rather than wrongly marked successful with nothing saved.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::ResultNotPersi.tech: ValueError subclass raised by `JobStore._serialised` when JSON serialisation fails; `_finalise_safely` turns it into FAILED / RESULT_NOT_SAVED.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::STALE_SECONDS.text: How long (90 seconds) a running job can go without a sign of life before GovOS treats it as stuck and recovers it.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::_row_to_job.text: Turns a stored database row into a job object, tolerating damaged saved data.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::_row_to_job.tech: Builds a `Job` from a sqlite Row; JSON columns are decoded with fallbacks ({} / None / []) on bad JSON; nullable text columns default to ''.

tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::init_job_table.text: Creates the database tables that hold background AI jobs and each job's history of events, if they do not exist yet. Safe to run many times.
tools/claude_cli/jobs.py::init_job_table.tech: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS claude_jobs (id, operation, exam/cycle, requester, role, input/fingerprint/dedupe/exclusive keys, status, stage, result, errors, timings, retry counts, cancel flag, evidence links, audit, access hashes, worker, heartbeat, not_before, created_epoch) with status and dedupe indexes, and claude_job_events (job_id, ts, event, detail) with a job index. Does not commit.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::DATA_RULES.text: The security rules added to every instruction GovOS gives Claude: anything inside the fenced-off data sections is untrusted material and must never be obeyed, only supplied material may be used for facts, no secrets may be revealed, and the reply must be a single structured answer with no extra prose.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::DATA_RULES.tech: Fixed string appended to every template's system prompt: treat <<<LABEL:nonce>>> blocks as data, only system rules and TASK lines are instructions, no outside knowledge for facts, never reveal secrets/files/env, reply with exactly one schema-matching JSON object.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::PromptTempl.text: The fixed definition of how GovOS asks Claude to do one kind of task: its version, its standing instructions, how the request is written out, which inputs are required, which tools (if any) it may use, how much longer it may take, how big the input may be, and whether results may be remembered.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::PromptTempl.tech: Frozen dataclass: operation, version, system, render(payload, nonce)->str, required keys, tools (only DISCOVER_SOURCES has WebSearch/WebFetch), timeout_factor, max_input_chars (default 40,000), cacheable.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_join.text: Prints a list of values in one line, separated by commas, with each value's line breaks squashed out.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_line.text: Reads one input value to print inside the instruction text itself, squashing every line break and extra space into single spaces, so the value can never start a new line that looks like an instruction.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_line.tech: `' '.join(_s(payload, key, default).split())`. Used for inline (non-block) values only; block bodies keep their exact text.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ans.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to answer a candidate's question about one exam using only the numbered facts supplied, citing the fact numbers it used and saying so if the facts do not answer it. The facts, recent conversation and question are each fenced off as data.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ans.tech: TASK, EXAM title -- authority, NAVIGATION TARGETS list, FACTS block ('[id] (section) label: text' lines), RECENT CONVERSATION block (last 6 turns, 2400 chars, '(none)' if empty), QUESTION block (600). Template 'answer-question/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_att.text: Writes out the request asking Claude what role a passage of a notice plays for a given field and value (for example whether a number is the total vacancies), choosing from a fixed list of roles.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_att.tech: TASK, FIELD, VALUE (value_json cut to 600), ROLES (payload roles or ATTRIBUTION_ROLES), EVIDENCE block (900 chars) and CONTEXT block (1500). Template 'classify-attribution/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_cla.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to label links found on an exam authority's website by what they point to (notification, question paper, application portal and so on), from a fixed list, leaving out any it is unsure about.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_cla.tech: Up to 50 dict links rendered as '[index] text | listed under | path' (each part whitespace-collapsed and length-capped), or a pre-rendered string passed through, inside a LINKS block (12,000); TASK, AUTHORITY and ROLES (SOURCE_ROLES). Template 'classify-source/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_com.text: Writes out the request asking Claude whether a quotation is a whole sentence or clause of the notice, not cut off at either end.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_com.tech: TASK naming `unit_kind` (default 'a complete quoted unit'), QUOTATION block and CONTEXT AROUND IT block. Template 'check-completeness/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_con.text: Writes out the request asking Claude whether a document is about the same recruitment (same post and year) as a given notice.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_con.tech: TASK, RECRUITMENT DESIGNATION, CYCLE, optional COMPONENTS line, and a DOCUMENT block of `document_block`. Template 'confirm-recruitment/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_dat.text: Writes out the request asking Claude which event one date in a notice is for (exam, last date, fee deadline and so on), from a fixed list.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_dat.tech: TASK, DATE (as read), ROW LABEL (200 chars), STATED AS block (600), ROLES (payload or DATE_ROLES), CONTEXT block (1500). Template 'classify-date/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_des.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to report, word for word, what post a recruitment notice says it is recruiting for.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_des.tech: TASK line plus a 'NOTIFICATION TEXT (its opening, verbatim)' block of `title_block`. Template 'extract-designation/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_dis.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to search the web for candidate official pages for a search query, reporting only links it actually found, and preferring government sites.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_dis.tech: TASK (web search/fetch, never URLs from memory), MAX RESULTS (int, default 8), optional PREFERRED DOMAIN SUFFIXES, QUERY block (300 chars). Template 'discover-sources/1', the only one with tools.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ext.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to read one document's text and propose values for the wanted fields, each with the exact quote that states it.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ext.tech: TASK, EXAM (+cycle), AUTHORITY, SOURCE title/url, WANTED FIELDS (payload or EXTRACTABLE_FIELDS) and a SOURCE TEXT block. Template 'extract-fields/1' (60,000-char input cap).

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_pra.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to write a few original multiple-choice practice questions on one syllabus topic at a chosen difficulty.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_pra.tech: TASK with count (default 3) and difficulty (default MEDIUM), EXAM line, TOPIC block (300), ALLOWED TOPICS block (6000), PATTERN NOTE block (600). Template 'generate-practice/2'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_roa.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to put an exam's fixed list of syllabus topics into a sensible study order, using every topic exactly once and adding nothing.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_roa.tech: Builds 'id | subject | name | high_yield(yes/no)' rows inside a TOPICS block, with a TASK naming `exam_label` and 'Return every id exactly once.' Template 'order-roadmap/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_sol.text: Writes out the request asking Claude to solve multiple-choice questions from scratch without being told the answers, so GovOS can check the answer key written earlier. Claude must say 'none' if no single option is correct.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_sol.tech: Renders each question as '[i] stem' plus 'A. ... | B. ...' (first four options), or passes a pre-rendered string through unchanged, inside a QUESTIONS block (10,000 chars), with a TASK defining choice 0-3 or -1. Template 'solve-practice/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ver.text: Writes out the request asking Claude whether a piece of evidence supports a claimed value for an exam (for example 'is the exam date 1 January 2027?'). The evidence goes inside a fenced data section.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_render_ver.tech: Lines: TASK with identity/evidence/claim_supported definitions, CLAIM exam (+cycle), FIELD, VALUE (or structural-claim note), SOURCE title/authority/url (all via `_line`), and an EVIDENCE `block`. Template 'verify-claim/1'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_s.text: Reads one input value as text, using a default if it is missing.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::_s.tech: Returns `default` when the payload value is None, else `str(value)`.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::block.text: Wraps one piece of untrusted material (a page's text, a candidate's question) in clearly marked start and end lines carrying the random code, optionally cutting it to a maximum length.
tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::block.tech: Serialises non-str `text` with json.dumps; repeatedly removes any occurrence of the nonce from the body; truncates to `limit` if given; returns '<<<label:nonce>>>\nbody\n<<<END label:nonce>>>'.

tools/claude_cli/prompts.py::new_nonce.text: Makes a fresh random code used to fence off data in a prompt, so text copied from a website cannot pretend to end its own section.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::LIMITER.text: The shared counter that limits how often candidates can ask the AI questions or request practice.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::LIMITER.tech: Module-level `RateLimiter()` used by /api/claude/ask (8 per 60 s per IP) and /api/claude/practice (4 per 60 s).

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_body.text: Reads the request's data, accepting it only if it is a proper record; anything else counts as empty.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_body.tech: `request.get_json(silent=True)` if it is a dict, else {}.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_candidate_v.text: The part of a job a candidate may see: its state and its checked result, without internal details like who asked, retries or audit records.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_candidate_v.tech: `job.as_dict(include_input=False)` with audit, requestedBy, role, evidenceLinks, inputFingerprint, maxRetries and retryCount removed.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_client_key.text: Makes the key used to count requests per caller for rate limiting.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_is_admin.text: Whether the current request comes from an administrator.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_limit_arg.text: Reads how many jobs to list from the address, defaulting to 30 if missing or invalid.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_limit_arg.tech: int of the `limit` query arg, 30 on missing/zero or parse errors (store clamps it further).

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_user.text: Works out which candidate is asking, from a header or the address, with unsafe characters removed; defaults to the single default candidate.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::_user.tech: Reads X-GovOS-User header or `user_id` query arg, strips chars outside [A-Za-z0-9._:-], caps at 64, falls back to 'default-candidate'.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::admin_denied.text: Checks whether the caller is allowed to do administrator tasks; if not, gives back a 'forbidden' reply explaining how to get access, otherwise nothing.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::admin_denied.tech: Runs `admin_check(request.remote_addr, request.headers)`; returns None if allowed, else a (json {error ADMIN_REQUIRED, message, hint naming ADMIN_HEADER}, 403) tuple.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::admin_requir.text: A guard that can be put on any web address of the app so only an administrator (with the admin token, or calling from the same machine) can use it.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::admin_requir.tech: Decorator: calls `admin_denied()` and returns its 403 response or the wrapped function's result. Local guard only, not production authentication.

tools/claude_cli/routes.py::create_bluep.text: Sets up all the web addresses of the Claude integration for the app: a health check, administrator job creation, listing, viewing, cancelling and retrying, and the two candidate features (ask a question about one exam, get practice questions). Candidate features are rate limited and refuse with a 'use the normal assistant' reply when Claude is not ready.
tools/claude_cli/routes.py::create_bluep.tech: Builds a Flask Blueprint and a `JobQueue` (default specs). Routes: GET /api/claude/health (gateway health + adminTokenRequired); POST/GET /api/claude/jobs (admin; create via `queue.submit`, 202 with pollUrl and token, 400/403/429 on errors; list with counts); GET /jobs/<id> and POST /jobs/<id>/cancel (admin or matching X-job token, otherwise 404 indistinguishable from missing); POST /jobs/<id>/retry (admin, only FAILED/CANCELLED, 409 otherwise, resubmits the stored input); POST /api/claude/ask and /practice (candidate role, LIMITER 8/60 and 4/60, 503 CLAUDE_UNAVAILABLE with fallback when not ready). Returns (bp, queue) and sets `bp.queue`.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::IS_WINDOWS.text: Whether GovOS is running on Windows, which changes how a stuck program is stopped.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::ProcessOutco.text: What happened when GovOS ran the Claude program: its exit code, what it printed, its error output, and whether it timed out, was cancelled, printed too much or could not start.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::ProcessOutco.tech: Dataclass: returncode, stdout, stderr, timed_out, cancelled, output_truncated, start_error ('not_found'|'denied'|'oserror').

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::Runner.text: The common shape of anything that can run the Claude program for GovOS. Tests swap in fakes that follow it.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::Runner.tech: Interface with `run(argv, *, stdin_text, env, cwd, timeout, max_output_bytes, cancel_event=None) -> ProcessOutcome`.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::Runner.run.text: Placeholder that real and fake runners replace.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::SubprocessRu.text: The one place in GovOS that actually starts the Claude program as a separate process, safely.

Starts the Claude program safely: no command shell is used, the request is sent through its input rather than its command line, it gets only a minimal environment, its output is capped, and it is stopped (with everything it started) if it is cancelled, prints too much or runs past its time limit.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::SubprocessRu.tech: Refused under test -> start_error 'denied'. Popen(list(argv), pipes, env, cwd, shell=False) with CREATE_NO_WINDOW|CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP on Windows or start_new_session on POSIX; start errors map to not_found/denied/oserror. Threads pump stdout (cap `max_output_bytes`), stderr (64 KB, drained) and feed stdin as UTF-8. Polls every 50 ms: cancel -> cancelled, stdout over cap -> output_truncated, past deadline -> timed_out, each killing the tree. Waits 10 s, joins threads, closes pipes, decodes output with replacement.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::TEST_MODE_EN.text: The name of the setting that marks GovOS as being tested. While it is on, the real Claude program can never be started.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::_pump.text: Reads a program's output in pieces into memory up to a limit. For the main output it stops at the limit; for the error output it keeps reading and throwing away the excess so the program never gets stuck.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::_pump.tech: Reads 8192-byte chunks; once the running total exceeds `cap` sets flags['truncated']; with `drain` keeps reading without storing, otherwise breaks. Exceptions swallowed.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::_refused_und.text: During tests, refuses to start any program other than the Python program running the tests (which hosts the fake Claude).
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::_refused_und.tech: True when GOVOS_CLAUDE_TEST_MODE=='1', argv is non-empty, and realpath(argv[0]) != realpath(sys.executable) (or realpath raises OSError).

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::build_child_.text: Builds the minimal set of system settings handed to the Claude program: only what it needs to start and find the computer's own sign-in, and never any API key or GovOS setting.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::build_child_.tech: Copies only keys in `_ENV_ALLOW` (case-insensitive), skipping any starting with ANTHROPIC_, OPENAI_, AWS_, AZURE_, GOOGLE_ or GOVOS_, from `parent` (default os.environ); adds NO_COLOR=1.

tools/claude_cli/runner.py::kill_process.text: Force-stops the Claude program and everything it started, so nothing keeps running after a timeout or cancel.
tools/claude_cli/runner.py::kill_process.tech: Windows: `taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` (no shell, 15 s timeout); POSIX: SIGKILL to the process group. Then `proc.kill()`. All errors swallowed.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ATTRIBUTION.text: The fixed list of roles Claude may assign when asked what a passage of a notice does for a value (total vacancies, a category count, an age relaxation, a fee rule, pay scale, and so on).
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ATTRIBUTION.tech: List of role strings: the enum for CLASSIFY_ATTRIBUTION's `role` and the default ROLES line in its prompt; callers restrict each field to a subset.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.text: The outcome of one call to Claude: which task, whether it worked or which infrastructure problem occurred, timings, the checked reply (only if it passed every check), validation errors, a safe message, version and fingerprint details, whether a remembered answer was reused, and usage counts.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.tech: Dataclass: operation, status (InfraStatus), job_id, timings, cli_available, exit_category, timed_out, output (only when schema-valid), validation_errors, message, template_version, input/output fingerprints, cache_hit, cli_version, stats. Has `ok`, `as_dict`, `failed`.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.text: The safe, shareable view of a Claude call's outcome, which never includes the command used, file paths, environment or raw error output.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.tech: camelCase dict of the fields (validationErrors copied); `output` included unless include_output=False; stats and cli_version omitted.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.text: A quick way to build a 'this call failed' outcome with the standard safe message for the problem.
Whether the call succeeded and produced a usable reply.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::ClaudeResul.tech: True iff status is OK and output is not None.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::DATE_ROLES.text: The fixed list of events a date in a notice may be classified as (notification, application start or close, fee deadline, exam, admit card, result, interview and so on), plus 'cited, not scheduled' and 'not a date'.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::DATE_ROLES.tech: List used as the enum for CLASSIFY_DATE's `role` and its prompt's default ROLES.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::DISCOVERY_K.text: The kinds of page Claude may say a found source is: notification, syllabus, result, admit card, answer key, portal or other.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::EXTRACTABLE.text: The only facts Claude may be asked to read out of a document: application dates, exam date, admit card and result dates, total vacancies, fee, minimum and maximum age, qualification, number of attempts, stage name and official portal.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::EXTRACTABLE.tech: List used by `norm_extract` (filter and default), the EXTRACT_FIELDS prompt and the `field` enum of its schema.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::InfraStatus.text: The possible outcomes of a call to Claude as a piece of machinery: worked, switched off, not installed, not signed in, unsupported version, busy, timed out, failed, gave broken or wrongly shaped output, input too large, web search unavailable, or cancelled. None of these ever says anything about an exam or an authority.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::InfraStatus.tech: str Enum: OK, CLAUDE_DISABLED, CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_INSTALLED, CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_AUTHENTICATED, CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED, CLAUDE_CLI_BUSY, CLAUDE_CLI_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_CLI_FAILED, CLAUDE_INVALID_OUTPUT, CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED, CLAUDE_INPUT_REJECTED, CLAUDE_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE, CANCELLED; with a `retryable` property. Deliberately not a factual status.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::InfraStatus.text: Whether a failure is temporary and worth trying again: only a timeout, Claude being busy, or a general program failure. A broken or wrongly shaped reply is never retried.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::InfraStatus.tech: True for CLAUDE_CLI_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_CLI_BUSY, CLAUDE_CLI_FAILED (`_RETRYABLE`); used by handlers' `_fail` and the job queue's retry decision.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::NAVIGATION_.text: The exam page sections an AI answer may point the candidate to (overview, dates, eligibility, application, syllabus, results, FAQs and so on), or none.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::NAVIGATION_.tech: List of section keys (mapped to section numbers by the UI); enum for ANSWER_QUESTION's `navigate_to` and checked again in `validate_answer`.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::Operation.text: The complete list of tasks GovOS may ask Claude to do: check a claim against evidence, classify a passage or a date, check a quote is complete, read a post name, confirm two documents are the same recruitment, order a roadmap, search for sources, extract fields, answer a candidate's question, write practice, solve practice independently, and label website links. A request can only name one of these.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::Operation.tech: str Enum allowlist: VERIFY_CLAIM, CLASSIFY_ATTRIBUTION, CLASSIFY_DATE, CHECK_COMPLETENESS, EXTRACT_DESIGNATION, CONFIRM_RECRUITMENT, ORDER_ROADMAP, DISCOVER_SOURCES, EXTRACT_FIELDS, ANSWER_QUESTION, GENERATE_PRACTICE, SOLVE_PRACTICE, CLASSIFY_SOURCE. Each has one template in prompts.TEMPLATES and one schema in OPERATION_SCHEMAS.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::REASONING_K.text: Names of reply parts that would hold Claude's hidden working-out ('thinking', 'reasoning', 'scratchpad' and so on). These are removed before a reply is checked or used.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::REASONING_K.tech: frozenset of top-level keys stripped by `strip_reasoning`.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::SAFE_MESSAG.text: A fixed, plain message for each kind of Claude problem, shown instead of the program's raw error text, file paths or commands.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::SAFE_MESSAG.tech: Dict InfraStatus -> fixed English string (OK -> ''); used by `ClaudeResult.failed`, handlers and routes.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::SOURCE_ROLE.text: The fixed list of roles Claude may give a link on an authority's website (exam page, notification, question paper, answer key, application portal, study material and so on). There is no 'unknown': if Claude cannot tell, it must leave the link out.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::SOURCE_ROLE.tech: Mirror of exam_builder's DocKind minus UNKNOWN (a test pins them together); enum for CLASSIFY_SOURCE's `role` and its prompt's ROLES.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::_arr.text: Shorthand for describing a list in a reply, with the shape of its items and a maximum number of items (50 by default).

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::_obj.text: Shorthand for describing a record-shaped part of a reply where every listed part is required (unless told otherwise) and nothing extra is allowed.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::_str.text: Shorthand for describing a text part of a reply, with a maximum length and optionally a minimum length or a fixed list of allowed values.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::_str.tech: Returns {'type': 'string', 'maxLength': max_len} plus minLength if set and enum if given (default max 600).

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::fingerprint.text: Makes a stable unique code for a piece of data, so the same request always gets the same code. Used to spot duplicate jobs and reuse earlier decisions.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::fingerprint.tech: SHA-256 hex of canonical JSON (sorted keys, compact separators, ensure_ascii False, default=str).

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::strip_reaso.text: Removes any hidden working-out sections from the top level of a Claude reply and counts how many were removed.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::strip_reaso.tech: For a dict returns ({k: v not in REASONING_KEYS}, number dropped); non-dicts return (obj, 0). Top level only.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::to_cli_sche.text: Produces a simplified copy of a reply shape to hand to the Claude program, keeping only the widely supported parts; the stricter limits are checked by GovOS afterwards.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::to_cli_sche.tech: Keeps only type, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, enum, description, recursing into properties and items.

tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::validate.text: Checks a reply from Claude against the exact shape GovOS expects for that task (types, allowed values, lengths, ranges, required parts and no extra parts) and lists every way it is wrong. An empty list means the reply is acceptable.
tools/claude_cli/schemas.py::validate.tech: Recursive strict JSON-schema subset: `type` (string/boolean/integer/number/null/array/object, bools excluded from numbers; a type mismatch returns immediately), `enum`, string maxLength/minLength/pattern, numeric minimum/maximum, array maxItems/minItems/items, object required/additionalProperties(False)/properties. Returns a list of '$.path: problem' strings.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::ADMIN_HEAD.text: The name of the request header that carries the administrator token.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::JOB_TOKEN_.text: The name of the request header that carries a candidate's one-off code for reading their own AI job.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::JOB_TOKEN_.tech: 'X-GovOS-Job-Token'; read by the job GET and cancel routes.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.text: A simple counter that limits how many requests a caller can make within a time window, so a page cannot hammer the AI features. It works within one server process only.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.tech: Sliding-window limiter: per-key deque of monotonic timestamps under a lock; injectable clock.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.text: Sets up an empty request counter.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.tech: Stores clock (default time.monotonic), a defaultdict(deque) of hits and a lock.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.text: Says whether one more request from this caller is allowed right now and, if not, how many seconds to wait. Only allowed requests are counted.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::RateLimite.tech: Drops timestamps older than `window_seconds`; if `limit` remain returns (False, seconds until the oldest expires, at least 1); else records now and returns (True, 0).
Clears the hits dict under the lock (used by tests).

tools/claude_cli/security.py::admin_chec.text: Decides whether a request may perform administrator actions. If an admin token is configured, the request must present it. If not, the request must come directly from this same computer, not through a proxy and not from a web page on another site. This is a local safeguard, not real login security.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::admin_chec.tech: Pure function returning (allowed, reason). With GOVOS_CLAUDE_ADMIN_TOKEN set: constant-time compare against the X-GovOS-Admin-Token header. Without: refuses any proxy header (X-Forwarded-For, Forwarded, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-Host), an Origin whose host is not localhost/127.0.0.1/::1, and any remote_addr not in the loopback set; else allows with 'loopback'.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::admin_toke.text: Whether the server has been set up to demand an admin token.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::admin_toke.tech: True when GOVOS_CLAUDE_ADMIN_TOKEN (from `env`, default os.environ) is non-blank.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::hash_token.text: Scrambles a job code one way, so only the scrambled form is stored and the code itself never is.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::hash_token.tech: SHA-256 hex of the UTF-8 token ('' for None).

tools/claude_cli/security.py::new_job_to.text: Creates a new random secret code that lets a candidate read their own AI job.

tools/claude_cli/security.py::token_matc.text: Checks whether a presented job code matches a stored scrambled one, in a way that does not leak timing clues.
tools/claude_cli/security.py::token_matc.tech: False if either is empty; else `hmac.compare_digest(hash_token(token), stored_hash)`.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ByOperation.text: Test support: a scripted reply that depends on which task Claude was asked to do; a task with no entry gets an empty reply (which fails the shape check).
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ByOperation.tech: dict subclass mapping Operation -> reply; `ScriptedRunner.run` looks up the call's operation (via `operation_of`) and uses {} if absent.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FAKE_CLI_SC.text: Test support: where the fake Claude program file is, for tests that need a real separate process.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FAKE_CLI_SC.tech: Absolute path of tools/claude_cli/fake_cli.py; used by `fake_cli_config`.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FAKE_VERSIO.text: Test support: the version number the fake Claude reports.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude.text: Test support: a real GovOS Claude gateway wired to the scripted fake runner, so tests exercise all of GovOS's own command-building, reply parsing and checking, with only the Claude program itself faked. It can simulate Claude being off, missing, signed out or out of date.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude.tech: ClaudeGateway subclass built on `ScriptedRunner`; exposes calls, argvs, ops, calls_for(op) and prompts.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude..text: Test support: builds the fake gateway with the given replies and any failure to simulate.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude..tech: CLAUDE_DISABLED -> enabled False; CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_AUTHENTICATED -> authenticated False by default; CLAUDE_CLI_UNSUPPORTED -> help text with only --print; CLAUDE_CLI_NOT_INSTALLED -> a nonexistent cli_path (else sys.executable). Builds ClaudeConfig(enabled, cli_path, max_concurrency=concurrency, slot_wait_seconds=2.0, **config_kw) and calls ClaudeGateway.__init__ with the scripted runner, audit and cache.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude..text: Test support: the command arguments of every AI call that reached the fake.
Test support: how many real AI questions reached the fake program (reused answers and refusals do not count).
Test support: how many AI calls were made for one particular task.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude..tech: Counts entries of scripted.ops that are `operation`.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::FakeClaude..text: Test support: the task of each AI call that reached the fake, in order.
Test support: the exact prompt text sent with each AI call.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ForbiddenCl.text: Test support: a gateway that makes the test fail if anything tries to call Claude, proving a code path stops before reaching the AI.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ForbiddenCl.tech: ClaudeGateway over an empty ScriptedRunner whose `run` increments `attempts` and raises AssertionError(message).

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ForbiddenCl.text: Test support: sets up the 'must not be called' gateway with its failure message.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ForbiddenCl.tech: Builds an enabled config with sys.executable and an empty ScriptedRunner; stores message and attempts=0.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ForbiddenCl.text: Test support: counts the forbidden attempt and fails the test.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::HELP_TEXT.text: Test support: the help text the fake Claude prints, listing every option GovOS needs, so start-up checks pass in tests.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::HELP_TEXT.tech: Built from client.REQUIRED_FLAGS + OPTIONAL_FLAGS; returned by `ScriptedRunner` for '--help'.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.text: Test support: a fake process runner that plays back scripted Claude replies without starting any program. It answers health checks, simulates each kind of failure on request, and records every call.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.tech: Runner holding `replies`, an optional `fail` InfraStatus, `authenticated`, `help_text`, and records argvs, prompts, envs, cwds, quick (auth probes) and ops.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.text: Test support: sets up the fake with its replies, any failure to simulate, sign-in state and help text.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.tech: Stores the arguments and initialises the record lists.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.text: Test support: takes the next scripted reply; the last one repeats forever, and with none it gives an empty reply.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.tech: Returns {} if empty; pops the head while more than one remains, else returns the last without removing it.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.text: Test support: answers one fake Claude call. Help, version and sign-in checks get healthy answers; a cancelled call reports cancelled; otherwise the call is recorded and either the requested failure is simulated (timeout, crash, rate limit, not signed in, broken output, wrong shape, web tools blocked) or the next scripted reply is returned in Claude's format.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::ScriptedRun.tech: Handles '--help', '--version', 'auth status' (loggedIn), pre-set cancel_event. Records argv/stdin/env/cwd/op. `fail` maps to ProcessOutcome(timed_out), returncode 1 'boom', a 429 error envelope, a not-logged-in envelope, 'this is not json', a wrong-shape envelope, or a permission-denied discovery envelope. Else the reply (ByOperation lookup, callable(args, stdin) evaluated) is returned as a ProcessOutcome as-is, raw string stdout, a ready envelope dict, or wrapped with `envelope`.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::envelope.text: Test support: wraps a reply in the same outer format the real Claude program prints, with options to simulate errors, blocked tools, web activity and so on.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::envelope.tech: Returns the `claude -p --output-format json` envelope: type, subtype, is_error, num_turns, result (explicit or JSON of `structured`), permission_denials, usage incl. server_tool_use web counts, total_cost_usd, plus `structured_output` when given and `extra` merged in.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::fake_cli_co.text: Test support: a Claude setup that runs the fake Claude program as a real separate process, following a given scenario file.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::fake_cli_co.tech: ClaudeConfig(enabled=True, cli_path=sys.executable, cli_args_prefix=(FAKE_CLI_SCRIPT, '--scenario', path), slot_wait_seconds default 3.0, **kw).

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::operation_o.text: Test support: works out which task a recorded Claude call was for, from the reply shape GovOS passed with it.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::operation_o.tech: Parses the argv value after '--json-schema' and returns the Operation whose `to_cli_schema(OPERATION_SCHEMAS[op])` equals it, else None.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::use_gateway.text: Test support: temporarily makes a given (usually fake) gateway the one the whole program uses, then puts the previous one back.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::use_gateway.tech: Context manager: saves client._DEFAULT, calls set_gateway(gateway), yields it, restores the previous in `finally`.

tools/claude_cli/testing.py::verdict_rep.text: Test support: builds a sample Claude reply to an evidence-check question with the chosen verdict.
tools/claude_cli/testing.py::verdict_rep.tech: Returns a VERIFY_CLAIM-shaped dict: decision, identity_supported, evidence_supported, claim_supported, reason.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::BANNER.text: The pattern for the '// =====' lines the code uses to divide a file into sections; the guide groups declarations under them.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::CSS.text: The guide's whole look: colours for light and dark mode, the sidebar, cards, tables, the two-column plain chapter, badges and the diagram styles, including fitting on a phone.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::CSS.tech: One stylesheet with :root tokens, a prefers-color-scheme: dark override, grid layout (290px sidebar), .topic/.two columns (stacked under 1000px), .ref entry styles, SVG flow styles, and code ligatures turned off.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::GLOSSARY.text: GovOS's own terms explained (exam record, provenance, VERIFIED, superseded, the admin guard and so on), shown in chapter 2.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::GLOSSARY.tech: List of (term, meaning-in-Markdown) pairs rendered with md_inline.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::INNER_DECL.text: The pattern for a declaration one level inside a component or function (a state pair, a handler, a helper value).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::INNER_DECL.tech: Matches two-space-indented const/let/var/function/async function, capturing the target (a name or a [destructured] pair) and the rest of the line.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::INNER_EFFECT.text: The pattern for an effect inside a component (work done after the screen is drawn).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::INNER_EFFECT.tech: Matches a two-space-indented useEffect( or useLayoutEffect(, optionally React.-prefixed.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::JS.text: The guide's small script: the search box that filters every entry, and links that open the right collapsed section before jumping to an entry.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::JS.tech: run() toggles .hidden on [data-s] by substring and opens/hides details.ref-group; openTo(id) opens every ancestor <details>, clears a search hiding the target, and scrolls to it; wired to clicks on '#' links, hashchange and the initial hash.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::KIND_PLAIN.text: A one-line everyday description of each kind of code (component, function, type, state, effect and so on), shown when you hover a kind badge.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::KIND_PLAIN.tech: dict kind -> description; also the prefix of the name-derived fallback text in plain_for.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::OBJ_ARROW.text: The pattern for a method written as 'name: (…) =>' inside an object.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::OBJ_ARROW.tech: Two-space-indented 'name:' followed by an arrow function (optionally async, typed).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::OBJ_METHOD.text: The pattern for a method inside a class or an object such as storageService.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::OBJ_METHOD.tech: Two-space-indented name with optional private/public/protected/static/readonly/async/get/set modifiers and generics, followed by a parameter list (and optional return type and brace).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::OUT.text: Where the finished guide is written: docs/GovOS_Guide.html.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::PLAIN.text: All the stored explanations, loaded once when the script starts.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::PLAIN.tech: load_plain() at import; --stamp mutates it in place and writes it back.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::PLAIN_PATH.text: Where the plain-language explanations of every declaration are stored: tools/docs/plain.json.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::PLAIN_PATH.tech: Path to the JSON store {version, entries: {'<file>::<name>': {text, tech, hash}}}.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::QUIET.text: Whether the script was asked to stay quiet (used by the automatic hook), printing only when the guide actually changes.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::QUIET.tech: True when '--quiet' is in sys.argv; suppresses the 'is current' line and build warnings.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::ROOT.text: The project's top folder, worked out from where this script sits, so the guide can be built from anywhere.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::ROOT.tech: Absolute path two levels above tools/docs/.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::TS_DECL.text: The pattern that recognises a top-level declaration in a TypeScript file (a const, function, type, interface, class or enum).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::TS_DECL.tech: Regex at line start with optional export/default/declare/async, capturing the keyword (group 5) and the name (group 6).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::anchor.text: Turns a name into a safe link target inside the page (lowercase, dashes), so any heading or entry can be linked to.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::api_calls.text: Finds every server address the page calls, and where.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::api_calls.tech: Scans the three frontend files for quoted '/api/...' paths, replaces ${...} with <id>, strips trailing slashes; sorted (path, ['file:line', ...]).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::build.text: Assembles the whole guide: reads the code, indexes every declaration for links, writes the twelve chapters, and returns the finished page with its counts.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::build.tech: Scans the five frontend files and every non-test Python file, routes, tables, tests, checks, storage keys and API calls; indexes REF_INDEX and DOC_HEADINGS; renders chapters 1-12 (guide_text STORY, words, start, architecture, flows with FIGURE_STEPS, exam page, frontend, backend, API, data, tests, files and design records); puts the stamp in stats so it stays out of the content hash.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::clean_comment.text: Strips comment markers (//, /*, *) from the lines written above a declaration, leaving the plain words.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::clean_comment.tech: Removes /**, */, leading * and // per line, drops '=====' rule lines, collapses 3+ blank lines; returns the stripped text.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::decorator_tex.text: Turns a decorator (like @app.route(...)) back into its source text.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::describe_file.text: Gives a one-line description of any file, taken from the file's own opening comment or docstring (or a Markdown file's first heading).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::describe_file.tech: .py: module docstring's first paragraph; .ts/.tsx/.mjs/.js: leading block comment or // lines (skipping /// references); .md: first heading; capped at 400 chars.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::diagrams.text: Defines the seven flow charts: the whole system, how a fact reaches a candidate, navigation, how 'verified' is decided, saving, Ask GovOS AI, and reading an uploaded scorecard.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::diagrams.tech: Returns {architecture, pipeline, navigation, evidence, persistence, ask, upload} -> svg_flow figures with hand-placed coordinates in 1000-wide view boxes.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::exam_sections.text: Reads the exam page's list of parts and reference parts straight from ui.tsx, so the guide's table of parts always matches the app.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::exam_sections.tech: Regex over the EXAM_SECTIONS / REFERENCE_SECTIONS array literals: num, label and optional under.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::file_lines.text: Counts the lines in a text file (images, databases and fonts count as zero).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::file_lines.tech: read(rel).count('\n') + 1, 0 for binary extensions or unreadable files.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::first_para.text: Tidies a docstring for display (trims surrounding space).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::frontend_chec.text: Lists every frontend check file and the names of the checks inside it, with the file's own description.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::frontend_chec.tech: For each tracked tools/frontend_checks/*.ts except fixtures and stub.ts: check('...') names via regex and the leading block comment.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::git.text: Asks git a question (for example the current commit) and returns the answer, or nothing if git is not available.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::git.tech: subprocess.run(['git', *args], cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30).stdout; OSError/SubprocessError -> ''.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::index_ref.text: Remembers where a declaration's entry is, so [[name]] links in the hand-written chapter can find it.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::index_ref.tech: REF_INDEX.setdefault(name, ref_anchor(rel, name)) -- the first file to declare a name (frontend files are indexed first) wins.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::load_plain.text: Loads the stored explanations, or starts empty if the file is missing or broken.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::main.text: Runs the build and writes the guide only if its content changed, so running it again (or committing) creates no noise. It also handles the upkeep commands.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::main.tech: build(); prints WARNINGS unless --quiet; --stale/--stamp via plain_maintenance (a rebuild after --stamp); digest = sha256 of the page with the stamp placeholder; skips writing when the old file's content-hash matches; else fills __STAMP__, __GENERATED_AT__ and __HASH__ and writes with LF line endings.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::md_inline.text: Converts the small inline parts of Markdown (code, links, bold, italic) into HTML, escaping everything else so no text can become markup.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::md_inline.tech: Protects `code` spans with \x00N\x00 placeholders, html-escapes, then converts [text](url), **bold** and *italic*, and restores the code spans.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::md_to_html.text: A small Markdown reader for the project's own documents (CLAUDE.md and the audits): headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, code blocks, quotes and rules, so they appear in full inside the guide.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::md_to_html.tech: Line-based state machine with a list stack keyed by indent; headings get ids anchor(id_prefix, title) and level <= 3 ones are appended to `toc`; tables need a separator row; fenced code is escaped verbatim. No dependency.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::name_words.text: Turns a code name into ordinary words ('evaluatePostEligibility' becomes 'evaluate post eligibility'), used when no explanation has been written yet.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::name_words.tech: Takes the last segment after ' > ' and '.', splits camelCase and acronym boundaries, replaces underscores with spaces, lower-cases.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_for.text: Finds the explanation of one declaration and says whether it is current, possibly out of date (the code changed after it was written), or missing (so only the name can be read).
tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_for.tech: Returns (text, tech, state) with state 'ok' | 'stale' | 'name'. Records the current hash in PLAIN_SEEN (first occurrence wins for duplicate names); 'stale' when the stored hash differs from it; with no entry, KIND_PLAIN plus name_words.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_key.text: Builds the label an explanation is stored under: the file and the name, joined.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_key.tech: f'{rel}::{name}' -- a method is 'Class.method', a component's inner item 'App > name'.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_mainten.text: The upkeep commands for the explanations: --stamp records the current code fingerprint on new or rewritten explanations; --stale lists explanations whose code has changed, declarations with none, and explanations whose code no longer exists.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::plain_mainten.tech: --stamp sets hash from PLAIN_SEEN where missing and rewrites plain.json sorted; --stale compares stored hashes with PLAIN_SEEN and prints the three lists.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::practice_engi.text: Reads which practice engine each exam gets, straight from the app's registry, for the guide's table.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::practice_engi.tech: Regex over the PRACTICE_ENGINES object: each exam id block's engine/component name and label.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::py_signature.text: Writes out a Python function's name and parameters as they appear in the code.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::py_signature.tech: f'{node.name}({ast.unparse(node.args)})', falling back to the bare name.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::py_tests.text: Lists every Python test and the classes they sit in, with each test's description.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::py_tests.tech: For tracked test_*.py: class methods named test* and module-level test* functions, with docstrings and lines; files with no tests are skipped.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::read.text: Reads a project file as text, given its path from the project's top folder.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::read.tech: open(os.path.join(ROOT, rel), encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read() -- unreadable bytes become replacement characters rather than failing the build.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::ref_anchor.text: Builds the link target of one reference entry, so the plain chapter can jump straight to it.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::ref_entry.text: Builds one entry of the reference: its kind badge, name and line, the explanation in simple words, how it works, a warning if the code changed since it was written, the signature, the notes written in the code, and what it keeps inside.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::ref_entry.tech: With rel: id = ref_anchor, plain_for(...) for simple/tech/state; with inner: a details 'Inside it: counts' list where methods and main.tsx items get their own anchors and explanations (shared names explained once). data-s carries every searchable word.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::rich.text: Turns the hand-written chapter's light markup into page HTML: paragraphs, lists, bold, code, and links into the reference and the design notes. A link to something that does not exist is reported, not silently printed.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::rich.tech: Splits on blank lines; '- ' blocks become <ul>. [[name]] -> link to REF_INDEX[name] (else <code> and a WARNINGS entry); {{doc:Heading}} -> link to that CLAUDE.md heading's anchor (warned if not in DOC_HEADINGS). Placeholders \x01N\x01 protect the links through md_inline.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::route_words.text: The one-line description of a route in the API table: its handler's plain explanation if one is written, otherwise the handler's docstring.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::route_words.tech: PLAIN[plain_key(file, func)]['text'] or the docstring's first paragraph.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::routes.text: Finds every address the server answers, which handler runs it, whether it needs the owner's admin access, and its explanation.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::routes.tech: For tracked non-test .py files containing '.route(': walks every function's decorators for <owner>.route(path, methods=[...]); prefixes a Blueprint's url_prefix; admin when decorated admin_required or the body calls admin_denied(). Sorted by path and methods.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_inner.text: Lists what a screen piece or function keeps inside itself: what it remembers (state), handles (refs), works out once (memos), its handlers and helpers, and its effects, each with its line and the comment above it.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_inner.tech: Over the declaration's span, at exactly two-space indent: [a, setA] = useState/useReducer -> state named a; useRef -> ref; useMemo/useCallback -> memo; handle*/on* or arrows/functions -> handler; else value; useEffect/useLayoutEffect -> effect. Comments directly above are kept. Each gets end and hash like top-level items.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_methods.text: Lists the methods of a class or of an object of functions (like storageService), each with its line, the comment above it and its own code fingerprint.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_methods.tech: Lines at exactly two-space indent matching OBJ_ARROW or OBJ_METHOD (not control keywords) become {kind: method, name, line, doc, sig}; end = line before the next method (or the container's end); hash = span_hash.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_py.text: Reads one Python file and lists its top-level functions, classes (with their methods) and constants, with signatures, decorators, docstrings and code fingerprints.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_py.tech: ast.parse; FunctionDef/AsyncFunctionDef -> function; ClassDef -> class with methods; single-name ALL_CAPS Assign -> constant (value unparsed, <=160 chars). Each has line, end (end_lineno) and hash (span_hash from the first decorator line). A syntax error yields an entry saying so.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_ts.text: Reads one TypeScript file and lists every top-level declaration with its line, kind and the comment above it, grouped under the file's section banners. For screen pieces and functions it also lists what they keep inside; for service objects and classes, their methods.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::scan_ts.tech: Walks lines tracking block comments and // runs; a banner (rule, title lines, rule) opens a group (title split on ' — '). Each TS_DECL match records name, kind, line, exported, signature (<=220 chars) and doc. Afterwards each item gets end (line before the next declaration), hash (span_hash) and inner (scan_inner for component/function/hook, scan_methods for a class or an object-literal value).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::span_hash.text: Makes a short fingerprint of a piece of code. If the code changes, the fingerprint changes, which is how the guide knows an explanation may be out of date.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::span_hash.tech: sha1 of the span's lines (rstripped, joined, stripped), first 12 hex characters.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::sqlite_tables.text: Finds every database table the server creates, with its columns, by reading the CREATE TABLE statements.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::sqlite_tables.tech: Regex over non-test .py files for 'CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS name (...)'; columns are non-constraint lines split into name and type; first definition wins; sorted by name.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::storage_keys.text: Finds every key the app stores in the browser, and where each one is used.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::storage_keys.tech: Scans services.ts, ui.tsx and main.tsx for quoted 'govos_*' strings; returns sorted (key, ['file:line', ...]).

tools/docs/build_guide.py::svg_flow.text: Draws one flow chart as a picture made of boxes and arrows, inside the page itself, so the diagrams need no image files or internet.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::svg_flow.tech: Nodes (id, x, y, w, h, text, tone; first text line bold) and edges (from, to, label, opts) with elbow paths whose exit side is horizontal or vertical by geometry or forced with 'h'/'v'; 'dash' dashes the line; labels are pill-shaped; optional dashed groups. Returns <figure class='diagram'> with an SVG and a caption.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::tracked_files.text: Lists every file in the project that git tracks, which is what the guide documents.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::tracked_files.tech: git ls-files, filtered to files that exist; outside a git checkout it walks the tree, skipping .git, node_modules, dist, __pycache__ and exam_data. Sorted relative paths with forward slashes.

tools/docs/build_guide.py::ts_kind.text: Decides what kind of thing a TypeScript declaration is (screen component, hook, type, constant, function, class or plain value) from how it is written.
tools/docs/build_guide.py::ts_kind.tech: interface/type/enum -> type; class -> class; use[A-Z] -> hook; capitalised React.FC / function / arrow returning JSX -> component; ALL_CAPS -> constant; arrow or function -> function; else value.

tools/docs/guide_text.py::FIGURE_STEPS.text: The step-by-step explanation in simple words printed under each of the seven flow charts.
tools/docs/guide_text.py::FIGURE_STEPS.tech: dict figure key -> rich() text, rendered in a .steps box after the matching svg_flow figure.

tools/docs/guide_text.py::STORY.text: The hand-written heart of chapter 1: 32 topics, each told in simple words and then under the hood, covering every screen, every part of an exam's page and every mechanism of GovOS.
tools/docs/guide_text.py::STORY.tech: List of (title, id, simple, tech) tuples in the rich() markup; [[name]] links must name a real declaration and {{doc:Heading}} a real CLAUDE.md heading, or the build warns.

tools/docs/guide_text.py::TECH_WORDS.text: Everyday explanations of the technical words the guide uses (React, component, API, database, OCR, hash and so on), shown in chapter 2.
tools/docs/guide_text.py::TECH_WORDS.tech: List of (word, meaning-in-Markdown) pairs rendered with md_inline.

tools/exam_authoring/__main__.py::main.text: The command-line tool for authoring an exam record from its authority's own documents. You name an exam; it finds the matching authority adapter and exam, reads that authority's pages and notice, runs the isolation checks, and prints what it found, what needs review, what the authority does not publish, and what the tool failed to read. It can also write the record as a TypeScript exam file or as JSON.
tools/exam_authoring/__main__.py::main.tech: argparse: exam, --json, --pick, --list, --emit. `resolve(exam)` -> adapter (none: lists `supported()`, returns 2); `adapter.discover` (none: 3); lists matches and returns 0 for --list or several matches without --pick; else `adapter.gather(targets[pick or 0])`, `run_all(rec)` (IsolationError: 4). Prints sources and the FOUND / NEEDS REVIEW / NOT PUBLISHED / NOT EXTRACTED lists, foreign mentions and notes. --emit writes `header(rec, rpt)` + `render_exam(rec)` with a low-coverage warning; --json writes ids, sources, log and every field's status/note/value/citation. Returns 0.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::A.text: The rules every authority adapter must follow: it can find exams on its own authority's site by name, and read those exams' documents into a record, never touching another authority's site.
Finds every exam on this authority's site whose name matches what was typed.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::A.tech: Protocol method stub (`...`); implemented per adapter.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::A.text: Reads a located exam's own documents into an exam record.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::A.tech: Protocol method stub; must read only the target's own URLs.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::E.text: One exam as located on its authority's website, before anything has been read: its id, code, title, authority, official site, its own exam page, its notice, and any other documents worth reading.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/base.py::E.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, code, title, authority_name, official_domain, optional exam_page_url and notice_url, extra_urls dict (e.g. 'paper::label' -> url).

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::L.text: The two UPSC pages that list its exams: active exams and forthcoming exams.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::L.tech: Tuple of ROOT + '/examinations/active-exams' and '/examinations/forthcoming-exams', read by `UPSCAdapter.discover`.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.text: The adapter that reads UPSC's own website for any UPSC exam. It finds exams on UPSC's exam lists, then reads the exam's page for dates and published documents and the notice PDF for the rules (age, qualification, attempts, fee, services, vacancies, how to apply, admit card, scheme). When the page and the notice disagree on the last date, the page wins and the notice's date is recorded as superseded.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.tech: authority_name 'Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)', official_domain ROOT. `discover` scans LIST_PAGES; `gather` builds an ExamRecord from the exam page (`extract.dates_from_rows`, notice/paper/key/cutoff links, published-document rows) and the notice PDF (scanned -> NEEDS_REVIEW and stop; else the extract.* readers, each error logged); dates reconciled via `_reconcile_close_date` (or `dates_from_notice` without a page); officialPapers/answerKeys FOUND with links or NOT_PUBLISHED.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.text: Checks whether the last date to apply printed in the notice PDF matches the last date shown on UPSC's exam page. If they differ (as when UPSC extended the CSE 2026 window by three days), the page's date stays the real one and the notice's date is kept on record as replaced.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.tech: Static method. Finds the APPLICATION_CLOSE entry in rec.value('dates'); if absent, returns. Searches notice.all_text() for 'applications can be filled/submitted up to ...', parses it with extract.parse_date, and if the ISO day differs from the page's dateTimeStr[:10], sets a FOUND 'lastDateSuperseded' field {noticeDate (date + parse_time), pageDate, noticeExcerpt} cited to the page found via notice.find_page (default 1), and logs the difference. No match or no parseable date leaves the record unchanged.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.text: Finds the UPSC exams whose names match what was typed, by reading UPSC's active and forthcoming exam lists. A close match missing one word is still accepted, and the best match is listed first.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.tech: Splits the query into 3+ letter words; for each list page (fetch errors skipped) reads `html_links(page, '/examinations/')`, skipping links whose href is not an exam page and whose label has no 4-digit year, and labels shorter than 8 chars; requires all words, or at least len-1 of them. Builds ExamTarget(id=_slugify_id, code=_code, title 'UPSC <label>', exam_page_url=href), de-duplicated by id (first kept). Sorted by (all words present, words covered, shorter title).

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.text: Collects everything GovOS can read about one UPSC exam from UPSC's own website. It first reads the exam's page on upsc.gov.in for dates and links, then opens the official notice PDF and pulls out the rules (age, degree, attempts, fee, services, vacancies, how to apply, admit card, exam scheme). If the notice is a scanned image it says a person must read it, and it records honestly whether UPSC has published any question papers or answer keys.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::U.tech: Builds an ExamRecord for the ExamTarget. Loads the exam page with load_html (an unreachable page becomes a log note), sets dates via extract.dates_from_rows over html_rows, and scans html_links for the notice PDF (first link mentioning notice/notif) plus question-paper, answer-key and cut-off links stored in target.extra_urls under 'paper::', 'key::', 'cutoff::' keys; rows naming question papers/keys/results/admit cards are logged. With no notice URL it sets notice NOT_PUBLISHED and returns; an unreachable notice is also NOT_PUBLISHED; a scanned notice is NEEDS_REVIEW and returns early. Otherwise it records notice FOUND, runs ten extract.* functions (each failure logged, not raised), takes dates from the notice only when the page was not read (else calls _reconcile_close_date), and sets officialPapers/answerKeys FOUND with a page citation or NOT_PUBLISHED when none were linked.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::_.text: Makes a short code for a UPSC exam from the first letters of up to four words of its name (ignoring anything in brackets) plus the year, such as UPSC_CS_2026.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::_.tech: Initials of the first 4 alphabetic words of the title with parentheticals removed, upper-cased; returns 'UPSC_<letters>' + '_<year>' when a 20xx year is present.

tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::_.text: Makes a stable GovOS exam id from UPSC's printed exam name, keeping qualifiers like '(Preliminary)' and '(Main)' so two different exams never end up with the same id, and adding the year at the end.
tools/exam_authoring/adapters/upsc.py::_.tech: Lower-cases, captures the first 20xx year, slugifies non-alphanumerics to '-', removes '-20xx' occurrences and a trailing or embedded 'examination'/'exam' segment, returns 'exam-upsc-<slug>' + '-<year>' if a year was found.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_applicati.text: Writes the exam's application guide. If the notice's 'How to Apply' section was found, it is kept whole as a single quoted step instead of being split into made-up steps; photo and signature rules are left blank and point to the portal's own upload screen.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_applicati.tech: Portal = rec.value('applicationPortal') or official_domain. When howToApply is usable, otrSteps is one step with instructions [how.value[:1200]] and empty mandatoryFields/mistakes; otherwise '[]'. photoRules/signatureRules are empty-valued placeholders labelled 'As stated on the portal's upload screen'; certificateRules and rejectionPitfalls empty. Returns the guide literal with otrSteps appended.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_corrigend.text: If the notice's last date was replaced by a later date on the authority's exam page, writes a correction-log entry explaining the change from one date to the other.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_corrigend.tech: Returns '[]' unless 'lastDateSuperseded' is usable. Otherwise emits a one-element corrigendum array: id corr-<examId>-lastdate, title and diffSummary naming notice date -> page date, publishedDate = page date, effectiveDate = notice date, summary quoting noticeExcerpt, pdfUrl from the field's citation, status ACTIVE.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_dates.text: Writes the exam's list of important dates in TypeScript, each with its source. Dates whose label matched no known kind are left out rather than forced into the wrong category, and a last date that the authority later changed is kept as a struck-through 'superseded' entry.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_dates.tech: Returns '[]' when the 'dates' field is missing or unusable. Emits one ImportantDate literal per value whose type is not 'OTHER' (id date-<examId>-<i>, IST timezone, isTentative false, status AVAILABLE, provenance via _prov). If 'lastDateSuperseded' is usable, appends an APPLICATION_CLOSE entry with status SUPERSEDED using its noticeDate. Builds literals by trimming ts()'s closing ' }' and appending the provenance.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_eligibili.text: Writes up to four short eligibility cards (age limits, educational qualification, number of attempts, fee), each only if that rule was actually found with a source.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_eligibili.tech: For ageLimits, qualification, attempts and fee, skips any field not usable or lacking a citation. Body: age shows 'min to max years', optional 'as on' and born-between dates; fee and attempts use value['text'][:400]; qualification uses str(value)[:400]. Each card carries _prov(...) provenance. Returns '[]' when no card qualifies.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_overview.text: Writes a short plain description of the exam: its name and authority, the vacancy count and closing date if known, and a note that it was read from the authority's own documents with unsourced sections left empty.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_overview.tech: Joins sentences: '<title>, conducted by <authority>.', optional vacancies sentence, optional 'Applications close <dateTimeStr>' from the first APPLICATION_CLOSE date, and a fixed sentence about the authoring pipeline.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_posts.text: Writes the list of posts or services for the exam, but only those whose Group classification the authority printed. The rest are handed back so they can be listed in the file's header for a person to complete by hand.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_posts.tech: Returns ('[]', []) if 'posts' is unusable. For up to 60 names, computes classification_of; names with none go to the skipped list. Each kept post gets id post-<examId>-<i>, postName with the trailing Group text stripped (_GROUP_TAIL_RX), department = authority, empty pay fields, min/max age from ageLimits (default 0), and provenance. Returns (TS array or '[]', skipped).

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_prov.text: Writes the 'where this came from' note (provenance) for one extracted field in TypeScript form, or nothing if the field has no source.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_prov.tech: Returns '' when f.citation is empty; otherwise calls f.citation.to_provenance with id 'prov-<examId>-<suffix>' and level f.verification_level (OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED for FOUND, else UNDER_VERIFICATION) and serializes it with ts().

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_resources.text: Writes the resource-library links for the exam: the official notice PDF and up to 12 official question papers. Only links are written, never copies of the documents, following GovOS's 'link, don't store' rule.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::_resources.tech: If 'notice' is usable with a citation, emits an OFFICIAL_PDF / DIRECT_PDF resource (subject 'Official Gazette', linkVerifiedDate from the citation). If 'officialPapers' is usable, emits up to 12 entries sorted by label (title = text after 'paper::', subject 'Previous Year Papers'). Each carries provenance. Returns '[]' when there are none.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::classifica.text: Reads the 'Group A' or 'Group B' classification that the authority printed beside a service's name. If no Group is printed (as with IAS, IFS and IPS in UPSC notices), it returns nothing rather than filling it in from general knowledge.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::classifica.tech: Matches _GROUP_RX (Group + optional straight or curly quote + A/B). Returns '' with no match, 'Group A (Gazetted)' for A, and for B 'Group B (Non-Gazetted)' if the name contains 'non-gazetted', else 'Group B (Gazetted)'.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::header.text: Writes a comment block placed above the generated exam entry that states exactly which sources were read, what was found, what needs review, what the authority does not publish, what the tool failed to extract, and which posts were left out because no Group was printed.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::header.tech: Takes the record and a report dict (from verify.report). Lists rec.sources_read, report['found'], and when present needsReview, notPublished and notExtracted; re-runs _posts to list the skipped posts with instructions to add them by hand. Ends with a note that empty arrays mean unauthored, not zero. Returns the '/** ... */' string.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::render_exa.text: Produces the complete TypeScript entry for one exam (the shape the app's data file uses), from the record gathered from the authority's documents. Anything that could not be sourced is written as empty, so the app shows it as not yet authored instead of showing invented content.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::render_exa.tech: Assembles 'export const <CODE>_EXAM: Exam = {...}'. Fills id, code, title, authority, domain, crucialEligibilityDate (ageLimits.asOn), overviewDescription (_overview), vacanciesTotal, posts (_posts), dates (_dates), corrigendums, resources, applicationGuide, eligibilityHighlights, and admitCardDetails (NOT_YET_ANNOUNCED with the clause text and portal, only when admitCard is usable, else undefined). stages, syllabus, practiceQuestions, cutoffsHistory, faqs and roadmapTracks are emitted empty; officialLinks is just the authority's website; isGoldenJourney/isDemoData false.

tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::ts.text: Turns a piece of Python data (text, numbers, lists, dictionaries) into the equivalent TypeScript code text, so a gathered exam record can be written into the app's data file.
tools/exam_authoring/emit.py::ts.tech: Recursive serializer: None -> 'undefined', bools -> true/false, numbers via str(), strings single-quoted with backslashes and single quotes escaped and newlines replaced by spaces, lists/tuples -> '[...]', dicts -> '{ k: v, ... }' with unquoted keys; any other type is stringified then serialized.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::MONTHS.text: The list of the twelve English month names, used when reading dates written in words such as '24th May, 2026'.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::MONTHS.tech: Tuple-like list of full month names 'January'..'December' (from str.split). Also used to build _MONTH_RX, which accepts full names and three-letter abbreviations.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::_clean.text: Tidies a piece of text by collapsing all runs of spaces and line breaks into single spaces.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::_month_.text: Turns a month name such as 'February' or 'Feb' into its number (2). Returns 0 if it is not a month.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::_month_.tech: Compares the first three letters (case-insensitive) with MONTHS; returns 1-12 or 0.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::admit_c.text: Finds what the notice says about the admit card (the entry pass for the exam), preferring the proper heading over passing mentions, and picks up the download web address if one is clearly written. A garbled address, for example from a badly scanned page, is not offered as a link.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::admit_c.tech: Tries three regexes in priority order (the 'ISSUANCE OF E-ADMIT CARD' heading + 80-700 chars; 'e-Admit Card will be made available ...'; any 'admit card' sentence of 40-400 chars) across all pages. On the first hit returns Field.found('admitCard', {text (500 chars), portalUrl}); a URL whose host fails _WELL_FORMED_HOST becomes ''. Else not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::age_lim.text: Finds the age rule in a notice: the minimum and maximum age, the date age is counted on, and the birth-date range, with the page it came from.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::age_lim.tech: Per page, matches 'attained the age of NN years ... not have attained the age of NN years'.
