On the first hit, also searches the page for 'born not earlier than X and not later than Y' and, within 400 characters of the match, 'on the Nth of Month, 20xx' for asOn. Returns Field.found('ageLimits', {minAge, maxAge, asOn, bornNotEarlierThan, bornNotLaterThan}) with an excerpt, or not_extracted. Missing parts are ''.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::applica.text: Finds the web address where candidates apply online, as written in the notice.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::applica.tech: Per page, matches 'apply online ... <url>' (within 80 chars) or 'website <url>'; returns Field.found('applicationPortal', url with a trailing period removed) with a 'How to Apply' citation, or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::attempt.text: Finds the 'number of attempts' rule in a notice (how many times a candidate may sit the exam) and, where it is written as a number, reads the count.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::attempt.tech: Per page, takes 'number of attempts' plus up to 400 following characters; extracts a count from 'permitted <word> (N) attempts' or 'N attempts' (None if neither). Returns Field.found('attempts', {text (400 chars), count}) with a citation, or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::cite.text: Creates a citation saying which document, page and clause a fact was read from, with the quoted words and the date it was read.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::cite.tech: Returns Citation(document_title=title, url=doc.url, page, clause, excerpt=_clean(excerpt), verified_date=doc.fetched_at).

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::dates_f.text: A backup way to find dates when there is no table: it looks in the notice's running text for date labels and the date written just after them. Because prose is less reliable, everything found is marked as needing a person's review.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::dates_f.tech: For each page (pages_of) and each DATE_LABELS regex match, parses the first date in the 220 characters from the match start; de-duplicates on (kind, iso). Records type, nice label, dateTimeStr, page and rawValue (160 chars). Returns Field.needs_review('dates', ...) cited to the first hit's page, or Field.not_extracted when none.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::dates_f.text: Reads the exam's dates from a two-column table (label and date), such as UPSC's exam page. Each date is sorted into a known kind (notification, last date, exam date, admit card, result and so on) based on its label, and an unrecognised label is kept as 'other' rather than forced into a category.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::dates_f.tech: For each row with >= 2 cells, parses the joined value cells with parse_date; skips rows with no date. Classifies the label by the first matching DATE_LABELS regex (else 'OTHER', keeping the raw label), de-duplicates on (kind, iso), and records type, label, dateTimeStr (iso + parse_time), rawLabel, rawValue. Returns Field.found('dates', ...) cited to page 1 'Examination details table' with the first six rows as excerpt, or Field.not_extracted when none.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::documen.text: Joins the whole document into one tidy line of text and remembers where each page starts, so a clause that runs across a page break can be read whole and still be cited to the right page.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::documen.tech: Uses pages_of; returns (' '.join(pages), starts) where starts[i] is page i's offset in the joined string (each page length + 1 for the separator). Pair with page_at.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::exam_da.text: Collects the exam-day instructions the authority printed, such as reporting time, documents to carry, items that are allowed or banned, and rules inside the exam hall. Each item is one sentence copied from the document and sorted by type; nothing generic is added.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::exam_da.tech: Splits each page into sentences; keeps 20-600 char sentences not seen before that match one of the _EXAM_DAY_CUES (TIMING, DOCUMENTS, ITEMS_PROHIBITED, ITEMS_ALLOWED, CENTRE_INSTRUCTIONS), with isMandatory from _MANDATORY_RX. Stops at 20 items. Note: it returns as soon as a page has yielded any items, so only the first page with matches contributes. Returns Field.found('examDayChecklist', items) or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::excerpt.text: Cuts out a short quotation around a matched piece of text, to show as the source excerpt.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::excerpt.tech: Returns _clean(text[start:match.end() + width]) where start = max(0, match.start() - width//3); width defaults to 260.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::faqs.text: Reads question-and-answer pairs that the authority itself printed (for example 'Q1. ... ?' followed by the answer), word for word. It never writes or answers a question itself, and reports nothing found if the document has no such section.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::faqs.tech: On document_flat text, finds questions with _FAQ_QUESTION_RX ('Q1.', 'Question 3 -', or a bare '12.' not inside a number, ending in '?'). Each answer runs to the next question or structural boundary; the last answer to unit_end (skipped if None). Strips an 'Ans.' marker; drops answers under 5 chars or ending in '?'. Returns Field.found('faqs', up to 40 {id, question, answer, officialClause, page, excerpt}), or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::fee.text: Finds the application fee clause in a notice, the rupee amounts it mentions, and the groups it says are exempt from paying.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::fee.tech: Per page, matches a 'FEE:' heading with up to 700 chars, or 'fee of Rs/₹ N' with up to 500. Returns Field.found('fee', {text (600 chars), amounts (first 3, commas stripped), exemptions (text after 'except (' up to 'who are exempted' or ')')}), or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::how_to_.text: Copies the notice's 'How to Apply' section word for word, from its heading to its last sentence. This is what the practice application form is built from.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::how_to_.tech: On document_flat text, for each 'HOW TO APPLY' match takes up to unit_end(flat, m.start(), clauses=False); skips if there is no end or it is under 300 chars. Returns Field.found('howToApply', section) cited to the heading's page, or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::page_at.text: Works out which page a given position in the joined document text falls on.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::page_at.tech: Given the starts list from document_flat and a character offset, returns the 1-based index of the last page whose start <= offset (1 if none).

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::pages_o.text: Gives back each page of a document as one tidy line of text. PDFs often break a sentence across lines, so tidying first means a rule split over two lines can still be found, while keeping the page number for citing.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::pages_o.tech: Returns [_clean(p) for p in doc.pages], or [_clean(doc.text)] when the document has no pages (HTML).

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::parse_d.text: Finds the first date in a piece of text and writes it in the standard year-month-day form. It understands '27/02/2026', '24th May, 2026', 'the 1st of August, 2026' and 'February 4, 2026', accepts 1900s years (needed for birth dates), and never guesses a missing part.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::parse_d.tech: Strips 'of' in 'Nth of Month' via _OF_RX, then tries _DATE_PATTERNS in order (d/m/y numeric, d Month y, Month d y; years 19xx or 20xx). Returns 'YYYY-MM-DD' for the first pattern whose match has month 1-12 and day 1-31; otherwise tries the next pattern; returns None if nothing matches. Does not validate day-of-month against month length.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::parse_t.text: Reads a clock time such as '6:00pm' and writes it as '18:00:00'. If no time is printed, it gives midnight ('00:00:00').
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::parse_t.tech: Searches _TIME_RX for 'h:mm am/pm' or 'h am/pm'; adds 12 for pm (except 12 pm), maps 12 am to 0. Returns 'HH:MM:00', or '00:00:00' when no match. A time without am/pm is not matched.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::qualifi.text: Finds the required educational qualification in a notice. It looks for the 'Minimum Educational Qualification' heading so it reads the real rule and not a passing mention; if there is no heading, it falls back to a 'must hold a degree' sentence and marks it for review.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::qualifi.tech: On document_flat text, for each heading match takes the clause up to unit_end(flat, m.end()), skipping matches with no end or a clause under 80 chars; returns Field.found with the clause and a page_at citation. Fallback: the first 'must hold a Bachelor/Graduate/Degree' sentence bounded by sentence_end/next_structural_boundary, returned as needs_review. Else not_extracted. Relies on tools.exam_builder.units.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::scheme_.text: Reads the exam's paper list (for example 'Paper I ... 200 marks ... 2 hours') from the notice as the exam pattern. Because these rows are read from loose text, they are marked as needing a person's check.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::scheme_.tech: Per page, finds 'Paper <roman|digit> <name> <NN> marks [<N> hours/minutes]' matches and records {paper, name, marks, duration, page}, de-duplicated. Returns Field.needs_review('examPattern', first 20 rows) cited to the first row's page, or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::service.text: Reads the list of services or posts that a notice numbers with Roman numerals in brackets, such as '(i) Indian Administrative Service'. It takes the full text between numbers so names with qualifiers like '(Traffic)' are kept whole, and uses the page with the longest list.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::service.tech: Per page with >= 3 '(roman)' markers, takes each item as the text between consecutive markers (the last capped at 140 chars), cuts at a following sentence, and keeps items 6-160 chars long that start with a capital and do not start with an article. Keeps the page with the most items; returns Field.found('posts', items) if at least 3, else not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::vacanci.text: Finds the number of vacancies a notice states, such as 'approximately 933'.
tools/exam_authoring/extract.py::vacanci.tech: Per page, matches 'number of vacancies ... (approximately|about|is|be) N' within 160 non-period chars; returns Field.found('vacancies', digits as a string with commas removed) with an excerpt, or not_extracted.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Citation.text: A record of exactly where a fact came from: the document's title and web address, the page, the clause, the quoted words and the date GovOS read it.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Citation.tech: Dataclass: document_title, url, page=1, clause='', excerpt='', verified_date=''. Converted for the frontend by to_provenance.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Citation.text: Turns a citation into the 'provenance' format the app shows in its Evidence panel. The publication date is filled only when the document states one, so the day GovOS read a document is never shown as the day it was published.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Citation.tech: Returns a DataProvenance-shaped dict: id, documentTitle, officialUrl, pageNumber, clauseNumber (or 'Whole document'), publishedDate (only the 'published' argument, default ''), verifiedDate, verifiedBy text naming the pipeline and date, taxonomyType (default FACT), verificationLevel (default OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED) and excerptText truncated to 600 chars.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.text: Everything gathered for exactly one exam: its identity (id, code, title, authority, official website), all extracted facts, every web address read, and a log of notes for a person to look at.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, code, title, authority_name, official_domain, fields (dict name -> Field), sources_read (list of URLs), log (list of strings). Methods set/get/value/note/summary. verify.py checks it before emission.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.text: Looks up a fact in the exam record by name.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.tech: Returns fields.get(name), i.e. the Field or None.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.text: Adds a message to the record's log for a person to read.
Stores a fact in the exam record, replacing any earlier fact with the same name.
Gives a short report of the record: which facts were found, which the authority does not publish, which the tool could not extract, which need review, and which sources were read.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.tech: Groups field names by status; returns {examId, title, found, notPublished, notExtracted, needsReview (each sorted), sourcesRead}.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.text: Gives the value of a fact if it holds a usable value; otherwise gives a default.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::ExamReco.tech: Returns f.value when the field exists and f.usable, else default (None unless passed).

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.text: One extracted fact together with its standing: its name, its state (found, not published, not extracted, needs review), the value, where it came from, and a note explaining any gap.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.tech: Dataclass: name, status (Status), value=None, citation (Optional[Citation]), note=''. Exposes ok, usable and verification_level properties and the static constructors found, not_published, not_extracted and needs_review.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.fo.text: Creates a fact marked as found, with its value and source.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.fo.tech: Static constructor: Field(name, Status.FOUND, value, citation).

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ne.text: Creates a fact that was read but not confidently, so a person must confirm it. It is never shown as officially verified.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ne.tech: Static constructor: Field(name, Status.NEEDS_REVIEW, value, note, citation (optional)).

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.no.text: Creates a fact marked as 'our tool could not find this'. Its note names the document and warns not to assume the authority said nothing.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.no.tech: Static constructor: Field(name, Status.NOT_EXTRACTED) with a note 'No <what or name> pattern matched in <where> ... do not assume the authority is silent.'

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.no.text: Creates a fact marked as 'the authority does not publish this', with a note explaining why. It is meant only for cases where the authority's own listing shows the thing does not exist.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.no.tech: Static constructor: Field(name, Status.NOT_PUBLISHED, note=note); no value or citation.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ok.text: Says whether the fact was found with a source.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ok.tech: Property: True only when status is Status.FOUND.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.us.text: Says whether the fact holds a real value that can be written out, either found or awaiting review.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.us.tech: Property: True when status is FOUND or NEEDS_REVIEW and value is not None, '', [] or {}.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ve.text: Says how the fact should be badged in the app: officially verified if found, otherwise under verification.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Field.ve.tech: Property: 'OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED' for FOUND, 'UNDER_VERIFICATION' for every other status.

tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Status.text: The four possible states of an extracted fact: found with a source; not published by the authority; not extracted (the tool failed to find it, which says nothing about the authority); and needs review by a person.
tools/exam_authoring/record.py::Status.tech: str Enum with FOUND, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_EXTRACTED and NEEDS_REVIEW. NOT_EXTRACTED is a pipeline gap and must never be reported as NOT_PUBLISHED.

tools/exam_authoring/registry.py::resolv.text: Takes an exam name typed by a user and picks the reader for the authority that runs it. Today only UPSC is supported (it matches names such as 'civil services', 'CDS', 'NDA').
tools/exam_authoring/registry.py::resolv.tech: Strips the query and returns the adapter of the first AUTHORITIES pattern matching it case-insensitively (currently only UPSCAdapter), or None if nothing matches.

tools/exam_authoring/registry.py::suppor.text: Lists the authority readers this tool supports.
tools/exam_authoring/registry.py::suppor.tech: Returns the class names of the adapters in AUTHORITIES (currently ['UPSCAdapter']).

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::CACHE_D.text: The folder where downloaded authority documents are kept for a while so the same document need not be downloaded again. It is not part of the stored project and can be deleted at any time.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::CACHE_D.tech: Absolute path '<repo root>/.exam_cache', computed three directories up from this file; created on demand by _cache_path and fetch.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.text: One downloaded document from an authority (a PDF or a web page), holding its address, when it was read, its text (page by page for PDFs) and whether it is a scan with no readable text.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.tech: Dataclass: url, kind ('PDF'|'HTML'), fetched_at, raw bytes, pages (PDF per-page text), text (HTML stripped text), is_scanned. html_document also attaches a dynamic .html attribute. Methods page_text, page_count, find_page, all_text.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.text: Gives the whole document's text in one piece.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.tech: Returns self.text for HTML, else the pages joined with newlines.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.text: Finds the first page on which a given piece of text appears, so a fact can be cited to its page.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.tech: Compiles the regex (case-insensitive by default) and returns the 1-based index of the first page it matches, or None.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.text: Gives how many pages the document has.
Gives the text of one page, counting from page 1 as the document itself does.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::Documen.tech: Returns pages[page_number - 1] for a valid 1-based index, else ''.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::FetchEr.text: The error raised when a document could not be downloaded. It exists so a failed download is reported, never quietly treated as an empty document.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::FetchEr.tech: Subclass of RuntimeError with no extra behaviour; raised by fetch().

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::SOURCE_.text: The largest document size GovOS will download: 40 MB. A larger file is refused outright rather than read in part.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::SOURCE_.tech: 40 * 1024 * 1024; passed to fetch_checked as max_bytes. A truncated result raises FetchError in fetch().

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::SOURCE_.text: The longest a single download may take in total: 180 seconds, so a slow website cannot hold up a build.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::SOURCE_.tech: 180; passed to fetch_checked as max_seconds, on top of the per-operation _TIMEOUT of 45 s.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::_cache_.text: Works out the file name under which a downloaded document is cached.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::_cache_.tech: Ensures CACHE_DIR exists and returns CACHE_DIR/<first 20 hex chars of sha1(url)><suffix>.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::_encode.text: Makes a web address safe to request, for example by encoding spaces in file names that authorities often use, without changing addresses that are already encoded.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::_encode.tech: Returns url unchanged if it has no scheme; otherwise urlsplit, percent-quotes only the path (safe set keeps '/', '%' and common sub-delimiters) and recombines. May raise ValueError for malformed URLs (fetch converts it to FetchError).

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::_now.text: Gives today's date in year-month-day form.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::documen.text: Reads already-downloaded bytes as a PDF if they start with the PDF signature, otherwise as a web page.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::documen.tech: Returns pdf_document if data starts with b'%PDF-', else html_document. No network access.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::estate_.text: Works out the main registered web domain a site belongs to, so that, for example, 'otr.tgpsc.gov.in' and 'websitenew.tgpsc.gov.in' are both recognised as 'tgpsc.gov.in', the same authority's sites.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::estate_.tech: Lowercases, removes 'www.' and outer dots. If there are >= 3 labels and the last two are a known two-label suffix (gov.in, nic.in, ac.in, co.in, org.in, net.in, res.in, edu.in), returns the last three labels; else the last two (or the host itself if a single label).

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::fetch.text: Downloads a document from an authority's website safely, trying up to three times when the site is slow or flaky. It checks every redirect goes to a public address, verifies security certificates, limits size and time, and keeps a copy for 24 hours. If it still fails, it raises an error that says why instead of returning nothing.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::fetch.tech: Returns cached bytes when '.checked.bin'/.checked.json' exist and are younger than max_age_hours (default 24) and use_cache. Otherwise requests _encoded(url) via claude_cli.discovery.fetch_checked (timeout 45, max_bytes SOURCE_MAX_BYTES, max_seconds SOURCE_MAX_SECONDS, browser-like headers). A truncated body raises FetchError; success writes the cache and returns the body. Retries (sleeping 1.5 s, 3 s) only for TIMEOUT/NETWORK errors or HTTP >= 500; otherwise stops and raises FetchError with the last error. A malformed URL raises FetchError immediately.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_do.text: Turns a downloaded web page into plain text, while keeping the original page code so its links and tables can still be read.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_do.tech: Decodes UTF-8 with replacement, removes script/style blocks, strips tags, unescapes entities and collapses whitespace into text. Returns Document(kind='HTML') with a dynamic .html attribute holding the raw markup. No network access.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_li.text: Lists the links on a web page, as their visible text and full web address, keeping only those whose text or address matches a given pattern. Relative links are turned into full addresses as a browser would.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_li.tech: Regex-scans document.html for ..., reads href in double, single or unquoted form (allowing spaces around '='), skips '#', javascript:, mailto: and tel:, resolves relative hrefs with urljoin against document.url, keeps only http(s) results, and filters by pattern (case-insensitive) on label or href. Returns [(label, url with spaces as %20)] in page order.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_ro.text: Reads every table row on a web page as a list of cell texts, such as 'Last Date for Receipt of Applications | 27/02/2026 - 6:00pm'.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::html_ro.tech: Regex-scans document.html (default '') for <tr> blocks and their <td>/<th> cells; each cell is tag-stripped, unescaped and whitespace-collapsed; empty cells dropped; rows with no cells skipped. Returns list[list[str]].

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::load_do.text: Downloads a document and reads it as whatever it really is: a PDF if its contents say so, otherwise a web page, regardless of what its address suggests.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::load_ht.text: Downloads a web page and reads it as text.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::load_pd.text: Downloads a PDF and reads it page by page.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::load_pd.tech: pdf_document(url, fetch(url, **kw)); keyword arguments go to fetch.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::pdf_doc.text: Reads a PDF that has already been downloaded into text, page by page. Gibberish pages are treated as having no text, and a PDF with almost no readable text is marked as a scan, so GovOS says 'we could not read it' rather than 'it says nothing'.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::pdf_doc.tech: Uses pypdfium2: extracts each page's text through pdf_text (a page that errors becomes ''), blanks pages where unreadable_text is True, and sets is_scanned when total stripped text < max(200, 40 * page count). Returns Document(kind='PDF', fetched_at=_now(), raw, pages, is_scanned). No network access.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::pdf_tex.text: Repairs hyphens in text read from a PDF, where the PDF reader turned a line-ending hyphen into a strange invisible character.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::pdf_tex.tech: Replaces U+FFFE and the soft hyphen U+00AD with '-'.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::same_es.text: Checks whether a web host is the authority's own site or a sister site on the same registered domain.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::same_es.tech: Lowercases and strips 'www.' from both; False if either is empty; True if equal, if host ends with '.'+own, or if estate_of() matches.

tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::unreada.text: Detects a page whose text is gibberish, such as Hindi typed in an old non-standard font or a bad scan, by checking how many words have no vowels. Short pages and pages in other scripts are left alone.
tools/exam_authoring/sources.py::unreada.tech: Takes Latin words of 3+ letters that are not all caps; returns False if fewer than 40; otherwise True when more than 20% contain no vowel (a-e-i-o-u-y).

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::Isolatio.text: The error raised when an exam record contains something that does not belong to its own exam, such as a page read from another authority's site. It stops the record from being written.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::Isolatio.tech: Subclass of RuntimeError; raised by assert_single_authority and assert_ids_consistent.

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::assert_i.text: Checks that the exam's id has the right form and that it has a code and title, stopping with an error otherwise.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::assert_i.tech: Raises IsolationError if exam_id does not start with 'exam-' or if code or title is empty.

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::assert_s.text: Checks that every web address read for an exam belongs to that exam's own authority (including its sister sites on the same domain), and stops with an error if any came from somewhere else.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::assert_s.tech: Takes the netloc of rec.official_domain (without www.); raises IsolationError if empty. Collects sources_read URLs whose host fails sources.same_estate; raises IsolationError listing up to three of them if any.

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::foreign_.text: Looks for mentions of other exam bodies (such as SSC, IBPS or APPSC in a UPSC record) inside the extracted facts and lists them for a person to judge, without blocking anything, because a notice may legitimately mention another body.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::foreign_.tech: Chooses the token list by exam_id prefix (exam-upsc/ssc/ibps/appsc); returns [] for any other prefix. For each usable field, searches str(value) for each foreign token regex and returns '<field>: matches <regex>' strings.

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::report.text: Writes a plain account of what a run can and cannot claim: facts found, gaps, mentions of other exam bodies, sources that were scans, the share of facts sourced, and a warning when so little was found that the run itself probably failed.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::report.tech: Returns rec.summary() plus foreignMentions, unreadableSources (NEEDS_REVIEW fields whose note contains 'no text layer'), coverage '<FOUND>/<total> fields sourced', lowCoverage (FOUND < max(3, total // 3)) and log.

tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::run_all.text: Runs all the checks on an exam record (correct id, one authority only) and then produces the report. Any failed check stops the record from being written.
tools/exam_authoring/verify.py::run_all.tech: Calls assert_ids_consistent and assert_single_authority (either may raise IsolationError), then returns report(rec).

tools/exam_builder/__main__.py::main.text: The command-line entry for the exam builder: you type an exam's name and GovOS works out which authority runs it, finds that authority's documents for the exam, reads them and prints what it found field by field. It can save a snapshot of which documents were used so the build can be repeated, replay a saved snapshot, and write the full result to a JSON file. When the name fits two real authorities, it stops and asks you to name the authority instead of guessing.
tools/exam_builder/__main__.py::main.tech: Parses argv (exam, --year, --siblings, --json, --capture, --replay [path|LATEST]); errors if neither exam nor replay. Sibling names are expanded with discover.exam_aliases. --replay LATEST resolves the exam via resolve/stable_exam_id and manifest.latest_for (returns 5 if none). Calls build(...). Exit codes: AmbiguousAuthority -> prints verdict.summary(), 6; SearchUnavailable -> 2; LookupError -> 3; IsolationError from verify.run_all -> 4; success -> 0. Prints the authority, documents kept/rejected by kind, the contract coverage per GROUPS with status and page, sources changed since capture, saves the manifest with --capture, coverage and low-coverage warning, up to 12 log notes, and with --json writes examId, authority, documents, rejected, coverage and all fields.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_cycle.text: Picks out the exam year (such as 2026) from a piece of text, or uses a given fallback.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_cycle.tech: Returns the first 20xx match of _YEAR, else fallback.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_dated.text: Finds the date that a phrase like 'admit card available from' actually refers to. The date must come shortly after the phrase, in the same sentence, with no rival phrase in between, and (for a release) with a release word like 'from' or 'available'. It returns that date as a fact with quoted evidence, and notes when only a month was printed.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_dated.tech: Scans 'dates' (from read_dates) for the first d with d.start >= at and d.start - edge <= window (default _DATE_WINDOW 140; edge = measure_from or at). Requires _RELEASE_CUE in between when require_release_cue, no claimant via _owns, and no _SENTENCE_END in between when same_sentence. Builds evidence with pattern._evidence over a 240-char span; returns (Fact.needs_review, d) if the span is not verbatim, else (Fact.verified(d.iso, ev, confidence 0.9, or 0.7 with a month-precision note), d). Returns (None, None) if no date qualifies.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_is_po.text: Checks whether a web address is just a website's front door (no specific page or file), which means it is a login portal, not a download link.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_is_po.tech: True when urlsplit(url).path stripped of '/' is empty, or when urlsplit raises ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_list_.text: Checks a passage against a list of known phrases (for example login details or documents to carry) and returns each one the passage mentions, with quoted evidence.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_list_.tech: For each (label, pattern) in cues, on the first match builds evidence from a 220-char span with reading '<reading>: <label>'; appends Fact.verified(label, ev, 0.8) or Fact.needs_review when the span is not verbatim. Returns the list.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_near.text: Cuts out the stretch of text around a found phrase, to use as quoted evidence.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_near.tech: Returns text[max(0, at - width//2) : at + width].strip(); width defaults to 200. A verbatim slice.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_opera.text: Finds the exam date that a notice currently states. If the notice mentions two exam dates (an original and a rescheduled one), the date after words like 'however', 'postponed' or 'revised' is taken as the current one, and the earlier date is mentioned in a note rather than dropped.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_opera.tech: For each _EXAM_DATE_CUE match before the signature, calls _dated_fact with no release cue required, window _EXAM_DATE_WINDOW (34) measured from the cue's end, and the admit-card kind cues as claimants. Returns None if none; the single fact if all values agree; otherwise the first hit after a _SUPERSEDED_CUE (or the last hit) with a note listing the earlier dates as superseded.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_owns.text: Checks that no competing phrase (such as 'exam on') sits between a phrase and the date after it, which would mean the date belongs to that other phrase.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_owns.tech: Returns True when none of the 'claimants' regexes matches text[at:end].

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_rule_.text: Finds a release rule such as '2/3 days before the exam date' near an admit-card phrase and keeps it exactly as the authority wrote it. GovOS deliberately does not turn it into a date, because the exam date it counts back from can change.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_rule_.tech: Searches _RELATIVE_RULE in text[at:at+320]; returns None if absent. Drops a trailing half-word if the match was cut mid-word, cleans with _rule_text, builds evidence from a 240-char span. Returns Fact.needs_review if the span is not verbatim, else Fact.verified(phrase, confidence 0.8) with a note explaining it is not resolved into a date.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_rule_.text: Cleans up a rule such as '7 days before examination' so it ends where the authority's own sentence ends, rather than running into the next table cell's words.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_rule_.tech: Normalises whitespace, then cuts at the first _CELL_SEAM (lower-case/','/')' followed by whitespace and a capital) whose preceding word is not in _OPEN_ENDED (the, of, to, prior ...). Returns the text stripped of ' ,-'.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_urls_.text: Finds the web addresses in a passage and picks the first that is the authority's sign-in portal and the first that is a real download link, each with evidence.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::_urls_.tech: Iterates _URL matches, strips trailing '.,;)', classifies with classify_url (skipping ''), builds evidence, and keeps the first PORTAL (with a note that it is not a direct download) and the first DOWNLOAD. Returns (portal_fact, download_fact), either possibly None.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::classi.text: Says which kind of document a label names: a city or centre intimation, an exam intimation slip, or an admit card (also called call letter, hall ticket or admission certificate). City intimation is checked first so it is never confused with the admit card.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::classi.tech: Returns the AdmitCardNoticeKind of the first _KIND_CUES regex matching the label (CITY_INTIMATION, then EXAM_INTIMATION, then ADMIT_CARD), or None.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::classi.text: Decides how a web address may be shown: as a direct download, as a portal where candidates sign in, or not at all. An address on any site other than the authority's own is not offered as the place to get the admit card.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::classi.tech: Strips trailing '.,;'; returns '' unless it fully matches _URL. If authority_domain is given, the host (minus www.) must equal it or be a subdomain of it, else ''. Returns 'PORTAL' for a path-less URL (_is_portal_only) and 'DOWNLOAD' otherwise. Note: the domain check is exact-host/subdomain, not estate-based.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::descri.text: Summarises the admit-card events found, counted by type and by what they carry (stage, date, rule only, exam date, download link), for a build report.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::descri.tech: Returns {events, byKind, publishable (is_publishable), withStage, withDate, withRuleOnly, withExamDate, withDownloadUrl, rows: [{kind, label, stage, cycle, released, rule, examDate, status}]}.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::may_su.text: Decides whether a document's admit-card information actually belongs to this exam and cycle. A notice that only mentions the exam in passing supplies nothing unless its own title names it.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::may_su.tech: Delegates to pattern.may_supply_pattern(text, target) and returns its (bool, reason) tuple.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_n.text: Reads a written notice and lists every admit-card event it announces: city intimation, exam intimation slip or admit card, each with its release date or release rule, the stage it is for, the exam date (kept separate), any portal or download link, login details and documents to carry. Dates after the signature are ignored, and a release date that is really the exam date is thrown out.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_n.tech: Normalises headline + text; read_dates; drops dates after _SIGNATURE; computes exam_fact via _operative_exam_date. Scope: from 160 chars around each cue, else the headline's stage_scope, else a single stage named anywhere in the body (with a note). For each _KIND_CUES match before the signature: release via _dated_fact (window 60 from cue end, claimant _EXAM_DATE_CUE) else _rule_fact; skips if neither or if the release equals the exam date; de-duplicates on (kind, stage ref, value). Builds an AdmitCardNotice with id, cycle (_cycle_in), released_at/release_rule/exam_date/portal/download (NOT_EXTRACTED facts when absent), credentials (_CREDENTIAL_CUES) and documents (_DOCUMENT_CUES) from a 700-char passage; status VERIFIED unless no evidence is official verbatim, then NEEDS_REVIEW. Returns events sorted by release value.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_r.text: Reads one row of a table, such as 'e-Admit Card | 15/05/2026' or 'Download of call letters - Preliminary | August, 2026', into one admit-card event with its kind, stage, release date or rule. It refuses rows that are not about an admit card, and stops a value at its own cell so it doesn't run into the next row.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_r.tech: classify_label(label) or None. Document name is the matching kind-cue phrase. Cleans value with _rule_text, joins label+value, reads dates, gets a release via _dated_fact (no release cue needed); else _rule_fact; else a needs_review rule from _RELATIVE_RULE on the value; returns None if nothing. Scope from stage_scope(label). A caller-supplied portal_url becomes a needs_review portal fact (no domain guard). exam_date and download_url are NOT_EXTRACTED. Sets released_precision from the matching date; status NEEDS_REVIEW if no evidence is official verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_r.text: Reads every row of a table and keeps only the rows that are admit-card events.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::read_r.tech: Calls read_row for each (label, value) pair and returns the non-None events.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::source.text: Sorts a failure to read a source into network problem, unreadable file, or general fetch failure, for the build report. This is never shown to candidates as 'no admit card issued'.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::source.tech: Lower-cases str(error): timeout/DNS/refused/unreachable words -> SourceOutcome.NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE; 'no text', 'not a pdf', 'cannot decode', 'unreadable', 'empty document' -> SOURCE_UNREADABLE; else SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE. Returns (outcome, message).

tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::stage_.text: Works out which stage of the exam (for example Tier-I, Phase 2, Preliminary, Main or Interview) a piece of text refers to, so an admit card is tied to the right stage. If no stage is named, it applies to the whole exam.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card.py::stage_.tech: Tries _STAGE_CUES in order (Tier/Phase/Stage with a Roman or digit, including en-dash hyphens; Preliminary; Main; Interview). On the first match returns Scope with one STAGE ScopeRef labelled e.g. 'Tier-I' (or just the name when the captured word is the name itself), ref = _slug(label). Returns an empty Scope() if none.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: The result of merging admit-card events: the list of decisions made and the final list of events.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Holds decisions: list[EventDecision] and events: list[AdmitCardNotice]; methods of() and summary().
Initialises decisions and events to empty lists.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Lists the decisions of one kind, for example all the conflicts.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Returns decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Counts how many events were added, confirmed, superseded or conflicted.
A record of what the merge decided about one admit-card event (added, confirmed, superseded or conflicted) and why.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Plain class holding action (MergeAction), label, event_id, reason, superseded; has describe().

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Sets up a decision record with its action, label, event id, reason and the event it replaced, if any.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Stores action, label, event_id='', reason='', superseded='' as attributes.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Writes the decision as one readable line, such as 'SUPERSEDED: ADMIT_CARD ... · supersedes ... · reason'.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Joins '<action>: <label>', optional 'supersedes <id>', and optional reason with ' · '.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Adds the evidence of a matching event to the one being kept, so an event confirmed by two sources shows both.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Appends other's evidence whose (source_id, span_digest) is not already in keeper.evidence, and copies official_label if keeper has none. Mutates keeper.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Checks whether a newly read event says it replaces an existing one, either by naming it or by coming from a later-published document. Re-reading the same document does not count as a revision.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: True if incoming.supersedes == existing.id, or if both have evidence with published_at and incoming's latest published_at is later than existing's.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Gives the stage an admit-card event belongs to, in a form that can be compared.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Takes the first STAGE ref of event.scope and returns its ref (or label) lower-cased; '' when there is none.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Gives an event's release date, or its release rule if it has no date.
The four things that must all match for two admit-card events to count as the same event: the exam, the year or cycle, the kind of document, and the stage.

Combines newly read admit-card events with the ones a record already holds. A matching event with the same date confirms the existing one; one from a later document replaces it but the old one is kept; a new one is added; and two with the same identity but different dates and no stated replacement are both kept and flagged for a person to settle.
tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.tech: Starts from a copy of existing. For each incoming: NOT_EXTRACTED status -> CONFLICTED decision, not added. No same_event twin -> appended, ADDED. Same _value -> _absorb, CONFIRMED. _revises -> twin set NEEDS_REVIEW with a superseded note, event.supersedes = twin.id, appended, SUPERSEDED. Otherwise the event is set NEEDS_REVIEW with a conflict note, appended, CONFLICTED. Returns AdmitCardMergeReport with events set. Mutates existing event objects.

tools/exam_builder/admit_card_merge.py::.text: Checks whether two admit-card events are the same event (same exam, cycle, kind and stage).

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.text: One authority the evidence points to as possibly running the exam: its domain, name, score, the evidence for it, any sister sites merged into it, and the name words that set it apart from rivals.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.tech: Dataclass: domain, name, score, name_is_evidence=True, evidence, absorbed, distinguishing, plus a private _share (set by decide) exposed through the share property.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.text: This candidate's share of all the evidence, between 0 and 1.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.tech: Property returning _share (0.0 until decide() sets it).

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.text: The final answer about which authority runs an exam: the decision, the chosen authority if resolved, every candidate considered, and the reason.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.tech: Dataclass: decision, chosen (only for RESOLVED), candidates, reason, infrastructure_note, resolved (untyped ResolvedExam). Has is_ambiguous and summary().

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.text: Says whether the name matched more than one real authority.
Writes the verdict as readable text: the decision, the reason, and each candidate with its score, share, what sets it apart and which sites were merged into it.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Authori.tech: Returns lines: decision, reason, then per candidate domain/score/share/name (marked '<- chosen'), optional 'told apart by' and 'same body as' lines.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Decisio.text: The possible outcomes when working out which authority runs an exam: resolved, ambiguous (two real authorities fit the name), infrastructure failure (for example search unavailable), or unresolved.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::Decisio.tech: str Enum: RESOLVED, AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, UNRESOLVED.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::PLAUSIB.text: The minimum share of the evidence (25%) a candidate authority must have to count as a real contender rather than a stray mention. It can only drop faint candidates; it never chooses between two real ones.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::PLAUSIB.tech: Float 0.25, used by decide() to filter bodies by share.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_label.text: Gives the first part of a web address's host, such as 'upsc' from 'www.upsc.gov.in'.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_label.tech: Strips the scheme and path and 'www.', returns the first dot-separated label lower-cased.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_merge.text: Combines each authority's own sites into a single candidate, adding up their scores and evidence under the strongest one.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_merge.tech: Iterates candidates by descending score; merges each into the first existing body where same_body is true (adds score, appends domain to absorbed, extends unique evidence), else starts a new body. Returns the bodies; mutates the candidate objects.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_set_di.text: Works out, for each remaining authority, which name words it has that none of the others has.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::_set_di.tech: For each body sets distinguishing = sorted(identity_tokens(b) minus the union of the others' identity_tokens).

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::decide.text: Decides which authority runs an exam. Sister sites are merged, faint mentions are dropped, and if only one real authority remains it wins. If two or more real authorities remain, only the words in the exam name the user typed can pick one; a difference in search scores is never used. If the name does not tell them apart, the answer is 'ambiguous' and the user is asked to name the authority.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::decide.tech: No candidates -> UNRESOLVED. _merge, compute each body's share of the total non-negative score, sort by score, keep bodies with share >= PLAUSIBLE_SHARE (or the top one if none), _set_distinguishing. One plausible -> RESOLVED. Otherwise, bodies whose distinguishing words intersect name_tokens(exam_query): exactly one -> RESOLVED with a reason naming the words; else AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY with all candidates and a reason. candidates always lists every merged body.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::identit.text: Gives the distinguishing name words of a candidate, but only if the name was printed by the authority itself. A name GovOS pieced together from a web address or a third-party page is not used for reasoning.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::identit.tech: name_tokens(candidate.name) if candidate.name_is_evidence else an empty set.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::name_to.text: Picks out the words in an authority's name that could tell it apart from another, ignoring words almost every body shares such as 'Public', 'Service' and 'Commission'.
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::name_to.tech: Lower-cases, splits on non-letters, keeps words longer than 2 chars not in _SHARED_BODY_WORDS; returns a set.

tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::same_bo.text: Decides whether two candidates are really one authority (for example its regional office or its application portal) rather than two different authorities. They are one body if one printed name contains all of the other's distinctive words (at least two), or if one site's short name is the start of the other's (like 'upsc' and 'upsconline').
tools/exam_builder/ambiguity.py::same_bo.tech: True if both identity_tokens sets are non-empty, the smaller has >= 2 words and one set is a subset of the other; or if both host labels exist, the shorter is >= 3 chars and the longer starts with it. Else False.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::Extra.text: The result of reading an exam's application procedure: the procedure itself, the points where two sources disagreed, the sources that could not be read, and a log.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::Extra.tech: Dataclass: process (ApplicationProcess), conflicts (field names already set NEEDS_REVIEW), unreadable (URLs), log. Property infrastructure_failed.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::Extra.text: Says whether any source could not be read, which is a technical problem rather than a fact about the authority.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_amou.text: Finds every rupee amount in a sentence, whether written 'Rs. 200', 'INR 850' or the Indian style '120/-', with where each appears.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_amou.tech: Collects _AMOUNT matches containing a digit, then _AMOUNT_SLASH matches not within 8 chars of one already found. Returns [(amount_text, position)] sorted by position.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_clea.text: Tidies a field name by trimming punctuation and removing a leading 'the', 'your', 'a' and similar words.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_clea.tech: normalise_ws, strip ' ,.;:-', then remove a leading the/his/her/their/your/a/an (case-insensitive).

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_dedu.text: Merges fee rules that are exactly the same (because the same sentence was repeated), keeping all of their evidence.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_dedu.tech: Key = (str(scope), amount.value, is_exempt.value). A duplicate's amount, is_exempt and accepted_modes evidence is appended to the kept rule when its span_digest is new. Returns the unique rules in order.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_evid.text: Creates a piece of evidence from a quoted passage, but only if the passage really appears word for word in the document. If it doesn't, nothing is returned, so the value cannot be recorded.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_evid.tech: Builds evidence.Evidence(span, source_url, document_title, page or 1, reading) and calls verify(text); returns None unless VERIFIED, else SourceEvidence.from_evidence(ev, source=doc, source_id=doc.id) with section set.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_fee_.text: Says which fee a sentence names (application/processing fee, examination fee or total fee), choosing the one closest to the amount when a sentence names more than one.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_fee_.tech: Scores every _FEE_TYPES match by its distance to 'at' (0 when at < 0) and returns the closest kind ('APPLICATION_PROCESSING', 'EXAMINATION', 'TOTAL'), or ''.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_kind.text: Works out what kind of form input a sentence describes (an upload, a choice from a list, a date in a set format, or a tick box), only from the words the document uses.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_kind.tech: Returns 'UPLOAD', 'SELECT', 'DATE' or 'CHECKBOX' for the first matching _KIND_FROM_WORDING pattern, else ''.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_requ.text: Says whether a sentence makes something required ('must', 'shall'), optional ('may'), or doesn't say. 'Doesn't say' is kept as unknown rather than assumed.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_requ.tech: Returns False if _OPTIONAL matches (checked first), True if _REQUIRED matches, else None.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_same.text: Checks whether two values are the same, ignoring case, spaces and a trailing slash for text.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_same.tech: For two strings compares strip().rstrip('/').lower(); otherwise ==.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_sent.text: Splits text into sentences without breaking at abbreviations like 'Rs.', and also treats a clause number such as '10.2' as the start of a new piece, so each rule is read on its own.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_sent.tech: Normalises whitespace, inserts newlines before 'N.N ' clause numbers (after '.'/';' or before 'N.N Capital'), then splits on newlines or on '.'/';' followed by whitespace and a capital or '('. Returns non-empty parts.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_slug.text: Turns text into a short id-friendly form, such as 'online-registration'.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_slug.tech: Lower-cases, replaces runs of non [a-z0-9] with '-', strips dashes, truncates to limit (default 40); returns 'x' if empty.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::_stat.text: Picks out the rules a sentence actually prints about an input, such as a date format, a size limit, a range or 'in capital letters'.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::_stat.tech: Runs seven regexes (in ... format, in X format, dd/mm/yyyy, more/less than ..., between N ..., maximum of ..., in capital/block letters) and returns the first match of each, whitespace-normalised.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::exemp.text: Finds the first passage that states a fee exemption or waiver in words. This lets GovOS tell 'we couldn't structure the exemption' apart from 'the authority published none'.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::exemp.tech: Scans _EXEMPTION_WORDING matches (exempt/waive/remission/not required to pay/no fee payable with up to 200 chars either side within a line) and returns the first normalised passage that also contains 'fee'; else ''.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Reads one exam's whole application procedure (portal, steps and fees) from documents already confirmed to belong to that exam. Disagreements between documents are kept and flagged, unreadable documents are listed as a technical problem, and several unexplained amounts are held for review instead of one being picked as 'the fee'.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Assumes sources passed identity/officiality checks. No sources -> log note, process.note 'no source read'. Per (doc, text): empty text -> unreadable; else extract_portal, extract_stages, extract_fees (logged; extract_fees is called twice). portal = merge_facts (NEEDS_REVIEW -> conflict). Stages from the first document that has any; a later document with a different list of titles marks them all NEEDS_REVIEW, adds its evidence and records a 'stages' conflict. fees = _dedupe_fees; more than one global VERIFIED amount -> each set NEEDS_REVIEW with a note and a 'fee amount' conflict. Returns ExtractionOutcome.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Lists the documents a step asks the candidate to upload or submit, such as a certificate or photograph, only where the document says so. It notes when a document is needed only in some cases (for example 'if claiming relaxation') and ignores phrases like 'submit the form'.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: For each _DOCUMENT_CUE match (upload/attach/submit ... name): cleans the name; skips short, seen, _NOT_A_DOCUMENT names and names without a _DOCUMENT_NOUN; requires verified evidence. required = None when _CONDITIONAL matches, else _requiredness; specifications = _stated_constraints plus the conditional phrase. Returns list[RequiredDocument].

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Lists the groups the document says are exempt from paying the fee, each with the authority's own sentence as the condition.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: From extract_fees, takes rules with is_exempt True; the label is stated_group or str(scope), or 'All Candidates (No Fee)' for a global rule; de-duplicated. Returns dicts {category, isExempt, evidenceSpan, condition (same sentence), status VERIFIED|NEEDS_REVIEW, exemptedFeeType when known}.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Reads the fee rules from a document: the amounts, who they apply to, which groups are exempt, and the accepted ways to pay. Salary figures are not mistaken for fees. Only an explicit 'no fee' statement is recorded as 'no fee'; exemptions are recorded as stated, never added because they are common.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Per sentence that mentions fee/charge, or tells you to pay/remit/deposit with an amount; skips remuneration sentences without 'fee'. A _NO_FEE sentence yields FeeRule(amount=NOT_PUBLISHED, is_exempt=True). Exemption words + reservation categories yield one exempt FeeRule per category (fee type nearest the exemption word); otherwise an _EXEMPT_GROUP match yields an exempt rule for the authority's own group label. Amounts yield a FeeRule with the first amount, scoped to the first category only when the sentence is not an exemption, fee_type nearest the amount, and accepted_modes from _PAY_MODE (or NOT_EXTRACTED). All need verified evidence.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Lists the details a step asks the candidate to enter (for example 'enter your date of birth'), only where the document says so. Any format rule is taken only from what the sentence prints, never from what such a field usually needs.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: For each sentence of body and each _FIELD_CUE match (enter/fill/provide/select ... label), cleans the label, skips labels under 3 chars, already seen, or in sentences mentioning upload/scanned. Requires verified evidence. Builds ApplicationField(id, label, input_kind=_kind_from, required=_requiredness, constraints=_stated_constraints, help_text = sentence[:240]).

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Collects up to 12 rules and warnings printed for a step (sentences with words like 'must', 'shall', 'will be rejected', 'ensure'), each kept as its own sourced fact.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Keeps sentences matching the instruction cue regex with verified evidence as Fact.verified(sentence[:400], ev); returns at most 12.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Finds the payment methods (such as net banking, card, UPI or challan) stated in a sentence about paying the fee.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Returns Fact.verified(lower-cased unique modes, ev) for the first sentence with a _PAY_MODE match and 'fee'/'pay', and verified evidence; else Fact.not_extracted.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Collects the photograph and signature rules the authority actually printed (size, format, dimensions, background, glasses and so on). Nothing is filled in when the document says nothing.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Keeps sentences mentioning photo/signature/thumb that carry a size, format, dimension or appearance word and have verified evidence; files each under photograph and/or signature. Returns None if neither list has entries, else {hasOfficialGuidelines: True, photograph, signature, evidenceSpans}.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Finds the web address where candidates actually apply, taken from a sentence about applying. Addresses in sentences about results, syllabus and the like, or hidden in page code, are ignored, and an apply-specific address is preferred over the authority's front page.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Considers sentences mentioning apply/application/registration/submit, skipping _NOT_A_PORTAL and _IS_MARKUP sentences and URLs preceded by an attribute/quote character. A URL on authority_domain without /apply|/online|/registration ranks 0, others 1; the best (first highest) wins. Returns Fact.verified(url, ev) or Fact.not_extracted (none found, or its sentence not verified).

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Lists the documents and certificates an application needs, from the whole document, each with the sentence it came from.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: Runs extract_documents over the full text (stage_id 'app'), de-duplicates by lower-cased name, and returns dicts {id, name, required, specifications, evidenceSpan}. Note: required is True unless the document's required is exactly False, so conditional or unstated (None) requirements become True.

tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.text: Reads the steps of the application procedure in the order the document lists them, using the authority's own step titles. Each step must be quoted exactly from the document or it is dropped. Steps the authority did not title are flagged for review. For each step it also collects the fields to fill, documents to provide and instructions.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::extra.tech: For each candidate from stages.discover_stages(text), builds evidence (dropped if None). Status VERIFIED for EXPLICIT_MARKER, TABLE_ROW and HEADING structures, else NEEDS_REVIEW with an explanatory note. Fills fields (extract_fields), documents (extract_documents) and instructions (extract_instructions) from the candidate body. Renumbers order 1..n after drops. Returns list[ApplicationStage].

tools/exam_builder/application.py::merge.text: Combines what several sources say about one item. If they agree, the evidence is pooled; if official sources disagree, the item is kept with all versions and held back for a person to resolve, never decided by which source ranked higher.
tools/exam_builder/application.py::merge.tech: usable = VERIFIED facts with values. None usable: return the first NOT_PUBLISHED, else facts[0], else Fact.not_extracted(). All agree (_same_value): Fact.verified with all evidence, confidence min(1, 0.6 + 0.2 * n). Otherwise Fact.needs_review(first value, note listing all values, all evidence).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::Attri.text: The verdict on whether a value's quoted evidence really states what the field needs: passed or not, the role found, the reasons, and any fee-exemption groups found to be out of scope.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::Attri.tech: Dataclass: ok (bool), role='', reasons (list[str]), out_of_scope (exemption groups to set aside).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::DateV.text: The result of checking a list of dates: dates kept, dates thrown out with the reason, dates held for review because no event is named, and dates in conflict.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::DateV.tech: Dataclass: kept (list[dict]), dropped, unresolved, conflicts (each list[(item, reason)]).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::FIELD.text: The fields that have an evidence-role check: vacancies, qualification, fee, fee exemptions, posts and exam pattern.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_bad_.text: Checks whether something read as a post name is not really a job title, for example leftover web code, a serial number or single letter, a reservation-category heading, a footnote, or a whole sentence. Returns the reason, or nothing if it looks fine.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_bad_.tech: Returns a reason string for: HTML entities; no word of 3+ letters; all words in _CATEGORY_LABELS; starting with note/abbreviation/N.B./symbols; or a sentence (':' with > 8 words, or > 6 words with a finite verb like is/shall/will). Else ''.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_boun.text: Checks whether a number in a passage is really stated as the count of vacancies or posts (for example '12,256 vacancies' or 'Total: 563'), and not a serial number, a share of the total, one cell of a table row, or a count of something else such as '22 offices'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_boun.tech: Normalises the span; for each _number_forms occurrence (not part of a larger number): skips it if preceded by 'including/of which/among these' or followed by 'vacancies reserved'; True if directly followed by (optional bracket) 'vacanc*/post(s)'. Otherwise looks back 90 chars for the last count noun (vacanc*/total/post): every word between must be in _CONNECTORS, with no digit between, the number not followed by another figure, and the next word (if any) a connector; then True. Returns False if no occurrence qualifies.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_clau.text: Splits a sentence into its list items, such as 'a) ...', '(ii) ...', '10) ...'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_clau.tech: Cuts the sentence at each _ITEM marker position and returns the stripped non-empty pieces (the first piece is the lead-in before any marker).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_cue_.text: Lists the kinds of event (exam, result, application window and so on) that a piece of text mentions.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_cue_.tech: Returns {c.kind for c in dates.EVENT_CUES if c.matches(text)}.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_date.text: Gives a date's label and the text the date was read from.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_date.tech: For table-row items (has rawValue) returns (rawLabel, rawValue); otherwise (label, provenance.excerptText or label), all whitespace-normalised.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_date.text: Decides whether a date should be thrown out or held for review. It is thrown out if it is not a real date, falls outside the exam's cycle years, sits in a footnote, is a cited date (like 'dated ...', 'as on', 'born') rather than a scheduled event, or for a table row sits inside a long clause. It is held for review if a different event is named right before it or no event is named at all.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_date.tech: Returns ('drop'|'unresolved'|'', reason). Drops: invalid day; year outside cycle-1..cycle+2 (when cycle is digits); _FOOTNOTE label; a _REFERENCE_CUE within 70 chars before the located date with no _EVENT_WORD after it (not for NOTIFICATION); for rows, located after char 40 with > 25 words of surrounding prose. Unresolved: a row whose nearest preceding cue is not allowed for its type (_TYPE_CUES); or date_role(item) empty.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_exem.text: Lists the reservation-category groups that a fee or fee-exemption reading claims are exempt.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_exem.tech: For 'feeExemptions' (list) takes category of exempt items; for 'fee' (dict) takes the scope of exempt rules whose scope contains ':' plus exemptCategories. Returns unique groups that pass _is_reservation_group.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_is_r.text: Checks whether a group name is one of the standard reservation categories (such as SC, ST, OBC, EWS, PwBD, women), as opposed to free-text groups like 'unemployed candidates'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_is_r.tech: Takes the part after ':' and returns True if it fully matches application._CATEGORY.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_loca.text: Finds where a given date appears in a piece of text.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_loca.tech: Returns the first dates.read_dates hit whose iso equals the target, or that shares year-month and has non-DAY precision; else None.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_name.text: Checks whether a clause names a particular group of candidates, such as 'SC' or 'women'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_name.tech: Takes the part of group after ':' with '-' as space; True if it appears as a whole word in the clause (hyphens normalised), or if it equals one of the _CATEGORY words found in the clause.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_near.text: Finds which kind of event is mentioned closest before a date.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_near.tech: Over every EVENT_CUES anchor regex matched in the lower-cased prefix, returns the kind of the match ending furthest right; '' if none.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_numb.text: Lists the ways a number can be printed in a notice, such as '12,256', the Indian style '1,23,456', plain '12256', or with leading zeros like '05'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_numb.tech: Returns unique forms in order: international grouping f'{v:,}', Indian lakh grouping, plain str, and for v < 100 the 2- and 3-digit zero-padded forms.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_stat.text: Splits text into separate statements: sentences, and list items such as 'x) For recruitment to ...'.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_stat.tech: Splits normalised text on whitespace after '.'/';', then each sentence before list markers like '(a) ', 'iv) '; returns non-empty normalised pieces.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_vaca.text: Reads a vacancy value as a whole number, whether it is given as text with commas or inside a record.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_vaca.tech: Takes value['count'] for dicts; returns int(str(value) without commas) or None on TypeError/ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::_vali.text: Checks that a date is a real calendar date (so 31 February fails).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: The single entry point that runs the right evidence check for a field (vacancies, qualification, fees, posts or exam pattern), or nothing for fields without a check.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: Dispatches to check_vacancies, check_qualification, check_exemptions (fee/feeExemptions), check_posts or check_pattern; returns None for other field names.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks a list of dates and sorts them into kept, thrown out and held for review. If two different current dates are given for an event that should have only one date (notification, applications open, applications close), both are set aside as a conflict rather than picking one.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: Applies _date_problem to each item. Then, among kept items of _SINGLE_EVENT types that are not SUPERSEDED and not tentative, any type with more than one distinct day moves all such items to conflicts. Returns DateVerdict. source_text is unused.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks that every group claimed to be exempt from the fee is named in the clause that grants the exemption. Groups that were picked up from a neighbouring clause are set aside; the reading fails only if none of its groups is in scope.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: out = groups from _exempt_groups that fail exemption_in_scope. If any: Attribution(ok = len(out) < len(groups), 'exemption-scope', [reason], out_of_scope=out). Else Attribution(True, 'exemption-scope').

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks the paper list of an exam pattern: each paper's name must be a real name, not a scrap of a sentence or another paper's label, and its marks must not be printed jointly with another paper.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: Only for dicts with 'papers' (else Attribution(True, 'pattern-tree')). Flags rows whose name starts with a function word or contains 'there will/shall be', names that contain a paper/tier/stage/phase label, and labels followed in the excerpt by 'and/&/or <paper label>'. Any -> Attribution(False, 'unbound-paper', up to 4 reasons); else Attribution(True, 'paper-scheme').

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks that every post in a list is a real job title. If any are not, the whole list is held back with examples of what went wrong.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: Non-list -> Attribution(True, 'posts'). For each item uses postName/name (dict) or str; collects _bad_post_name failures. Any -> Attribution(False, 'not-designations', [summary of up to 4]); else Attribution(True, 'post-designations').

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks that the evidence for an educational qualification actually requires a qualification (a degree, diploma and so on), and is not instead a clause that relaxes an age limit, exempts someone, or disqualifies.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: Uses value['text'] (dict) or str(value); collects _statements of excerpt + text that mention an _EDUCATION term. None -> Attribution(False, 'no-qualification'). If every such statement fails (_REQUIRES or not _RELAXES) -> Attribution(False, 'relaxation-or-exception'). Else Attribution(True, 'qualification-requirement').

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.text: Checks that a vacancy number is actually stated as a vacancy count in its quoted evidence. If it isn't, the number is held back with an explanation.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::check.tech: _vacancy_value(value) None -> Attribution(True, 'unreadable-value'). If _bound_count(normalised excerpt, n) is False -> Attribution(False, 'unbound-number', [reason with the first 160 chars]); else Attribution(True, 'vacancy-count'). source_text is unused.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::date_.text: Works out what event a date is for, using only its own evidence: its assigned type, the event words in its label or text, or for a table row a label that names an exam stage.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::date_.tech: Returns item['type'] if not 'OTHER'. Else the alphabetically first cue kind found in the label (or, for non-row items, in the text); else 'EXAM' for a row label matching _STAGE_LABEL but not _NOT_A_STAGE; else ''.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::exemp.text: Checks whether the document grants a fee exemption to a given group in a clause that actually names that group, or in the list that clause introduces, rather than in a neighbouring item.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::exemp.tech: For each sentence (application._sentences) containing an exemption word, splits into _clauses; True if an exempting clause names the group, or if it is a lead-in ('following' or ending in ':'/'-') and any later clause in the sentence names the group. Else False.

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::model.text: Checks whether the event Claude names for a date agrees with the event GovOS's own reading of the evidence already established.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::model.tech: own = date_role(item); True if own is non-empty and role is in _FITS.get(own, {own}).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::resol.text: Decides whether Claude's suggestion of what event a date is for can be accepted. It is accepted only if Claude's quoted evidence contains the date and also contains words for that same kind of event.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::resol.tech: Calls verification.attribution_claude.validate_date(item, reply, source_text, need_role=None); on failure returns (False, why). Then requires the evidence_span's cue kinds to intersect _ROLE_CUES[reply['role']], or a stage label for role EXAM. Returns (bool, reason).

tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::witho.text: Gives back the fee reading with the out-of-scope exemption groups removed.
tools/exam_builder/attribution.py::witho.tech: For 'feeExemptions' filters items whose category is in groups (case-insensitive). Otherwise copies the dict, filters exempt rules by scope, rebuilds the 'exemptions' string from the remaining exempt rules, and filters exemptCategories.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: What one exam may take from a discovery run: the documents to send on to the reading pipeline, and how each official item relates to this exam (this exam, this exam but no year stated, another year, another exam, not this exam, or unidentifiable).
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, docs (DiscoveredDoc list), relation (node id -> relation string), matched, identified (THIS_EXAM ids), cycle_unstated, unidentifiable, mismatches (OTHER_EXAM entries), unlinked (listing id -> unlinked items naming this exam).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: One link found on a web page, with the words around it that say what it is: its own text, the table row or list label it sits in, the heading above it, and whether it is listed without a working address.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Dataclass: url, text, context (row, else list label, else heading), heading, unlinked (href '#' or empty), label, row (data-row text), table_heading.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: The kinds of document whose listing page, when it lists many items, counts as a 'repository' of that kind: question papers, answer keys, results, notifications, cut-offs, syllabus, corrigenda, admit cards and calendars.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: frozenset of DocKind: QUESTION_PAPER, ANSWER_KEY, RESULT, NOTIFICATION, CUTOFF, SYLLABUS, CORRIGENDUM, ADMIT_CARD, CALENDAR. Used by _read_page and _schedule.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Reads a web page's code and collects every link together with the heading, list label and table row it sits under. It is plain rule-based reading; Claude is never asked to read the page.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: html.parser.HTMLParser subclass tracking title, current heading (h1-h6/caption/legend), open <li> labels, open tables (heading in force) and open rows (text and link indices); skips script/style/noscript/template. Produces self.links (list[Link]) and self.title.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Sets up the page reader with the page's address (used to complete relative links) and empty lists for links, headings, list items and table rows.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Calls HTMLParser.__init__(convert_charrefs=True) and initialises base, links, title, heading, _in_title, _skip, _hbuf, _li, _a, _rows and _tables.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: When a link ends, records it with its full address and context. A link with no address becomes the list item's label; an item listed with no working address is kept as 'listed but not obtainable'; email, phone and script links are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Builds text and _browser_href(href). href None: may set the li label and return. Empty or '#' href: places an unlinked Link if the text sits in a labelled/linked li or a table row. Skips _SKIP_SCHEMES. Otherwise marks the li linked (setting its label from its buffer if missing) and places Link(url=urljoin(base, href), text, context, heading).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: When a table row ends, its text becomes the description of every link in it, so a link called just 'Addendum' is known to belong to the recruitment named in that row. Rows that are too long or carry too many links are page layout, not listings, and are ignored.
