tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Skips rows with no links, no text, > _ROW_MAX_CHARS (600) chars or > _ROW_MAX_LINKS (8) links. Otherwise sets each link's row = text[:300] and context = 'label · row' (when the label is not already in the row) or the row, capped at 400.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Gives the best available description of where a link sits: its list label, or else the section heading.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: self._label() or self.heading.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Gives the label of the list item currently being read, if any.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Returns the innermost li's label, or its collected buffer text; '' outside a list.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Adds a found link to the list, remembering its list label, the heading of its table, and the row it sits in so the row's text can describe it later.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Sets link.label and table_heading (innermost table), appends to self.links, and records its index in the innermost open row.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Collects text as it is read, adding it to whatever title, heading, row, link or list item is currently open.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Ignored while _skip; appends to title, _hbuf, the innermost row's buffer, the open anchor's buffer, or (when no anchor is open) the innermost unlabelled, unlinked li buffer.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Reacts to a closing page tag: finishes the heading, link, list item, row or table that was open.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Decrements _skip; clears _in_title; on heading end sets self.heading to the collected text if non-empty; on calls _close_anchor; pops li; on pops and _close_row; on pops _tables.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Reacts to an opening page tag: starts collecting a title, heading, list item, table, row, cell or link as appropriate, and ignores script and style blocks.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech:
Increments _skip for script/style/noscript/template; sets _in_title on title; opens _hbuf on headings; pushes a li dict; pushes the current heading on table; pushes a row on tr; appends a space to the row buffer on td/th; opens _a with its href on a; on
inside a li with no label, sets the label from the text so far.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Turns a link's address into the form a browser would actually request, removing tabs and line breaks and encoding spaces, so documents with spaces in their names are not wrongly refused.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Drops \t\n\r, strips, and percent-encodes with urllib.parse.quote keeping URL syntax characters and '%' (_URL_SAFE).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Gives the standard safe downloader used during discovery, with the run's time and size limits.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Returns lambda url: fetch_checked(url, timeout=limits.timeout_seconds, max_bytes=limits.max_content_bytes).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Picks out the words in a listing that could say which recruitment an item belongs to, ignoring generic words like 'download', 'notification', 'addendum', language names, numbers and single letters.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Filters resolve.id_words(text), dropping _THIN words, Roman numerals, tokens starting with a digit and single letters.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Checks whether a downloaded item is a web page rather than a file.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: True if the content_type contains 'html' or the first 600 chars of result.text contain '<html'.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Describes one found resource for display: its title, address, kind, which page section it belongs to, whether it is official, who runs it, whether it can be opened, where it was found, how it relates to the exam, whether its kind came from GovOS's rules or only from Claude, and any year, stage or paper it names.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Returns a dict: title, url, context, role, section (SECTION_FOR_ROLE), sourceLabel, sourceClass, status, owner, relationship, obtainable (not FETCH_FAILED/BLOCKED), foundOn/foundOnTitle (first parent), relation (from admission), roleFrom ('CLAUDE' via role_by_claude else 'RULES'), identity (non-empty cycle/stage/paper/session from identity_from_text), duplicateOf URL.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Guesses whether a link is a file (such as a notice) rather than a menu item: it is already known to be a file, or its title reads like a notice headline.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: True for NodeType.DOCUMENT; False for roles UNKNOWN, EXAM_PAGE, OFFICIAL_PORTAL and service roles; otherwise resource_roles.is_headline(child.title).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Tidies text by collapsing spaces and line breaks into single spaces.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: ' '.join((text or '').split()).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Checks whether a web host belongs to the authority's own sites.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: any(same_estate(host, e) for e in run.estates).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Fixes a page title that the site prints twice in a row, keeping just one copy.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: If the first half (or half+1) equals the rest after stripping, returns that half; else the title unchanged.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Reads one page during discovery: finds its links, decides whether the page is a listing (repository) of items, classifies each link (what kind of document it is and whether it is official), adds it to the source graph and schedules it to be fetched if appropriate. Site menu links repeated from the home page are ignored, and a page with no links is noted as possibly built by script.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: extract_links on the result text against final_url; records home-page link keys as chrome. Sets status READ, or READ_NO_LINKS with SCRIPT_RENDERED when it has no own links (a root with any links is READ). A non-root page with >= 3 items whose title/context/headings match REPOSITORY_WORDS (or whose role is a repository role) becomes REPOSITORY. Unlinked items are kept in listed_without_link. Each link: classify_link; out-of-scope (not repository, not hub/social/video) increments skipped_out_of_scope; node limit -> ITEM_BUDGET frontier entry; edge kind from parent class/repository/portal/archive; classify_source and source_ownership by the link's own address; adds node and edge; UNVERIFIED -> BLOCKED/REFUSED_ADDRESS; new nodes go to _schedule.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Decides whether and when a newly found link should be fetched. Only official links are fetched; videos, social accounts and login portals are only recorded. Repository items are fetched (one level past the depth limit at most), notice-like files are fetched later if budget remains, and off-site pages are not crawled except an archive one step from the authority's own page.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Returns early unless child is PRIMARY_OFFICIAL and not VIDEO/SOCIAL/PORTAL or a service role. From a repository: _skip DEPTH_LIMIT if depth > max_depth + 1, else queue (id, True). _looks_like_document -> later (id, True). Off-estate children are dropped unless the parent is on-estate and the title matches _OFF_ESTATE_REPOSITORY. Beyond max_depth: _skip DEPTH_LIMIT only for repository/UNKNOWN roles or repository words, else silently dropped. Otherwise queue (id, False).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Decides whether a registration or application service may be shown on one exam's page. It may if its listing names this exam and year, or if it is clearly the authority's general service for all recruitments: its own words or address make it that service, the site links to it as a service and not just as one entry in a list of recruitments, and its listing names no recruitment year.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: relation THIS_EXAM -> True; OTHER_EXAM or THIS_EXAM_OTHER_CYCLE -> False. False if classify_link on the node's own title/url gives a different role than node.role, or if every parent edge is REPOSITORY_ITEM. Otherwise True only when identity_from_text(title + context) finds no cycle.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Records that a page or file that should have been looked at was left unread, and why (for example the page limit was reached), so the report can say what was not checked.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: No-op if node.skipped is already set. Sets status SKIPPED_LIMIT and skipped = reason.value, and appends {url, title, role, skip, reason} to run.frontier.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Adds search-engine results to the source graph as 'found by search'. A result on the authority's own site counts as official because of where it is, not because it ranked well; anything else is classified by the trust rules and never crawled.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: For each hit (object or dict with url/title), classify_link, classify_source(via=DISCOVERED_BY_SEARCH), source_ownership; adds a depth-0 node with a DISCOVERED_BY_SEARCH edge from ''. UNVERIFIED nodes are BLOCKED. Loads TrustRegistry if none is passed.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Records a social-media post or news item as a lead only, never as a fact. A post saying 'hall ticket released' becomes 'look for an official admit-card notice'. A post on an account the authority's own site links to is marked as linked from the official site, but it is still not the authority's statement.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Returns None for empty url. Derives the account URL (first path segment); linked_account if that node exists with an official parent edge. classify_source with role DISCOVERY_SIGNAL; SECONDARY social -> DISCOVERY_ONLY; relationship INDEPENDENT upgraded to LINKED_FROM_OFFICIAL when linked. Adds a SOCIAL node and DISCOVERY_SIGNAL edge, and appends one UNCONFIRMED lead for the first matching _LEAD_PATTERNS role. Returns the node.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Decides which official items from the discovery run belong to one exam, judging each item by its own listing text and address, never by the page it sits on (which lists every exam). Items that name the exam but no year are kept separate from items that name this year. Items listed without a link that name the exam are recorded as 'listed but not obtainable'.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: For each PRIMARY_OFFICIAL node that is not a discovery signal, root, social, video, repository or duplicate: computes page specificity from non-repository parents (page_is_specific_to), runs discover.gate on title + context, reads the cycle with pyq.identity_from_text. Not rejected (with exam_words) -> THIS_EXAM_OTHER_CYCLE / THIS_EXAM_CYCLE_UNSTATED / THIS_EXAM by the cycle; else OTHER_EXAM if foreign words, NOT_THIS_EXAM if _identifying_words, else UNIDENTIFIABLE. THIS_EXAM ids go to identified; THIS_EXAM and CYCLE_UNSTATED nodes of _PIPELINE_KINDS become DiscoveredDoc entries. Also gates each listed_without_link item on official hubs into unlinked. Returns Admission.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Asks Claude, once per run, what kind of document each official link is when GovOS's own rules could not tell. Claude may only pick a kind from a fixed list; it never decides whether something is official and never adds links. If Claude is off or fails, the kind stays unknown, and any kind Claude assigns is marked as Claude's reading, not evidence.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Candidates: UNKNOWN-role PRIMARY_OFFICIAL nodes that are not SITE_ROOT/SOCIAL, capped at limits.max_claude_links. None -> run.claude status NOT_NEEDED; gateway disabled -> CLAUDE_DISABLED. Otherwise one gateway.run(Operation.CLASSIFY_SOURCE, {authority, links:[{index, text, context, path}]}). Failure -> status recorded and notes added. Success applies rows with a valid index and a DocKind other than UNKNOWN, setting role_reason = CLAUDE_ROLE_REASON (is_repository only adds a note). Records counts and templateVersion in run.claude.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Explores an authority's official website to map where its information lives: menus, lists of papers, results, keys and notifications, its application portals and its social accounts. It works through pages in order within fixed limits on pages, files and depth, records everything in a 'source graph' with how each item was found, and notes everything it could not read and why. It never follows pages off the authority's site except an archive one step away, and never treats something as official because a search engine or Claude said so.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Normalises roots, derives estates (estate_of) and creates a DiscoveryRun. Seeds each root as SITE_ROOT / OFFICIAL_PORTAL / PRIMARY_OFFICIAL. Breadth-first over queue (pages and repository items), then 'later' (loose documents). Enforces max_documents/max_pages with _skip; a failed fetch is recorded as FETCH_FAILED with a note and still charged to the budget; non-HTML results are hashed via record_content as documents; a page arriving where a file was expected after the page budget is spent is skipped; off-estate pages not named as archives are READ with LINKS_NOT_FOLLOWED; others go to _read_page. Afterwards adds search hits, social signals, optional classify_ambiguous with a gateway, resolve_leads, and sets ended_at. should_continue can cancel. fetch and registry are injectable.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Gives the words that identify this particular exam, leaving out the authority's own name or acronym, because that appears on every exam the authority runs.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Builds an identity.ExamIdentity probe to get authority_aliases, and returns resolve.exam_aliases(query, official_name) minus those aliases.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Reads all links from a page and the page's title. If the same address is linked twice (for example an icon and a text link), only the version with the most text is kept. Items listed without an address are added at the end.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Feeds _LinkParser (parse errors swallowed). De-duplicates linked entries by url_key keeping first-seen order and replacing with the longer-text copy (filling missing context/heading/label/row/table_heading from the earlier). Returns (deduped links + unlinked links, _once(normalised title)).

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Marks a fetched document as unreadable (for example a scan with no text), so it is not counted as read.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: If the node exists, sets status UNREADABLE and appends why or a default note.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Builds what one exam's page sections may show from a discovery run: the listings that hold this exam's items (or where its papers, keys, results or cut-offs would be, so 'none of these is yours' is itself the answer), its official portals, practical guidance, learning material, and a plain account of how thoroughly the site was searched.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Computes exam words (exam_words_for) and admission (admit_for_exam). Repositories: candidate-visible REPOSITORY nodes with their REPOSITORY_ITEM children as _item rows; kept if any row relates to this exam or the role is in _ANSWERING_REPOSITORIES, with counts and a note. Portals: PRIMARY_OFFICIAL OTR/APPLICATION/OFFICIAL_PORTAL nodes that are not documents, on estate, not staff-only, unique by title, and pass _serves_exam. Guidance: APPLICATION_GUIDE/EXAM_GUIDE that may_corroborate, labelled official or practical. Learning: is_learning roles that may_corroborate or are visible with an official parent. Returns examId, runId, authorityName, discoveredAt, repositories, portals, practicalGuidance, learning, searchStates, exhaustive and a coverage summary from coverage_report.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Marks each lead as confirmed only if an official source of that kind was actually found; otherwise it stays unconfirmed and is shown to nobody as a fact.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: For each run.leads entry, finds graph.of_role(role) nodes that are PRIMARY_OFFICIAL and not SOCIAL; sets state OFFICIAL_SOURCE_FOUND with up to 5 officialSources URLs, else UNCONFIRMED.

tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.text: Says how thoroughly the run searched for one kind of document (for example found, not found after a full search, or search incomplete), optionally for one exam.
tools/exam_builder/authority_discovery.p.tech: Wrapper over source_graph.role_search_state(run, role, identified=, unidentifiable=, unlinked=, relation=) taking those from the Admission when given; returns (SearchState, reason).

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: a plain 'About Us' page with no documents (also served as the Contact page).
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Fixture HTML: NAV + one paragraph.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: the invented commission's 'apply online' portal, on a sister site of its main domain.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture constant 'https://apply.epsc.gov.in/', linked from HOME.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: the name of the invented commission used in the discovery tests.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture constant 'Example Public Service Commission'.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: the invented commission's YouTube channel address.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture constant 'https://www.youtube.com/@epsc_official', linked from HOME.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: an address on a made-up coaching website linked from the old-papers page, used to check that someone else's site is never treated as official.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture constant 'https://coaching.example.com/epsc-papers'; served as COACHING_PAGE.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test data: the made-up coaching site's page listing three papers, which discovery must not treat as official.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Fixture HTML (no NAV) with three absolute links to coaching.example.com.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test helper: a pretend download result with the same fields discovery reads from a real one (success, status, address, content type, text, error, fingerprint).
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Dataclass mirroring the FetchResult fields used by authority discovery: ok=True, status=200, final_url, content_type='text/html', text, error, content_hash, truncated, hops.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Test helper: a pretend version of the invented commission's whole website that answers download requests from memory, without touching the internet, and keeps a list of every address requested.
tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.tech: Callable fetch stub. Holds pages (ROOT, notifications, old papers, syllabus, results, about, contact, COACHING, archive pages 2025..2016, plus 'extra'), a failing set (default LEGACY_PDF) and calls.

tools/exam_builder/authority_fixture_sit.text: Answers one pretend download request: a failure for addresses set to fail, the page for known pages, a pretend PDF for addresses ending in .pdf (two particular addresses give the same file), and 'not found' for anything else.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::BuildResult.text: Everything one exam build produced: the authority found, the documents found and rejected, what the build covered, the exam record, notes, whether the build finished, what each document says it is about, the snapshot of sources used, which sources changed, and the completeness check.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::BuildResult.tech: Dataclass: resolved (ResolvedExam), sources (SourceSet), coverage, record (ExamRecord), notes, build_state (default COMPLETE), identity (url -> IdentityCheck), manifest, changed_sources, completeness, reacquisition_attempts, searched_not_found, authority_run.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::NoClaude.text: A stand-in for the Claude connection that is always switched off, so every step of a build takes its non-AI, rule-based path.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::NoClaude.tech: Gateway stub with name 'none' and is_enabled() returning False.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::NoClaude.is.text: Always says Claude is not available.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_amending_n.text: Checks whether a given document is a correction notice amending the schedule, and if it prints exactly one 'Dated:' line for itself, gives that date.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_amending_n.tech: Finds the DiscoveredDoc with that url in sources.docs; returns (False, '') unless its kind is CORRIGENDUM. Reads all_text from loaded and matches _DATELINE (a line 'Dated: dd.mm.yyyy'); exactly one -> (True, 'YYYY-MM-DD'), else (True, '').

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_build.text: The full exam-building pipeline. It works out the exam and its authority (or uses a saved document list), finds the official documents, reads up to a limit of them with the most specific first, checks each one really belongs to this exam (keeping only this exam's rows from listing pages), then reads every fact the contract asks for. Missing facts trigger targeted searches on the authority's site and a re-read. Finally it records official sources, vacancy breakdowns and date revisions, runs consistency checks, and scores how complete each of the 17 sections is.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_build.tech: Replay: builds ResolvedExam from the manifest and to_source_set; else resolve(), stable_exam_id, optional authority_discovery(resolved), discover(). Creates ExamRecord; loads _load_order(docs)[:max_docs] (FetchError -> infrastructure failure), _reclassify_from_content, content hashes and changed-since-manifest notes; coverage_from(kinds). Builds ExamIdentity (designation mode -> _establish_designation), runs _identify per doc with _listing_entry fallback; MISMATCH docs are removed from loaded. Sets officialName/authority, then per CONTRACT field: skip INTRINSIC, NO_SOURCE -> not_extracted (infra failure) or not_published('No document of kind ...'), else _dispatch_domain_extraction. If not replay and no infra failure, _targeted_reacquire for unpopulated fields (cap = their count) and re-dispatch fields now covered. Then record_official_sources, record_vacancy_breakups, record_date_revisions, enforce_semantic_states, searched_not_found, evaluate_completeness, and returns BuildResult with build_state PAUSED_INFRASTRUCTURE or COMPLETE plus manifest snapshot.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_dispatch_d.text: Reads one fact of the exam and then runs the general quality checks that apply to it: fixing page numbers, checking posts, splitting the fee into its named parts, checking dates, checking that the quote really states this fact, and checking that quoted text is not cut off mid-sentence.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_dispatch_d.tech: Calls _dispatch_domain_extraction_raw, then _place_citation_page and _place_row_pages. For 'posts' applies _vet_posts; for 'fee' _type_fee_components; for 'dates' returns _vet_dates(cycle=resolved.year). All other fields (and posts/fee) then pass through _vet_attribution and _vet_completeness, whose result is returned.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_dispatch_d.text: The main reading switchboard: for one fact of the exam (dates, pattern, syllabus, posts, vacancies, age limits, qualification, past papers, answer keys, admit card, results, corrigenda, portal, how to apply, fee, fee exemptions, documents, photo rules, FAQs, next steps) it sends the right documents to the right specialised reader. It first tries a meaning-based reading, then the specialised reader, then older fallback readers. When nothing can be read it records why in honest terms: GovOS's own gap versus the authority genuinely publishing nothing.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_dispatch_d.tech: Restricts to identity-matched docs via _facts_view and to docs whose kind is in cf.sources. Step 1: _semantic_read (skipped for ageLimits), returned if ok and _states_something. Step 2: per-field branches, e.g. dates (X.dates_from_rows on HTML tables with any non-OTHER type, else D_DATES.extract_milestones per doc + reconcile + COMPAT.important_dates, else X.dates_from_notice); examPattern (HTML table heuristic, else D_PATTERN.extract_pattern + _place_tree_pages + COMPAT.pattern_tree, NEEDS_REVIEW without a VERIFIED stage); syllabus (extract_syllabus + syllabus_tree); posts (HTML table, else extract_posts with post_code_clauses/post_scoped_sentences, held name-only rows noted); vacancies (HTML column sum, printed_vacancy_total, else extract_vacancies with NEEDS_REVIEW for several figures); ageLimits (single band or NEEDS_REVIEW for post-scoped minima/maxima, with _printed_relaxations); results (every result doc's declarations collected); feeExemptions/requiredDocuments/photoSignatureGuidelines fall back to exemption wording, _unread_by_us, _missed_by_us, then not_published; faqs fall back to clauses.procedure_clauses from MATCH notifications; nextSteps combines results.admission_rules with derive_next_steps. Most branches fall back to the legacy extractor named by cf.extractor; reader exceptions are logged as '<reader> failed on <url>'. Final fallback: Field.not_extracted.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_establish_.text: Some exams have no distinctive name of their own (for example a generic post title), so GovOS has to learn the exact name the recruitment goes by from the authority's own notification. This step looks only at notification documents on the authority's own website and tries to find that exact official name, optionally with Claude's help. If no single official name can be established, the exam is left without one and no document can later be confirmed as belonging to it.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_establish_.tech: Designation-mode only. Builds the wanted designation with designation.query_designation; if None, notes it and returns the target unchanged. Collects (url, text) for loaded docs of kind NOTIFICATION on the authority's estate (same_estate), noting off-estate ones, then calls designation.establish_canonical with a Claude extractor (verification.designation_claude.extract_designation via the run gateway) and claude_enabled flag. Notes every message; returns dataclasses.replace(target, designation=canonical) on success, else the original target.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_extract_ht.text: Pulls tables out of a web page as plain rows and cells of text, dropping the page's formatting.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_extract_ht.tech: Regex-based: finds each <table>, each <tr> within it and each <td>/<th> cell, strips tags and collapses whitespace, drops empty cells and empty rows, and returns a list of tables, each a list of rows of strings. Tables with no rows are omitted. No handling of nested tables, colspan or rowspan.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_facts_view.text: Chooses which documents a fact may be taken from. Facts about this exam come only from documents confirmed to be about this exam; authority-wide facts (the application portal, how to apply, photo rules, exam-day instructions, FAQs) may also come from general pages that name no exam.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_facts_view.tech: Returns all of loaded when identity is None or field_name is in _AUTHORITY_WIDE; otherwise a dict of only the loaded docs whose identity verdict is MATCH.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_identify.text: Decides whether a document really is about this exam. Normally it uses GovOS's ordinary name-matching check. For exams identified by their official designation, a positive match is also put to Claude, which may only veto the match (say the document is about a different recruitment), never create one; if Claude is off, unreachable or gives an unusable answer, the decision falls back or is withheld.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_identify.tech: Returns identity.verify_identity(text, target, ...) unchanged unless target.designation_mode, a designation exists and the verdict is MATCH. Then, if the gateway is disabled, appends a reason and returns the MATCH. Otherwise calls designation_claude.confirm_same_recruitment on the first TITLE_BLOCK_CHARS of normalised text; non-OK infra, an unusable reply (validate_confirmation returns None) or a 'different recruitment' answer each yield an AMBIGUOUS IdentityCheck with the reason; a confirmed answer appends the quoted span to reasons and keeps MATCH.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_listing_en.text: Commission websites often list dozens of recruitments on one page. This picks out only the rows of such a page that name this exam, so facts are taken from this exam's own row and not from the other recruitments listed beside it.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_listing_en.tech: For an HTML document only: collects html_rows plus every <option> text (drop-down entries), keeps rows whose ' | '-joined text verify_identity judges MATCH. Returns None if no row matches or every row matches (not a listing). Otherwise returns a new exam_authoring Document with the same url/raw/fetched_at, text = the matching rows joined by newlines, and html set to '' so table readers do not treat the row as a label/value table.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_load.text: Downloads a discovered document in a form the readers can use: as a PDF if it is known to be one, otherwise by looking at the file's contents to see what it is.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_load.tech: load_pdf(doc.url) if doc.is_pdf else load_document(doc.url) (which sniffs the PDF magic bytes).

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_load_order.text: Orders discovered documents so the ones most clearly about this exam are read first: those naming more of the exam's names, then those found directly, then those of a known kind.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_load_order.tech: Stable sort by (-specificity where multi-word matched aliases count 2 and others 1, DIRECT before others, known kind before UNKNOWN).

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_missed_by_.text: If a readable document clearly talks about something (like photo and signature rules or documents to upload) but GovOS's reader could not pull out the details, this records it as GovOS's own gap, quoting the sentence, instead of claiming the authority published nothing.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_missed_by_.tech: Searches each candidate document's all_text() with the given regex; on the first match returns Field(status=NOT_EXTRACTED) whose note names the document, quotes up to 200 chars of the matched wording and says it is a gap here. Returns None when no document matches.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_page_of.text: Works out which page of a document a quoted passage appears on, so a citation can name the page. If it cannot find it, it says page 1.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_page_of.tech: Takes the first 60 chars of the whitespace-normalised span and returns the 1-based index of the first entry in document.pages whose normalised text contains it; returns 1 when there are no pages, the needle is empty or nothing matches.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_cita.text: If a fact's citation says page 1 (often just a default), this checks the actual document and moves the citation to the real page, but only when the quoted words appear on exactly one page. It does the same for individual items in a list that carry their own quote.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_cita.tech: Acts only when the Field's citation has a url and page in (None, 1) and the loaded document has >= 2 pages. Sets cite.page when _span_pages(excerpt) has exactly one hit; for list values, each dict item with an 'evidenceSpan' and no 'page' gets 'page' set on a unique hit. Mutates and returns the same Field.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_row_.text: Each date row in the timeline carries its own source quote, but the date reader labels them all page 1. This moves each row's page to the page where its quote is actually printed, when that page is unambiguous.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_row_.tech: For a Field with a list value: for each dict item whose 'provenance' has pageNumber in (None, 1) and an excerptText, looks up the loaded document by provenance.officialUrl (must have >= 2 pages, normalised pages cached per url) and sets pageNumber when _span_pages finds exactly one page. Mutates and returns the Field.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_tree.text: The exam-pattern and syllabus readers treat a PDF as one long text, so every piece of evidence they produce says page 1. This puts each piece of evidence back on the page it is actually printed on, using the document's real pages, and handles headings that are printed on more than one page by preferring the page where the rest of that item sits.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_place_tree.tech: Needs a document with >= 2 pages, else None. Walks the node tree (node.evidence plus evidence of any schema Fact fields) in document order, recording each evidence's owning node and each node's descendant evidence range. Candidates come from _span_pages on the full span or its first 80 chars. Unique hits set ev.page and advance a cursor; multi-page hits take the most common unique page among the same node's subtree, else the first page >= cursor, else max(cands); no hit leaves the page. Mutates evidence in place and returns the first placed page, or None if no span is uniquely placed.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_post_item.text: Turns one post read from a notice's table into the shape the exam record stores: its name, department, pay, vacancies, age band, qualification, physical and other conditions, plus the quote and page it came from.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_post_item.tech: Builds {id, postName, classification, department, payLevel} from the post's Facts (empty strings when absent), plus postCode, vacancies (only if exactly one count has a value), minAge/maxAge parsed from an 'NN-NN' or 'NN to NN' age band, qualification (first requirement), physicalRequirements / conditions split on other_requirements' note == 'physical requirement', evidenceSpan and page (_page_of) from the first evidence, and status NEEDS_REVIEW when the post's status is NEEDS_REVIEW.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_post_name.text: Gets the name of a post from an item, whether it is stored as a record or as plain text.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_post_name.tech: For a dict returns stripped postName or name (or ''); otherwise returns str(item) stripped, '' for None.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_printed_am.text: Formats a fee amount the way the notice printed it, for example 100 rather than 100.0.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_printed_am.tech: Converts to float; returns str(int) for whole numbers, repr(float) otherwise (12.50 becomes '12.5'), and str(value) unchanged if it is not numeric.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_printed_re.text: Collects the age relaxations a notice prints (for example extra years allowed for certain categories), each with its figure and the exact quote. A plain figure is marked verified; a figure with conditions, or a relaxation described only in words, is kept but marked for review. Nothing is filled in from general national rules.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_printed_re.tech: Iterates age rules' relaxations, skipping NOT_PUBLISHED years and any without evidence; de-duplicates on (category, years, maximum, post ids). Emits dicts {category, status VERIFIED|NEEDS_REVIEW, evidenceSpan, years?, maximumAge?, condition?, appliesToPostId?}; VERIFIED only when the governing Fact is VERIFIED and a figure exists. A rule with no figure gets condition 'stated in words without a figure: ...'. appliesToPostId is set only when the rule scopes exactly one POST.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_reclassify.text: If a document's link said nothing about what kind of document it is, works out its kind from its own opening text (for example a file starting 'NOTIFICATION NO. 02/2024') and notes the change.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_reclassify.tech: Only when doc.kind is UNKNOWN: classify_kind on the first 600 normalised chars of document.all_text(); if not UNKNOWN, sets doc.kind and logs a record note. Mutates doc.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_run_gatewa.text: Picks which Claude connection a build step should use: the one passed in, else the one set for this build run (which may be the switched-off stand-in), else the app-wide one.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_run_gatewa.tech: Returns explicit if not None; else _RUN_GATEWAY.get() (a contextvar) if set; else tools.claude_cli.get_gateway().

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_semantic_r.text: Tries every loaded document to read one particular fact (such as a fee or a date) by its meaning rather than by a fixed layout, and keeps the best-supported reading. If the reading is strong it is marked found; if it is weaker it is kept but flagged for a person to check. A document that mentions several exams can only supply the fact if the exact passage names this exam.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_semantic_r.tech: Returns None if field_name is not in semantic.SPEC_BY_NAME. For each loaded doc with text calls semantic.extract(field_name, text, source_url, document_title, page_of=_page_of); for docs whose identity verdict is AMBIGUOUS, skips (with a note) unless field_is_attributable(text, target, span). Keeps the highest-confidence result. Builds a Citation (clause 'Read semantically (<field>)') and returns Field.found when confidence >= 0.66 and evidence status VERIFIED, else Field.needs_review naming how many cues fired.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_span_pages.text: Lists every page of a document on which a given passage is printed, ignoring spacing and punctuation. Passages too short to place reliably are not placed at all.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_span_pages.tech: Lower-cases the span and strips everything but a-z0-9; if fewer than 8 chars remain returns []. Otherwise returns the 1-based indexes of norm_pages (pages already normalised the same way) that contain it.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_states_som.text: Checks that a meaning-based reading actually contains the substance of the fact, not just a nearby sentence. For the exam pattern, it must name at least one paper.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_states_som.tech: Returns bool(value.get('papers')) for field 'examPattern' with a dict value; True for every other field or shape. Used to reject a semantic examPattern reading so the scheme reader can run.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_targeted_r.text: When some facts are still missing after the first read, GovOS runs a small number of targeted web searches restricted to the authority's own website (for example 'syllabus scheme of examination' plus the site), loads any new official documents it finds, checks they are about this exam, and adds them to the pile to read. It stops if the search or network fails and records that as an infrastructure problem.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_targeted_r.tech: Returns 0 immediately if discover._search_for_missing_kinds is the 'no_search' stub. For each unpopulated field with an entry in _REACQUISITION_KEYWORDS (up to max_queries), queries '<official name> <keywords> <host>' via search_fn or search.search (max_results=5), appending to queried. SearchUnavailable or any other exception sets sources.infrastructure_failed/note and returns. Each unseen hit on the same estate is classified (classify_kind, else the expected kind), loaded (_load; FetchError marks infrastructure failure and continues), skipped if its content hash duplicates one already read, identity-checked with _identify (MISMATCH -> sources.rejected), else added to loaded, hashes, sources.docs and rec.sources_read. Returns the number of searches issued. Mutates all passed collections.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_today.text: Gives today's date in year-month-day form.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_type_fee_c.text: Some notices charge two fees with two names, such as an application processing fee and an examination fee. This reads the cited document again to find each amount the notice itself names as a particular fee type, and adds them to the fee record with their own quotes. Nothing is added up, and unrelated amounts (like pay scales) are not mistaken for fees.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_type_fee_c.tech: For a usable dict-valued fee Field with a citation and readable text, runs D_APPLICATION.extract_fees on the cited document (exceptions are noted and the field returned unchanged). Keeps rules with a fee_type, a VERIFIED amount with evidence and global scope, de-duplicated on (fee_type, amount), as {feeType, label (from _FEE_TYPE_LABEL), amount, currency (default INR), evidenceSpan}. If any, returns a new fee Field with value plus 'components' and notes them; else the original.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_unread_by_.text: When no document offered for a fact had any readable text (for example scanned images), this records the fact as 'GovOS could not read it' rather than letting it look like the authority never published it.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_unread_by_.tech: Returns None if any doc in docs has a loaded document whose all_text() is non-blank. Otherwise returns Field(status=NOT_EXTRACTED) with a note: either that N documents had no text layer, or (when docs is empty) that no document established as this exam's own was available; both say it is a gap, not a statement the authority published none.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_attrib.text: Matching the exam's name is not enough: this checks that the quote behind a fact actually states that fact for this exam. It runs a fixed rule check first; for fee exemptions it drops category groups that the granting clause does not name. If Claude is enabled it is asked to judge the quote's role too, and can only hold a fact back. A fact that fails is held for a person, not published.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_attrib.tech: Only for attribution.FIELDS fields that are FOUND, usable, cited, with readable source text. ATT.check(field, value, excerpt, text) -> verdict (None means no rule; returns unchanged). out_of_scope groups are removed via ATT.without_groups (feeExemptions left empty -> needs_review); otherwise not verdict.ok -> needs_review. Then, with the gateway enabled, attribution_claude.classify on ~600 chars of context either side; non-OK infra or a failed validate -> needs_review; success is noted and the field returned.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_comple.text: Makes sure quoted pieces of text (a qualification, an application step, an exam-day rule, a syllabus entry) are complete, not cut off in the middle of a word or sentence. A cut quote holds the whole fact back for a person to review. If Claude is enabled it is also asked whether each quote is whole; it can only hold a fact back, never add text.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_comple.tech: Only for units.UNIT_FIELDS fields with status FOUND, a usable value, a citation and a readable cited document. For 'syllabus' uses units.syllabus_problems; for others units.check_value on each (label, quoted) from units_of, and any cut unit -> Field.needs_review (noted). If deterministic checks pass and the gateway is enabled, each unit is sent with ~400 chars of surrounding context to verification.completeness_claude.classify; a non-OK infra or a failing validate holds the field. Otherwise returns the field unchanged, noting Claude's confirmation.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_dates.text: Checks every date read for an exam: each date must be clearly tied to a named event of this recruitment. Dates that are clearly not events (another cycle's, a document reference, a footnote) are set aside; dates with no clear event, a different event, or competing with another date for the same event are held for a person. With Claude enabled, each surviving date is also put to Claude, which can hold it back or, for a date with no named event, give it one only if the quoted words support it.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_dates.tech: Only for FOUND list-valued dates. Runs attribution.check_dates over the items and the joined source texts (per-item provenance url, else the field citation) for the cycle, giving kept / dropped / unresolved / conflicts. With the gateway enabled: classify_date + validate_date (need_role via ATT.model_role_fits) on every kept item; held items whose reason is not rival/conflict/infra and that have no role get a second classify_date and ATT.resolve_with_model_reply. Dropped items are noted. Any held -> Field.needs_review with kept + held items; nothing kept -> needs_review []; otherwise a FOUND field of the kept items (or the original if unchanged).

tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_posts.text: A list of documents to bring (like 'Hall Ticket' or 'Caste Certificate') can look just like a list of posts. This checks any list read as posts, using the item names and the instructions printed just before them. If they are really documents, or cannot be told apart, the list is held for a person to review instead of being published as posts; stray document names in a real post list are removed.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::_vet_posts.tech: No-op unless the Field is usable with a list value. Context = up to 600 chars of the cited document's flattened text before the citation excerpt. Calls eligibility.classify_post_candidates(names, context). DOCUMENTS or AMBIGUOUS verdicts return Field.needs_review with an explanatory note and the same citation. Otherwise, if any candidates were classified as documents, returns a new posts Field without them (noting the removal); else returns the original.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::build.text: The public entry point that builds one exam's record, either by discovering its official documents fresh or by re-reading a saved list of documents. It sets which Claude connection the whole build should use, then hands over to the real build.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::build.tech: Sets the _RUN_GATEWAY context variable to gateway (None means the process-wide gateway), calls _build with the same arguments (minus gateway), and always resets the context var in a finally block. Returns the BuildResult. replay freezes the document list; authority_discovery is an optional callable producing a DiscoveryRun.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::enforce_sem.text: A final consistency check on an exam record: a fact's status must match what its content actually is. Posts that are really documents get sent back for review, an exam pattern with no confidently read stage gets sent back for review, and a 'no fee exemptions published' is overturned to 'needs review' if the fee's own quote mentions an exemption.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::enforce_sem.tech: Mutates rec and returns a list of change descriptions (each also noted). (1) posts FOUND whose classify_post_candidates verdict is DOCUMENTS/AMBIGUOUS -> NEEDS_REVIEW. (2) examPattern FOUND whose dict roots all carry 'level' and 'status' but none is a VERIFIED STAGE -> NEEDS_REVIEW. (3) feeExemptions NOT_PUBLISHED while D_APPLICATION.exemption_wording(fee.citation.excerpt) finds wording -> NEEDS_REVIEW with a single uncategorised exemption item and a citation built from the fee citation.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_date.text: Turns every date that was replaced by a later official statement into an entry in the exam's correction history, showing the old date, the new date, and quotes from both documents. If no separate correction notice exists, the entry says so rather than calling itself one.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_date.tech: Groups 'dates' rows with status SUPERSEDED by their supersededBy id. For each newer row builds an entry {id rev-<newerId>, title '<Type> revised: old → new', sourceTitle, publishedDate (from _amending_notice or ''), effectiveDate, evidenceSpan quoting all printed and later excerpts, sourceUrl, oldSourceUrls, status ACTIVE, affectedField, oldValue, newValue, note}. Untyped 'other' events are named by the old row's label. Appends new ids to an existing usable 'corrigenda' field, else sets a new FOUND field with a citation and note. Returns the number of entries built (even if some ids already existed).

tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_offi.text: Records the list of documents this exam's record was read from, with their titles and kinds, but only documents whose own text was confirmed to be about this exam, so they can appear in the candidate's library.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_offi.tech: Collects docs that were loaded and whose identity check is IdentityVerdict.MATCH as {url, title (220), kind, identity}. If any, sets Field.found('officialSources', items) with a citation to the authority domain listing up to six titles. Returns the count.

tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_sear.text: For facts that still have no reading after GovOS searched the authority's own listings, this records 'we searched these places and found nothing for this recruitment' as GovOS's gap, never as 'the authority did not publish it'. A 'not published' that came from the authority's own statement is left alone.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_sear.tech: For each (field, where) in searched: skips fields with status FOUND or NEEDS_REVIEW, and NOT_PUBLISHED fields whose note lacks 'No document of kind'; otherwise sets Field(status=NOT_EXTRACTED, note='searched <where>; nothing ... found there ...'). Returns a frozenset of the fields it set (to be reported as SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH).

tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_vaca.text: Reads the vacancy break-up tables (how many posts per category) drawn as ruled tables in this exam's own PDFs and attaches them to the exam's posts. A table is used only if its printed totals add up and every row matches one post.
tools/exam_builder/build.py::record_vaca.tech: Requires a non-empty 'posts' list. For each loaded PDF with raw bytes and an identity MATCH, calls vacancy_breakup.breakups_in(raw, posts); exceptions and refusals are logged as notes. Tables gain documentTitle/Url/Kind. If any, sets Field.found('vacancyBreakup', tables) cited to the first table's page and checks, with an explanatory note. Returns the count.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.text: The verdict for one fact after comparing every source: which value (if any) may be presented as the authority's, and the lists of claims that govern, agree, disagree, are secondary only, are mere leads, or could not be backed by their quote.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.tech: Dataclass: field, state (Resolution), value (None unless an official statement governs), governing, corroborations, agreeing_unreviewed, conflicts, secondary, leads, unsupported (lists of SourceClaim), note. Methods publishable, as_fact, as_dict.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.text: Turns the verdict into a plain record for a report, listing every group of claims.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.tech: Returns {field, state, value, publishable, note, governing, corroborations, agreeingUnreviewed, conflicts, secondary, leads, unsupported}, each list mapped through SourceClaim.as_dict.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.text: Converts the verdict into GovOS's standard fact shape. A publishable fact is marked verified with official evidence first and agreeing trusted sources after; an unsupported one is marked 'could not read'; anything else is held for review with no value, so a secondary or disputed reading is never shown as the authority's.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.tech: publishable -> Fact.verified(value, evidence of governing + corroborations) with note. UNSUPPORTED -> Fact(status=NOT_EXTRACTED, note). Otherwise Fact(value=None, status=NEEDS_REVIEW, evidence of conflicts + secondary, note).

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.text: Says whether this fact may be shown as the authority's value: only when an official statement governs it.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::ClaimResol.tech: Property: value is not None and state in (OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL_CORROBORATED, OFFICIAL_CONTESTED).

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::Resolution.text: The possible outcomes when GovOS compares what different sources say about one fact: only the official source said it, a trusted source agrees, a non-official source disagrees, official sources disagree with each other, only non-official sources said it, or no claim's quote could be found.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::Resolution.tech: str Enum: OFFICIAL, OFFICIAL_CORROBORATED, OFFICIAL_CONTESTED, OFFICIAL_CONFLICT (nothing published), SECONDARY_ONLY, UNSUPPORTED.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.text: One source's statement of one fact, for example 'this coaching site says the last date is 14 March', with the quote, the page, which kind of source it is (official, trusted secondary, and so on) and whether the quote was actually found in the page GovOS fetched.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.tech: Dataclass: field, value, source_url, source_class (SourceClass), quotation, document_title, published_at, page, node_id, quotation_status (EvidenceStatus, default UNCHECKED, set only by check_quotation). Has is_supported, check_quotation, as_evidence and as_dict.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.text: Turns the claim into a plain record for a report, including a human label for the kind of source.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.tech: Returns a camelCase dict: field, value, sourceUrl, sourceClass, sourceLabel (source_class.candidate_label), quotation, documentTitle, publishedAt, page, quotationStatus.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.text: Turns the claim into the standard evidence record used elsewhere in GovOS, keeping which kind of source it came from.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.tech: Returns SourceEvidence(source_id=node_id or source_url, url, document_title, published_at, page, span=quotation, span_status=quotation_status, reading='<field> = <value>', source_class=source_class.value).

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.text: Checks the claim's quote against the text GovOS fetched itself, and records whether it is really there.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.tech: Sets quotation_status = Evidence(span=quotation, source_url).verify(fetched_text) and returns it.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.text: Says whether this claim's quote was actually found in the source text.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::SourceClai.tech: Property: True only when quotation_status is EvidenceStatus.VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::_default_k.text: The default way of comparing two values: ignore extra spaces and capital letters.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::reconcile.text: Decides what may be said about one fact from every source's claim. The official value governs; a trusted secondary source agreeing is noted as support; anyone disagreeing is recorded but does not change it; if only non-official sources say it, it stays their claim; if official sources disagree with each other, nothing is published. Claims whose quotes were not found count for nothing, and social posts are only leads.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::reconcile.tech: Filters claims to field_name; drops UNVERIFIED-class claims; unsupported quotes -> unsupported; DISCOVERY_ONLY -> leads; the rest split by source_class.may_state_official_fact. No official: SECONDARY_ONLY with secondary=others, else UNSUPPORTED with a note. Groups official values by key (default _default_key); more than one -> OFFICIAL_CONFLICT with all official and other claims in conflicts. One -> value from the first governing claim; others matching are corroborations (TRUSTED_SECONDARY) or agreeing_unreviewed, mismatches conflicts; state OFFICIAL_CONTESTED / OFFICIAL_CORROBORATED / OFFICIAL. The key only compares; values are never rewritten.

tools/exam_builder/claims.py::reconcile_.text: Runs the comparison for every fact any claim mentions, each on its own.
tools/exam_builder/claims.py::reconcile_.tech: Returns {field: reconcile(field, claims, key=keys.get(field))} over the sorted set of claim fields; keys is an optional per-field comparison function map.

tools/exam_builder/clauses.py::procedure.text: Reads a notice's own numbered procedure clauses (for example 'PARA-15 MEMORANDUM OF MARKS' with clauses 15.1, 15.2) and returns each clause word for word under the heading the notice printed. This feeds the FAQs section without inventing questions or rewording anything. Only procedural headings (objections, answer keys, marks, recounting, malpractice, instructions, centres, selection procedure, normalisation) are used.
tools/exam_builder/clauses.py::procedure.tech: Flattens whitespace; finds PARA/SECTION/CHAPTER N headings and their capitalised titles via regex. For each heading whose title matches _PROCEDURE and whose number has not been seen, finds 'N.k ' clause markers in the region up to the next heading; each clause body ends at the next marker or units.next_structural_boundary(clauses=False), has page footers stripped, and is kept if >= 25 chars. Returns [{heading (capitalised title), number 'N.k', text, page (page_of(body[:120]) or 1)}]. A heading number is used only once, so a repeat in a table of contents is skipped if the first had clauses.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::SUPERSEDED.text: The label the website uses for a fact that a later official statement replaced.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::UNVERIFIED.text: The label the website uses for a fact that is still being verified.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::VERIFIED_L.text: The label the website uses for a fact that is officially verified.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_fact_valu.text: Gets a fact's value if it has one, otherwise a fallback.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_fact_valu.tech: Returns fact.value when fact is not None and fact.has_value, else default.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_identity_.text: Describes which exact question paper something is (exam, cycle, stage, paper, subject, language, set, session), keeping only the parts that were printed, plus a readable description.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_identity_.tech: Returns {examId} plus cycle, stage, paper, subject, language, setCode, session where truthy, plus describe=identity.describe().

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_pattern_p.text: Builds the citation for an exam-pattern item (a stage, paper or section) from its own evidence.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::_pattern_p.tech: Returns None if node.evidence is empty; otherwise to_legacy_provenance of a Fact(value=node.name, status=node.status if it carries a value else NEEDS_REVIEW, evidence=node.evidence). The exam_title argument is unused.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::admit_card.text: Turns admit-card events read from notices into the cards the website's Admit Card section shows. A city intimation and an admit card stay separate, a release date and an exam date are separate, a direct download link appears only if the authority actually published one, a portal link is labelled as a portal, and the precision (day or month) the authority printed is kept. It trusts that the events given to it are this exam's: that is decided earlier, by the gates.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::admit_card.tech: Projects every event, stamping examId = exam_id (events carry no exam of their own; may_supply_admit_card and the merge decide membership upstream): id, kind, officialLabel, sourceLabel, status, cycle?, stageLabel/stageRef from the first STAGE scope, releasedAt + releasePrecision (default DAY) + releaseNote, releaseRule + note, availableUntil, examDate + note, portalUrl + portalNote, downloadUrl only when download_url.is_publishable, credentials, documents, instructions, supersedes, note, and provenance from released_at or else release_rule.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::answer_key.text: Turns official answer keys into the list the website shows, each tied to the exact paper it answers, with its type, link, publication date, objection window and access route. Where the authority only lets each candidate see the key through their own login, the answers list is simply empty; GovOS never fills it in. Keys for another exam are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::answer_key.tech: Skips keys whose paper.exam_id != exam_id. Row: id (key.id or 'key-<slug>'), identity, kind, url, status, sourceStatus (or 'NEEDS_REVIEW'), optional publishedAt, windowOpens, windowCloses, access, revises, note, entries [{questionNumber, accepted, value, status}], and provenance from key.url when key.evidence exists.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::applicatio.text: Turns an application process read from an authority's instructions into the practice application form the website shows: each step becomes a module and its fields become inputs, in the authority's own words. It deliberately adds no 'common mistake' traps, since those need a person's judgement. If no usable steps were read, it returns nothing rather than an empty form.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::applicatio.tech: Uses process.stages with status VERIFIED or NEEDS_REVIEW; returns None if none. Modules: moduleNumber, cardName/title from stage.title, introduction, noticeReference from the first evidence's locator, fields with kind SELECT/DATE else TEXT and noteFromNotice=help_text. Returns {examId, portalName (arg or primary source title), portalUrl, sourceDocumentTitle/Url, modelledOnNote, modules, traps: [], cleanSubmissionNote, provenance (to_legacy_provenance of portal or Fact.not_extracted(), or {})}.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::citation_f.text: Converts a newer evidence record back into an old-style citation.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::citation_f.tech: Returns Citation(document_title or url, url, page or 1, clause=section, excerpt=span, verified_date=accessed_at).

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::describe_f.text: Gives a short plain explanation of each of the four fact states, for a report or a legend.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::describe_f.tech: Returns a dict keyed by Status values VERIFIED, NEEDS_REVIEW, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_EXTRACTED with one-line descriptions.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::evidence_f.text: Converts an old-style citation into the newer evidence record. The quote is marked as not checked, because old citations were never checked word for word against the document.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::evidence_f.tech: Returns SourceEvidence(source_id or citation.url, url, document_title, document_type=kind, page, section=clause, span=excerpt, accessed_at and published_at both = citation.verified_date, span_status=UNCHECKED, reading='carried over from a citation ...').

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::evidence_f.text: Converts evidence produced by the reading step into the standard evidence record, keeping whether its quote was verified.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::exam_stage.text: For an exam date, says whether its stage was actually named in the source ('stated') or still needs checking. Non-exam dates get no value.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::exam_stage.tech: Returns '' when kind != 'EXAM'; 'STATED' when exam_stage_of(stage_label) is non-empty, else 'NEEDS_REVIEW'.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::exam_stage.text: Reads an exam date's label to tell whether it names the first stage (for example 'Preliminary', 'Tier I') or a later stage (for example 'Mains', 'Phase II'). Paper or shift numbers do not count.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::exam_stage.tech: Returns 'LATER' if _LATER_STAGE matches (mains, tier/phase/stage 2-9, ii-v, b-d, two/three/second/third), else 'FIRST' if _FIRST_STAGE matches (preliminary, prelims, screening, tier/phase/stage 1/i/a/one/first), else ''. The later check runs first.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::fact_from_.text: Converts an old-style exam field into the newer fact format, keeping its value, status, note and citation.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::fact_from_.tech: Returns Fact(value, status=status_from_legacy(field.status), evidence=[evidence_from_citation(...)] if a citation exists else [], confidence 1.0 for FOUND else 0.0, note).

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::field_from.text: Converts a newer fact back into an old-style field for code that still expects one. Because the old format has room for only one citation, the first source is used and any others are listed in the note.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::field_from.tech: Citation from fact.primary_source (or None); if fact.evidence has more than one item, appends 'also stated in: <locators>' to the note. Returns LegacyField(name, status_to_legacy(status), value, citation, note).

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::important_.text: Turns the timeline events read from documents into the list of dates the website's Dates and Timeline section shows. Events with no date are left out, replaced dates are kept but marked superseded, uncertain dates are marked tentative, multi-day exams show their first day, duplicate statements of the same date are merged, and an application window also produces a separate opening-date row.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::important_.tech: For each milestone: skip if no effective date and not superseded; shown = effective or ends/starts value, or starts_at for multi-day EXAM/DV/PHYSICAL_TEST/INTERVIEW/SKILL_TEST ranges. De-dups on (legacy type, date, kind). Provenance from ends_at or starts_at via to_legacy_provenance (row skipped if None). isTentative when is_tentative, non-DAY precision or NEEDS_REVIEW. For a window kind mapping to APPLICATION_CLOSE (not APPLICATION_END) with different start/end, adds an APPLICATION_OPEN row ('<id>-open'). Row: id, type, label, dateTimeStr '<date> 00:00:00', timezone, isTentative, status SUPERSEDED|AVAILABLE, provenance, plus supersededBy/supersessionNote and stageAssociation/stageLabel where applicable.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::legacy_dat.text: Maps a date's event kind (like application end, admit card, exam) onto the fixed set of date types the website understands. An exam date is placed on the first or later stage according to its label; dates the website has no word for keep a general 'other' type.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::legacy_dat.tech: Base lookup in _KIND_TO_LEGACY_TYPE (unknown kinds -> 'NOTIFICATION'). For kind 'EXAM' with a stage label: LATER -> 'EXAM_TIER2', FIRST -> 'EXAM_TIER1', else a label containing 2/ii/b as a word -> 'EXAM_TIER2'; otherwise the mapped value ('EXAM_TIER1').

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::milestone_.text: Reads one date row from an existing hand-written exam record back into the event format the pipeline uses, so it can be compared with dates read from documents. The hand-written row is treated as verified, since a person read the document to write it, but its quote is marked as not re-checked by the pipeline. The opening and the closing of the application window are two separate events.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::milestone_.tech: Builds a SourceEvidence from row.provenance (span_status UNCHECKED). Date = first 10 chars of dateTimeStr as a VERIFIED Fact. Kind from _LEGACY_TYPE_TO_KIND (APPLICATION_OPEN->APPLICATION_START, APPLICATION_CLOSE->APPLICATION_END, EXAM_TIER1/2->EXAM, unknown -> the type or 'OTHER'). EXAM_TIER2 gets a 'Tier II' STAGE scope. The date goes on starts_at for APPLICATION_OPEN, else ends_at. Returns a Milestone with DAY precision, ANNOUNCED state, is_tentative from the row, superseded_by set when status is SUPERSEDED, status VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::notificati.text: Picks out only the dates that are safe to send reminders for: verified, still in force, and given to the exact day.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::notificati.tech: Returns [m for m in milestones if m.is_actionable]; the rules live in Milestone.is_actionable.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::official_p.text: Turns the catalogue of official past question papers into the list the website's Previous Year Papers section shows, each with its identity, link, status, whether its contents could be read, and citation. Papers belonging to another exam are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::official_p.tech: Skips papers whose identity.exam_id != exam_id. Row: id 'paper-<slug of identity.key()[:60]>', identity (_identity_dict), title, url, status, contentsStatus, contentsNote?, provenance from paper.url when paper.evidence exists. source_const is unused.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::pattern_tr.text: Turns the exam pattern read from a notice (stages, papers, sections) into the nested structure the website's Exam Pattern section shows. Figures the authority did not print are left out rather than shown as zero, figures GovOS calculated are flagged as computed, figures not verified are flagged as under review, and each item carries its own citation. If the pattern belongs to a different exam, nothing is returned.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::pattern_tr.tech: Returns [] when pattern.exam_id is set and differs from exam_id. Otherwise recursively projects each stage: id, level, levelLabel, name, code, order, status; questions/marks/durationMinutes/marksPerQuestion where present (with 'derived' and 'underReview' key lists); negativeMarking as printed plus per-wrong / fraction; qualifying {asPrinted, qualifyingOnly, countsTowardsMerit, minimumMarks, minimumPercent, byCategory}; languages, mode, questionType, sectionalTiming, durationVariants, note, provenance (_pattern_provenance) and children.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::result_dec.text: Turns official result announcements into the cards the website's Results section shows. A result actually declared and one only scheduled are kept apart, 'qualified' is shown only where the source says it, a result document link appears only where the authority published one, and revisions keep their link to the result they replaced. It trusts that the declarations given to it are this exam's: that is decided earlier, by the gates.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::result_dec.tech: Projects every declaration, stamping examId = exam_id (a ResultDeclaration carries no exam; membership is decided upstream): id, kind, label, isDeclaration, status, lifecycle, sourceLabel (if different), cycle, stage and post labels from scope, declaredAt/declaredPrecision/declaredNote from published_at, expectedAt/expectedPrecision/expectedNote, qualification unless 'UNSTATED', qualifiedCount, nextStep, nextStageRef, documentUrl only when is_publishable, portalUrl, cutoffs [{marks, basis, scope}], supersedes, note, and provenance from published_at, else expected_at, else document_url.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::round_trip.text: A check used by tests: does an old-style field come back unchanged after converting it to the new format and back? If so, switching formats cannot change what a record says.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::round_trip.tech: Runs field_from_fact(field.name, fact_from_field(field)) and returns True when name, status and value match and the citation is either absent on both or has the same url, page and excerpt.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::source_doc.text: Creates a source-document record from what the discovery step already knows about a link, such as its type, title and a fingerprint of its content.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::source_doc.tech: Returns SourceDocument(id=url, url, kind, title, authority, accessed_at, content_hash, exam_id).

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::status_fro.text: Translates the older four-state status (where 'found' is the first state) into the newer one (where it is called 'verified').
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::status_fro.tech: Looks up _LEGACY_TO_STATUS: FOUND->VERIFIED, NEEDS_REVIEW, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_EXTRACTED map to themselves. Raises KeyError on an unknown value.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::status_to_.text: Translates the newer status back into the older one.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::status_to_.tech: Inverse lookup of _LEGACY_TO_STATUS (VERIFIED->FOUND, others identical). KeyError on an unmapped value.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::syllabus_t.text: Turns the syllabus read from a notice into the nested structure the website's Syllabus section shows, with each topic's status, scope (which paper or stage it belongs to) and citation. It makes sure every topic has a unique id and stops after a very large number of topics.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::syllabus_t.tech: Recursive projection of syllabus.roots to {id, title, levelLabel, order, status, note?, scope? [{kind,label}], provenance?, children?}. Repeated ids are re-qualified as '<parentId>-<lastSegment>' with -2, -3 suffixes. Provenance from a Fact(title, status or NEEDS_REVIEW, evidence). Stops adding children after max_nodes (default 4000) nodes. Does not check exam_id (the caller and syllabus.may_supply_syllabus do).

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::to_legacy_.text: Builds the source-citation record the website displays (document, link, page, clause, dates, quote, verification badge) from a fact's main source. If the fact has no source, it returns nothing, so the website never shows a citation button that opens nothing.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::to_legacy_.tech: Returns None when fact.primary_source is None; otherwise a dict {id, documentTitle (or url), officialUrl, pageNumber (or 1), clauseNumber (or 'Whole document'), publishedDate (published_at or accessed_at), verifiedDate, verifiedBy, taxonomyType, verificationLevel via verification_level_for, excerptText (full span)}.

tools/exam_builder/compat.py::verificati.text: Chooses the badge the website shows for a fact: 'superseded' if replaced, 'officially verified' only if verified, otherwise 'under verification'.
tools/exam_builder/compat.py::verificati.tech: Returns SUPERSEDED_LEVEL when superseded, VERIFIED_LEVEL for Status.VERIFIED, else UNVERIFIED_LEVEL.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Comp.text: The possible states shown for each of the exam's 17 sections: verified, built from verified facts, derived at runtime, not yet published, not applicable, not found after searching, source unreadable, reading failed, needs review, or a network failure.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Comp.tech: str Enum: VERIFIED_AVAILABLE, SUPPORTED_AND_PROJECTED, RUNTIME_DERIVED, NOT_YET_PUBLISHED, NOT_APPLICABLE, SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH, SOURCE_UNREADABLE, EXTRACTION_FAILED, NEEDS_REVIEW, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.text: The full completeness report for one exam across all its sections, with counts of verified, derived, not yet published, not applicable, needs review, failed and not-found sections, and whether extra searches were made.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, cycle, total_sections (default 17), verified_count, derived_count, not_yet_published_count, not_applicable_count, needs_review_count, failure_count, source_not_found_count, sections, reacquisition_performed, reacquisition_attempts. Methods completeness_percentage, get_section, to_dict.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.text: The share of applicable sections that are usable (verified or built from verified facts), as a percentage.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.tech: Property: (verified_count + derived_count) / (total_sections - not_applicable_count) * 100, rounded to 1 decimal; 100.0 when no section is applicable.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.text: Finds one section's result by its name, website number or order.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.tech: Returns the first SectionCompleteness whose section_id, section_num or section_order equals the argument, else None.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.text: Turns the whole report into a plain record, including the percentage and every section.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Exam.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of all counts, completenessPercentage, reacquisition fields and sections (each via SectionCompleteness.to_dict).

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::GovO.text: The fixed definition of one of the 17 exam sections: its order, its number in the website, its title, which record fields it depends on, which document types usually supply it, where it sits in a candidate's journey, and what it answers for the student.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::GovO.tech: Frozen dataclass: order, num (UI deep-link number), id, title, nature, canonical_domain, canonical_fields, preferred_sources, lifecycle_stage, student_purpose, target_group (default 'JOURNEY'), verification_requirement, supported_states (default FACTUAL_SUPPORTED_STATES). Instances form GOVOS_17_SECTIONS.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::GovO.text: An older name for the section's preferred document types, kept so old code still works.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Sect.text: The completeness result for one section of one exam: its state, how much evidence backs it, a student-facing summary, a technical note and the state of each field it depends on.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Sect.tech: Dataclass: section_order, section_num, section_id, section_title, nature, state, is_applicable (default True), evidence_count, student_status_summary, technical_note, fields (field -> state string). to_dict serialises it.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Sect.text: Turns one section's completeness result into a plain record.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Sect.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of every attribute, with nature and state as their enum values.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::Sect.text: Says whether a section's content is read directly from official documents or built by GovOS from other verified facts (like the study roadmap or mock tests).

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_cla.text: Decides the honest state of one fact for the completeness report, without changing the record: verified, needs review, not yet published by the authority, not applicable, not found after searching, unreadable source, reading failed, or a network failure. It is careful never to say 'not published' when GovOS simply did not find or could not read the document.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_cla.tech: not_applicable entry -> NOT_APPLICABLE. Missing field -> INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE (if infra_failed) or SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH. FOUND -> VERIFIED_AVAILABLE; NEEDS_REVIEW -> NEEDS_REVIEW. NOT_PUBLISHED -> INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE if infra failed, SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH if the note starts 'No document of kind', else NOT_YET_PUBLISHED. NOT_EXTRACTED -> NEEDS_REVIEW if 'withheld by reviewer' in the note, then INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, EXTRACTION_FAILED (_reader_raised), SOURCE_UNREADABLE (unreadable_docs), SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH (in searched_not_found), else EXTRACTION_FAILED. Returns (state, note).

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_der.text: For a section built from other facts (like the study roadmap), finds the weakest of the facts it depends on and reports the section in that fact's state, with a note naming each missing input.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_der.tech: Classifies each needed field with _classify_field_status, keeps non-VERIFIED ones, sorts by _INPUT_STATE_ORDER (infrastructure failure weakest, not applicable last) and returns (weakest state, '; '-joined notes). If every input is verified, returns NEEDS_REVIEW with a defensive note.
