tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_ext.text: Looks up the name of the reader that handles a given fact.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_ext.tech: Returns the extractor name of the CONTRACT entry with that field name, or '' if none or not found.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_rea.text: Checks the build log to see whether any reader for a fact crashed on a document it was given, which is proof the content existed but GovOS failed to read it.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::_rea.tech: True when any line of rec.log contains '<name> failed on ' for the field's contract extractor or any of its DOMAIN_READERS names (e.g. extract_pattern, 'extract_eligibility (age)'). It used to check only the contract extractor, missing domain-reader failures; test_review_fixes re-reads build.py so a new reader cannot be left out of DOMAIN_READERS.

tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::eval.text: Produces the completeness report for one exam across all 17 sections from the student's point of view: which have verified information, which are built from verified facts, which are genuinely not yet published, and which hit reading or network problems. Each section's state is worked out from the states of the facts it depends on, with the worst problem taking priority.
tools/exam_builder/completeness.py::eval.tech: Derived sections: roadmap needs examPattern + syllabus FOUND, mock-tests needs examPattern; ready -> SUPPORTED_AND_PROJECTED (derived_count), else _derived_input_state with _DERIVED_SUMMARY wording and the matching counter; any other derived section raises ValueError, since it must declare its inputs. Factual sections: officialSources from rec.sources_read; nextSteps FOUND only if non-empty (an empty FOUND becomes SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH); others via _classify_field_status, counting cited fields as evidence. Section state priority: INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, SOURCE_UNREADABLE, VERIFIED (or NEEDS_REVIEW if any input needs review), EXTRACTION_FAILED, NEEDS_REVIEW, NOT_YET_PUBLISHED, NOT_APPLICABLE, else SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH. Cycle from rec.cycle or the exam id's last segment. build_result is accepted but unused. Returns ExamCompletenessReport.

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Contract.text: One item on GovOS's universal list of things to find out about every exam (such as the fee or the syllabus), with which kinds of document could answer it in order of preference, which reader reads it, why it matters, and whether it is required.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Contract.tech: Frozen dataclass: name, group (the candidate-facing section), sources (tuple of DocKind, best first), extractor (function name in exam_authoring.extract), purpose, required (default False). Instances form CONTRACT.

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Coverage.text: A summary of which facts could, in principle, be answered from the documents GovOS found for an exam, and which kinds of document were missing for the rest.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Coverage.tech: Dataclass: supplied (field -> 'INTRINSIC' | 'CAN_ANSWER_FROM:<kind>' | 'NO_SOURCE') and missing_sources (field -> list of kind values).

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Coverage.text: Groups the coverage summary by section, so a gap can be seen against the screen it affects.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::Coverage.tech: Returns {group: [(field name, supplied status or 'NO_SOURCE')]} for every group in GROUPS, in CONTRACT order.

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::coverage.text: Before reading anything, works out which facts could be answered by the kinds of document found. This keeps 'nothing was found that could answer this' separate from 'we read the document and failed'.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::coverage.tech: For each CONTRACT field: no sources -> 'INTRINSIC'; else the first source kind present in available_kinds -> 'CAN_ANSWER_FROM:<kind value>'; else 'NO_SOURCE' with missing_sources listing all its source kinds. Returns a Coverage.

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::fields_f.text: Lists every fact a given kind of document could help answer.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::fields_f.tech: Returns [f for f in CONTRACT if kind in f.sources].

tools/exam_builder/contract.py::supplier.text: Lists which kinds of document could answer a given fact.
tools/exam_builder/contract.py::supplier.tech: Returns the sources tuple of the CONTRACT entry named field_name, or () if not found.

tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::Corrig.text: One official change taken from a corrigendum (correction notice), such as a deadline extended or the vacancy count revised, with the old and new values, when it was issued, the exact quote and the source.
tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::Corrig.tech: Dataclass: id, exam_id, cycle, title, affected_domain, affected_field, old_value, new_value, effective_date, evidence_span, source_url, source_title, status (default VERIFIED), note. to_dict serialises it.

tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::Corrig.text: Turns one correction into a plain record.
tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::Corrig.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of every attribute; status as its enum value (or str).

tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::extrac.text: Reads a correction notice line by line and pulls out each change it announces: date extensions or reschedulings (sorted into application deadline or exam date by the words used) and vacancy revisions. Each change keeps its line as an exact quote, and only lines that really appear in the document are kept. The date check and the vacancy check on a line are independent.
tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::extrac.tech: Per non-empty line: if _DATE_EXTENSION matches and the line verifies in the text, records a 'dates' notice with field exam_date (line mentions exam/tier/prelim/written/conduct) or application_close, new_value = last captured group, old_value = first group when two were captured. Independently, if _VACANCY_REVISION matches and verifies, records an 'overview' vacanciesTotal notice from the captured integers (a failed date verification no longer skips it). ids are 'corr-<exam>-date|vac-<n>'; cycle falls back to doc.published_at[:4]; effective_date = published_at or accessed_at.

tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::is_cor.text: Checks whether a document presents itself as a correction or amendment, by looking for words like corrigendum, addendum, amendment, extension of date or postponement near its start.
tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::is_cor.tech: True when _CORRIGENDA_CUES matches within the first 3000 characters of the text.

tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::notice.text: Turns extracted corrections into change records that can be laid over an exam's existing data. If an earlier matching fact exists (the same kind of date, or the vacancy total), the correction is marked as replacing it and keeps the old value; otherwise it is recorded as a new addition.
tools/exam_builder/corrigenda.py::notice.tech: For each notice builds a provenance dict (page 1, taxonomyType 'REVISION', verificationLevel OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED, excerpt up to 600 chars). Finds a target among existing overlays of the same domain (dates: 'close' or 'exam' matching the overlay value's type; overview: any). Dates produce an ImportantDate-shaped value (type APPLICATION_CLOSE or EXAM_TIER1); overview produces {vacanciesTotal}. Returns ExamFactOverlay objects with kind SUPERSEDE (target found, target_id/supersedes_id/previous_value set) or ADD, status VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::DateReading.text: One event as a passage stated it, before it becomes a timeline entry: what kind of event, its label, the quote, its dates, whether it is a range, tentative, postponed or cancelled, which stage and cycle it belongs to, and whether it is only the opening of an application window.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::DateReading.tech: Dataclass: kind, label, span, dates (ReadDate list), is_range, tentative, state (MilestoneState, default ANNOUNCED), stage_ref, cycle, precision (default DAY), opens_only.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::EventCue.text: A set of wording patterns that signal a particular event, like an application window, an admit card, a result or an exam being held, plus wording that rules the event out.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::EventCue.tech: Frozen dataclass: kind, anchors (regexes; one must match), against (regexes that veto), range_role. The ordered EVENT_CUES tuple holds the vocabulary, most specific first.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::EventCue.ma.text: Checks whether a passage talks about this event and does not contain wording that rules it out.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::EventCue.ma.tech: Lower-cases the passage; False if any 'against' regex matches; otherwise True if any anchor regex matches.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::ReadDate.text: One date as a document wrote it, with how precise it was (an exact day or just a month), where it sits in the text and the original wording.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::ReadDate.tech: Dataclass: iso (YYYY-MM-DD; day 1 for month precision), precision (DatePrecision), start, end (character offsets), text. sort_key returns iso.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::ReadDate.so.text: The value used to put dates in order.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_cited.text: Decides whether a date is just part of a reference to a document (like 'Notification No. 02/2024 dated 19/02/2024' or 'issued on ...') or the end of a period counted from an event, rather than the date something happens.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_cited.tech: True if the 70 chars before start end in 'dt'/'dated', or match _CITATION_BEFORE (notice/G.O./memo ... No. ... dated), or the 180 chars before match _ISSUED_BEFORE (in continuation / vide / as per ... issued on), or _ends_a_period on the 160 chars before.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_collapse_s.text: If an authority posts the same file under two names, the same date gets read twice. This merges those duplicates into one entry while keeping the proof from both copies.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_collapse_s.tech: Dedupes a bucket of (doc, milestone) on (milestone.id, effective_date, state); later duplicates have their evidence merged into the first via _merge_evidence. Returns the reduced list, order preserved.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_cue_beside.text: When a passage mentions more than one kind of event, this decides which event its dates belong to: the one whose wording ends nearest before the first real date.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_cue_beside.tech: Collects matching EVENT_CUES; with fewer than two returns the one or None. Otherwise finds the first uncited date and picks the cue whose anchor match ends closest before it (ties by list order); falls back to the first matching cue when no anchor precedes it or no uncited date exists.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_ends_a_per.text: Checks whether the text just before a date says the date is the end of a period counted from some event (like 'within one year from the closing date, i.e. ...'), which is a condition's deadline, not an event.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_ends_a_per.tech: Removes abbreviations like i.e./e.g./viz./approx. from 'before' and returns whether _PERIOD_END (a number + years/months/weeks/days + from/after + an event phrase, at the end) matches.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_ends_sente.text: Checks whether a piece of text ends a sentence, treating a colon that introduces a value (like 'dated:') as not ending one.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_ends_sente.tech: False if _VALUE_COLON matches the end (dated/dt/on/from/to/no/date/w.e.f + ':'); otherwise True when the stripped text ends in . : ; ! ? or ).

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_evidence.text: Makes the evidence record for a timeline entry, but only if the quoted words really appear in the document.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_evidence.tech: Builds Evidence(span, doc.url, doc.title, page=1, reading); returns None unless verify(text) is VERIFIED; else SourceEvidence.from_evidence with section 'timeline'.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_is_a_label.text: Checks that a label has at least two real words, so a stray clause number is not treated as an event name.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_is_a_label.tech: True when at least two alphabetic words longer than 2 characters are present.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_iso.text: Turns a day, month and year into a standard date, treating two-digit years as 2000s, and gives nothing back for impossible dates.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_iso.tech: Adds 2000 to years < 100; returns date(year, month, day).isoformat(), or None on ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_label_for.text: Takes the authority's own wording for an event and trims it into a short label, usually the words before the date. It handles listing rows, alternative months like 'May/June', and leftover words like 'From'.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_label_for.tech: On normalised text, takes the text before the first date (extending to the date end when it ends in 'Month /'), strips leading clause numbers, keeps the last '|' cell for listing rows ('Start Date / End Date' when both labels appear), drops a trailing from/between if what remains is still a label, and returns it if 3-90 chars. Otherwise returns the first 90 chars of the number-stripped text or the kind title-cased.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_later_word.text: When a notice and the authority's later page (or a correction notice) disagree on an application or fee deadline, this checks whether the later source is a genuine extension. It only accepts the later source if those higher-ranked sources agree with each other and their date is later than every printed one; otherwise the disagreement stays for a person to resolve.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_later_word.tech: Takes a bucket of (SourceDocument, Milestone); returns the governing (doc, milestone) or None. Only for _EXTENDABLE_KINDS (APPLICATION_WINDOW, FEE_PAYMENT_END, CORRECTION_WINDOW). Ranks docs by _AUTHORITY_ORDER (CORRIGENDUM 0, EXAM_PAGE 1, NOTIFICATION 2, ...); requires the best rank to beat NOTIFICATION, all best-rank items to share one effective_date, no source ranked between best and NOTIFICATION, and no lower-ranked date later than the governing one.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_merge_evid.text: Adds the proof (quoted words) from one timeline entry to another that says the same thing, without adding the same quote twice.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_merge_evid.tech: Mutates keeper: for starts_at and ends_at, appends each evidence item from other whose (source_id, span_digest) is not already on the keeper's Fact.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_mid_senten.text: Checks whether the text before a given point stops in the middle of a sentence.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_mid_senten.tech: True when context[:at] (stripped, only if at > 0) is non-empty and not _ends_sentence.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_nearest_cu.text: When a date's own line names no event, this looks at the surrounding lines and picks the event wording that ends nearest before the date line (its label). If the wording runs into the date line, that wins. Only if no event wording comes before it is wording after it used, unless the line above is an unfinished sentence.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_nearest_cu.tech: Locates the passage in context; for each matching EVENT_CUE, measures the gap from each anchor match ending before the passage, keeping the smallest gap; an anchor starting before the passage's end is an 'overlapping' fallback. Returns the best preceding cue, else the overlapping one, else None if _mid_sentence(context, at), else the first matching cue in list order.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_paragraph_.text: Rebuilds proper sentences from PDF text that was broken across lines: a line is joined to the previous one unless that one ended a sentence or the new line starts a list item. Lines of bare numbers (like a list of hall-ticket numbers) break paragraphs instead of being treated as prose.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_paragraph_.tech: Runs pair_label_columns over the stripped lines (no blocks). Blank or digits-only lines close the current paragraph; a line is appended to the current paragraph unless _ends_sentence(current without trailing ')') or _LIST_START matches. Each paragraph is then split on '.'/';' followed by whitespace and a capital or '('. Returns the stripped sentences.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_same_event.text: Decides whether two timeline entries are talking about the same event, so they can be compared. They must be the same kind of event, for the same stage or paper, in the same exam year. Events that happen in several rounds (like document verification or interviews) are only the same if they are literally the same statement.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_same_event.tech: Returns False for kinds in _RECURRING_KINDS unless ids match; otherwise True when kind and str(scope) are equal and cycles are equal or either is empty (an unlabelled cycle is treated as the record's own).

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_sentence_m.text: Reads exam dates out of long sentences in a notice that span several lines or mention more than one event, such as 'Mains held from X to Y, verification on A, B and C'. It works out which dates belong to which event and turns each into a timeline entry with the exact quoted words as proof. Anything the earlier line-by-line reading already picked up is skipped.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_sentence_m.tech: Splits text into sentences via _paragraph_sentences, skips single-line single-event sentences (already read by the line pass), optionally joins the next sentence when a date follows, strips 'page N of M' footers, and drops furniture sentences. Binds each date to the nearest preceding EVENT_CUES anchor (listed dates chain to the same event; a _NEW_PREDICATE after an already-dated event rebinds to the nearest earlier unbound event of another kind), filters by cycle year (cycle-1..cycle+2), skips dates already placed by the line pass (`placed`) and (kind, iso) keys in `taken` (mutated). Builds verbatim evidence with _evidence (falling back to the clause), and emits Milestone objects with start/end Facts, stage scope, precision (non-DAY precision -> NEEDS_REVIEW with a note), listed-days note, and is_tentative from the clause.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_slug.text: Turns text into a short lowercase id fragment.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_slug.tech: Lowercases, replaces non-alphanumeric runs with '-', strips dashes, truncates to 40 chars; 'x' if empty.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_uncited_da.text: Lists the dates in a text that are real event dates, dropping document-reference dates. A date listed right after a reference date (like '09/04, 24/04 and 06/06') is treated as part of the same reference.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_uncited_da.tech: Iterates read_dates(text); a date is cited if _cited is true or it is joined to a cited previous date by only spaces, commas, '&' or 'and'. Returns the uncited ReadDates.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_window.text: Takes a passage together with its neighbours, because a table often puts the label on one line and the date on the next.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_window.tech: Joins parts[index-before : index+after+1] (clamped) with spaces; defaults one before and one after.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_without_da.text: Removes every date from a piece of text, so a year inside a date is not mistaken for a cycle label.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::_without_da.tech: Replaces each read_dates span with a space, working from the end; returns the result.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::extract_mil.text: Reads every dated event a document states and turns each into a timeline entry in the authority's own words: application windows, exam dates, admit cards, results and so on. It joins windows split across two lines, skips page footers, keeps only dates belonging to this exam's cycle, and requires the exact quote to be in the document. Month-only dates are flagged for review, and events the authority says will be announced later are kept without a date. A second pass then reads events written across several lines of prose.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::extract_mil.tech: parts = pair_label_columns(statements(text), blocks). For each part with a date or _AWAITED wording: joins the next part when it continues a 'from X' window (to/till next line, trailing to/and, or an open bracket closed next line); read_statement with table heading context for rejoined rows, else _window and the previous line as lead. Skips furniture, non-labels, dates outside cycle-1..cycle+2 and passages with a different cycle label; requires _evidence. APPLICATION_START when opens_only. De-dups on (kind, first date, stage), recording restated spans. Builds Milestone with STAGE scope, starts/ends from range/opens_only/single date, alternatives, NEEDS_REVIEW for non-DAY precision, ids with the date appended for _RECURRING_KINDS. Finally extends with _sentence_milestones(taken=..., placed=...).

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::pair_label_.text: Fixes two-column tables that a PDF printed column by column: a run of numbered labels with no dates followed by the same number of dash-led cells each holding a date is rejoined into proper rows (label plus date). Anything that does not fit this exact shape is left alone.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::pair_label_.tech: Scans parts for a run of n >= 2 enumerated, dateless items followed by exactly n items matching _VALUE_CELL and containing a date (and not followed by another value cell); emits '<label> <value>' rows. When blocks is given, maps each rejoined row's output index to (the whole printed table text, up to 3 preceding parts as heading). Returns the new parts list.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::read_dates.text: Finds every date in a piece of text, in formats like '21 May 2026', 'May 21, 2026', '21.05.2026' and 'June 2026', and records whether each was given to the day or only to the month. Day-first is assumed for numeric dates unless only the other order is possible.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::read_dates.tech: Applies _WORDED, _WORDED_MONTH_FIRST, _NUMERIC and _MONTH_ONLY in that order, skipping matches overlapping an earlier one. Numeric dates swap day/month only when the second number exceeds 12. Month-only dates get DatePrecision.MONTH and day 1. Invalid dates are dropped. Returns ReadDates sorted by start offset.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::read_statem.text: Works out what event, if any, a passage states and which date it gives. It reads the passage first, then its neighbours when the label and date sit on separate lines. It ignores document-reference dates, notices whether the event is postponed, cancelled, rescheduled or still awaited, whether the authority called it tentative, which stage and cycle it names, whether it is a date range, and whether a single application date is only the opening.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::read_statem.tech: Cue from _cue_beside_dates(passage), else _nearest_cue(context) with the lead line joined into 'stated' when it matches. Uncited dates come from the passage's own dates (judged with the lead's tail; returns None if every kept date ends a period), else from the haystack. State from _LIFECYCLE on the wider text, RESCHEDULED via _WINDOW_REVISION; with no dates returns None unless the state is non-ANNOUNCED or _AWAITED matches (then AWAITED). Stage from _STAGE_REF/_STAGE_NAME on stated (or the lead tail for a bracket continuation), cycle from _CYCLE on date-free text, is_range for 2+ dates with range words, opens_only for a lone APPLICATION_WINDOW date with an opening and no closing word. Returns DateReading or None.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::reconcile.text: Builds one exam timeline out of dates read from several official documents. If documents agree, it keeps one entry backed by all of them. If one document says it reschedules or cancels an event, or a later official page extends a deadline, the old date is kept but marked as replaced. If two documents simply disagree, both are kept and flagged for a person to check rather than picking one.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::reconcile.tech: Input: list of (SourceDocument, [Milestone]). Groups milestones into buckets with _same_event, collapses duplicates with _collapse_same_statement. Per bucket: single -> kept; one distinct date -> first kept with merged evidence keyed on (source_id, span_digest); a RESCHEDULED/POSTPONED/CANCELLED dated milestone (when >=2 dated) supersedes the others (superseded_by, note, supersedes, revision_source_id), same-date ones merged as corroboration; else _later_word extension handling (keeps the notice's opening evidence when start dates match); else all marked Status.NEEDS_REVIEW with a note listing the dates. Output sorted by (effective_date or '9999', kind). Mutates the milestone objects.

tools/exam_builder/dates.py::statements.text: Splits a document's text into short passages that could each state one event, breaking at sentence ends, numbered clauses and line breaks, since timelines are often tables where each row is a statement.
tools/exam_builder/dates.py::statements.tech: Inserts a newline before 'N.N ' clause numbers that follow '.' or ';', splits on newlines, then splits each line on '.'/';' followed by whitespace and a capital or '('. Returns the non-empty stripped pieces.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Canon.text: The official name of a recruitment as read from its own notification, together with the extra words that notice allows. Every other document is compared against this to decide if it belongs to the same recruitment.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Canon.tech: Frozen dataclass carried on ExamIdentity: core, qualifiers, components, year, text, source_url, basis ('deterministic' | 'deterministic+claude' | 'claude-located', or 'mixed:...'), evidence spans and notes. Has as_dict().

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Canon.text: Turns the official recruitment name record into a plain dictionary so it can be saved or shown.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Canon.tech: Returns a dict with keys designation, core, qualifiers (sorted), components (sorted), cycle, sourceUrl, basis, evidence, notes.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Desig.text: One post name as a document prints it, broken into its main words, the words in brackets, extra words after it, and the year.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Desig.tech: Frozen dataclass: core (ordered tuple of tokens), qualifiers (bracketed tokens), components (words after the core before the cycle, minus context words), year, text (as printed, whitespace-normalised), at (offset in the normalised document).

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::EXTRA.text: The only fields Claude is allowed to return when helping find a recruitment's name in a notice. Anything else makes the answer be rejected.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::EXTRA.tech: Tuple: designation_core, qualifiers, cycle, declared_components, evidence_spans, confidence, ambiguities. validate_extraction refuses output with any other key.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Judge.text: The verdict on whether one document belongs to the recruitment: match, mismatch or ambiguous, with the reasons.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Judge.tech: Dataclass: verdict ('MATCH' | 'MISMATCH' | 'AMBIGUOUS'), evidence, matched, competing, reasons.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::TITLE.text: How much of the start of a document (1,500 characters) counts as its title area when GovOS looks for the name of the recruitment.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::TITLE.tech: Constant 1500; duplicates identity._TITLE_BLOCK_CHARS to avoid an import cycle. Used by establish_canonical and judge to limit designation reading to the head of a document.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Valid.text: The result of checking Claude's answer about a recruitment's name: either accepted, with the pieces that passed, or refused with reasons.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::Valid.tech: Dataclass: ok, designations, components (Designation lists), qualifier_words, cycle, evidence spans, confidence, reasons. ok=False means the whole output is refused.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_admi.text: Checks whether a post name found in a notification could be the one being asked for: same main words, same year, and a shared bracketed qualifier if one was asked for.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_admi.tech: True when d.core == want.core, d.year == year, and either want has no qualifiers or they share one.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_cont.text: The list of ordinary words (like 'panel', 'year', 'paper', 'I', 'II') that can appear next to a post name without meaning it is a different recruitment.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_cont.tech: Returns a frozenset: tokens of identity._STRUCTURAL plus cycle labels, connectors, Roman numerals and single letters a-d. Imported lazily to avoid a cycle.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_read.text: Reads the post name that starts at a given point in a document, stopping at the year, a colon, a full stop or words like 'examination' or 'result'. It separates the main name from bracketed qualifiers and trailing words.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_read.tech: Takes up to 260 chars from `start` in normalised text, cuts at ' in <authority>' if given, masks full dates, ends at the first _YEAR or _STOP match. Core is text before '(' or a spaced dash; qualifiers are tokens in brackets; components are other trailing tokens minus _context_words. Returns None if core is empty, longer than _MAX_CORE (10) tokens, or only context words; else a Designation.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_rela.text: Spots a post name that matches the official one but adds words the notification never mentioned. That is not proof of a different recruitment, but not proof of this one either.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_rela.tech: True when cores match, _same is False, and qualifiers are compatible (either side empty or overlapping).

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_same.text: Checks whether a post name in a document is exactly the official recruitment, allowing only the extra words the notification itself declares.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::_same.tech: True when cores match, qualifiers overlap (or both have none), and d's qualifiers and components are all within canonical qualifiers | components | context words.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::estab.text: Works out the official name of a recruitment by reading the title of its own notification. If Claude is switched on, Claude's reading must pass the checks and agree with the notice's own wording, or no official name is set. If two notifications name different recruitments, it also refuses.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::estab.tech: Inputs: wanted Designation, year, list of (url, text) notifications, optional extractor and claude_enabled. Per notice: deterministic matches in the title block via read_designations + _admits; if Claude is enabled, calls extractor(block) and requires infra 'OK' and validate_extraction ok, else returns (None, notes); skips if Claude's cycle differs. Basis 'deterministic', 'deterministic+claude' or 'claude-located'; merges Claude components/qualifier words (minus context words and digits). Across notices, refuses if cores differ or qualifiers do not overlap; otherwise merges into one CanonicalDesignation. Returns (canonical or None, notes).

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::judge.text: Decides, without any AI, whether a document belongs to this recruitment by reading the post name in its title area and comparing it with the official one. It says match only when the title names this recruitment for this year and nothing else; a different year or a different post is a mismatch; anything unclear is ambiguous.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::judge.tech: Returns AMBIGUOUS if canonical is None. Reads designations; in the title block (at < TITLE_BLOCK_CHARS) classifies own (_same, same year), wrong_year, unexplained (_related) and rivals. MATCH if own and no rivals/unexplained (body rivals listed as competing); AMBIGUOUS if own plus rivals, or unexplained; MISMATCH for wrong year or rivals; else AMBIGUOUS (no cycle beside it, or no designation).

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::link_.text: Before the official name is known, checks a link's text: yes if it names the post being looked for, no if it names a different post, and no opinion if it names none. Being let in here is not final; the document is checked again later.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::link_.tech: Returns None if read_designations finds nothing in link_text; True if any found designation has want's core and compatible qualifiers; otherwise False.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::parse.text: Reads a single post name from a short piece of text, such as what a person searched for.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::parse.tech: Normalises the string, starts after the first _INTRO match if present (else at 0), and returns _read_at's result or None.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::query.text: Turns what the person asked for into a post name to look for, after removing the authority's own name and abbreviations.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::query.tech: Uses official_name (else query), drops words whose lower-cased, quote/bracket-stripped form is in authority_aliases, and passes the rest to parse_designation.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::read_.text: Finds every post name a text introduces with recruitment wording such as 'Recruitment of' or 'Selection to the post of', in order.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::read_.tech: Normalises whitespace, iterates _INTRO matches and calls _read_at at each match end; returns Designations with `at` set to the intro match start.

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::token.text: Breaks a piece of text into simple lower-case words so two post names can be compared, for example treating 'Officers' and 'Officer' as the same word. It does not swap in synonyms.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::token.tech: Lower-cases, replaces quote characters with spaces, splits on non-alphanumerics, and strips a trailing 's' from words longer than 3 letters not ending in 'ss'. Returns list[str].

tools/exam_builder/designation.py::valid.text: Checks Claude's answer about a recruitment's name against the actual notice. Every word Claude returns must be printed in the notice, and its quoted proof must appear word for word. If anything is invented, ambiguous or contradictory, the whole answer is thrown out.
tools/exam_builder/designation.py::valid.tech: Parses raw (JSON string or dict); refuses on non-object, extra keys, wrong types, no evidence_spans, a span not in the normalised notification, non-empty ambiguities, any designation_core/qualifier/component item not printed, no parseable designation, or disagreeing cores. Components are kept only if their core matches (others set aside and reported in reasons); cycle must have a year printed in a span; each qualifier must be printed within a span carrying the designation, and its bracketed tokens (minus core) become qualifier_words. Returns ValidatedExtraction.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::Discover.text: One document found while searching an authority's site: its address, kind, title, why it was kept or rejected, and where it was found.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::Discover.tech: Dataclass: url, kind (DocKind), title, relevance, matched words, found_on, foreign_words (another exam's words when rejected). Property is_pdf.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::Discover.text: Says whether the document's address ends in .pdf.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::Discover.tech: True when url lower-cased, with query string removed, ends with '.pdf'.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::DocKind.text: The list of kinds of document GovOS recognises, such as notification, correction notice, syllabus, question paper, answer key, admit card, result, application portal, study material or video.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::DocKind.tech: str Enum. The first group (EXAM_PAGE..UNKNOWN) is what classify_kind returns; OTR_PORTAL, OFFICIAL_PORTAL, APPLICATION_GUIDE, EXAM_GUIDE, EXAM_DAY_INSTRUCTIONS, STUDY_MATERIAL, LECTURE_VIDEO, PRACTICE_TOOL and DISCOVERY_SIGNAL are used only by the source-graph role classifier (resource_roles.py).

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::Relevanc.text: How a found document earned its place: it names the exam itself, it was found on a page about the exam, or it was rejected.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.text: The full set of documents found for one exam, plus the ones rejected, a log, and a flag saying whether searching or fetching failed (so a gap is not mistaken for 'nothing published').
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, authority_domain, docs, rejected, log, infrastructure_failed, infrastructure_note. Methods of_kind and kinds_found.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.text: Counts how many documents of each kind were found.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.tech: Returns dict kind.value -> count over docs.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.text: Lists the found documents of one kind.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::SourceSe.tech: Returns docs whose kind is the given DocKind (identity comparison).

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_dedupe.text: Removes duplicate documents that share the same address, keeping the copy with the stronger reason for being kept.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_dedupe.tech: One doc per URL; a DIRECT copy replaces an earlier INHERITED one, otherwise the first is kept. Rewrites out.docs.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_designa.text: Decides whether this exam must be recognised by its post name (because it has no distinctive words), and if so, which post name to look for.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_designa.tech: Builds a probe ExamIdentity from the ResolvedExam; if identity.designation_mode(probe) is False returns (None, False); else (query_designation(...), True).

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_merge_a.text: Takes the documents found by a survey of the whole authority's site and adds those that pass this exam's check, skipping ones already found.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_merge_a.tech: Gets exam words without authority tokens via authority_discovery.exam_words_for; if none and no designation, logs and returns. Calls admit_for_exam(run, ...) and appends new admission.docs (found_on suffixed '(authority discovery)'), logging counts of added and mismatched items. Mutates out.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_search_.text: For each needed document kind not found by crawling (notification, syllabus, papers, answer key, admit card, result, cut-off, correction), runs a web search limited to the authority's own site, and passes every hit through the same exam check.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_search_.tech: Kinds already had are those of DIRECT or PDF docs. For each missing _KIND_QUERIES kind calls search.search(query + phrase + host, max_results=8); SearchUnavailable sets infrastructure_failed and returns. Off-estate hits skipped; others gated (rejected recorded), UNKNOWN kinds skipped, kept docs appended with found_on '(targeted search)'.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::_title_o.tech: Regex-extracts <title> from page.html, strips tags and collapses whitespace; '' if absent.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::classify.text: Guesses what kind of document a link points to from its words, for example 'answer key' or 'admit card'. It trusts the link's visible text first, then the web address.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::classify.tech: Checks link text, then url, against the ordered _KIND_PATTERNS regexes (corrigendum/re-opening/extension first, then answer key, admit card, cut-off, question paper, result, syllabus, pattern, calendar, application portal, notification); returns the first match or DocKind.UNKNOWN.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::discover.text: Searches an authority's website for one exam's documents. It starts from known starting pages, follows links, also reads the site's general listing pages, and keeps only documents that pass the exam check. If a separate whole-authority survey is available it adds that survey's matching documents, then uses web search for any document kinds still missing.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::discover.tech: Computes exam aliases and designation mode; PDF seeds are gated and recorded directly. Crawls up to max_pages seeds (most exam-specific path first) via crawl(): load_html (FetchError sets infrastructure_failed), records exam-specific pages as EXAM_PAGE, gates every link, inherits page kind for UNKNOWN DIRECT links, collects on-estate listing pages, skips UNKNOWN non-direct and off-estate non-portal links. Then crawls up to max_pages listing pages, optionally _merge_authority_run, then _search_for_missing_kinds and _dedupe. Returns SourceSet.

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::gate.text: The rule that decides whether a link belongs to this exam. A link is kept if its text or address names this exam, or if it sits on a page about this exam and does not name another exam. A link naming only another exam is rejected. The website's own domain is ignored, since it names the authority, not the exam.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::gate.tech: Matches exam_words against link text + URL path/query (never host) with alias_in. In designation mode uses designation.link_admission: True -> DIRECT, False -> REJECTED, None -> INHERITED if the page is exam-specific else REJECTED. Otherwise: foreign sibling words without own words -> REJECTED; own words -> DIRECT; exam-specific page without foreign words -> INHERITED; else REJECTED. Returns (Relevance, matched, foreign).

tools/exam_builder/discover.py::page_is_.text: Checks whether a web page is about this one exam rather than the whole site, by requiring at least two of the exam's distinctive words in its title or address.
tools/exam_builder/discover.py::page_is_.tech: In designation mode returns link_admission(title, designation) is True. Otherwise counts exam_words found (alias_in) in title + URL path and returns hits >= min(need, len(exam_words)), need defaulting to 2.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::Eligi.text: Everything read about who may apply from one document: the posts, the eligibility rules, the vacancy counts and a short log.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::PostV.text: The verdict on a list of possible post names: are they posts, documents, a mix, or unclear, with the names sorted into each group and the reasons.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::PostV.tech: Dataclass: kind ('POSTS' | 'DOCUMENTS' | 'MIXED' | 'AMBIGUOUS'), posts, documents, ambiguous, reasons.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_add_.text: Copies the details printed in one table row (department, class, pay, vacancies, age band, qualification) onto the post it describes, without overwriting anything already known.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_add_.tech: Mutates post: sets department (if different from the name), classification, pay (row cell or table heading_values PAY), one VacancyCount if the cell is all digits, age_band if it parses as a range/age cell, and one QualificationRule, each only when not already set, each Fact.verified with the row's evidence.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_code.text: Reads a list of post codes written like '02 & 09' or '03 to 05' and expands it into individual two-digit codes.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_code.tech: Expands 'a to b' ranges, then adds the remaining standalone numbers; all zero-padded to 2; deduped preserving order.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_evid.text: Makes a proof record for a rule: the quoted words, the document they came from and what was read. If the quoted words are not actually in the document, it returns nothing, so the rule is not kept.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_evid.tech: Builds an Evidence (page=1, reading) and calls verify(text); returns None unless VERIFIED, else SourceEvidence.from_evidence(...) with section='eligibility'.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_grou.text: Makes a simple comparison key for a group name so 'Ex-Servicemen (ESM)' and 'Ex-Servicemen' count as the same group.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_grou.tech: Removes bracketed parts, lower-cases and strips everything non-alphanumeric.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_iso_.text: Finds dates written like '02.08.1994' or '1st August 2026' in a piece of text and rewrites them in one standard form (year-month-day).
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_iso_.tech: Iterates _DATE matches (numeric d/m/y with . / - separators, or day + month name + year); swaps day and month when the month exceeds 12; skips invalid ones. Returns list of 'YYYY-MM-DD' strings (no calendar validation beyond that).

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_join.text: For a row in a second table that starts with a known post's full name, takes the rest of the row as that post's qualification. It only does this when the full name matches word for word, so the split point is never a guess.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_join.tech: Returns False if post is None, already has a qualification, the table has no QUALIFICATION column, or no raw cells. Requires the raw row's leading words to equal _tokens(post.name) exactly and a remainder of at least 15 chars; requires verified evidence. Appends a QualificationRule scoped to the post and returns True.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.text: Makes a simple comparison key for a post name by keeping only lower-case letters and digits.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.tech: Lower-cases and removes every non [a-z0-9] character.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.text: Spots a table row that names a post but prints nothing else (often because the PDF merged cells across a page break). Such a post is reported for review rather than published or silently dropped.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.tech: Returns the single non-empty raw cell when the row has exactly one and an ordinal, the name is at least 4 chars, has no digits and is not a document; else ''.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.text: Checks whether two tables are naming the same post, by seeing if most of their meaningful words overlap, so line wrapping or punctuation does not matter.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_name.tech: Word sets of 3+ letter words minus the/and/for/including; True when both non-empty and overlap / min size >= 0.6.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_plau.text: Checks that an age range looks like the age of a job applicant (between 14 and 70), so a period like '3-5 years' of debarment is not mistaken for an age limit.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_post.text: Reads a table row's post code, but only if the table's own header calls that column a code.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_post.tech: Finds the SERIAL column; returns '' unless its label contains 'code'; otherwise the digits of row.ordinal zero-padded to 2, or ''.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_rela.text: Finds the parts of a notice that talk about age relaxation (extra years allowed for some groups), starting at each mention.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_rela.tech: For each _RELAXES match returns the next 1600 chars (_RELAXATION_REGION); at most 6 regions.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_slug.text: Turns a phrase into a short, simple id made of lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_slug.tech: Lower-cases, replaces non-alphanumeric runs with '-', strips dashes, truncates to 40 chars; returns 'x' if empty.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_stat.text: Checks whether a table row with the same post name as an existing post actually prints a different pay, class, age or department, which means it is really a second, separate post.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_stat.tech: Compares post.pay (row PAY cell or table heading PAY), classification, age_band and department with the row's cells; True if any held Fact has a value and the row prints a different non-empty value (compared via _name_key).

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_toke.text: Splits text into lower-case words and numbers.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_year.text: Pulls out every number of years mentioned in a sentence, whether written as digits ('5 years') or as a word ('five years').
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::_year.tech: Returns ints from _YEARS.findall plus _NUMBER_WORD lookups for _WORD_YEARS matches (digits first, then words).

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::class.text: Decides whether a list of names read from a table are really posts or a list of documents to bring. It weighs each name's own words (like 'officer' versus 'certificate') and the surrounding text (like 'name of the post' versus 'upload at verification'). Posts are published only when the list is clearly posts or a clear mix.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::class.tech: Scores each name: own document signal 2 (is_document_not_post), own post noun 2 (_POST_NOUN), plus 1 for document context (_DOCUMENT_CONTEXT) or post-table context (_POST_TABLE_CONTEXT). No own signal and no post context -> ambiguous; higher score wins; ties ambiguous. List kind: only documents -> DOCUMENTS; documents + ambiguous -> AMBIGUOUS; documents + posts -> MIXED; ambiguous in a document context with no posts -> AMBIGUOUS; else POSTS (ambiguous folded into posts). Returns PostVerdict.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads the age rules from a notice: minimum and maximum age, 'born not earlier/later than' dates, and the date on which age is counted. Each rule is kept exactly as printed with its quote; GovOS does not convert an age into a birth date itself. If a post is named in the sentence, the rule is tied to that post.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: For each statements() passage, skips experience/validity passages and age-change narration (_AGE_CHANGE). Collects stand-alone reckoning dates (_CUTOFF without a band). Reads a range (_AGE_RANGE, plausibility-checked) or min/max cues (_AGE_BAND/_AGE_MAX), DOB earliest/latest dates and cutoff dates (first date within 45 chars after the cue). Requires verified evidence; scopes to the first post whose name appears; keeps rules with at least one age/DOB value. If exactly one distinct reckoning date was found, applies it to rules without a cutoff_date. Returns list[AgeRule].

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: The main reader for eligibility in one document. It reads the posts, the age rules (each post's own first, then the general ones), the age relaxations, qualifications, other requirements such as nationality, and vacancy counts, and links vacancies to the posts they name.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: Calls extract_posts, post_age_rules + extract_age_rules, extract_relaxations (attached to the first global AgeRule, else the first rule, else a new 'age-<exam>-relaxations' rule), extract_qualifications, extract_requirements (nationality = NATIONALITY statements) and extract_vacancies (appended to posts whose id is in the vacancy's POST scope). Returns EligibilityOutcome with a one-line count log.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads the list of posts from tables in a notice. Each post's details (department, class, pay, vacancies, age, qualification) come only from its own row. Tables of documents to bring or lists of places are skipped. When a second table describes the same post by the same code and name, its details are added to that post instead of making a duplicate. Rows that cannot be read produce no post.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: Iterates reconstruct(text) + reconstruct_lists(text); skips _NOT_A_POST_TABLE headings and tables without a NAME column or any _POST_TABLE_COLUMNS. Unreconstructed rows are tried with _join_by_known_name, and name-only rows are appended to `held` (ordinal, name, heading). Name from NAME or DEPARTMENT cell; splits a trailing count into an empty VACANCY cell; drops short names, _SPILLED_CELLS and documents. Joins to an existing post by code, or by name unless _states_otherwise (namesake gets a numbered id), requiring _names_agree; else creates Post (NEEDS_REVIEW if row.note) and applies _add_row_facts. Returns at most 80.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads the educational qualifications a notice asks for (degree, diploma, Class 10 or 12 and so on) and keeps each requirement exactly as written, with its quote. It notes whether it is stated as essential and any 'as on' date, and ties it to a post if one is named.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: For statements() passages matching _QUALIFIES and not _NOT_QUALIFICATION, at least 25 chars, with verified evidence, deduped on the first 80 normalised chars. Builds QualificationRule(requirement verified, is_essential True when 'essential/must/shall hold...' else None, optional as_on). Post scope by name substring. Returns at most 20.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads numbered rows of an age relaxation table where the PDF has spread a single row over several lines. It rebuilds each row, separates the group, any exclusion in brackets, and the number of years. A plain figure is accepted; a figure with a condition (such as 'up to 5 years depending on service') is kept as printed and marked for review, so it is never simply added to an age limit.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: Within each relaxation region assembles items from lines whose leading number continues the sequence (_ITEM_START), stopping at _TABLE_END and ignoring bare page numbers. Finds _ITEM_FIGURE; category is the text before it, minus a trailing bracketed exclusion and leading serials; must match _CATEGORY and be <= 8 words; deduped by lower-case category. 'up to' or a _FIGURE_QUALIFIER makes years Fact.needs_review, else verified; conditions Fact holds the qualified printed figure and/or exclusion.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads one-line rows of an age relaxation table, like 'SC/ST 5 years', keeping the group's name exactly as printed. Rows where the figure has extra conditions are left to another reader.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: In each relaxation region matches _RELAXATION_ROW (optional code, category, N years). Skips categories not matching _CATEGORY, with unbalanced brackets, followed by a _FIGURE_QUALIFIER, or longer than 6 words; dedupes on category|years. Each needs verified evidence; returns AgeRelaxation with CATEGORY scope and verified years.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Collects all age relaxations a notice states for different groups, in the authority's own words. It reads tables first, then sentences. It records 'relaxed by N years', 'the upper age limit for this group is N years', and also statements that a group gets no relaxation. A relaxation mentioned without a number is kept for review.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: Starts with extract_relaxation_rows, adds extract_relaxation_items for groups not already tabled (_group_key). Then per statements() passage with a relaxation, denial or ceiling cue and _CATEGORY hits: denial -> Fact.not_published; increment (_INCREMENT, figure taken near the cue) -> years; ceiling -> absolute_maximum; plain years -> years; none -> needs_review(None). Scopes to category and optionally a named post; adds a condition clause (subject to/only for/provided that/in accordance with). Finally drops figure-less entries for groups that already have a figure.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads other conditions besides age and qualification, such as nationality, domicile, experience, physical or medical standards, a driving licence, language or gender. Each is kept as the authority's own sentence. If a notice says nothing about, say, physical standards, no such requirement is created.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: For statements() passages of at least 25 chars, takes the first matching kind in _REQUIREMENT_CUES (NATIONALITY, DOMICILE, EXPERIENCE, PHYSICAL, MEDICAL, LICENCE, LANGUAGE, GENDER), deduped on (kind, first 70 chars), with verified evidence and optional post scope. is_essential True on essential/must/shall else None. Returns at most 40 Requirement objects.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.text: Reads the number of vacancies a notice prints, along with words like 'tentative' or 'approximate' that the authority attached. It never estimates or adds up numbers. If the notice says the vacancies will be announced later, that is recorded too.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::extra.tech: Per statements() passage: _NO_VACANCY -> VacancyCount with Fact.not_published and qualifier 'to be announced'. Otherwise the first _VACANCY count (not preceded by a digit or dot, so clause numbers are refused), non-zero and not seen before, with verified evidence; scopes by post name and _CATEGORY; qualifier is the _TENTATIVE word lower-cased. Returns at most 30.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::is_do.text: Checks whether something read as a post name is actually a document a candidate has to submit, such as a certificate, hall ticket or application form. Used everywhere post names are produced so a document checklist never shows up as a list of jobs.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::is_do.tech: True when the whitespace-normalised name is non-empty and matches _DOCUMENT_ROW at the start or contains a _DOCUMENT_WORD (whole words, so 'Photographer' does not match).

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.text: Reads the age limit printed in each post's own table row and makes it an age rule for that post only, rather than treating it as a rule for the whole exam.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.tech: For reconstructed rows with an AGE cell, matches the row's NAME/DEPARTMENT to a post (exact lower-case, then _name_key); parses _AGE_RANGE or a bare _AGE_CELL band; with verified evidence emits AgeRule(id 'age-<post id>', POST scope, min/max verified, note=post.note).

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.text: Within a given section of a notice (for example physical requirements), finds clauses that say 'For Post Code Nos. 02 & 09: ...' and attaches each clause, word for word, to those posts.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.tech: Builds a code->post map; for each `heading` regex match reads up to 6000 chars (stopping at a PARA or numbered clause heading), splits at _CODE_SCOPE matches, takes the first sentence of each clause (sentence_end) with verified evidence, and appends a Fact (note 'physical requirement') to other_requirements of each coded post. Returns None; mutates posts.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.text: Finds sentences anywhere in a notice that name posts by their codes (such as 'for Post Code 07, men only are eligible') and attaches each sentence, as printed, to those posts. Clauses already attached are skipped.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::post_.tech: On whitespace-normalised text, for each _CODE_SCOPE match takes the surrounding sentence (from the previous '. ' or ': ' to the next '. '); skips sentences over 320 chars or overlapping an existing other_requirements value; requires verified evidence; appends a Fact (note 'post-scoped statement') to each coded post not already holding it.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::print.text: Reads the total number of vacancies printed on a post table's 'Total' line, but only if the table's own rows add up exactly to that total. GovOS never calculates a total itself.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::print.tech: For each reconstructed table with a VACANCY column and a total_line ending in a number: requires every row reconstructed with a digit count summing to the printed figure and verified evidence of the total line. Returns the first VacancyCount (verified, qualifier explaining it is the printed total) or None.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::state.text: Splits a notice's text into short passages, each likely to state one rule. Table rows count as passages too, because notices put rules in tables.
tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::state.tech: Removes CRs, inserts a newline before clause numbers like '4.2 ' that follow a '.' or ';', then splits each non-empty line at '.'/';' followed by whitespace and a capital or '('. Returns stripped non-empty pieces.

tools/exam_builder/eligibility.py::vet_p.text: Splits a list of possible post names into real posts and documents.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.text: The proof behind a value: the exact words it was read from, the document's address and title, the page, what the reader thought the words said, and whether the words were confirmed to be in the document.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.tech: Dataclass: span, source_url, document_title, page (default 1), reading, status (default UNCHECKED). Property digest; method verify(source_text).

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.text: A short fingerprint of the quoted words, used to tell whether two pieces of proof are the same quote.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.tech: First 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of the whitespace-normalised span.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.text: Checks that the quoted words really appear in the document, ignoring differences in spacing and line breaks. It never trusts the reader's own claim about where it looked.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.tech: Sets and returns status: UNCHECKED if source_text is empty; NOT_IN_SOURCE if the normalised span is empty or not a substring of the normalised source; else VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Evidence.text: The three possible results of checking a quote: found word for word in the document, not in the document (so the value is rejected), or not checked because no document text was available.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Extracte.text: A value read from a document together with its proof, a confidence score based on how many clues supported it, and the list of those clues.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Extracte.tech: Dataclass: field, value, evidence (Evidence), confidence (0..1, default 0), cues_matched. Property is_usable.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Extracte.text: Says whether a read value can be used: it must not be empty and its quote must have been confirmed in the document.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::Extracte.tech: True when value is not None/''/[]/{} and evidence.status is VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::normalis.text: Squashes all runs of spaces, tabs and line breaks in text into single spaces, so a quote from a PDF that wraps lines can still be matched against the document.

tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::verified.text: Accepts a read value only if its quote is found in the document; otherwise the value is dropped entirely, not just marked uncertain.
tools/exam_builder/evidence.py::verified.tech: Calls candidate.evidence.verify(source_text) and returns the candidate if is_usable, else None.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::Blocker.text: One reason a build was stopped from publishing, naming the field and why.
tools/exam_builder/gate.py::Blocker.tech: Dataclass: field, reason, detail. __str__ formats 'field: reason — detail'.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::Blocker.__st.text: Writes the blocking reason as one readable line.
tools/exam_builder/gate.py::Blocker.__st.tech: Returns f'{field}: {reason}' plus ' — {detail}' when detail is non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::BuildState.text: How a build of an exam's record went overall: finished, paused because a network search or download failed, or failed.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateDecision.text: The final yes/no on whether a built exam record may be published: pass or block.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateReport.text: The publication check's full answer: pass or block, how the build went, every blocking reason, the gaps that were allowed through, and notes.
tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateReport.tech: Dataclass: decision, build_state, blockers, allowed, notes. Property may_publish; method summary().

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateReport.m.text: Says whether the record is allowed to be published.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateReport.s.text: Writes the publication check's result as a short readable text report.
tools/exam_builder/gate.py::GateReport.s.tech: Multi-line string: decision, build state, each blocker, allowed absences (sorted) and notes.

tools/exam_builder/gate.py::evaluate.text: The final check that decides whether a built exam record may go live. It blocks if the network failed or the build failed, if any field cites a document belonging to another exam, if a required field rests on a document that names several exams, if a required field is missing, unpublished or unreadable, if any field is only uncertainly read, if sources contradict each other, or if the record fails schema, compile or isolation checks. An optional field the authority has not published, or that GovOS could not read, is allowed through and keeps its honest state.
tools/exam_builder/gate.py::evaluate.tech: Inputs: ExamRecord plus build_state, identity_by_source (url -> IdentityVerdict), required (default REQUIRED_FIELDS from CONTRACT), conflicts, schema_ok, typecheck_ok, isolation_ok, optional completeness report (used only for notes). Blocks on PAUSED_INFRASTRUCTURE/FAILED; on a MISMATCH source whose URL is cited by a field other than officialName/authority (uncited MISMATCH sources become notes); on a FOUND required field (other than officialName/authority) whose citation URL is AMBIGUOUS. Per CONTRACT field: missing+required blocks; FOUND passes; NOT_PUBLISHED allowed (blocks if required); NOT_EXTRACTED blocks if required, else allowed with a note naming its completeness state; NEEDS_REVIEW blocks. Adds blockers for conflicts and failed schema/typecheck/isolation flags. Returns GateReport (PASS only with no blockers).

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamIden.text: A description of the exam being looked for: its id, the search query, official name, year, authority name and website, optional stage or paper, and (for exams with no distinctive words) its official post name.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamIden.tech: Frozen dataclass: exam_id, query, official_name, year, authority_name, stage, paper, authority_domain, designation (CanonicalDesignation or None). Properties aliases, designation_mode, authority_aliases.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamIden.text: The short names and words that identify this exam, worked out from the query and the official name.

The words that name the authority rather than the exam, such as its initials or the parts of its web address. These appear on every exam the authority runs, so they never identify one exam on their own.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamIden.tech: Set of: initials of authority_name's words (skipping of/and/the/for/to/in) when there are at least 2 words, plus host labels of authority_domain excluding _HOST_GENERIC labels (www, gov, nic, in, ...) and numeric labels.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamIden.text: Says whether this exam has to be recognised by its post name because none of its words are distinctive.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamRefe.text: One exam name that a document mentions about itself, with its year and the key words it carries.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::ExamRefe.tech: Dataclass: text, year, tokens (distinctive words), group (suffixes of one title phrase share a group so they are not counted as rival exams).

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::Identity.text: The result of checking whether a document belongs to an exam: the verdict, the quoted proof, the exam names that matched or competed, and the reasons.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::Identity.tech: Dataclass: verdict, evidence (Evidence or None), matched, competing, reasons. Property may_supply_facts.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::Identity.text: Only a document judged a clear match may supply facts to the exam's record; an ambiguous one may not.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::Identity.tech: True only when verdict is IdentityVerdict.MATCH.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::Identity.text: The three answers to 'does this document belong to this exam?': match, mismatch, or ambiguous.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_acronym.text: Works out the possible abbreviations of a phrase from its initials, so 'Combined Graduate Level' can be recognised as 'CGL'.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_acronym.tech: Initials of the phrase's words (skipping of/and/the/for/to/in), returned as the set of prefixes of length 2 to min(len, 6).

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_identif.text: Decides whether an exam name in a document names the exam being looked for. It is not enough to share one word: the name must carry one of the exam's own short names and add no distinctive words of its own, though words for a stage or paper and bracketed notes are allowed. Matching abbreviations also count. The authority's own name never counts on its own.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_identif.tech: Compound aliases (with a space, e.g. 'group i') are matched on their boundary; a match with no foreign unbracketed distinctive words returns True, a bare head with a different ordinal returns False. Naming aliases exclude authority_aliases (unless that leaves nothing). True if _acronyms_of(ref.text) intersects naming; with no token overlap, True only if a naming alias of 4+ chars occurs inside the joined tokens. Otherwise True if there are no foreign core tokens (unbracketed, minus aliases and _STRUCTURAL), else True only if an overlapping alias of <= 5 chars is not part of the official name.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_is_gene.text: Checks whether an exam-like phrase is made only of general process words (like 'Computer Based Examination'), which names a way of testing, not a different exam.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_is_gene.tech: True when the reference's tokens contain nothing outside _STRUCTURAL.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_verify_.text: Checks whether a document belongs to an exam that has no distinctive words, by comparing the post name in its title area with the official one. A match whose quote cannot be found word for word in the document is downgraded to ambiguous.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_verify_.tech: AMBIGUOUS for empty text; otherwise calls designation.judge(text, target.designation, year, authority_name). If the judgement has evidence, builds and verifies an Evidence; an unverified MATCH becomes AMBIGUOUS. Returns IdentityCheck carrying the judgement's verdict, matched, competing and reasons.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_year_co.text: Checks whether a mentioned exam's year differs from the year being looked for.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::_year_co.tech: True when both target.year and ref.year are set and differ.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::designat.text: Decides whether an exam must be recognised by its official post name instead of by its distinctive words. This happens only when every word of the exam's name is generic once the authority's own name is removed.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::designat.tech: True when set(target.aliases) - target.authority_aliases is empty.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::exam_ref.text: Finds every exam name a document uses to describe itself, such as 'Combined Graduate Level Examination, 2026' or 'Recruitment of Assistant Officers', with the year printed beside it. It also reads listing rows like '02/2024 - GROUP-I SERVICES'.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::exam_ref.tech: Runs _TITLE_RX over normalised text; skips phrases under 12 chars or matching _NOT_A_TITLE. Year from the phrase, else the nearest non-full-date year within 24 chars after or 48 chars before. Emits every word-suffix of the phrase (>= 12 chars) as an ExamReference sharing a group id, with distinctive_words tokens. Then adds _NUMBERED_TITLE matches (year from the notice number). Deduped by lower-case text; stops at `limit` (400).

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::field_is.text: For a document that mentions several exams, checks whether one particular fact can still be credited to this exam, because the sentence it comes from names this exam itself (in the right year). Never allowed for exams identified by post name.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::field_is.tech: False in designation mode or for an empty span; otherwise True when any exam_references(span) ref satisfies _identifies and has no year conflict.

tools/exam_builder/identity.py::verify.text: Decides whether a document's own text belongs to the exam being built. It reads the exam names the document uses about itself, then: match if it names this exam and no rival in its opening section; mismatch if it names this exam only for another year, or names only other exams; ambiguous if it names several exams up front, names none, or the proof cannot be checked. Only a match may supply facts.
tools/exam_builder/identity.py::verify.tech: Delegates to _verify_by_designation in designation mode. Else AMBIGUOUS for empty text or no exam_references. Groups refs by group; each group is matching (identifies + no year conflict; shortest), wrong_year, other (longest; skipped if all generic). Verifies evidence for the best match (prefers a year, more tokens), unverified -> AMBIGUOUS. MISMATCH if the title block (1500 chars) names a wrong-year form and no dated matching form; MATCH if matching and no others; with others, MATCH if the target is in the title block and no rival is, else AMBIGUOUS; else MISMATCH for wrong_year; AMBIGUOUS if nothing rivals; else MISMATCH.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::MANIFEST.text: The folder ('.exam_manifests') where snapshots of which documents were found for each exam are saved.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::MANIFEST.tech: Constant os.path.join('.exam_manifests') — a relative path, resolved against the current working directory.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::Manifest.text: One entry in a snapshot: a found document's address, title, kind, why it was accepted or rejected, where it was found, a fingerprint of its contents and what its own text said it was about.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::Manifest.tech: Dataclass: url, title, document_type, relevance, discovery_evidence (matched or foreign words), found_on, content_hash, identity_verdict (default 'UNCHECKED').

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SCHEMA_V.text: The version number of the snapshot file format. Older snapshots with a different version are refused rather than replayed.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SourceMa.text: A frozen snapshot of which documents were found for one exam at one moment, so a later rebuild can be compared with it. It records the documents, the rejected ones and whether the network failed. It never supplies facts itself; every document is fetched and checked again on replay.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SourceMa.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, query, authority_name, authority_domain, discovered_at, sources, rejected, schema_version, infrastructure_failed, notes. Property urls; method digest().

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SourceMa.text: A fingerprint of the set of document addresses, so two snapshots can be compared quickly.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SourceMa.tech: content_hash of the sorted source URLs joined by newlines.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::SourceMa.text: Lists the addresses of the documents in the snapshot.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::content_.text: Makes a short fingerprint of a document's contents so GovOS can tell later whether it has changed.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::content_.tech: First 24 hex chars of SHA-256 of the bytes (str is UTF-8 encoded; None -> b'').

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::from_sou.text: Turns the result of a document search into a snapshot, adding the identity verdict and content fingerprint of each document where known.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::from_sou.tech: Maps each DiscoveredDoc in docs and rejected to a ManifestSource (discovery_evidence = matched or foreign_words; content_hash and identity_verdict from the optional dicts, default '' / 'UNCHECKED'); discovered_at is local time now; copies infrastructure_failed and the log as notes.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::latest_f.text: Finds the newest saved snapshot file for an exam, if there is one.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::latest_f.tech: Returns the path for version next_version - 1, or None if that is below 1 (existence of that exact file is not checked).

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::load.text: Reads a snapshot file back in, refusing it if it was written in a different file format version.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::load.tech: Opens the file in a with-block and json.loads it; raises ValueError if schema_version != SCHEMA_VERSION; rebuilds ManifestSource lists for sources and rejected and returns a SourceManifest.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::next_ver.text: Finds the next unused version number for an exam's snapshot files.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::next_ver.tech: Returns 1 if the directory is missing; else max parsed N from files '<exam_id>.vN.json' plus 1, or 1 if none parse.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::path_for.text: Works out the file name for an exam's snapshot, such as '<exam>.v3.json', using the next free version number unless one is given.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::path_for.tech: Creates `directory` if missing (side effect), uses next_version when version is None, returns os.path.join(directory, f'{exam_id}.v{version}.json').

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::save.text: Saves a snapshot as a new version file. An existing snapshot is never overwritten, because it records what a past build actually saw.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::save.tech: Gets a new path via path_for; raises FileExistsError if it already exists; writes asdict(manifest) as UTF-8 JSON (indent 1, ensure_ascii False). Returns the path.

tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::to_sourc.text: Rebuilds the list of found documents from a snapshot without searching again, including the documents discovery turned away, so the record of what was considered survives. The documents are only named; everything after this re-downloads and re-checks them.
tools/exam_builder/manifest.py::to_sourc.tech: Creates a SourceSet whose docs and rejected are DiscoveredDocs built by one inner doc() helper (unknown kinds -> DocKind.UNKNOWN, unknown relevance -> DIRECT), copies infrastructure_failed, and logs that it was replayed.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.text: The report card for one automatic exam build: what was asked for, how it ended, why, and summaries of each step (finding the authority, reading documents, checking, the gate, building the page data, saving it).
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.tech: Dataclass with query, year, state (EngineState), reason, and dict sections resolution, identity, acquisition, verification, completeness (optional), gate, materialization, registry, reviews, plus the produced exam dict and the OrchestrationResult. Has registered, to_dict and summary helpers.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.text: Says yes or no: did this build end with the exam published?
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.tech: Property; True only when state is EngineState.REGISTERED.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.text: Writes a short, readable multi-line summary of the build for the command line: the query, the outcome, the authority, how many fields were found, completeness, the gate decision, the registry result and the reason.
