tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.tech: Builds lines from whichever sections are non-empty (resolution authority name/domain, acquisition fieldsFound/fieldsTotal/documentsKept, completenessPercentage, gate decision, registry status/examId/version, reason) and joins them with newlines.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.text: Turns the build report into a plain data form that can be stored or sent as JSON.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.tech: Returns a dict of query, year, state value, reason, the section dicts (resolution through registry) and examId taken from exam['id'] (None if no exam). Omits the orchestration object and reviews.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.text: The list of possible end results of trying to build an exam automatically: it was published, or one of several distinct reasons it was not (blocked by the quality gate, could not find the authority, the authority was ambiguous, a network or system failure, a document could not be fetched, it mixed in another exam's material, the result had the wrong shape, it lost verified facts, the registry refused it, or it was cancelled).
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Engin.tech: str Enum of build outcomes: REGISTERED, BLOCKED_BY_GATE, RESOLUTION_FAILURE, AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE, ISOLATION_VIOLATION, MATERIALIZATION_INVALID, PROJECTION_LOSS, REGISTRY_REJECTED, CANCELLED. Orchestrator states are mapped onto it via _ORCH_TO_ENGINE; failures are never collapsed into one value.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: The database store for exams GovOS built automatically from authority documents, one entry per exam and year. It only accepts an exam that passed the publication check and the page-shape checks, never overwrites a hand-authored exam, and keeps every replaced version in a history table. It can retire, fetch and list published exams.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: SQLite-backed (default 'govos.db'; ':memory:' or mode=memory uses one shared connection). Tables exam_registry (PK exam_id, cycle) and exam_registry_history (PK exam_id, cycle, version). register() requires gate.may_publish, validate_runtime_exam == [], validate_projection == [] (else MaterializationLoss), matching id, id not in the authored register (render.target_in_register) and a cycle; archives the old row then INSERT OR REPLACE with version+1. retire(), get() and list_published() (sqlite errors -> None / []).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Sets up the exam store for a given database file, creating its tables if they do not exist.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Stores db_path; for in-memory paths opens one shared sqlite3 connection with Row factory; then calls _init_db() (creates tables — a side effect on the target database).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Opens a connection to the exam store's database.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Returns the shared connection for in-memory stores, else a new sqlite3 connection with row_factory sqlite3.Row.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Creates the exam store's two tables (current entries and history) if they are missing.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Executes DDL and HISTORY_DDL (CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS), commits and releases the connection.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Closes a database connection after use, except for the shared in-memory one.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Calls c.close() unless the store is in-memory.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Turns one saved database row back into a registry entry the code can work with.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Internal helper: maps a sqlite3.Row from exam_registry into a RegistryRecord, JSON-decoding exam_json, record_json and the nullable completeness_json, and converting published/retired to bool.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Looks up the live (published and not retired) version of one machine-built exam, for a given year or, if no year is given, the latest year.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Queries exam_registry for published = 1 AND retired = 0, for (exam_id, cycle) or, without a cycle, ORDER BY cycle DESC LIMIT 1. Returns a RegistryRecord via _row, or None if absent or on any sqlite3.Error; the connection is released on every path.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Lists every earlier version of one exam and year that was later replaced, oldest first.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: SELECT from exam_registry_history by exam_id and cycle ORDER BY version; returns dicts with version, gateDecision, exam, record, completeness (JSON-decoded), createdAt, updatedAt, supersededAt.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Lists every machine-built exam currently live. If the database is broken it returns an empty list rather than an error, so the hand-written exams still show.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: SELECTs all published, unretired exam_registry rows ordered by exam_id, cycle and returns them as RegistryRecords. Any sqlite3.Error yields []. Connection always released.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Puts a machine-built exam into GovOS's live list of exams that candidates can see. Before saving, it checks that the exam passed the publishing gate, has the shape the website expects, lost none of its verified facts, is not one of the hand-written exams, and states which year (cycle) it is for. If an older version is already saved, that older version is archived first so nothing shown before is lost.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Takes an ExamRecord, its GateReport, the materialized runtime exam dict, optional completeness report, cycle and data.ts path. Raises RegistryRejected if the gate did not pass (may_publish false), validate_runtime_exam reports errors, the payload id differs from rec.exam_id, target_in_register finds the id among authored exams, or no cycle can be derived (from the argument, exam['cycle'] or get_exam_cycle); raises MaterializationLoss if validate_projection finds lost facts. On success, in one transaction it copies any existing (exam_id, cycle) row into exam_registry_history, then INSERT OR REPLACEs exam_registry with version+1 (published=1, retired=0), and returns a RegistryRecord.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.text: Takes a machine-built exam out of the live list without deleting it, either for one year or for every year.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::ExamR.tech: Sets retired = 1 on exam_registry rows for exam_id, limited to one cycle when given. Returns True if any row changed. Rows are kept, not deleted.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::MATER.text: A version label ('materialize-2') stamped on every exam page built by this step, so it is clear which version of the converter produced it.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::MATER.tech: Constant string written to exam['materialization']['version'] by materialize_exam.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Mater.text: The error raised when a fact that was confirmed in an exam's master record would be silently lost on the way to the page candidates see.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Mater.tech: ValueError subclass; raised by ExamRegistry.register when validate_projection returns losses.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.text: One stored entry in the live list of machine-built exams: the exam, its year, authority, version, publication check result, the page data, the master record snapshot, the completeness report, timestamps and whether it is retired.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.tech: Dataclass mirroring an exam_registry row: exam_id, cycle, authority_name, authority_domain, official_name, version, gate_decision, published, exam, record, completeness, created_at, updated_at, retired. Method meta().

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.text: Gives a short summary of a stored exam entry, without the full page data.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of the scalar fields plus origin 'MACHINE_ACQUIRED' (no exam/record/completeness payloads).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.text: The error raised when a built exam page is refused entry to the live list of exams, with the reason.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::Regis.tech: ValueError subclass raised by ExamRegistry.register (gate not PASS, contract errors, id mismatch, authored id, missing cycle).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_NoCl.text: A stand-in that tells the study-order generator Claude is switched off, so building an exam page never depends on an AI reply.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_NoCl.tech: Stub gateway with name 'none' and is_enabled() returning False; passed to roadmap_guidance.generate.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_NoCl.text: Always says Claude is not available.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_admi.text: Prepares the admit card events for the page. An older single-card style reading is turned into one event in its own words, never presented as a date.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_admi.tech: Uses _event_list(rec, 'admitCard', 'admit'); items lacking kind or officialLabel become {kind 'OTHER', officialLabel, status VERIFIED if the field is ok else NEEDS_REVIEW, instructions [text], portalUrl, provenance}. Sets examId.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_age_.text: Prepares the age relaxations the notice itself printed for different groups. Nothing is filled in from general national rules. A relaxation with a condition or no clear figure is shown in the notice's words and marked for review, so it is not added to an age limit.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_age_.tech: From a usable dict 'ageLimits' value's relaxations: skips items without a category or without numeric years/maximumAge (unless NEEDS_REVIEW with a condition). Entry: category, status VERIFIED only if f.ok and the item status is VERIFIED, provenance with excerpt, plus years, maximumAge, condition, appliesToPostId when present.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_answ.text: Prepares the list of official answer keys for the page.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_appl.text: Builds the application guide for the exam page: the portal, the how-to-apply steps as the notice states them, photo and signature rules, required documents and fee. Certificate rules and common rejection reasons are left empty because no source supplies them.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_appl.tech: Returns {officialPortal (_portal_link), otrSteps (one step from _how_to_apply_lines when howToApply is usable), photoRules/signatureRules (_upload_spec from photoSignatureGuidelines photograph/signature lists), certificateRules: [], rejectionPitfalls: []} plus requiredDocuments and fee when present.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_atta.text: Adds the 'where did this come from' evidence to the built exam page: sources for the vacancy total and the age reference date, links between a correction and the dates it changed, evidence for calculated pattern figures, and a practice application form built from the same facts. Every source is then stamped with an id and type.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_atta.tech: Mutates exam: factEvidence for vacanciesTotal and crucialEligibilityDate via runtime_evidence.fact_provenance; corrigendums with id 'rev-<dateId>' copy that date's provenance; derive_pattern_evidence(patternTree); build_simulator(exam) stored as applicationGuide.simulator when non-empty; stamp_exam(exam).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_clea.text: Tidies a piece of text by collapsing spaces and cutting it to a maximum length.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_clea.tech: Collapses whitespace in str(text or ''), strips, truncates to `limit` (default 600).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_corr.text: Prepares the list of corrections to the notice for the page: each correction's title, notice number, dates, quoted words, link and what changed from old to new. If the authority's own page moved the last date, a correction entry explaining that is added.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_corr.tech: From a usable 'corrigenda' list builds entries with provenance overridden by the entry's own sourceTitle/sourceUrl/evidenceSpan (pageNumber cleared when the URL differs), title, noticeNumber, publishedDate (explicit, else effectiveDate, first 10 chars), effectiveDate, summary (evidence span + note), pdfUrl, status ACTIVE/SUPERSEDED, diffSummary. Appends a 'corr-<exam>-lastdate' entry from a usable 'lastDateSuperseded' value describing notice date -> page date.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_cuto.text: Prepares the cut-off marks history for the page exactly as recorded: year, stage, category, post, value and type. A figure is only labelled as the first stage's cut-off if the record says so.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_cuto.tech: From a usable 'cutoffs' list: value from value/cutoffMarks/marks/tier1Cutoff (must be float-convertible), year from the first 4 chars (must be int); entries carry category (default 'Not stated'), value, stage, post, cutoffType, provenance (item's or indexed field), plus tier1Cutoff/tier2Cutoff/postsEligible when present.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_date.text: Prepares the exam's important dates for the page, each with its type, label, date, whether it is tentative, its status and its source. Dates of a type the page does not know are left out (the page's list includes OTHER for a printed date no specific type names). If the notice's original last date was later replaced, it is added as a struck-through 'superseded' entry and linked to the date that replaced it.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_date.tech: From a usable 'dates' list keeps rows whose type is in _DATE_TYPES (which includes OTHER); emits id, type, label, dateTimeStr, timezone (default IST), isTentative, status (AVAILABLE unless SUPERSEDED), row provenance or the field's, optional stageAssociation/stageLabel/displayWhen. Collects supersededBy links. If 'lastDateSuperseded' is usable, appends a SUPERSEDED APPLICATION_CLOSE row and links it to the single AVAILABLE close date. Calls runtime_evidence.link_revisions(out, replaced).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_elig.text: Builds the short summary cards on the eligibility section: age limits, educational qualification, number of attempts and fee, each in the notice's words with its source. If posts have different age limits, the card shows the whole spread and says so instead of one figure.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_elig.tech: For ageLimits, qualification, attempts, fee fields that are usable and cited: ageLimits with differing minima/maxima -> spread text; else 'min to max years' with asOn and DOB window; dict with text -> text; fee components -> 'label: Rs. N' joined; fee amounts -> 'Rs. a / Rs. b'; other dict -> citation excerpt or str(v)[:400]. Returns [{title, body, provenance}].

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_even.text: Copies a list of events from the master record (such as admit card notices or results) for the page, making sure each has an id and a source; an event without its own source borrows the field's.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_even.tech: Requires a usable field; wraps a non-list value in a list; deep-copies dict items, setdefault id '<suffix>-<exam>-<i>', and fills an empty provenance from the field's _prov with an indexed id.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_exam.text: Prepares the exam-day checklist items (documents to carry, timing, allowed and banned items, centre instructions), each with its source.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_exam.tech: From a usable 'examDayChecklist' list keeps items with a description; category forced into _EXAM_DAY_CATEGORIES (default CENTRE_INSTRUCTIONS); emits id, category, title (or description), description, isMandatory, provenance with excerpt/page.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_faqs.text: Prepares the exam's frequently asked questions for the page, each with its answer, the notice clause and its source.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_faqs.tech: From a usable 'faqs' list keeps items with question and answer; emits id faq-<exam>-<i>, question, answer, officialClause (default 'Official clause') and provenance with per-item excerpt, page and clause.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_fee_.text: Prepares the application fee details exactly as the notice printed them: amounts, rules by category, named fee parts, accepted payment methods and the groups exempted. Nothing is calculated and no group is assumed exempt.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_fee_.tech: Returns None if neither 'fee' nor 'feeExemptions' is usable. Builds {amounts, rules, acceptedModes, exemptions}: amounts from amounts/amount (deduped strings), modes, rules (scope, amount, isExempt only when True), fee components appended as rules with feeType/statedAs and their amount; a non-dict fee becomes one amount. Adds statedAs (citation excerpt) and provenance; exemptions carry category, statedAs, provenance and optional exemptedFeeType.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_garb.text: Spots a name that is empty or only punctuation, fractions or numbers, which is leftover noise from a PDF table rather than a real name.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_garb.tech: True when name is empty or fully matches _GARBAGE_NODE_RX (non-word chars, digits, vulgar fractions, whitespace).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_how_.text: Turns the 'how to apply' instructions read from the notice into tidy readable lines, one per step, in the notice's own words.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_how_.tech: List of dicts -> 'title — description' (or whichever is present; title omitted if contained in the description); list of strings, a dict's 'text', or a scalar are whitespace-collapsed. Returns at most 20 lines.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_mate.text: The last steps of a build, shared by fresh builds and re-builds: convert the checked record into the data the website shows, make sure it has the right shape and has kept every verified fact, then save it to the live registry. Each kind of failure is reported separately and nothing is saved.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_mate.tech: Runs materialize_exam(rec, cycle, completeness, gate), validate_runtime_exam and (if no errors) validate_projection; records out.materialization (errors, losses, MATERIALIZER_VERSION, postsWithoutPrintedGroup, heldForReview) and gate.runtimeDecision. Returns MATERIALIZATION_INVALID on contract errors, PROJECTION_LOSS on losses, else calls registry.register (default ExamRegistry()), mapping MaterializationLoss to PROJECTION_LOSS and RegistryRejected to REGISTRY_REJECTED. On success sets REGISTERED with examId, cycle and version. Mutates and returns out.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_minu.text: Reads a duration like '90 minutes' or '2 hours' and returns it as a number of minutes.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_minu.tech: First _MINUTES_RX match -> int; else _HOURS_RX -> round(hours * 60); else None.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_noti.text: Works out which document the exam's facts were mainly read from (the notice), by finding the PDF cited most often across the record's fields.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_noti.tech: Visits fields in sorted name order (excluding officialName and authority); counts usable citations whose URL contains '/preview/' or ends in .pdf. Returns (most-cited URL, first field citing it), ties broken by URL; ('', None) if none.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_offi.text: Builds the Official Links list: the authority's website, the online application portal (or a note that the printed portal is not on the authority's current site), and the authority's own pages for this recruitment, such as its exam page or hall-ticket service, where the page's own text identified it as this exam.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_offi.tech: Starts with the official_domain link (no provenance). Adds the _portal_link URL when it differs from the domain (with applicationPortal provenance if ok), or a 'named in the notice' entry carrying the note. Adds non-PDF 'officialSources' entries of kind EXAM_PAGE or ADMIT_CARD with identity MATCH, each with a generated OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED provenance (pageNumber None, excerpt = title).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_offi.text: Prepares the list of official question papers for the page. It handles both the newer format and an older list of 'label: link' pairs.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_offi.tech: Keeps _event_list items carrying identity and url; if none and the field value is a dict, builds one entry per sorted (label, url) with title after '::', identity {examId, describe}, status VERIFIED/NEEDS_REVIEW by f.ok and indexed provenance.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_over.text: Writes the short overview paragraph for an exam: its name and authority, the number of vacancies (saying 'approximately' only if the notice did), the current application closing date, and a note that it was read from the authority's own documents.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_over.tech: Joins: title/authority; vacancies via _vacancy_count; the first APPLICATION_CLOSE date not SUPERSEDED and not tentative (displayWhen, else dateTimeStr with a trailing 00:00 removed); a fixed provenance sentence.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_pape.text: Turns a flat row describing one paper (for example 'Paper-I, Civil Engineering, 150 marks, 150 minutes') into a paper entry of the exam pattern, adding nothing the row did not print.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_pape.tech: Builds {id paper-row-<i>, level PAPER, levelLabel 'Paper', name 'label — name', code label, status} plus numeric marks/questions, duration, and when given negativeMarking with derived ['negativeMarking'].

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_path.text: Checks whether a built exam page has something filled in at a given location, such as 'applicationGuide.fee' or a card titled 'Age limits'.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_path.tech: Supports 'a|b' (either), 'list[Title]' (a card in list with that title and a non-empty body) and dotted object paths; True when the final value is not None/''/[]/{}.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.text: Accepts the exam pattern in any of the shapes the different readers produce and turns it into one list of parts, or explains why there is nothing to show.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.tech: Dict with 'papers' rows -> _paper_row_node per row (with the scheme's negativeMarking); dict without rows -> ([], reason). List of row dicts with paper/label and no tree keys -> paper nodes; other lists -> dict nodes as-is. Anything else -> ([], 'the reading is not a pattern structure').

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.text: Converts one part of the exam pattern (a stage, paper, subject or section) into the form the exam page shows. Only figures that were actually read are kept. If a figure looks unreliable, such as an impossibly high number of questions or one the reader was unsure of, the numbers are withheld (but the name and structure kept) and the reason is logged.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.tech: Returns None (logging to `withheld`) for _garbage_name names. Level from the structural 'level' if in _PATTERN_LEVELS, else the label, else OTHER. Copies id, levelLabel, name, status, provenance, code, order. Marks/questions/duration (duration via _minutes) are kept only when not unreliable (status NEEDS_REVIEW or questions > 300), else logged. Copies negativeMarking, mode, languages (max 8), selected qualifying keys and _PATTERN_PASSTHROUGH fields, dropping derived per-question figures of an unreliable node; prunes 'derived' to published keys; recurses into children; drops None values.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.text: Builds the exam pattern tree for the page from the master record. If nothing usable remains, the pattern is recorded as held for review with the reason.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_patt.tech: Requires a usable 'examPattern' field; normalises via _pattern_input and maps through _pattern_node (logging into `withheld`). If the tree is empty and `held` is given, sets held['examPattern'] with the reason and raw value.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_port.text: Picks the application portal link to show. If the portal address printed in the notice is on the authority's current website, it is used. If not (for example, the authority has since been renamed and the old address may not work), the authority's own site is linked instead, with a note quoting the printed address.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_port.tech: Returns (url, note). Non-http or missing applicationPortal -> (official_domain, ''); same_estate(printed host, own host) -> (printed, ''); else (official_domain, explanatory note naming the printed URL).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_post.text: Prepares the list of posts for the exam page: name, department, pay, Group (only where printed), age band, post code, vacancies, qualification, physical requirements and conditions, each citing its row in the notice. Anything that looks like a document or certificate rather than a post is held back for review instead of being shown.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_post.tech: Returns (rows, names without a printed group, held items). For up to 80 items of a usable 'posts' field: name from postName/name, classification from the item or emit.classification_of; is_document_not_post names go to held. Row: id post-<exam>-<i>, postName with _GROUP_TAIL_RX stripped, department, payLevel or payScale (a 'n-n' range of 4+ digit figures counts as a scale), classification, min/maxAge from the post's own values else _single_age_band, provenance with the row's evidenceSpan/page. Optional postCode, vacancies, specialQualification, physicalRequired/physicalNote, postConditions.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_prov.text: Builds the source record (where a fact came from) for one field of the exam's master record, if that field has a citation.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_prov.tech: Returns f.citation.to_provenance(prov_id=f'prov-{exam_id}-{suffix}', level=f.verification_level), or None when the field has no citation.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_reco.text: Takes a full copy of the exam's master record (each field's status, value, note and source) so it can be kept for audit alongside the published page.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_reco.tech: Returns {examId, code, title, authorityName, officialDomain, sourcesRead, fields: {name: {status, note, value (JSON round-tripped), citation (__dict__ or None)}}}.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_requ.text: Prepares the list of documents a candidate must have for the application guide, each with its specifications and the notice's quote. Names that are only stray symbols or numbers are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_requ.tech: From up to 60 items of a usable 'requiredDocuments' list: dicts give id, name, required (default True), specifications and per-item provenance (excerpt/page); strings give a required item with no specs. Skips empty or _garbage_name names.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_reso.text: Builds the list of official links for the exam: the notice PDF, the online application portal, result and verification notices (newest first), other official documents the record was read from, and published question papers. Only links are stored, never the files themselves.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_reso.tech: Emits resource dicts: the notice from _notice_url (DIRECT_PDF, isEssential); the portal when applicationPortal is an http string (URL from _portal_link, its note as description); up to 20 results with http documentUrl sorted by declaredAt desc (isEssential for SELECTION/FINAL_RESULT); 'officialSources' entries with identity MATCH (PDF vs portal by .pdf or /preview/ and kind != EXAM_PAGE); up to 12 entries of a dict-valued 'officialPapers' field. URLs are deduped across groups except papers.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_resu.text: Prepares the list of official result announcements for the page.

Prepares the 'what happens next after a result' steps. Steps quoted from the authority's own document are marked as official; steps GovOS worked out from the result and the pattern are clearly marked as GovOS guidance, not official statements.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_resu.tech: From a usable 'nextSteps' list: items with source 'OFFICIAL_RULE' -> isGuidance False with provenance FACT/OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED from the item's document/page/evidence; others -> isGuidance True, a 'Derived by GovOS...' basis, and provenance marked RECOMMENDATION/UNDER_VERIFICATION (pointed at the item's document and basis page when given). All have status AWAITING_RESULT, headline, summary, empty actions, fromStage, nextStage.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_sect.text: Records, for each section of the exam page, whether its content is confirmed, missing or under review, so the page can tell 'the authority has not published this' apart from 'GovOS has not finished this'. A section whose content was held back is shown as under review, and a section GovOS would generate itself (like a study roadmap) is marked 'not yet generated' when empty.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_sect.tech: Returns {} without a report. Per report section: VERIFIED_AVAILABLE becomes NEEDS_REVIEW (with a summary) when any of its fields is wholly held; sections in _DERIVED_SECTION_CONTENT (roadmap, mock-tests) with no runtime content and state SUPPORTED_AND_PROJECTED/RUNTIME_DERIVED/NOT_YET_PUBLISHED become NOT_YET_GENERATED, noting a missing patternTree. Emits {state, nature, studentStatusSummary, sectionNum, isApplicable} keyed by section_id.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_sing.text: Gives the one age range that applies to the whole exam, but only if the notice states a single range. If different posts have different limits, it returns zero, which the site reads as 'not published' rather than as a real limit.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_sing.tech: Returns (minAge, maxAge) as ints from a field passing f.ok, or (0, 0) when the field is absent/not ok, or minima/maxima lists hold more than one distinct value; non-numeric values become 0.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_slug.text: Turns a title into a short id made of lower-case letters, digits and dashes.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_slug.tech: Lower-case, non-alphanumeric runs -> '-', stripped, max 48 chars, 'x' if empty.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_stud.text: Produces a suggested study order over the exam's confirmed syllabus topics, labelled as GovOS guidance. It adds no hours, durations or new topics, and is skipped if the syllabus is not confirmed.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_stud.tech: Requires the 'syllabus' field to pass f.ok and a non-empty flat syllabus; calls verification.roadmap_guidance.generate(exam_id, syllabus, authority, exam_label, gateway=_NoClaude()); returns None if not available, else g.as_dict() with a 'basis' sentence.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_subj.text: Uses a syllabus heading, tidied, as the subject name; if it is empty, uses 'Syllabus'.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_syll.text: Takes the syllabus tree already read from the notice and passes it through for the page, making sure no two parts share the same id.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_syll.tech: Deep-copies (JSON round trip) the usable 'syllabus' list's dict nodes that have a title, then calls _unique_node_ids. Returns [] when not usable.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_uniq.text: Fixes repeated ids in a syllabus tree by giving later repeats a new id based on their parent's id, without changing any content.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_uniq.tech: Depth-first; a repeated id under a parent becomes '<parent>-<last id segment>' (with -2, -3... until unique) and its provenance id is updated to 'prov-<new id>'. First occurrence keeps its id. Mutates in place.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_uplo.text: Builds the photo or signature upload instructions for the application guide using only the notice's own sentences. Size, format and dimension slots are left empty rather than guessed.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_uplo.tech: Returns {documentType, dimensions:'', fileFormat:'', fileSize:'', rules (cleaned, non-empty, max 20), sampleDescription:''} plus provenance when given.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_vaca.text: Prepares the vacancy break-up tables (how many posts per category, fresh and carried forward) for the exam page, exactly as the authority printed the columns, with each row linked to its post and each table citing its document, pages and the checks it passed.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_vaca.tech: Requires a usable list 'vacancyBreakup' field. Maps canonical post ids to runtime ids by position (post-<exam>-<i>, first 80). For each table emits id vb-<exam>-<i>, document title/url, pages, checks, columns (header paths joined ' / '), rows (postId, postCode, printedName, zone, fresh/carriedForward counts, optional postTotal, page), tableTotal, and provenance overridden with the table's document, first page and checks as excerpt.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_vaca.text: Turns a vacancy figure into plain digits for display, and notes whether the notice called it approximate. A figure from a printed table total is never called approximate.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::_vaca.tech: Accepts a dict {count, isApproximate}, a number or a string; strips commas; returns (digit string or '', is_approximate). Non-dict inputs always return False for approximate.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::build.text: The single front door for building any exam automatically. Give it an exam name and year; it finds the official authority, reads its documents, checks the facts, and runs the publishing gate. Only if everything passes does it turn the result into page data and save it to the live registry. It never edits the hand-written exam file, and any failure returns a clear reason with nothing published.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::build.tech: Calls orchestrate(..., dry_run=True) with the given search/Claude/cache/review/replay/authority_discovery options, then fills an EngineBuildResult with resolution, identity verdicts, acquisition counts by Status, verification and completeness, and gate blockers. If should_continue() returns False it returns CANCELLED. If the orchestration state is not STAGED, or there is no build/gate, or the gate does not allow publishing, it returns the mapped EngineState (default BLOCKED_BY_GATE) with registry NOT_REGISTERED. Otherwise derives the cycle (resolved year, argument, or get_exam_cycle) and delegates to _materialize_and_publish.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::flat_.text: Turns the syllabus tree into a flat list of topics with subtopics, which the syllabus map, checklist and topic views use. The subject is the heading each topic sits under; if the top heading is just the word 'Syllabus', its papers become the subjects. No weightage is invented: every weight is zero because the authority printed none.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::flat_.tech: Walks each root: a bare 'Syllabus'/'Syllabi' root with children uses each child (or each child of a 'Stage'-labelled child) as the subject; otherwise the root title is the subject. A node with no children is a topic; one whose children are all leaves is a topic with those leaves as subtopics (max 40); deeper branches recurse, their leaves becoming topics. Topics: id syltopic-<n>-<slug>, subject, tier 'BOTH', topicName, subtopics, weightagePercentage 0, avgQuestions 0, isHighYield False, officialProvenance. Garbage titles skipped; max 200 topics.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::main.text: Command-line entry point: build one named exam (optionally for a year) and print the result summary.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::main.tech: argparse CLI taking exam, --year, --db (default govos.db) and --claude; runs build_exam with ExamRegistry(args.db), prints summary(), returns exit code 0 if registered else 1.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::mater.text: Converts an exam's master record (read from the authority's documents) into the full exam page data the website shows: overview, posts, dates, stages, syllabus, corrections, cut-offs, resources, FAQs, application guide, eligibility cards, official links and more. Only sourced values are written; anything missing stays empty rather than invented. Items held back for review are listed with reasons, and section states and evidence are attached.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::mater.tech: Input ExamRecord, optional cycle, completeness report and gate report; returns a runtime Exam dict. Uses _posts (document-like candidates into heldForReview), vacancies via _vacancy_count (NEEDS_REVIEW vacancies held), _pattern_tree, _syllabus_tree, stages_from_pattern, flat_syllabus_from_tree, _dates, _corrigendums, _cutoffs, _resources, _faqs, _application_guide, _eligibility_highlights, _official_links; crucialEligibilityDate from ageLimits.asOn only; practiceQuestions and roadmapTracks empty; origin MACHINE_ACQUIRED. Adds optional studyGuidance, patternTree, syllabusTree, examDayChecklist, admitCardEvents, officialPapers, answerKeys, resultDeclarations, resultNextSteps, ageRelaxations, vacancyBreakups when non-empty. Then _attach_evidence, sectionStates and a materialization ledger (version, UTC timestamp, gate decision, posts without printed group, heldForReview).

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::recor.text: Rebuilds the full checked exam record from the copy saved in the registry, exactly as it was, so it can be turned into page data again.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::recor.tech: Constructs an ExamRecord from snapshot keys examId, code, title, authorityName, officialDomain; extends sources_read; for each fields entry sets a Field with Status(status), value, Citation(**citation) when a dict, and note. Imports Citation from exam_authoring.record lazily.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::remat.text: Re-runs the final build steps on an exam already in the registry, without reading any website again. Used when the way GovOS turns records into page data has changed, or to apply a person's review decisions. The quality gate is checked again before anything is saved.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::remat.tech: Loads registry.get(exam_id, cycle); returns NOT_REGISTERED if absent. Rebuilds the record via record_from_snapshot, optionally applies review.apply_reviews, re-evaluates completeness (evaluate_completeness, keeping fields previously SOURCE_NOT_FOUND_AFTER_SEARCH, infrastructure_failed=False) and the gate (gate.evaluate). If the gate does not pass returns with blockers; otherwise calls _materialize_and_publish into target or the same registry using the row's cycle. No network access.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::stage.text: Builds the older 'stages' list from the exam pattern tree: one stage for each top-level part the tree marks as a stage, with its sections. Figures the tree does not state are set to zero and listed as 'not stated', so the page can say so instead of showing '0 marks'.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::stage.tech: For each root node with level 'STAGE': id, stageNumber, stageName, tier (code, levelLabel or 'Stage N'), durationMinutes/totalQuestions/totalMarks (0 when absent, listed in unstatedFields), negativeMarking, mode, qualifyingNature (qualifying.asPrinted), sections from children (name, up to 20 module names, numeric figures or 0, negativeMarking), derivedFrom 'patternTree', provenance.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::valid.text: Makes sure nothing confirmed in the exam's master record went missing when the candidate-facing page was built. Every confirmed field must appear where it belongs, or be listed as held back with a reason; lists must not lose items; stages must exist if the pattern names them; and every official item must carry its source.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::valid.tech: Returns a list of loss strings. For each PROJECTION_MAP field that is FOUND with a value, unless wholly held in materialization.heldForReview, every mapped path must pass _path_has_content. For _ITEM_PRESERVING pairs, runtime count must be >= canonical dict items (dates exclude the '-close-superseded' row). Flags a STAGE-bearing patternTree with empty stages, and any item in _PROVENANCED collections without a non-empty provenance dict.

tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::valid.text: Checks that a built exam page has the shape the website expects: every required field present with the right type, an id starting with 'exam-', complete dates and posts, no two items sharing an id, a valid rules group and application guide, and properly identified evidence. It checks structure only, not whether facts are true.
tools/exam_builder/materialize.py::valid.tech: Returns a list of error strings ([] = valid). Checks RUNTIME_EXAM_REQUIRED keys and types (bool not accepted for non-bool), 'exam-' id prefix, each date's required keys and type within _DATE_TYPES, each post's postName and string classification, repeated ids (recursively through children) in dates/posts/resultDeclarations/admitCardEvents/syllabusTree/vacancyBreakups, globalRuleGroup id/operator/rules, applicationGuide required keys, then up to 20 runtime_evidence.evidence_problems.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::FieldDecisi.text: A record of the decision about one detail of a post, with the old and new values and the reason.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::FieldDecisi.tech: Dataclass: field name, outcome (FieldOutcome), existing, incoming, reason.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::FieldOutcom.text: The possible outcomes for one detail of a post (job) when merging: kept, confirmed, added, or held for review.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::FieldOutcom.tech: str Enum: KEPT, CONFIRMED, ADDED, UNDER_REVIEW.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::IDENTITY_TH.text: The minimum similarity score (0.85) at which two post names are treated as the same post.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::IDENTITY_TH.tech: Constant 0.85 used by merge_posts; below it posts are not merged.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeAction.text: The possible outcomes when a newly read fact meets what the exam record already holds: added as new, confirmed, replaced by an official correction, in conflict, or untouched.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeAction.tech: str Enum: ADDED, CONFIRMED, SUPERSEDED, CONFLICTED, UNCHANGED. Used by milestone and post merge reports.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeDecisi.text: A record of one merge decision about a date or event: what was decided, for which kind of event, the old and new readings, and why.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeDecisi.tech: Dataclass: action (MergeAction), kind, existing and incoming Milestone (optional), reason. describe() prints the compared values.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeDecisi.text: Prints a one-line description of a decision showing the two values that were actually compared.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeDecisi.tech: When both milestones exist uses comparable_values (so a window is compared by its matching end), else each side's effective_date; returns a fixed-width line 'ACTION kind left -> right' with '—' for missing values.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.text: The result of merging dates: the combined list of events and every decision that produced it.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.tech: Dataclass with milestones and decisions lists, plus of(), has_conflicts and summary() helpers.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.text: Says whether any two readings disagreed without either claiming to correct the other.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.tech: Property: True if any decision is CONFLICTED.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.text: Picks out the decisions of one particular kind, such as all conflicts.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.tech: Returns the decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.text: Counts how many decisions of each kind were made.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::MergeReport.tech: Returns a dict mapping action value to count over decisions.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostDecisio.text: A record of the decision about one whole post when merging, including the per-detail decisions and how sure GovOS is that the two names mean the same post.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostDecisio.tech: Dataclass: action (MergeAction), name, post_id, fields (list of FieldDecision), reason, identity score (float).

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostDecisio.text: Finds the decision about one named detail of the post.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostDecisio.tech: Returns the first FieldDecision whose field equals name, or None.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.text: The result of merging posts: every post-level decision.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.tech: Dataclass holding decisions (list of PostDecision) with of(), summary() and fields_of() helpers.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.text: Lists every post detail that ended with a given outcome, for example everything held for review.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.tech: Returns (PostDecision, FieldDecision) pairs across all decisions whose field outcome is the given FieldOutcome.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.text: Picks out the post decisions of one kind.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.tech: Returns decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.text: Counts how many posts got each kind of decision.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::PostMergeRe.tech: Returns a dict of action value -> count.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_absorb_evi.text: When two readings agree, adds the second one's supporting quotations to the first, without duplicating any.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_absorb_evi.tech: For starts_at and ends_at, appends evidence from other to keeper unless (source_id, span_digest) is already present. Mutates keeper.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_age_decisi.text: Decides what to do with a post's age limits: keep the record's if the document states none or only part, add the document's if the record had none, confirm if they match, otherwise hold for review.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_age_decisi.tech: rule is an age rule with minimum_age/maximum_age values. No rule or a missing end -> KEPT; record missing either end -> ADDED; equal as floats -> CONFIRMED; else UNDER_REVIEW. Returns a FieldDecision for 'age'.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_claims_to_.text: Checks whether a new reading says it is changing an earlier one (postponed, rescheduled, cancelled), or comes from a corrigendum (a correction notice). Merely printing a different date does not count.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_claims_to_.tech: True if incoming.state is RESCHEDULED, POSTPONED or CANCELLED, or source.kind is SourceKind.CORRIGENDUM.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_classifica.text: Decides what to do with a post's group classification. If only the document states it, it is added; if both agree, confirmed; if they differ, or the record claims a group the document does not print, it is held for review rather than shown as the authority's own.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_classifica.tech: incoming counts as stated if it has_value. Neither -> KEPT; only incoming -> ADDED; only existing -> UNDER_REVIEW (unsupported); same letter per _same_classification -> CONFIRMED; else UNDER_REVIEW. Returns a FieldDecision for 'classification'.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_classifica.text: Pulls the group letter (A, B, C or D) out of a classification such as "Group 'B' (Non-Gazetted)".
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_classifica.tech: Regex for 'group' plus optional dash/quote and a letter a-d, case-insensitive; returns the lowercase letter or ''.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_kinds_alig.text: Decides whether two event types are about the same thing, treating an application window and its opening or closing date as related.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_kinds_alig.tech: True if kinds are equal, or one is APPLICATION_WINDOW/CORRECTION_WINDOW and the other is that window's START or END kind (from _WINDOW_ENDS).

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_name_token.text: Breaks a post's name into its distinctive words, ignoring common words like 'officer' or 'assistant' and bracketed abbreviations, so names can be compared.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_name_token.tech: Removes bracketed abbreviations via _ABBREVIATION, lowercases, splits on non-alphanumerics and keeps words longer than one character that are not in _COMMON_POST_WORDS. Returns a set.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_same_class.text: Checks whether two classifications name the same group letter.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_same_class.tech: True when both _classification_letter results are non-empty and equal.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_same_value.text: Checks whether two readings point to the same date.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::_same_value.tech: Uses comparable_values; True when both are equal and not None.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::comparable_.text: Chooses the two dates to compare. If one side is a whole window and the other is just its closing date, it compares the window's closing date with that date, rather than mixing up opening and closing.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::comparable_.tech: For window vs START kind, pairs starts_at (falling back to ends_at) on both sides; for window vs END kind, pairs ends_at (falling back to starts_at); orientation preserved as (a, b). Otherwise returns (a.effective_date, b.effective_date).

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::matches.text: Decides whether a newly read event and an existing one are about the same thing: same type of event, same part of the exam (for example the same paper), and the same year if both say one.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::matches.tech: Requires _kinds_align, str(scope) equality, and equal cycle when both cycles are non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::merge_miles.text: Folds newly read exam dates into the dates the record already holds, without deleting anything. A matching date with the same value is confirmed and gains a source; one an official correction says it changes is kept but marked as replaced; two different dates with no stated correction are both kept and flagged for a person to review; anything new is added.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::merge_miles.tech: For each existing milestone finds the first unused incoming one that matches(). No partner or partner with no effective_date -> UNCHANGED. _same_value -> CONFIRMED, _absorb_evidence, status raised to VERIFIED if the partner is. _claims_to_revise(partner, source) -> SUPERSEDED: sets old.superseded_by, partner.supersedes and revision_source_id, keeps both. Otherwise CONFLICTED: both set NEEDS_REVIEW with an explanatory note. Unused incoming become ADDED. Milestones are sorted by (effective_date or '9999', kind). Mutates the input milestones; returns a MergeReport.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::merge_posts.text: Compares the posts (jobs) a document lists with the ones the exam record already holds, one detail at a time. A post is matched only when the names are clearly the same post; if two document posts match equally well nothing is merged. For a matched post the record's wording is kept, and the group and age are confirmed, added or held for review. Posts only in the document are reported as new.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::merge_posts.tech: Indexes age_rules by POST scope ref. For each existing row (dict with postName, id, classification, minAge, maxAge, department, payLevel, payScale) scores incoming posts with post_identity. Best < IDENTITY_THRESHOLD -> UNCHANGED; runner-up also >= threshold -> CONFLICTED (ambiguous). Otherwise builds FieldDecisions: name KEPT, _classification_decision, _age_decision with the matched post's rule, and KEPT for present department/payLevel/payScale; action CONFIRMED unless any UNDER_REVIEW, then CONFLICTED. Unmatched incoming posts -> ADDED. Returns a PostMergeReport; does not modify the record.

tools/exam_builder/merge.py::post_identi.text: Scores from 0 to 1 how sure GovOS is that two post names mean the same post. Identical distinctive words score 1; one name's words fully contained in the other's score high; merely sharing a word or two scores low.
tools/exam_builder/merge.py::post_identi.tech: Using _name_tokens: empty -> 0.0; equal -> 1.0; no overlap -> 0.0; subset either way -> 0.9 if at least 2 shared words else 0.5; otherwise 0.4 * shared / max(len).

tools/exam_builder/names.py::AuthorityNa.text: The name GovOS has settled on for an exam authority, together with how it got it, the page it came from, and (only when verified) the exact words quoted from that page.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::AuthorityNa.tech: Dataclass: value, status (NameStatus), source_url (empty if built from the address), evidence (Evidence, only for VERIFIED), reason. Has is_identity_evidence and __str__.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::AuthorityNa.text: Shows the name itself when the object is printed.
Says whether this name may be used to decide who the authority is. Only a name the authority printed itself counts.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::AuthorityNa.tech: Property: True only when status is CANONICAL_NAME_VERIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::NameStatus.text: How sure GovOS is about an exam authority's name: read from the authority's own pages (verified), worked out from other sources or the web address (inferred), or not known at all.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_acronym_of.text: Makes the initials of a name, skipping small words like 'of' and 'the'.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_acronym_of.tech: First letters of alphabetic words excluding of/and/the/for, lowercased.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_harvest.text: Scans search results or pages for anything that looks like the name of an official body, such as 'Board of ...' or '... Commission'.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_harvest.tech: For each hit, joins title and content and runs _PREFIX_FORM ('Institute/Board/... of X') and _SUFFIX_FORM ('X ... Commission/Bank/...', optional 'of X' tail) regexes; cleans whitespace, strips leading noise, drops matches hitting _NOT_AN_AUTHORITY, and keeps 3-8 words (prefix form) or 2-8 words (suffix form). Returns a list with repeats.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_is_own_pag.text: Checks whether a page is on the authority's own website.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_is_own_pag.tech: Compares hit.host and host case-insensitively with 'www.' removed; False if host is empty.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_label_from.text: Builds a placeholder label from a website address, for example turning a short address into capital letters, when no page names the body.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_label_from.tech: Takes the host's first label; returns '' if empty, shorter than 2 chars or all digits; uppercased if 6 chars or fewer, else hyphens to spaces and title-cased.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_matches_ad.text: Checks whether a name's initials match the first part of the website address, which supports that the name belongs to that site's owner.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_matches_ad.tech: True when the first dot-separated label of host (lowercased) is non-empty and equals _acronym_of(name).

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_pick.text: Chooses the most likely institution name from a list of candidates. A name whose initials match the website address wins; otherwise partial fragments of longer names are dropped and the most frequently seen name is chosen.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_pick.tech: Counts candidates. If any _matches_address(host), returns the most frequent (ties: shorter). Else removes candidates that are substrings of another candidate, then returns the highest count, ties broken by shorter length.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::_strip_lead.text: Removes titles and filler words from the front of a body's name, such as 'Chairman' or 'The', as long as at least two words remain.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::_strip_lead.tech: Repeatedly applies the _LEADING_NOISE regex (the, office, chairman, secretary, shri, dr, welcome, to, of, ...) until stable, only accepting a strip that leaves 2 or more words.

tools/exam_builder/names.py::resolve_nam.text: Works out what an exam authority is called and records how. It prefers a name printed on the authority's own pages (verified, with a quote), then a name read from its home page if the initials match the address (verified), then a name other websites use (inferred), then a label made from the web address (inferred, a placeholder only), and otherwise reports the name as unknown.
tools/exam_builder/names.py::resolve_nam.tech: Step 1: _harvest over hits on the own host, _pick, build an Evidence span from the matching page and verify() it against that page's normalised text; VERIFIED -> CANONICAL_NAME_VERIFIED. Step 2: if fetch is given, fetches https://host, harvests, keeps only names matching the address, verifies -> VERIFIED. Step 3: harvest other hosts' hits -> CANONICAL_NAME_INFERRED with that page's URL. Step 4: _label_from_host -> INFERRED with no evidence. Else NAME_UNRESOLVED. Returns an AuthorityName.

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::Offic.text: The result of checking whether a website is the real exam authority: the site, yes or no, a confidence score, quoted evidence and the reasons.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::Offic.tech: Dataclass: domain, is_official, confidence (float), evidence (list of Evidence), reasons (list of str).

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_full.text: Returns the authority's full name if the hint is a real name of two or more words; a single word is treated as an acronym and gives nothing.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_full.tech: Alphabetic words longer than 2 chars from the hint; returns them joined if there are at least 2, else ''.

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_name.text: Splits an authority hint into its words of three letters or more.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_name.tech: Lowercase alphabetic tokens longer than 2 chars, as a set.

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_says.text: Checks whether a text contains a phrase as whole words, so a short acronym is not found inside a longer word.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::_says.tech: Builds a word-bounded, case-insensitive regex joining the phrase's words with optional spaces/hyphens; False for an empty phrase.

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::best_.text: Tries the most-mentioned website addresses in turn (up to six) and returns the first one that proves to be the official authority, along with every check that was made.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::best_.tech: Iterates candidate_domains(hits)[:limit], calling verify_domain for each; returns (first official check, all tried) or (None, tried).

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::candi.text: Collects the website addresses mentioned inside search results (not the sites hosting them), most-mentioned first, as candidates for the official authority site.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::candi.tech: Finds bare domains with _BARE_DOMAIN in each hit's title and content, skipping excluded hosts, _NEVER_AN_AUTHORITY, the hit's own host, domains with more than 3 dots or under 5 chars. Returns domains sorted by mention count descending.

tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::verif.text: Visits a candidate website and asks whether it presents itself as the body that runs the exam. It scores the site on describing recruitment, naming the exam, naming the authority, having an address that echoes the exam's short name, and printing the authority's full name, and takes points off if it looks like a coaching or seller site. It is accepted only with enough score, a mention of the exam, and either the full name or a matching address. A site that cannot be loaded is reported as a fetch problem, not as unofficial.
tools/exam_builder/officiality.py::verif.tech: Fetches the domain (fetch defaults to safe_load_html). None -> not official with an infrastructure reason; empty text -> not official. Scores: _SELF_DESCRIPTION +0.4; any alias via _says +0.4 (with a verified Evidence snippet around the first alias); >=2 hint tokens present +0.3; domain root equal to or containing an alias +0.2 (label_echo); full name printed +0.3 (names_itself); two or more _THIRD_PARTY_POSTURE cues subtract min(0.6, 0.3 per cue). is_official = score >= 0.7 and alias hit and (names_itself or label_echo). Returns OfficialityCheck with confidence clamped to 1.0 and reasons.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.text: The full report of one pipeline run: what was asked, whether it was a trial run, how it ended, how far it got, the built record, the gate's verdict, any Claude checks and human reviews, proof that other exams were left untouched, where the review file was saved, and notes.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.tech: Dataclass: query, year, dry_run, state, reached (Stage), build (BuildResult), gate (GateReport), verifications (field -> Verdict), reviews, isolation_ok, fingerprint_before/after (per-exam digests of data.ts), staging_path, published, reason, notes. Has exam_id and summary().

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.text: The id of the exam that was built, or empty if nothing was built.
A short readable report of the run for the command line: query, outcome, furthest step, trial-run flag, fields found, gate result, Claude checks, isolation, staging file, publish status and reason.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.tech: Builds lines from the present parts: FOUND/total fields, gate decision with blocker count, count of SUPPORTED Claude decisions, isolation_ok, staging_path, published, reason; joined by newlines.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.text: The possible outcomes of a pipeline run: published, staged (passed but not written live), blocked by the quality gate, authority not found or ambiguous, a system or fetch failure, a change that would affect another exam, or refused because it would overwrite a hand-written exam.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Orche.tech: str Enum: PUBLISHED, STAGED, BLOCKED_BY_GATE, RESOLUTION_FAILURE, AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY, INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE, ISOLATION_VIOLATION, PRESERVATION_BLOCKED.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Stage.text: The named steps of the exam-building pipeline, used to report how far a run got (from finding the authority through to publishing).
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::Stage.tech: str Enum: RESOLUTION, DISCOVERY, SOURCE_CAPTURE, IDENTITY, EXTRACTION, DETERMINISTIC, CLAUDE_VERIFICATION, MERGE_REVISION, SCHEMA, ISOLATION, STAGING, PUBLICATION_GATE, ATOMIC_PUBLISH.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_fing.text: Takes a per-exam fingerprint of the hand-written exam file, so GovOS can later prove no other exam changed.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_fing.tech: Reads data_ts and returns P.fingerprint(text); {} on OSError.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_fini.text: Closes a run by fingerprinting the exam file again and confirming every other exam is exactly as it was before.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_fini.tech: Sets fingerprint_after and isolation_ok = every exam in fingerprint_before except this exam_id has an equal digest after. Returns res.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_shor.text: Shortens a long value for display, adding an ellipsis.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_shor.tech: str(value) truncated to limit (default 240) with '…' appended when cut.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_writ.text: Saves a JSON review file describing the run (authority, sources, each field's value and citation, checks, gate verdict, reviews and notes) so a person can inspect the build without running it again. It never touches the live exam data.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::_writ.tech: Builds a payload from res and res.build (fields with status, note, _short value and citation with excerpt truncated to 300 chars; verification decisions; gate.summary(); rec.log; isolationOk; conflicts always []). Writes '<examId or unresolved>-orchestration-<timestamp>.json' under P.STAGING_DIR (created if needed) and returns the path.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::main.text: Command-line entry point to run the pipeline for one named exam and print the summary. It is a trial run unless --publish is given.
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::main.tech: argparse: exam (required, else error), --year, --claude, --publish. Calls orchestrate(dry_run=not publish, use_claude). Note: with --publish and no render, orchestrate falls back to R.render_exam, despite the help text saying the CLI supplies none. Exit 0 for PUBLISHED or STAGED, else 1.

tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::orche.text: Runs the whole exam-building pipeline for one exam name and year: find the authority, collect and read its documents, optionally have Claude double-check facts (Claude can only hold a fact back, never add one), apply any human review, check that nothing from another exam crept in, and run the publishing gate. It always saves a review file. By default it is a trial run that changes nothing live; when asked to publish, a new exam is written through the safe publisher, while an existing hand-written exam is never overwritten (at most, verified extra facts are saved as separate overlays).
tools/exam_builder/orchestrate.py::orche.tech: Fingerprints data.ts, then calls build(...) with NoClaude() unless use_claude. Maps AmbiguousAuthority -> AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY, SearchUnavailable -> INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, LookupError -> RESOLUTION_FAILURE. With use_claude, runs claude_verify on each FOUND, cited field (claim_from_field); a CONTRADICTED decision sets the field NEEDS_REVIEW, infra failures only add a note. Applies review.apply_reviews and re-evaluates completeness if any applied. run_all isolation checks, then gate_evaluate with build_state, identity verdicts, empty conflicts and completeness. Always _write_staging. State: PAUSED_INFRASTRUCTURE -> SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE; gate block -> BLOCKED_BY_GATE; dry_run -> STAGED; existing authored target without allow_overwrite -> overlays via create_overlays_from_record + OverlayStore.record when allow_overlay (PUBLISHED, or BLOCKED_BY_GATE if persisting fails), else PRESERVATION_BLOCKED; otherwise renders (render or R.render_exam), P.stage and P.publish (IsolationViolation -> ISOLATION_VIOLATION). Returns via _finish.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.text: One machine-read fact layered on top of a hand-written exam without changing the original file. It records which exam and year it belongs to, which area, what kind of change it is, the value, where it came from (the source document and quote), its state, what it replaces, and whether it has been switched off.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.tech: Dataclass: id, exam_id, cycle, domain, kind (OverlayKind), value, provenance (dict: documentTitle, officialUrl, verificationLevel, excerptText), status (default VERIFIED), target_id, target_scope, supersedes_id, previous_value, effective_date, conflict_note, created_at, created_by (default 'GovOS Machine Pipeline'), retired. Has is_active, to_dict and from_dict.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.text: Rebuilds an overlay from stored data, accepting either naming style.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.tech: Classmethod: requires 'id' and 'domain'; reads other fields from camelCase or snake_case keys with defaults (kind ADD, status VERIFIED, created_by 'GovOS Machine Pipeline'). Note previous_value uses 'or', so a falsy stored value becomes the snake_case fallback or None.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.text: Says whether this overlay should show up on the exam page: it must not be switched off, must be verified or 'not published', and must not be a conflict.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.tech: Property: not retired and status in PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES and kind != CONFLICT.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.text: Turns the overlay into plain data with camelCase names for storage or sending.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamFactO.tech: Returns a camelCase dict of every field; kind as its value, targetScope via to_dict, and createdAt defaulting to the current UTC time when empty.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.text: Pins an overlay to an exact part of an exam (a particular stage, paper, post, rule, category, subject, topic or level) so a fact about one paper cannot leak onto another.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.tech: Dataclass of optional ids/labels: stage_id, paper_id, post_id, rule_id, category_label, subject, topic_id, level_label. to_dict drops None values; from_dict accepts snake_case or camelCase keys.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.text: Rebuilds a scope from stored data, accepting either naming style.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.tech: Classmethod; returns an empty scope for a falsy or non-dict input, else reads each field from its snake_case or camelCase key.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.text: Turns the scope into plain data, leaving out the parts that are not set.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::ExamOverl.tech: dataclasses.asdict filtered to non-None values (snake_case keys).

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlayKi.text: The kinds of change an overlay can make to an exam: add a new fact, amend an existing one, replace an old one while keeping it on record, retire (switch off) an overlay, or flag a conflict for review.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlayKi.tech: str Enum: ADD, AMEND, SUPERSEDE, RETIRE, CONFLICT.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Saves and loads machine-read exam facts (overlays) in the GovOS database, so they can be shown over hand-written exams and their history kept.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: SQLite-backed store over table exam_fact_overlays (index on exam_id, cycle, domain, retired). Uses one shared connection for in-memory databases, a fresh connection per call otherwise. Methods: record, retire, get_active, get_history.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Opens the overlay store on a database file (GovOS's main database by default) and makes sure its table exists.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: Stores db_path (default 'govos.db'); for ':memory:' or 'mode=memory' paths opens a shared connection with Row factory; then calls _init_db.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Gets a database connection to use.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: Returns the shared in-memory connection, or a new sqlite3 connection with row_factory = sqlite3.Row.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Creates the overlay table and its lookup index if they are missing.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS exam_fact_overlays (id PK, exam_id, cycle, domain, target_id, target_scope_json, kind, value_json, provenance_json, status, supersedes_id, previous_value_json, effective_date, conflict_note, created_at, created_by, retired) plus CREATE INDEX idx_exam_fact_overlays_lookup; commits.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Closes a database connection when finished, except for the shared in-memory one.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: conn.close() unless the store is in-memory.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Turns one saved database row back into an overlay object.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: JSON-decodes value, provenance, optional target scope and previous value; builds ExamFactOverlay with OverlayKind(row['kind']) and retired as bool.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Fetches the overlays for an exam that should currently show, optionally for one year and one area, oldest first.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: SELECT where exam_id matches, retired = 0, status in VERIFIED/NOT_PUBLISHED and kind != CONFLICT, optionally filtered by cycle and domain, ORDER BY created_at ASC; converted with _row_to_overlay.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Fetches every overlay ever saved for an exam, including switched-off ones and conflicts, oldest first.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: SELECT by exam_id (optionally domain) ORDER BY created_at ASC, converted with _row_to_overlay.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Checks an overlay and saves it. If the overlay fails the checks, nothing is saved and an error is raised.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: Runs validate_overlay; raises ValueError listing errors. Otherwise JSON-encodes scope, value, provenance and previous_value and INSERT OR REPLACEs by id, filling created_at with the current UTC time if empty. Returns the overlay.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.text: Switches an overlay off so it no longer shows, while keeping it in the history.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::OverlaySt.tech: UPDATE exam_fact_overlays SET retired = 1 WHERE id = ?; returns True if a row changed.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::PUBLISHAB.text: The states that are allowed to reach candidates: verified, or confirmed as not published by the authority.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::PUBLISHAB.tech: frozenset {'VERIFIED', 'NOT_PUBLISHED'}; used by validate_overlay, ExamFactOverlay.is_active and OverlayStore.get_active.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::VALID_DOM.text: The list of exam areas a machine-added fact (an overlay) is allowed to belong to, such as dates, posts, syllabus, resources, results or the overview.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::VALID_DOM.tech: frozenset of 19 domain names (the comment says 17): dates, posts, eligibility, application, pattern, syllabus, resources, practiceQuestions, officialPapers, answerKeys, admitCard, examDayChecklist, results, faqs, corrigendums, officialLinks, cutoffsHistory, roadmapTracks, overview. validate_overlay rejects any other domain. practiceQuestions is accepted but has no projection branch.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::VALID_STA.text: The four states a machine-read fact can be in: verified, needs review, not published by the authority, or not extracted.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::VALID_STA.tech: frozenset {'VERIFIED', 'NEEDS_REVIEW', 'NOT_PUBLISHED', 'NOT_EXTRACTED'}. Defined for reference; validation uses PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::_upsert_b.text: Adds an item to a list, or replaces the existing item with the same id.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::_upsert_b.tech: Mutates lst in place: appends when item has no id or no match, else replaces the first matching id. Returns lst.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::_validate.text: Checks that an overlay's value has the required parts for its area, for example a date needs a type and a date, a post needs a name, department and pay level, a resource needs a title and a web link.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::_validate.tech: Value must be a dict. Per domain: dates need type in a fixed set and dateTimeStr (AMEND only checks type if present); posts need postName, department, payLevel (not for AMEND) and integer 0 <= minAge <= maxAge if both given; eligibility category or ruleType; syllabus topicName and subject; resources title and http(s) url with officialityTier in OFFICIAL/TRUSTED_REFERENCE/PENDING_REVIEW; application at least one known key; officialPapers/answerKeys paperTitle and pdfUrl; admitCard eventName or noticeTitle; results stageName, declarationTitle or nextSteps; faqs question and answer; corrigendums title and noticeNumber; cutoffsHistory category and year; officialLinks title and url; examDayChecklist item or instruction; overview overviewDescription or vacanciesTotal; pattern one of stageName/name/stages/level/levelLabel. Other domains unchecked. Returns errors.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::apply_ove.text: Produces the version of an exam that candidates see by laying the active machine-read facts over the hand-written exam, without changing the original. Only overlays for this exact exam and year that are active are used. Depending on the area, it adds items, edits matching items, or marks an old date as superseded and adds the new one.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::apply_ove.tech: Returns exam unchanged if no overlays or none active for exam_id and matching cycle (a missing cycle on either side matches). Otherwise deep-copies and applies each overlay by domain: dates (SUPERSEDE marks the old date status SUPERSEDED and upserts a new AVAILABLE date with provenance; AMEND updates by target_id; ADD upserts); posts (ADD/AMEND by target_id or scope.post_id/SUPERSEDE removes the old post); syllabus (ADD/AMEND, provenance as officialProvenance); resources (ADD with officialityTier default OFFICIAL); eligibility -> ageRelaxations keyed by category; cutoffsHistory, faqs, officialPapers, admitCard -> admitCardEvents, corrigendums, examDayChecklist, roadmapTracks, pattern -> examPatternStages (ADD upsert); officialLinks replace by url or label; answerKeys ADD/SUPERSEDE; results -> resultDeclarations, or nextStepGuidance when nextSteps present; application merges into 'application' and mirrors howToApply, applicationPortal, requiredDocuments, photoSignatureGuidelines, applicationFee, feeExemptions to the top level; overview sets overviewDescription/vacanciesTotal. Overlays apply in list order.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::create_ov.text: Turns the facts of a machine-built exam record that passed the publishing gate into overlays that can sit on top of a hand-written exam. Only facts that were actually found and carry a citation are used, each one is checked, and any that fail the checks are silently left out.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::create_ov.tech: Returns [] unless gate.may_publish. Cycle from get_exam_cycle(exam_id/title), defaulting to '2026'. For each FOUND field with a citation, builds provenance via citation.to_provenance and ADD overlays (status VERIFIED, created_by 'GovOS Universal Pipeline', ids containing a millisecond timestamp and index) for: dates (needs type and dateTimeStr), posts (needs postName), syllabus, examPattern/pattern, officialPapers and answerKeys (need a URL), admitCard, results, cutoffs, corrigenda (noticeNumber defaulted), an http(s) applicationPortal (both an officialLinks and an application overlay), ageLimits and qualification (eligibility rules with details as text), vacancies (overview.vacanciesTotal), overview dict, resources (need http(s) URL), other application fields, and nextSteps (results). Keeps only overlays with no validate_overlay errors. Ids are time-based, so re-running produces new ids; results and resources share the 'res-' id pattern.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::get_exam_.text: Finds the exam's year (like 2026) from its id or, failing that, its title.
tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::get_exam_.tech: First word-bounded 20xx in exam_dict['id'], else in 'title'; returns '' if none.

tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::validate_.text: Checks that a machine-read fact is safe to save: it names a proper exam id and a year, belongs to an allowed area, has a publishable state, cites an official document with a web link and an 'officially verified' level, carries an exact quote if verified, has a correctly shaped value, and (for changes and replacements) says what it changes. Returns the list of problems; an empty list means it is valid.
