tools/exam_builder/overlay.py::validate_.tech: Checks: non-empty id; exam_id starting 'exam-'; non-empty cycle; domain in VALID_DOMAINS; status in PUBLISHABLE_STATUSES unless CONFLICT; provenance dict with a documentTitle, an http(s) URL (several key aliases), verificationLevel OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED unless CONFLICT, and an excerpt when VERIFIED; non-None value checked by _validate_domain_payload for non-RETIRE VERIFIED overlays; AMEND/SUPERSEDE need target_id or a non-empty target_scope; SUPERSEDE needs supersedes_id or target_id. Returns list[str].

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_Cursor.text: A small helper that holds a document's text split into lines, for walking through it.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_Cursor.tech: Holds text and lines (text split on newline); joined() rejoins a line range.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_Cursor._.text: Stores the text and splits it into lines.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_Cursor._.tech: Sets self.text and self.lines = text.split('\n') (empty text gives [''']).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_Cursor.j.text: Joins a range of lines back into one line of text, skipping blank lines.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_la.text: Finds sentences like 'The Main Examination will be conducted in English, Telugu and Urdu' anywhere in the document and attaches the languages to the one stage the sentence names, if that stage has no language yet.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_la.tech: Iterates _LANGUAGE_SENTENCE; skips captures with digits, without a _LANGUAGE_CELL word, over 70 chars, or describing mode. Requires exactly one stage whose distinguishing words are all in the sentence and which has no languages; splits on and/&//, and sets languages via _fact.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_me.text: Finds sentences anywhere in the document saying a stage's or paper's marks will not count towards the final merit (it is only qualifying), and attaches each one to the specific part it names by that part's distinctive words or code. A sentence that names no part is left unattached rather than guessed.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_me.tech: Iterates _MERIT_SENTENCE over the flattened text; trims with _trim_to_statement; skips sentences over 420 chars or with 3+ standalone numbers. If a stage's distinguishing words are all in the sentence, candidates are restricted to that stage's subtree. Scores nodes by distinguishing-word hits (excluding _GENERIC_NODE_WORDS) and requires a coded node's code to be spelled in the sentence; prefers more hits, then a leaf over a parent, then nearer printed position (_distance_in). Sets best.qualifying to a verified QualifyingRule(is_qualifying_only=True, counts_towards_merit=False) preserving existing minimums; with only_unset, skips nodes that already have one.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_st.text: Fills in a stage's own rules from the text under its heading: the penalty for wrong answers, any minimum qualifying marks, whether it is online or written, the question type, the languages, and whether each section is timed separately. It also takes the stage's totals from the table's total row, or adds up its rows' questions and marks when every row states them (marked as computed). Whether the whole stage counts for merit is left to the document-wide pass.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_apply_st.tech: Sets negative_marking from read_negative_marking; qualifying from read_qualifying with is_qualifying_only/counts_towards_merit reset to None (dropped if no minimum remains); mode (_MODE), question_type (_QUESTION_TYPE), languages (_LANGUAGE_PROSE, rejected if digits, no language word or >70 chars), sectional_timing (_SECTIONAL_TIMING) — all via _fact. From totals: numbers[0] questions, numbers[1] marks, minutes duration. If still unset and every child has a value, questions/marks become Fact.derived sums of the children with up to two evidences.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_category.text: Reads the authority's own names for the candidate groups that a qualifying-marks column is split into (for example 'SC/ST/PWBD' and 'Others'), from the line under the table heading. If it cannot find them it uses numbered placeholders.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_category.tech: Scans up to 6 lines forward from header_end, considering at most 3 non-empty lines and stopping at one with a digit; splits on double spaces, tabs or before capitalised words; accepts a line with exactly count parts of 24 chars or less where none is a _HEADER_WORD. Fallback: '<column.label> 1..n'.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_classify.text: Fixes the case where a 'Scheme of Examination' heading sits over a table covering several stages. If the table can be split into its stages, those stages replace the heading; otherwise the heading is kept as a heading (not a stage) and all its figures are held for review, since a total across stages belongs to no single stage.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_classify.tech: For each stage with a recorded container span: if _stages_named_in finds 2+ names, tries _segmented_stages and splices the results in (renumbering order); failing that sets level HEADING, status NEEDS_REVIEW and _hold_figures with the stage names. Replaces pattern.stages in place.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_continue.text: Checks whether a line is just the continuation of the line above (because the line above ends on a word like 'of' or 'for'), unless it starts with its own list marker.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_continue.tech: False if the line begins with a list/clause marker; otherwise looks at the nearest non-empty line among the previous two and returns whether it ends in a _DANGLING function word.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_distance.text: Measures how far, in the document's text, a part's own quoted words are from a given sentence.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_distance.tech: For the first node evidence span (first 120 chars, whitespace-normalised) found in flat, returns abs(position - where); 10**9 if none is found.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_duration.text: Reads a row's time allowance and any extra time printed for a named group of candidates (for example those using a scribe), without confusing the two.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_duration.tech: First _DURATION match is the main duration (minutes and its text). Each later match becomes a DurationVariant only when a _DURATION_GROUP phrase follows it within 140 chars and before the next duration; duplicates skipped. Returns (minutes or None, main text, variants).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_evidence.text: Creates a citation for a value only if its exact words can be found in the document; otherwise gives nothing.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_evidence.tech: Builds an Evidence (page defaults to 1), verify(text); returns SourceEvidence.from_evidence with section 'pattern' when VERIFIED, else None.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_extend_p.text: Works out how far down a stage's table should be read, continuing past lines that look like headings but are really table rows, and stopping at a real next stage (one with its own table, or labelled tier/phase/stage/round).
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_extend_p.tech: Starting from the next region, while the region line matches _ROW_LABEL, has no scheme header under it (_find_scheme_header), and lacks tier/phase/stage/round, extends end to the following bound. Returns the end line index.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_fact.text: Wraps a value as a verified fact if its quoted words are found in the document, otherwise as a fact that needs review.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_fact.tech: Fact.verified(value, ev) when _evidence returns evidence, else Fact.needs_review(value, reason that the span was not found verbatim).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_find_sch.text: Looks inside a stage's part of the notice for the heading row of a scheme table and the columns it declares (such as number of questions, marks, duration). Text containing a verb is treated as a sentence, not a heading.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_find_sch.tech: For each start line, accumulates up to 16 following lines (max 400 chars), skipping accumulations with _SENTENCE_VERB; uses tables._columns_in and accepts when QUESTIONS or MARKS is present, at least 3 columns and _header_density >= 0.55, keeping the candidate with the most columns. Returns (header_end_line, columns) for the first start line that yields any, else None.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_first.text: Returns the first piece of text matching a pattern, trimmed and capped in length.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_first.tech: First non-empty capture group (or the whole match) of pattern.search, stripped of ' .,;:' and capped at 160 chars; '' if no match.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_fold_res.text: Merges duplicate stage headings. When a heading is immediately repeated above its table (for example 'Phase-II: Main Examination' then 'Main Examination'), the two become one stage. A heading that only repeats a label or name already carried by a stage or paper with real content is removed, after handing over any facts it stated.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_fold_res.tech: Pass 1: a childless stage followed by one with children where _restates(name, next.name) takes the next's children, fills its unset fields from it, concatenates evidence and drops the next. Pass 2: builds maps of codes and names of nodes inside stages with children; a childless stage whose code or name (exact or suffix) matches one is removed after copying its set fields to that twin where unset. Then _merge_overlapping_stages and renumbers order. Mutates pattern.stages.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_header_d.text: Measures what share of a piece of text is made up of column names; a real table heading is almost all column names, a sentence is not.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_header_d.tech: Sum of word counts of the columns' labels divided by the number of whitespace-separated words in joined; 0.0 for empty text.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hold_fig.text: Marks every verified number (questions, marks, time, marks per question) on an exam part and everything under it as needing review, with the reason.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hold_fig.tech: Walks node.walk(); for each of _FIGURES with a value and VERIFIED status sets NEEDS_REVIEW and note=why. Mutates in place.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hold_fig.text: Makes sure that any table row already flagged for review does not carry figures shown as verified.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hold_fig.tech: For every node under every stage whose status is NEEDS_REVIEW, calls _hold_figures with a 'could not be delimited' reason.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hours_to.text: Converts an hours figure such as '2 ½' or '3' into minutes.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_hours_to.tech: Removes spaces, detects a trailing '½' or '1/2' as +0.5, parses the rest as float hours and returns round(hours*60); None if unparseable.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_is_headi.text: Decides whether a line could be a heading: short, not ending in a comma or a small connecting word, containing no verb, and at most 14 words. This stops the middle of a sentence from being read as a heading.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_is_headi.tech: False if empty, over 110 chars, ending in ';' or ',', ending in a function word (for/of/in/the/and...), or matching _IS_STATEMENT (verb list). Otherwise True when it has 14 words or fewer.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_is_marke.text: Checks whether a line of a notice is marked the way authorities mark headings: a clause number, a lettered item, a colon, or mostly capital letters.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_is_marke.tech: True if _MARKED_HEADING matches (leading numeric clause, (a)/a. style letter, or a colon anywhere) or more than 80% of the line's letters are uppercase.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_keeps.text: After reading what sits under a heading, decides whether it really is a stage of the exam. It is kept if a table with figures was read under it, if it states a measurable fact of its own (time, marks, penalty, languages), or if it is a short labelled heading like 'Phase-III: Interview'. Headings over a syllabus or fee list, scheme titles on their own, and cross-references are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_keeps.tech: False if the bare line matches _NOT_THE_SCHEME. With children: True if any child has questions, marks or duration. _SCHEME_HEADING without children -> False. Any measurable field (questions, marks, duration_minutes, negative_marking, qualifying, languages) -> True. _CROSS_REFERENCE -> False. Otherwise True only if it contains tier/phase/stage/round or _STAGE_NAMED and has 6 words or fewer.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_medium_t.text: Finds the 'medium' (language) part of a table row: the short bit of words left after the first number once figures and times are removed.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_medium_t.tech: Removes marks products, takes the text from the first ' <digit>', removes durations, numbers and 'total =', tidies whitespace and punctuation; returns it if 60 chars or fewer, else ''.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_merge_ov.text: Combines two headings that describe the same stage when neither has a table, for example 'Preliminary' and 'Civil Services Preliminary Objective', keeping the first one's name and filling in what only the second stated.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_merge_ov.tech: For childless stages, finds an earlier childless stage in the output whose distinguishing-word set is a subset or superset of this one's; copies unset fields to it and appends evidence, dropping this stage. Stages with children pass through. Returns the new list.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_minutes.text: Turns a written duration such as '2 hours 30 minutes' or '90 minutes' into a number of minutes.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_minutes.tech: Uses the first _DURATION match: returns the minutes group directly, else hours*60 plus any trailing minutes; None if no duration.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_node_lev.text: Decides what the rows of a table are (papers, sections or subjects) from the table's column heading, or failing that from the row label's own word.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_node_lev.tech: First column of kind PAPER, SECTION or SUBJECT gives (level, column.label); else the first _LEVEL_WORDS word that the label starts with; default (SECTION, '').

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_numeric_.text: Picks out the table columns that hold numbers: question count, marks and qualifying marks.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_numeric_.tech: Filters columns to kinds QUESTIONS, MARKS, QUALIFYING_MARKS, keeping the header's own order (the order dict is used only for membership).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_ordinal_.text: Reads the position number in a row label, such as 2 from 'Paper-II', 3 from 'C' or 1 from '1.'.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_ordinal_.tech: Splits the label on non-alphanumerics and inspects the last part: digits -> ('num', n), Roman i..x -> ('roman', n), a single letter -> ('alpha', position). Else None.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_push_dow.text: Copies a stage's negative-marking rule down to each of its papers that has none, marking it as inherited from the stage rather than printed against that paper.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_push_dow.tech: For each stage with negative_marking, gives each child lacking one a new Fact with the same value, status, evidence and confidence, derived_from=['stage.negative_marking'] and an explanatory note.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_read_pro.text: Reads papers that a notice lists as labelled lines (for example 'Paper-A ... 300 marks') rather than in a table, and treats the headings above them ('Qualifying Papers', 'Papers to be counted for merit') as saying whether those papers count. It returns nothing unless there are at least two papers and at least one states its marks.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_read_pro.tech: Walks lines; _QUALIFYING_HEADING sets a qualifying group, a short _MERIT_HEADING line sets a merit group; _PROSE_PAPER lines (paper/part + ordinal) start a paper unless the rest reads as a statement (_IS_STATEMENT); following lines under 200 chars accumulate. flush() builds a PAPER PatternNode with evidence, marks from _PROSE_MARKS, a QualifyingRule from the current heading, and question_type. Returns [] if fewer than 2 nodes or none has marks.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_read_tab.text: Reads each row of an exam scheme table into a structured entry: its name, number of questions, marks, minimum qualifying marks (including per category), marks per question, time allowed, language and question type. Each value is verified against the document's words. A row whose figures cannot be matched cleanly to columns, or that sums several parts together, is kept but marked for review instead of guessing. The totals row is returned separately.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_read_tab.tech: For each _split_rows row: total rows (without an inline 'Total =') populate totals {numbers, minutes, span}. Otherwise builds a PatternNode (id prefix-slug, level from columns or the label's own level word, code from a non-numeric label), with row evidence -> VERIFIED else NEEDS_REVIEW. Rows with _CELL_TOTAL -> NEEDS_REVIEW with remarks. Numbers are zipped to numeric columns when counts match; one extra with a qualifying column -> category minimums labelled by _category_labels; other counts -> zipped but NEEDS_REVIEW. Sets questions, marks, qualifying via _fact; marks_per_question from a product cell, else Fact.derived when marks/questions divides to 2 decimals; duration_minutes and variants; languages from _medium_text when a LANGUAGE column exists; question_type from _QUESTION_TYPE. Returns (nodes, totals).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_restates.text: Checks whether a second heading is the same as the first one, apart from its label (for example 'Phase-II: Main Examination' and 'Main Examination'), or, if the first is only a label, whether both carry the same label.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_restates.tech: Removes _STAGE_LABELLED matches and non-letters; True if both bare strings are equal and non-empty. If the outer is a bare label (nothing left), compares the two label matches with spaces and hyphens removed, case-insensitively.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_row_name.text: Works out a table row's own name, such as the subject, by removing its label, numbers, times and bracketed notes.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_row_name.tech: Drops a leading label (case-insensitive), marks products, durations and parenthesised text, cuts at the first ' <digit>', tidies punctuation and caps at 120 chars.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_row_numb.text: Collects the numbers in one row of a scheme table. It first handles written arithmetic like '60*3 = 180' (3 marks a question) and 'Total = 60', and ignores the row's serial number and any durations, so they are not mistaken for marks or question counts.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_row_numb.tech: Strips a leading label; a _MARKS_PRODUCT match whose product checks out gives per_question and product_total and is removed; a _CELL_TOTAL gives stated_total and is removed; durations removed; remaining _INTEGER matches collected, excluding values equal to stated_total. Returns (numbers, per_question, product_total, residue text).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_segmente.text: Handles a single scheme table that lists several stages inside it (for example a 'Preliminary Test' block and a 'Main Examination' block). It splits the table into those stages and reads each paper's time and marks, but only if every row reads cleanly; otherwise it gives up and returns nothing.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_segmente.tech: Needs at least two _ROW_STAGE heads in the span; header text before the first head must declare DURATION and MARKS columns (via tables._columns_in) and mention hours. For each stage builds a STAGE node with verified evidence (else returns []); rows end on a line whose tail (_ROW_TAIL) holds two figures, assigned by the header's column order; papers get verified marks, duration (_hours_to_minutes), optional question count, '(objective|descriptive|conventional type)' and a qualifying rule if the name says qualifying; a following 'TOTAL MARKS' line sets the stage's marks. Any unreadable row, missing evidence or empty stage returns [].

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_sentence.text: Pulls out the full sentence around a given point in the text, without being fooled by full stops inside clause numbers or decimals, and drops a leading clause number or page header.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_sentence.tech: Finds the last _SENTENCE_END (a . or ; followed by space/end, not after i.e/e.g/Rs/No/viz) before index and the next one after it (or index+width); strips _LEADING_CLAUSE (page furniture and a clause number) and caps the result at 300 chars.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_slug.text: Makes a short, simple id fragment out of a name (lowercase letters, numbers and dashes).
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_slug.tech: Lowercases, replaces non-alphanumeric runs with '-', strips dashes, caps at 44 chars; 'x' if empty.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_split_ro.text: Splits a flattened table from a PDF into its rows. Since a PDF loses row boundaries, it uses the labels rows carry (a number, a letter, or words like 'Paper II'), and only accepts a numbered label if it continues the count, so a line of figures in the middle of a row is not mistaken for a new row. It stops when the text turns into prose.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_split_ro.tech: Walks lines from start to limit, skipping blanks and _FURNITURE; breaks on a long clause-numbered line (>60) or a long line not starting with a digit (>90). _ROW_LABEL matches (not bare ordinals) start rows: total rows always (sequence kept), level-word labels always (sequence reset to their ordinal), plain numbers/letters only if equal to sequence+1 (or <=2 with no sequence); other lines append to the current row. Returns [(label, lines, start_index)].

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stage_na.text: Reads a stage's name, its label word (like 'Phase' or 'Tier') and its code (like 'Phase-II') from its heading.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stage_na.tech: Strips a leading clause number and edge punctuation; if _STAGE_LABELLED matches returns (text[:110], label.title(), whole match); otherwise (text[:110], 'Stage', '').

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stage_re.text: Finds every line in a notice that announces a stage of the exam (for example 'Phase-II: Main Examination' or 'Scheme of Examination'), skipping lines that are wrapped tails of a heading, table rows, prose mentions, or mere mentions of words like 'Interview'.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stage_re.tech: For each line passing _is_heading and not _continues_previous: requires _STAGE_LABELLED, _STAGE_NAMED or _SCHEME_HEADING; rejects a labelled match preceded by a bare Roman ordinal (_ROW_LEADING_ORDINAL), an opening that starts lowercase after removing a clause number, a cue starting beyond column 40, a line failing _is_marked, and a named-only match without exam/test/round/paper/phase/stage/tier. Returns [(line_index, line, 'labelled'|'named'|'scheme')].

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stages_n.text: Lists the distinct stage names (like 'preliminary' or 'main') that short row headings inside a part of the text name.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_stages_n.tech: Over lines[start:end], collects _ROW_STAGE matches on lines of 8 words or fewer without a statement verb; returns the lowercased name group with a trailing 's' stripped.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_trim_to_.text: Cuts away any table figures printed in front of a rule sentence, keeping the sentence itself.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_trim_to_.tech: Normalises whitespace; if the cue matches, returns the text after the last digit before the cue, stripped of ' *.,;:'; otherwise the whole text.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_under_ot.text: Checks whether a line sits just under a heading for some other list (like the syllabus), in which case a stage name on it refers to that list, not to the exam's structure.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::_under_ot.tech: Looks back up to reach (5) lines for a line that is a marked heading matching _NOT_THE_SCHEME but not _SCHEME_HEADING; True if found.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::describe.text: Produces a count summary of an extracted exam structure for a build report: number of stages, papers, sections, subjects and parts, the depth, and how many values of each kind are verified, under review or computed.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::describe.tech: Returns a dict with stages, papers, sections, subjects, parts (of_level counts) and depth (max_depth), plus, for each of questions, marks, duration_minutes, negative_marking, qualifying, languages, mode, question_type and marks_per_question, a map of status value (or 'DERIVED' for derived facts with a value) to node count.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::extract_p.text: Reads the exam's structure (its stages, papers and sections, with questions, marks, time, penalties, whether each part counts for merit, and languages) out of one official document, for one named exam only. It finds stage headings, reads the scheme table or listed papers under each, attaches rules stated elsewhere in the document to the part they name, removes duplicate headings, and holds back any figure it cannot read with confidence. Every value is tied to the exact words in the document.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::extract_p.tech: Returns an empty ExamPattern(exam_id, cycle) without text or exam_id or without _stage_regions. For each region not inside an already-consumed stage and not a duplicate id: _stage_name, _find_scheme_header (extending the region via _extend_past_rows if found), _read_table_rows or else _read_prose_papers, a STAGE PatternNode with heading evidence, _apply_stage_rules over up to 60 lines; kept only if _keeps and not (empty and _under_other_heading). Records scheme-kind containers. Then _fold_restated_stages, _apply_merit_statements, _push_down_stage_rules, _classify_scheme_containers (and a second only_unset merit pass plus push-down if containers exist), _apply_language_statements and _hold_figures_of_unsure_rows.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::may_suppl.text: Decides whether a document is allowed to supply exam-structure facts for a given exam. Yes if it names only this exam; no if it belongs to another exam; if it names several exams, yes only when this exam is named in the document's opening title area, and never for an exam identified only by a common job title.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::may_suppl.tech: identity.verify(text, target): MATCH -> (True, ...); MISMATCH -> (False, refused + reason). If designation_mode(target) -> (False, ...). Otherwise verifies the first _TITLE_BLOCK (3000) chars and returns True if that is MATCH or has any matched alias; else (False, not published). Returns (allowed, reason).

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::read_nega.text: Reads what a passage of a notice says about marks lost for wrong answers. It recognises an explicit 'no negative marking', a fixed number of marks deducted, or a fraction (like one-third) of the question's marks. If the passage mentions a penalty but in a form it cannot read, it keeps the wording without inventing a number. If the passage says nothing about it, it returns nothing, which is different from 'no penalty'.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::read_nega.tech: Normalises whitespace. _NEG_NONE -> NegativeMarking(deducted_per_wrong=0.0). No _NEG_CUE -> None. _NEG_FLAT -> deducted_per_wrong from the first non-empty group. _NEG_FRACTION -> fraction_of_marks from a word (via _FRACTION_WORDS, overridden by a parenthesised decimal) or num/den, rounded to 4 places. Otherwise NegativeMarking with only as_printed. as_printed always comes from _sentence_around.

tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::read_qual.text: Reads whether a part of the exam is only qualifying (must be passed but does not count towards the final ranking) or counts for merit, and any minimum percentage or minimum marks the notice states. Returns nothing if the passage says none of this.
tools/exam_builder/pattern.py::read_qual.tech: Builds a QualifyingRule: _QUALIFYING_ONLY sets is_qualifying_only True and counts_towards_merit False; _MIN_PERCENT sets minimum_percent; _MIN_MARKS sets minimum_marks; _MERIT_HEADING sets counts_towards_merit True if still unset. as_printed is the first matching sentence. Returns None unless as_printed or a minimum was found.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::IDE.text: The minimum similarity score (0.85) at which a record's stage and a document's stage are treated as the same.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Pat.text: The result of comparing an exam's recorded stages with those read from a document: one decision per stage.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Pat.tech: Holds decisions (list of StageDecision) with of(), summary() and fields_of().

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Pat.text: Lists every stage field that ended with a given outcome, such as all those held for review.
Picks out the stage decisions of one kind.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Pat.tech: Decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Pat.text: Counts how many stages got each kind of decision.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.text: A record of what the merge decided about one exam stage, including the per-figure decisions and how sure the match was.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.tech: Plain class with action (MergeAction), name, stage_id, fields (list of FieldDecision), reason and identity score.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.text: Sets up a stage decision with its outcome, name, id, field decisions, reason and match score.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.tech: Assigns the constructor arguments; fields defaults to [].

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.text: Finds the decision about one named field of the stage.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::Sta.tech: First FieldDecision whose field equals name, or None.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_co.text: Reduces a stage code such as 'Tier-II' to plain letters and digits ('tierii') so codes can be compared.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_co.tech: Lowercases and removes every non-alphanumeric character.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_ne.text: Compares the wrong-answer penalty described in the record with the one read from the document: kept, added, confirmed if they state the same figure, or held for review if they differ.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_ne.tech: No fact -> KEPT; empty record text -> ADDED with as_printed; _same_penalty -> CONFIRMED; else UNDER_REVIEW. Field name 'negativeMarking'.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_nu.text: Compares one figure for a stage (total questions, total marks or duration) between the record and the document: kept if the document is silent, added if the record lacked it, confirmed if they match, otherwise held for review.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_nu.tech: stated requires a VERIFIED fact with a value; existing of None, 0 or '' counts as absent. Returns a FieldDecision KEPT / ADDED / CONFIRMED (float equality) / UNDER_REVIEW.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_sa.text: Checks whether the record's sentence about negative marking and the rule read from the document state the same penalty, comparing the actual figure (or 'no negative marking').
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_sa.tech: deducted_per_wrong == 0 -> record must say no...negative/none/nil. A flat deduction must appear among the record's numbers. A fraction matches a number rounded to 2 or 4 places, or a fraction word (one-third, one-fourth, quarter, half) within 0.02. Otherwise False.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_wo.text: Breaks a stage name into its distinctive words, ignoring common ones like 'examination', 'paper' or 'phase'.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_wo.tech: Lowercase alphanumeric tokens longer than 2 chars not in _GENERIC, as a set.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_wo.text: Breaks a stage name into all of its words, including the common ones.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::_wo.tech: List of lowercase alphanumeric tokens, none dropped.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::mer.text: Compares the exam stages a record already holds with the stages read from an official document and reports what would change, without changing anything. Each recorded stage is matched to a read stage only when clearly the same; its name is kept, and its question count, marks, duration and negative marking are confirmed, added or held for review. Read stages the record lacks are reported as new.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::mer.tech: existing is a list of ExamStage dicts. For each, the code is the _STAGE_LABELLED match in stageName, else row['tier']; scores incoming.stages with node_identity. Best < IDENTITY_THRESHOLD -> UNCHANGED; runner-up >= threshold -> CONFLICTED. Otherwise FieldDecisions: stageName KEPT, _numeric_decision for totalQuestions/questions, totalMarks/marks, durationMinutes/duration_minutes, and _negative_decision; CONFIRMED or CONFLICTED if any UNDER_REVIEW. Unmatched incoming stages -> ADDED. Returns PatternMergeReport; writes nothing.

tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::nod.text: Scores from 0 to 1 how sure GovOS is that a stage in the exam record and a stage read from a document are the same stage. If both have a code like 'Tier-II', the codes alone decide. Otherwise the distinctive words in the names decide, and sharing only common words counts for nothing.
tools/exam_builder/pattern_merge.py::nod.tech: Both codes present: 1.0 if equal after _code, else 0.0. If either name has no distinguishing words, compares full word sequences: equal or one contained in the other -> 0.9, else 0.0. Equal word sets -> 1.0; no overlap -> 0.0; subset -> 0.9 with 2+ shared words else 0.5; otherwise 0.4 * shared / max(len).

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::DATA_TS.text: The location of the hand-written exam file (src/data.ts) that the publisher works on.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::DATA_TS.tech: os.path.join('src', 'data.ts'), relative to the working directory.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::ExamSlice.text: One exam's block of text cut out of the hand-written exam file, with its name, id and position, so it can be fingerprinted on its own.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::ExamSlice.tech: Dataclass: const_name, exam_id, start, end, text; digest property.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::ExamSlice.text: A short fingerprint of this exam's text, used to prove it did not change.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::ExamSlice.tech: First 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of the UTF-8 text.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::Isolation.text: The error raised when publishing one exam would change another exam's content; the build is then void.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::Isolation.tech: RuntimeError subclass, caught by orchestrate as ISOLATION_VIOLATION.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::PublishRe.text: The record of one publish attempt: which exam, where it was staged, the fingerprints before and after, which exams were added, replaced or left untouched, and whether it went live.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::PublishRe.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, staged_path, before, after (id -> digest), added, replaced, untouched (lists of ids), published (bool); summary() prints a short report.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::PublishRe.text: Produces a short, readable printout of what happened when one exam's record was prepared for the exam register: which exam, where the trial copy was saved, what was added or replaced, how many other exams were left alone, and whether it went live.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::PublishRe.tech: Returns a multi-line string built from exam_id, staged_path, added, replaced ("-" when empty), the count of untouched exam ids (with the fixed claim that their hashes are identical) and the published flag. No side effects.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::STAGING_D.text: The folder where build outputs are staged for review before anything goes live.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::STAGING_D.tech: '.exam_staging', relative to the working directory; also used by orchestrate._write_staging.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::assert_on.text: The safety check that proves building one exam did not disturb any other exam in the register. It compares a fingerprint of every exam before and after, and stops everything with an error if another exam was removed, changed or added.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::assert_on.tech: Takes before/after maps of exam id -> digest (from fingerprint) and the exam_id being built. Raises IsolationViolation if any id was removed, if any id other than exam_id changed digest, or if any id other than exam_id was added. Otherwise returns (added ids, [exam_id] if it changed, untouched ids with identical digests).

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::fingerpri.text: Makes a list of fingerprints, one per exam in the file, so before-and-after copies can be compared.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::publish.text: Makes a staged exam record live by copying the trial register over the real one. It first re-checks that only this exam differs from the register as it is right now, and (by default) runs the TypeScript type check; if that check fails, the original file is put back.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::publish.tech: Reads report.staged_path and the current data_ts, re-runs assert_only_this_exam_changed against the live file now (raises IsolationViolation on violation). With typecheck=True: backs up data_ts to <staged>.live-backup, writes the staged source over data_ts, runs `npx tsc --noEmit` via subprocess (shell on Windows), and on non-zero exit restores the backup and raises IsolationViolation with up to 1500 chars of output. With typecheck=False it just overwrites. Sets report.published=True and returns the report.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::slice_exa.text: Cuts the hand-written exam file into one piece per exam, using each exam's own declaration line and its closing brace, and reads each piece's id.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::slice_exa.tech: Finds 'export const X: Exam = {' declarations; each slice ends at the first '};' alone on a line before the next declaration (or that declaration / end of file if none). exam_id from the first "id: '...'" line, else '(no id: X)'. Returns list of ExamSlice.

tools/exam_builder/publish.py::stage.text: Prepares a trial copy of the exam register (src/data.ts) with one exam's new record put in, without touching the real file. It replaces that exam's old block if there is one, or adds the new one at the end, saves the copy in a staging folder, and checks that no other exam changed.
tools/exam_builder/publish.py::stage.tech: Reads data_ts, fingerprints it, and if slice_exams finds a block with this exam_id splices record_ts in its place; otherwise appends record_ts at the end (deliberately never between records). Writes the result to staging_dir/<exam_id>-<timestamp>.ts, fingerprints it and runs assert_only_this_exam_changed (which may raise IsolationViolation). Returns a PublishReport with before/after digests and added/replaced/untouched lists; published stays False.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_iso.text: Turns a date found in a notice, written like '17.06.2026' or '17 June 2026', into the standard form 2026-06-17.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_iso.tech: Takes a match of the module _DATE regex. Numeric form (groups 1-3) returns YYYY-MM-DD zero-padded; month-name form (groups 4-6) looks up the month in _MONTHS; returns '' if neither applies.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_iso_from.text: Finds the first date in a piece of text and returns it in the standard year-month-day form, or nothing if there is no date.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_iso_from.tech: Searches value with _DATE and returns _iso(match), or '' when no date is found.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_link_evidenc.text: Checks that a paper's link really appears on the listing page GovOS read, and if so returns the proof (a quoted piece of that page).
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_link_evidenc.tech: Returns None when page_text is empty; otherwise _evidence(href[-90:], doc, page_text, reading='a paper linked on the listing'), i.e. evidence only if the last 90 chars of the href occur verbatim in the page text.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_next_option_.text: Works out what the next answer choice label should be after the ones already read, for example 'c' after 'b' or '3' after '2'. Used to tell an answer choice apart from the next question number.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_next_option_.tech: Returns None for an empty list; otherwise looks at the last option's label: a digit returns str(n+1), a single letter returns the next character, anything else returns None.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::_roman_or_num.text: Tidies a small label such as a paper number or shift number by trimming spaces and putting it in capitals, so 'ii' becomes 'II'.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::catalogue_pap.text: Goes through the list of file links on an authority's question-paper page and keeps only the ones that belong to this exam. A file is kept only if its own name carries this exam's code, does not carry another exam's code, and names a specific paper (not just a year). Each kept paper is recorded with its link, marked as 'not yet read into questions'; everything refused is returned with the reason.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::catalogue_pap.tech: For each href: takes the decoded file name; rejects it if no exam_codes entry occurs in it, if any reject_codes entry does, or if identity_from_text (with codes and subject_from_name) is not is_paper_level. Otherwise builds an OfficialPaper whose url is Fact.verified when _link_evidence finds the href verbatim in page_text (absolute URLs only), else Fact.needs_review; contents = Fact.not_extracted; status VERIFIED or NEEDS_REVIEW to match the url; evidence copied from the url. Returns (kept papers, list of (name, reason)).

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_keys.text: Gives a short count of the answer keys found: how many, of which kinds, how many contain actual answers, how many replace an earlier key, and which papers they are for.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_keys.tech: Returns {'keys': n, 'kinds': count by kind value, 'withEntries': keys with non-empty entries, 'revisions': keys with revises set, 'papers': sorted distinct paper.describe()}.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_pape.text: Gives a short count of the question papers found: how many, how many have readable contents, how many are in each check state, and which years they cover.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_pape.tech: Returns {'papers': n, 'withContents': count where contents.has_value, 'states': count by status value, 'cycles': sorted distinct identity.cycle values}.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_ques.text: Gives a short count of the questions read: how many, in each check state and question type, how many have a publishable answer, and which papers they came from.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::describe_ques.tech: Returns {'questions': n, 'states': count by status, 'formats': count by format, 'withAnswer': questions whose answer exists and is_publishable, 'papers': sorted distinct paper.describe()}.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::extract_quest.text: Reads the questions out of a question paper whose text can be read, and ties every one of them to the paper the caller names. It picks up each question's number, wording, answer choices with their printed labels, and the marks where printed, and groups questions under a reading passage when there is one. It never produces an answer: every question is recorded as 'answer not published' because a question paper is not an answer key.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::extract_quest.tech: Returns [] for empty text or a paper without exam_id. Walks lines with _Cursor: a passage cue line (before any question) sets passage_id/passage_text; lines matching both the option and question-number patterns are disambiguated by sequence (continuing the options or a first a/1/i option wins, noting ambiguity when it also continues question numbering; otherwise continuing the question numbering wins). New question numbers start an OfficialQuestion with VERIFIED status and evidence when the line is verbatim in the text, else NEEDS_REVIEW. finish() joins the body (max 1200 chars), sets format (MULTIPLE_CHOICE / PASSAGE_BASED / DESCRIPTIVE) and reads marks via _MARKS. Finally every question without an answer gets AnswerEntry(status NOT_PUBLISHED).

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::identity_from.text: Reads which exact paper a piece of the authority's own wording refers to: a file name, link text or notice subject line. It picks out the year, the stage (for example Preliminary or Main), the paper number, the shift, the set and the language where they are printed, and leaves any part blank rather than inventing it. This identity is what later decides whether an answer key belongs to a paper.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::identity_from.tech: URL-decodes text and turns underscores into spaces. Cycle: the cycle argument, else the first 4-digit 19xx/20xx year. Stage: from the caller's codes dict (code -> {'stage': ...}), matched with separators normalised, also reading a 2- or 4-digit year right after the code when no cycle was found (2-digit becomes 20xx); else from _STAGE_WORDS (Preliminary/Main/Interview as-is, others as 'Label-ORDINAL'). Paper, session ('Shift N' or titled word), set ('Set X') and language come from module regexes. Returns a frozen PaperIdentity with exam_id and the given subject.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::link_revision.text: Links each answer key to the earlier key it replaces for the same paper, for example a final key to the provisional one. Both are kept, so a candidate who challenged an answer can see both versions.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::link_revision.tech: Groups keys by paper.key(), sorts each group by kind order (PROVISIONAL 0, UNSPECIFIED 1, REVISED 2, FINAL 3) then published_at value, and for each consecutive pair of different kinds sets later.revises = earlier.id. Mutates and returns the same list.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::mark_unreadab.text: Records why a paper's questions are missing when the file is a scanned image with no text in it. It notes that the paper exists but could not be read, and explains that GovOS does not use text recognition on it because that misreads answer labels.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::mark_unreadab.tech: If words == 0, sets paper.contents to Fact.not_extracted with the scan/no-text-layer/OCR-unreliable reason and paper.note='scan, no text layer'. Otherwise leaves the paper unchanged. Returns the same paper object (mutated in place).

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::read_answer_k.text: Reads an authority's notice announcing an answer key and records that key against the exact paper it answers. It notes what kind of key it is (provisional, revised or final), when it was published, the window for viewing or challenging it, and how candidates reach it (for example through their own login). If the notice is not about a key, or the exact paper cannot be identified, it records nothing rather than guessing.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::read_answer_k.tech: Returns None unless 'answer key' appears in the headline/first 400 chars or the first 1500 chars of the body. Kind from _KEY_KIND (FINAL/REVISED/PROVISIONAL, else UNSPECIFIED). Identity from identity_from_text on the subject, then the body; returns None if not is_paper_level. Builds AnswerKey with id 'key-<slug>-<kind>'; url and published_at (argument or first date in body) are Fact.verified when the subject is verbatim in the text, else needs_review; window_opens/closes from 'from X to Y'; access from login wording. Sets status/source_status VERIFIED/OFFICIAL_VERIFIED or NEEDS_REVIEW, and a note that per-question answers are not public when entries is empty.

tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::subject_from_.text: Works out what a question paper is about from its file name, using the authority's own words. It removes filing codes, years and words like 'paper' or 'optional', so 'Optional-AGRICULTURE_PAPER_I' becomes 'Agriculture'. Nothing is translated or guessed.
tools/exam_builder/pyq.py::subject_from_.tech: URL-decodes the name, drops the extension, splits on -, _ and spaces. Skips a leading run of filing tokens (2-4 letter all-caps codes, 2-8 digit numbers, qp/paper/optional/compulsory/final/revised/copy) but never the last token; then removes remaining noise tokens and Roman numerals I-XXXX. Returns '' if fewer than 3 characters remain, else the words joined with all-caps words capitalised, truncated to 70 chars.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.text: A record of what the merge step decided about one question paper, question or answer key: whether it was added, confirmed, left alone, replaced or disputed, and why.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.tech: Plain class holding action (MergeAction), label, item_id, fields (list of FieldDecision), reason and superseded (id of the item it replaces). Used in PyqMergeReport.decisions.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.text: Sets up a decision record with its outcome, a label, an optional id, per-field details, the reason and anything it replaces.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.tech: Stores action, label, item_id (default ''), fields (default []), reason (default '') and superseded (default '') as attributes.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.text: Looks up the decision made about one named detail (for example the question's wording) within this item's decision.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::ItemDec.tech: Returns the first FieldDecision in self.fields whose .field equals name, or None.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.text: The full list of decisions from merging question papers, questions or answer keys into an exam's record.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.tech: Holds decisions: list[ItemDecision], with helpers of() to filter by action and summary() to count by action.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.text: Returns only the decisions of one kind, for example all the added items.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.tech: Returns [d for d in decisions if d.action is action].

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.text: Counts how many decisions of each kind the merge made.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::PyqMerg.tech: Returns a dict mapping MergeAction value -> count over self.decisions.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::_answer.text: Turns a key's list of answers into a simple lookup from question number to the answer given, so two keys can be compared question by question.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::_answer.tech: (entries) -> {question_number: (sorted lower-cased accepted labels, printed value)} for AnswerEntry objects or record dicts (question_number / questionNumber, accepted, value); entries with no number or no stated answer are skipped.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::_normal.text: Simplifies text for comparison by collapsing spaces and ignoring capital letters.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::_questi.text: Sorts question numbers the way a person would: 2 before 10, numbers before anything else.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::_questi.tech: (number) -> (0, int) for digit strings, else (1, number); used as a sort key when naming disagreeing questions.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_a.text: Compares newly found answer keys with those an exam record holds, matching only on the exact paper. A later kind of key (for example a final key after a provisional one) is recorded as replacing the earlier one, which is kept. A key of the same kind is confirmed only if no answer differs; if two keys of the same standing give different answers, it is a conflict and neither wins. New keys are added, and record entries whose paper is not exactly identified are left alone.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_a.tech: For each existing row (dict with 'paper' PaperIdentity, 'kind', 'id', optional 'entries'): non-paper-level identity -> UNCHANGED; no incoming key with same_paper -> UNCHANGED; any incoming key of a higher _KEY_ORDER -> SUPERSEDED naming the newest; else same-kind keys are compared via _answer_map (question number -> sorted accepted labels and value) against the row's entries and against each other: any difference -> CONFLICTED naming the questions, otherwise CONFIRMED; else UNCHANGED (only earlier kinds found). Same-kind keys are consumed either way; other incoming keys become ADDED. Returns a PyqMergeReport.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_a.text: Combines the question-by-question answers of two answer keys for the same paper. It refuses outright if the papers differ. Where the answers agree the earlier one is kept; where a later kind of key changes an answer, the new answer replaces it and remembers the old one; where two keys of the same standing disagree, no answer is published for that question.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_a.tech: Raises ValueError unless same_paper(existing.paper, incoming.paper). revises = incoming kind ranks above existing in _KEY_ORDER. For each incoming entry: new number -> kept; equal sorted accepted and value -> existing entry kept; differing and not revises -> new AnswerEntry with status UNKNOWN and an explanatory note; differing and revises -> entry.supersedes=earlier and status REVISED when it has accepted/value. Existing entries with numbers absent from the output are appended. Returns the list of AnswerEntry.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_q.text: Compares newly read questions with those an exam record already holds, matching on the exact paper and the question number together, never the number alone. Matching questions with the same wording are confirmed; if the wording differs it is flagged as disputed and neither wins; questions the record lacks are added; record entries that cannot be matched are left exactly as they are.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::merge_q.tech: Existing rows are dicts with a PaperIdentity under 'paper' and 'number'/'questionNumber'. Rows without both are UNCHANGED. Candidates are incoming questions with same_paper and equal number (case/space-insensitive): none -> UNCHANGED; more than one -> CONFLICTED; one -> compares whitespace/case-normalised text ('text' or 'promptEnglish'): differing non-empty text -> CONFLICTED with a 'text' UNDER_REVIEW FieldDecision, else CONFIRMED. Unused incoming questions become ADDED. Returns a PyqMergeReport; does not modify inputs.

tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::same_pa.text: Decides whether two descriptions refer to exactly the same question paper. One may leave out a detail the other has, but if both state a detail (such as the shift) and they differ, they are different papers. This is what stops one shift's answers reaching another shift.
tools/exam_builder/pyq_merge.py::same_pa.tech: Returns left.matches(right) (PaperIdentity.matches); a thin named wrapper used throughout the module.

tools/exam_builder/render.py::EXISTS.text: A label meaning the exam being built already has a record in the exam register.
tools/exam_builder/render.py::EXISTS.tech: String constant 'EXISTS', the counterpart of NEW.

tools/exam_builder/render.py::NEW.text: A label meaning the exam being built is not yet in the exam register.
tools/exam_builder/render.py::NEW.tech: String constant 'NEW', exported alongside EXISTS for callers describing a build target.

tools/exam_builder/render.py::target_in_.text: Checks whether an exam with a given id already has a record in the exam register file. If the file cannot be read it answers no.
tools/exam_builder/render.py::target_in_.tech: Reads data_ts (default publish.DATA_TS) and returns exam_id in publish.fingerprint(source), reusing the textual exam slicing rather than parsing TypeScript. Returns False on OSError.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Ambiguous.text: An error raised when two or more real organisations answer to an exam's name, so GovOS cannot honestly say which one runs it. It carries all the candidates and the evidence, so the person can be told or asked instead of GovOS picking one.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Ambiguous.tech: RuntimeError subclass carrying .verdict (an AuthorityVerdict with every candidate and the reason); the message is verdict.reason. Raised by resolve() when ambiguity.decide returns AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY; resolve_authority turns it back into the verdict.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Ambiguous.text: Creates the error with the full decision attached.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Ambiguous.tech: Calls RuntimeError.__init__(verdict.reason) and stores self.verdict = verdict.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Authority.text: Describes the organisation found to conduct an exam: its name, its official web address, how confident GovOS is, where the name came from, which page vouched for a non-government site, the pages the decision was based on, and any rival organisations.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::Authority.tech: Dataclass: name, domain, confidence (float), corroborated_by (official page URL vouching for a non-.gov host, else ''), name_status (default 'CANONICAL_NAME_INFERRED'), name_source, evidence (list of URLs), rivals (list of (domain, share)).

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::ResolvedE.text: The result of identifying an exam: what the person searched for, the exam's official name, its year, the organisation that runs it, and official pages to start reading from.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::ResolvedE.tech: Dataclass: query, official_name, year, authority (Authority), seed_urls (list of official page URLs that mentioned the exam, used by discovery).

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_authorit.text: Gets an organisation's name as plain text from its web address and search results. A simpler form of the name lookup that drops the record of where the name came from.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_authorit.tech: Returns names.resolve_name(host, hits).value (imported lazily). The docstring says to prefer resolve_name, which keeps provenance.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_authorit.text: Collects every word by which a page might be naming the organisation rather than the exam: the words of its name, its initials, and the parts of its web address.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_authorit.tech: Returns a set of distinctive_words(authority_name), plus the initials of its words (excluding of/and/the/for) when at least 2 letters, plus every label of the host minus 'www.'. Used by resolve's looks_like_a_name to reject titles that only name the authority.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_corrobor.text: Finds non-government websites (such as IBPS or LIC) that an official government page points to for this exam. Such a site is only accepted when a government page names it, so no random website can claim to be the recruiter.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_corrobor.tech: Runs a wide search (official_only=False) for '<query> official notification apply' and takes non-OFFICIAL hosts not in _AGGREGATORS; then an official-only search for '<query> official website', and maps each candidate host appearing in an official page's title/content to the first such page URL. Returns {} when nothing is found or SearchUnavailable is raised by either search.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_label_of.text: Takes a web address's first part, such as 'upsc' from upsc.gov.in, which is often the organisation's short name.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_label_of.tech: Strips 'www.', returns the first dot-separated label lower-cased; '' for an empty host.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::_year_in.text: Finds a year such as 2026 in a piece of text.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::alias_in.text: Checks whether a name for the exam appears in a piece of text. A pair like 'group i' must appear as its own term, so it is found in 'Group-I' but never inside 'Group-II'.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::alias_in.tech: A single-word alias is a plain substring test. An alias with a space is split into head and ordinal and matched with a word-bounded regex allowing space or dash separators and forbidding a following alphanumeric (optionally after a dash). Returns bool.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::distincti.text: Picks out the words in an exam's name that actually tell it apart, dropping common words like 'exam', 'recruitment' or 'the', numbers, and very short words.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::distincti.tech: Lower-cases, splits on non-alphanumerics and returns words longer than 2 characters, not in _GENERIC and not all digits.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::exam_alia.text: Lists every short form and spelling that legitimately names an exam, both the full words and the abbreviation, for example 'combined graduate level' and 'cgl'. Abbreviations are made from the name itself, never from a hand-kept list of exams.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::exam_alia.tech: Collects distinctive_words of query and official_name; replaces the bare head of each ordinal compound with the compound. For each source adds the acronym of all distinctive words and of all but the first (when 2-6 letters), plus any 2-6 letter all-caps tokens typed in the source (lower-cased). Returns the sorted aliases of length >= 3.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::id_words.text: Picks out the words used to build an exam's id. Unlike distinctive_words it keeps short words such as 'PO', 'SO' or 'I', because those are exactly what separate two similar exams.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::id_words.tech: Same split as distinctive_words but with no length filter: returns non-empty words not in _GENERIC and not all digits. Used by stable_exam_id.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::ordinal_c.text: Finds pairs like 'Group-I', 'Paper-II' or 'Grade B' in an exam's name and keeps them together as one term, so 'Group-I' and 'Group-II' are never treated as the same exam.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::ordinal_c.tech: Lower-cases the name and finds _ORDINAL_COMPOUND_RX matches (a 3+ letter word, a space/dash separator, then a Roman numeral, a-d or 1-2 digits on a boundary). Skips heads in _GENERIC and returns de-duplicated 'head ordinal' strings in order.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::resolve.text: Works out which organisation conducts an exam, using official websites only. It searches official sites for the exam's name and lets the results vote: the site with the most pages carrying the exam's distinctive words wins. If no government site is about the exam, it accepts a non-government site only when an official page vouches for it or the site identifies itself. It refuses (raises an error) when it cannot search, when nothing official matches, or when two organisations are equally plausible, because naming the wrong one would attach one body's rules to another's exam.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::resolve.tech: Raises LookupError for a query with no distinctive words. Runs two official-only searches; if none hit, tries corroborated non-gov hosts, then officiality.best_official_domain over a wide search (forced_host). Scores each non-aggregator host by covered distinctive words/len(words) plus 0.5 per word in the host; if no score, retries with best_official_domain and _corroborated_hosts. Raises LookupError if still nothing. Names each host with names.resolve_name (fetching with safe_load_html), then ambiguity.decide; AMBIGUOUS_AUTHORITY raises AmbiguousAuthority, and a chosen share below min_confidence with rivals raises LookupError. Picks the official name as the title segment that looks like a name, names the exam (alias_in), is not only authority words, and best matches the words/year; falls back to the query. Returns ResolvedExam with Authority (domain https://host, rounded confidence, corroboration, evidence, up to 3 rivals) and seed_urls.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::resolve_a.text: The same authority lookup as resolve, but it always returns an answer instead of raising an error. The answer is one of four outcomes kept strictly apart: resolved, ambiguous (several organisations), could not search (says nothing about any organisation), or unresolved (searched and nothing matched).
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::resolve_a.tech: Calls resolve(); maps AmbiguousAuthority -> its verdict, SearchUnavailable -> AuthorityVerdict(INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, infrastructure_note), LookupError -> AuthorityVerdict(UNRESOLVED, reason). On success builds an AuthorityCandidate from the resolved authority (setting _share to its confidence) and returns AuthorityVerdict(RESOLVED) with .resolved set to the ResolvedExam.

tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::stable_ex.text: Builds a lasting id for an exam from the organisation's web address and the exam's own name, plus the year, for example 'exam-ssc-cgl-2026'. It uses what the person typed first, and keeps short distinguishing words like 'PO' so similar exams get different ids.
tools/exam_builder/resolve.py::stable_ex.tech: Takes the first label of the authority domain's hostname as org, id_words(query) or else id_words(official_name) de-duplicated and joined with '-' (max 60 chars), and returns 'exam-<org>-<slug>' plus '-<year>' when resolved.year is set.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::HU.text: Words that show a link leads to a useful listing page (notifications, results, papers, admit cards and so on). A link with none of these words and no known kind is treated as site furniture like 'About us' and not followed.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::HU.tech: Case-insensitive compiled regex of hub vocabulary (notification, recruitment, exam, results, keys, question papers, archive, syllabus, hall ticket, OTR, application, cut-off, calendar, interview, merit, etc.). Used by is_hub_link.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::LE.text: The three kinds of resource that count as learning material (study material, lecture videos and practice tools). Only these appear in an exam's Resources section.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::LE.tech: frozenset {DocKind.STUDY_MATERIAL, DocKind.LECTURE_VIDEO, DocKind.PRACTICE_TOOL}; checked by is_learning.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::RE.text: Words in a page's name that show it is a list of many documents of one kind, such as 'previous year question papers', 'results', 'notifications' or 'archive'.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::RE.tech: Case-insensitive compiled regex matching repository/listing names (old/previous/past question papers, archives, downloads, repository, answer keys, results, notifications, syllabus, cut-offs, selection lists, keys).

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::SE.text: The table saying which section of an exam's page each kind of document belongs in: notices under Official Links, question papers and answer keys under Practice, application portals under Application, study material under Resources, and so on. News leads and unclassified items are shown nowhere.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::SE.tech: Dict DocKind -> section key ('OFFICIAL_LINKS', 'CORRIGENDA', 'SYLLABUS', 'PATTERN', 'PRACTICE', 'ADMIT_CARD', 'RESULTS', 'CUTOFFS', 'DATES', 'APPLICATION', 'OVERVIEW', 'EXAM_DAY', 'RESOURCES') or None for DISCOVERY_SIGNAL and UNKNOWN. Mirrored by RESOURCE_SECTION in ui.tsx and pinned by resource_role_cases.json.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::cl.text: Decides what role a link found while exploring an authority's website plays (notification, question paper, registration portal, study material, lecture and so on), using its words, its address, the heading it sits under and the listing it belongs to. If none of that says what it is, the role stays unknown rather than being guessed.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::cl.tech: Returns (DocKind, NodeType, reason, video kind). Videos go through video_kind on text+context; social URLs are DISCOVERY_SIGNAL. Then _EARLY rules (OTR, application guide, exam-day instructions), then discover.classify_kind; an APPLICATION_PORTAL whose text is_headline becomes CORRIGENDUM (if it changes a date) or NOTIFICATION. Then mock/practice test -> PRACTICE_TOOL; a repository item inherits parent_role; then _LATE rules (study material, lecture video, official portal); then classify_kind on the context heading; then parent role again; else UNKNOWN.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::cl.text: Decides the role of a resource card already stored in an exam's record (from its title, subject, type and format), so each card is shown in the right section. Third-party pages are filed by what they carry, videos are lectures unless they are news or walkthroughs, tools are practice tools, official documents are sorted into their kind, and a law's text counts as study material. This mirrors the same rule in the app's screen code.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::cl.tech: An explicit valid 'role' wins. THIRD_PARTY/EXTERNAL_PAGE: first _ITEM_RULES match on title+officialTag, else QUESTION_PAPER for 'previous year papers' subject, else STUDY_MATERIAL. VIDEO_LECTURE or YouTube formats: video_kind, with UNKNOWN/EXAM_GUIDE coerced to LECTURE_VIDEO. ONLINE_TOOL -> PRACTICE_TOOL. 'previous year papers' -> ANSWER_KEY or QUESTION_PAPER. Official subjects: study reference (constitution, India Code, NCERT...) -> STUDY_MATERIAL; application portal; three or more named kinds or a portal naming only notifications -> OFFICIAL_PORTAL; gazette/archive -> OFFICIAL_PORTAL; else first rule match or OFFICIAL_PORTAL. Other subjects: ANSWER_KEY/QUESTION_PAPER if named, else STUDY_MATERIAL. Mirrors resourceRoleOf in ui.tsx.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::is.text: Tells a notice title apart from a menu label: a title is either long (more than seven words) or contains a reference number or a date.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::is.tech: Returns True if the text has more than 7 words or matches _HEADLINE (no/dt/dated followed by a digit, or a d/m/y date).

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::is.text: Decides whether a link is worth following as a listing page: either it has a known role, or its words include listing vocabulary.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::is.tech: Returns True when role is neither UNKNOWN nor DISCOVERY_SIGNAL, or when HUB_WORDS matches the text.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::is.text: Answers whether a kind of resource is learning material that belongs in the Resources section.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::no.text: Decides what sort of thing a link points to: a video, a social media post, a document file, a portal, or an ordinary link.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::no.tech: Returns NodeType.VIDEO if is_video(url), SOCIAL if is_social(url), DOCUMENT if the path ends with a document extension (pdf, doc(x), xls(x), ppt(x), zip, rar, odt, ods), PORTAL for OTR/APPLICATION/OFFICIAL portal roles, else LINK.

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::se.text: Says which section of the exam page a kind of resource belongs in, or none.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::se.tech: Returns SECTION_FOR_ROLE.get(role) (None for unknown or unlisted roles).

tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::vi.text: Decides what a video is from its title and description: an application walkthrough, a news update, an exam explanation, a study lecture, or something else. The order matters, so a video saying a result is 'out' counts as news, not a lesson.
tools/exam_builder/resource_roles.py::vi.tech: Checks regexes in order and returns (kind, DocKind): APPLICATION_WALKTHROUGH/APPLICATION_GUIDE; NEWS_UPDATE/DISCOVERY_SIGNAL; EXAM_EXPLANATION/EXAM_GUIDE; STUDY_LECTURE/LECTURE_VIDEO (class, lecture, subject words etc.); else ('OTHER', UNKNOWN).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_count.text: Reads how many candidates cleared, such as '13,343 candidates'. If the notice prints several different totals (for example one per day of a schedule), it records no count rather than picking one or adding them up.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_count.tech: Returns Fact.not_extracted when _COUNT_CUE finds nothing or when its matches yield more than one distinct integer (listing up to six). Otherwise parses the first match (commas removed) and returns Fact.verified(value, evidence, 0.8) when the 200-char window is verbatim, else Fact.needs_review; not_extracted if it cannot be parsed.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_cycle_in.text: Finds the exam year mentioned in a piece of text, or uses a given fallback year.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_cycle_in.tech: Returns group(1) of the first admit_card._YEAR match in text, else fallback.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_dated.text: Finds the first date that appears shortly after a given point in the text and records it with proof from the page. If the authority printed only a month, it says so instead of inventing a day.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_dated.tech: Iterates pre-read dates; takes the first whose start lies in [at, at+window] (default 120 chars). Returns (Fact, date) where Fact is needs_review(d.iso) if the 240-char window is not verbatim, else Fact.verified(d.iso, evidence, 0.9 or 0.7 for non-DAY precision) with a month-precision note. Returns (None, None) if no date is in range.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_dated_no.text: Finds the date a notice carries as its own, the 'Date: ...' line just above the signature, which is when the declaration was issued. Dates printed for each session in a schedule table are ignored.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_dated_no.tech: For each 'Date:' line match, looks for a date starting within 3 chars after it that is followed within 80 chars by a signature word (secretary, sd/-, signed, controller of exams, chairman); returns _dated(...) for that date with window 3. Returns (None, None) otherwise.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_declarat.text: Finds the date a notice says the result was declared, by looking right after words like 'declared on' or 'uploaded on'.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_declarat.tech: For each _DECLARED_CUE match, takes the first date beginning within 25 chars after the cue and returns _dated('result declared', ...) for it; (None, None) if none.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_document.text: Picks the document's own name out of a longer row of text, for example just 'Result' from 'Result of Online examination - Preliminary September, 2026'.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_document.tech: Returns the whitespace-normalised text of the first _KIND_CUES match in the label, stripped of spaces/dashes; falls back to the normalised whole label.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_followin.text: Finds the stage that comes after a given stage in the exam's own list of stages, or nothing if the list does not place it. It matches on stage markers and never guesses.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_followin.tech: Computes _stage_words(stage_name); returns '' when empty. Returns the name after the first entry in names sharing any stage word, or '' if that entry is last or none match.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_new.text: Creates a blank result declaration for one exam, kind and stage, with every detail (dates, links, counts, next step) marked 'not read yet' until something fills it in.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_new.tech: Returns ResultDeclaration with id '<exam_id>-result-<kind-slug>-<stage slug>-<key>' (stage label from scope.refs[0] or 'exam'), the given kind/scope/cycle, and published_at, expected_at, document_url, portal_url, qualified_count and next_step all Fact.not_extracted with explanatory reasons; status VERIFIED by default (callers downgrade).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_next_sta.text: Finds the next stage a notice says successful candidates move on to, such as 'shortlisted for Tier-II' or 'sent for Medical Examination'. It skips a mention of the notice's own stage, and records nothing if no next stage is stated.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_next_sta.tech: Iterates _NEXT_STAGE_CUE matches, skipping ones whose 4+ letter destination words are a subset of the own-stage words (plus 'certificate(s)'). Returns (Fact, stage ref): Fact.not_extracted and '' when none; otherwise Fact.verified(phrase, evidence, 0.85) when a 220-char window is verbatim in the text, else Fact.needs_review; ref from stage_scope(destination) or a slug of it.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_qualific.text: Reads what the notice says happened to the candidates (recommended, selected, waitlisted, shortlisted or qualified), only where it actually says so. A shortlist is never read as a selection.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_qualific.tech: Returns the first QualificationState in _QUALIFICATION_CUES (RECOMMENDED, SELECTED, WAITLISTED, SHORTLISTED, QUALIFIED) whose regex matches the text, else QualificationState.UNSTATED.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_stage_ma.text: Reduces a stage name to its meaningful words, ignoring general words like 'examination', 'written' or 'objective'.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_stage_ma.tech: Returns the set of 4+ letter lower-case words in name minus _STAGE_GENERIC.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::_stage_wo.text: Reduces a stage name to a few key markers (prelim, main, a tier or phase number, interview) so two ways of writing the same stage can be matched.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::_stage_wo.tech: Returns a set containing 'prelim', 'main', the tier/phase/stage ordinal (roman or digits) and/or 'interview' (interview, personality, viva) found in the lower-cased name.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::admission.text: Finds the authority's own rule for how many candidates move on to a stage, for example 'the number of candidates to be admitted to the Main Examination would be fifty times the vacancies', and ties it to that stage and the one before it. The sentence is quoted as printed, never reworded, so it stays the authority's statement.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::admission.tech: Takes stage names (stageName/name of dicts with level None or 'STAGE'). For each _ADMISSION_RULE match, keeps it only if exactly one stage (not the first) has non-empty _stage_marks all within the matched stage phrase; de-duplicates by (previous stage, stage). Returns dicts with isDerived False, source 'OFFICIAL_RULE', fromStage, nextStage, action, guidance/evidenceSpan = the sentence, documentTitle, documentUrl and page (page_of(sentence) or 1).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::classify_.text: Decides what kind of result a label names in the authority's own words, for example a merit list, a shortlist for interview, a final result or a scorecard. It checks the most specific kinds first, so 'final result' is not read as a plain 'result'.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::classify_.tech: Returns the first ResultKind in _KIND_CUES (ordered most specific first: DV_SHORTLIST, INTERVIEW_SHORTLIST, MERIT_LIST, WAITLIST, RECOMMENDATION, SELECTION, SCORECARD, MARKS, FINAL_RESULT, WRITTEN_RESULT, SHORTLIST, QUALIFIED_LIST, STAGE_RESULT, RESULT) whose regex matches the label, or None.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::derive_ne.text: Suggests the candidate's next step after a declared result, using only what the notice says is next or the stage that the exam's own pattern puts after this one. Every suggestion is labelled as GovOS's derived guidance, not an official fact. If no result is declared it says it is awaiting the declaration, and if neither source names a next stage it suggests nothing.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::derive_ne.tech: With empty results_facts returns one 'Awaiting Official Result Declaration' item (isDerived True, source 'DERIVED_FROM_LIFECYCLE').
