Otherwise collects stage names from stages (level None/'STAGE'); for each result uses nextStep/nextStage/next_stage when present ('Next: X'), else _following_stage(stageLabel or stageName) ('Prepare for X'), skipping results with neither. De-duplicates by lower-cased (fromStage, nextStage) and returns the list.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::describe.text: Gives a summary of the result entries found for a build report: how many of each kind, how many are declared or only scheduled, how many can be published, and a row-by-row list.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::describe.tech: Returns a dict: events, byKind counts, declared (is_declaration), scheduled (kind SCHEDULED), publishable, withStage, withDocument (document_url publishable), withCount, withNextStage, and rows (kind, label, stage, cycle, declared, expected, qualification, count, nextStage ref, status).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::may_suppl.text: Decides whether a document's result information belongs to this exam and this year. It uses the same cautious rule as the exam-pattern reader, so last year's result notices never feed this year's record.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::may_suppl.tech: Delegates to pattern.may_supply_pattern(text, target) and returns its (bool, reason).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_noti.text: Reads a result notice written as prose and records the result it declares: what kind of result, which stage, when it was declared, how many candidates cleared, what happened to them, and the next stage where named. The notice's title decides what it is, and one notice gives one declaration. If no part can be matched word for word in the document, it is marked for review rather than shown as the authority's own.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_noti.tech: Normalises headline+text, reads dates (only those before the signature count as declaration candidates). Scope: from the 240 chars around the cue, else the headline's stage, else a single stage named in the document. If the title names a kind, only that kind is tried. For the first matching kind: declaration date via _declaration_date then _dated_notice, builds _new(...) with label, source_label, published_at/precision, qualification, qualified_count (_count) and next_step (_next_stage); evidence from those facts plus the cue span. Sets NEEDS_REVIEW with a note when no evidence is official verbatim. Returns a list of at most one ResultDeclaration (empty for an empty body).

tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_row.text: Reads one row of a results table (a label and what sits beside it) into a result entry. A row with a file and a date is a declared result; a row giving only a month and year with no file (for example 'Result ... September, 2026') is recorded as scheduled, not declared. A bare file name is turned into a link on the authority's own site.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_row.tech: Returns None unless classify_label(label) gives a kind. Cuts the value at _CELL_SEAM, reads dates, marks scheduled when _SCHEDULE_CUE matches and no URL/.pdf is present (kind becomes SCHEDULED). Scope from the label, else default_stage. The first date becomes expected_at (scheduled) or published_at with its precision. document_url: first URL classify_url calls DOWNLOAD, else a bare *.pdf resolved to <authority_domain>/sites/default/files/<name>; verified when the joined row is verbatim. portal_url, if a full URL is given, is needs_review. Evidence from the date or document fact, falling back to the row; NEEDS_REVIEW if none is official verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_rows.text: Reads every row of a results table and keeps only the rows that are actually about results.
tools/exam_builder/results.py::read_rows.tech: Calls read_row for each (label, value) pair with the shared arguments and returns the non-None ResultDeclarations.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: A record of what the merge decided about one result declaration (added, confirmed, replaced or in conflict) and why.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Plain class with action (MergeAction), label, result_id, reason and superseded (id of the declaration it replaces), plus describe().

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: Sets up the decision record with its outcome, label, id, reason and anything it replaces.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Stores the five arguments as attributes; result_id, reason and superseded default to ''.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: Writes the decision as one readable line, for example 'SUPERSEDED: Final result · supersedes X · reason'.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Returns '<action>: <label>' joined with ' · ' to 'supersedes <id>' and the reason when each is set.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: The outcome of merging result declarations: the list of decisions and the resulting full list of declarations.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Holds decisions (list[ResultDecision]) and results (list[ResultDeclaration]), with of() and summary() helpers.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: Returns only the decisions of one kind.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Returns decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.text: Counts how many decisions of each kind were made.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::Res.tech: Returns a dict of MergeAction value -> count.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_ab.text: Adds the proof from a second source to a declaration already held, without duplicating proof it already has, and fills in its label if it had none.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_ab.tech: Appends other's evidence items whose (source_id, span_digest) is not already in keeper.evidence; copies other.label when keeper has none. Mutates keeper.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_ca.text: Answers whether a result declaration cancels an earlier one.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_ca.tech: True when the note contains 'cancel' (case-insensitive) or lifecycle is CANCELLED.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_do.text: Gets the name of a result's document file with the numbers removed, so two different documents of one result (for example a roll-number list and a name list) are kept apart, while a second reading of the same file still matches.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_do.tech: Returns '' when document_url has no value; else the lower-cased URL basename with all digit runs removed.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_po.text: Gets the post a result declaration belongs to, in a form that can be compared.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_po.tech: Returns the lower-cased ref (or label) of the first scope ref of kind POST, or ''.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_re.text: Decides whether a newly read declaration replaces an existing one: it names the old one, is marked as revised or cancelled, or comes from a later-dated document. A second reading of the same document does not count as a revision.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_re.tech: True if incoming.supersedes == existing.id, or incoming.lifecycle is REVISED/CANCELLED, or the max evidence published_at of incoming is later than that of existing (both must have one).

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_st.text: Gets the stage a result declaration belongs to, in a form that can be compared.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_st.tech: Returns the lower-cased ref (or label) of the first scope ref of kind STAGE, or ''.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::_va.text: Gets the date a result declaration carries: its declaration date, or else its expected date.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::ide.text: The set of details that must all match for two result declarations to count as the same one: exam, year, kind of result, stage, post and document.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::mer.text: Combines newly read result declarations with those an exam's record already holds, never overwriting history. A match with the same date is confirmed; a genuine revision or cancellation replaces the old one but keeps it, marked as superseded; something new is added; and two declarations that disagree with neither claiming to revise the other are both kept and flagged as a conflict, with neither shown as settled.
tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::mer.tech: Starts from a copy of existing. Incoming NOT_EXTRACTED events are recorded CONFLICTED and skipped. No same_result twin -> appended, ADDED. Same _value and not cancelling -> _absorb into the twin, CONFIRMED. _revises -> twin lifecycle SUPERSEDED, status NEEDS_REVIEW and note; event.supersedes = twin.id, lifecycle CANCELLED or REVISED; appended, SUPERSEDED. Otherwise the event is NEEDS_REVIEW with a conflict note, appended, CONFLICTED. Mutates the declaration objects; returns a ResultMergeReport with results set.

tools/exam_builder/results_merge.py::sam.text: Answers whether two result declarations are the same declaration.

tools/exam_builder/review.py::FieldRevie.text: One reviewer's decision about one field of an exam record: which field, approve or withhold, who reviewed it, a note, and optionally a corrected value.
tools/exam_builder/review.py::FieldRevie.tech: Dataclass: field, decision (ReviewDecision), reviewer, note (default ''), value (Optional; APPROVE only, None keeps the reader's value).

tools/exam_builder/review.py::ReviewDeci.text: The two choices a human reviewer can make about a field in a build: approve it for publication, or withhold it.
tools/exam_builder/review.py::ReviewDeci.tech: str Enum with APPROVE and WITHHOLD.

tools/exam_builder/review.py::ReviewOutc.text: The result of applying reviews: which fields were changed, which were skipped, and notes explaining each.
tools/exam_builder/review.py::ReviewOutc.tech: Dataclass with applied, skipped and notes lists and a to_dict() method.

tools/exam_builder/review.py::ReviewOutc.text: Turns the review outcome into plain data for a report.

tools/exam_builder/review.py::apply_revi.text: Applies a person's review decisions to an exam record, field by field. Approving publishes the field as read (or with the reviewer's corrected value) under the same document citation and names the reviewer; withholding removes it from publication and records it as a gap the reviewer chose, never as the authority's silence. A review with no reviewer named, or an approval of a field with no cited reading, is skipped.
tools/exam_builder/review.py::apply_revi.tech: For each FieldReview: blank reviewer -> skipped. WITHHOLD: missing field -> skipped; else rec.set(Field.not_extracted(field, citation url or official_domain, reason naming reviewer and prior status)). APPROVE: requires an existing field with a citation and status NEEDS_REVIEW or FOUND, else skipped; sets Field.found(field, corrected or original value, same citation) with an 'approved by reviewer' note (including the reader's note), and rec.note(...). Mutates rec; returns ReviewOutcome.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Cell.text: One cell of a table drawn with lines in a PDF, recorded by which rows and columns it spans (a merged cell can span several) and the lines of text inside it.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Cell.tech: Dataclass: r0, r1, c0, c1 (inclusive atomic grid row/column bounds) and lines (list of text lines, top to bottom), with a text property.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Cell..text: The cell's text as one line.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Count.text: A number read from a vacancy-style table cell, split into fresh vacancies and carried-forward ones, with the cell's text as printed and whether the cell was empty.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Count.tech: Dataclass: fresh, carried_forward, as_printed, blank (True when the cell was empty rather than '-'), with a total property.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Count.text: The full count: fresh plus carried forward.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Ruled.text: A table read from one PDF page by its drawn grid: its page number, the number of rows and columns, its cells, and a lookup from any row and column position to the cell covering it.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Ruled.tech: Dataclass: page (1-indexed), n_rows, n_cols, cells (list[Cell]) and grid (grid[r][c] -> the merged Cell covering that atomic position), with a cell(r, c) accessor.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Ruled.text: Returns the cell covering a given row and column.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Table.text: One whole table as read (possibly across several pages): its column headings, its data rows, its total row, whether its own printed totals add up, which checks were made and what went wrong.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::Table.tech: Dataclass: pages, columns (header path per leaf column), rows (dicts with cells, shared, span_rows, page, row_index, optional continued_on), total_row, verified, checks and problems lists.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_comp.text: Groups the lines on a page into separate tables: lines that touch or cross belong to the same table. Groups with fewer than three lines in either direction are ignored.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_comp.tech: Union-find over all h/v segments: collinear same-orientation segments that overlap within tolerance, and every horizontal-vertical crossing, are joined. Returns a list of (horizontal segments, vertical segments) per group, keeping groups with at least 3 of each.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_cove.text: Checks whether a border line is drawn at a given position across the middle of a stretch, which tells whether two neighbouring cells are separated or merged.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_cove.tech: Returns True if any (pos, a, b) segment has pos within _SNAP+0.5 of `at` and spans the midpoint of [lo, hi] (with 0.5 tolerance).

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_grid.text: Builds one table from a group of lines: it makes a grid from the line positions, joins neighbouring grid squares into one cell wherever no line separates them (merged cells), and puts each character into the cell containing it. A table with an irregular, non-rectangular merged cell is refused.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_grid.tech: Snaps rule positions into ys (top to bottom) and xs; returns None if fewer than 2 rows or columns. Union-find merges horizontally adjacent atoms where _covers finds no vertical rule and vertically adjacent atoms where no horizontal rule; returns None if a merged group is not a full rectangle. Assigns each character by centre to its atom's cell and sets cell.lines via _lines. Returns RuledTable(page_no, ...).

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_is_t.text: Answers whether a column is a total column, by its headings.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_is_t.tech: True when any _key element is exactly TOTAL or GRANDTOTAL.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_is_v.text: Answers whether a cell's text is a non-empty count.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_is_v.tech: True when parse_count(text) is not None and the text is not blank.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_key.text: Normalises a column's headings for comparison, ignoring spaces and capitals, so 'MZ 1', 'M Z1' and 'MZ1' count as the same.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_key.tech: Returns a tuple of each path element with whitespace removed and upper-cased.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_line.text: Turns the characters inside a cell into lines of text, top to bottom, adding spaces where there is a visible gap between letters.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_line.tech: Sorts chars by descending y and groups those within 0.45 x character height into a row; within a row sorts by x and inserts a space when the gap from the previous char's right edge exceeds 0.28 x height. Returns non-empty stripped lines.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_nume.text: Finds the columns that hold counts in every data row, ignoring a serial-number column (1, 2, 3 ...).
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_nume.tech: Returns column indices where every non-shared value parses as a count, at least one is non-blank, and the totals are not exactly 1..n.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_rule.text: Finds the thin horizontal and vertical lines drawn on a PDF page, which are the borders of a table's cells.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_rule.tech: Iterates the page's objects (pypdfium2, max_depth 6), keeps PATH objects, and classifies each by its bounds: height <= _THIN (2.2) and width > 3x height is horizontal (y, x0, x1); width <= _THIN and height > 3x width is vertical (x, y0, y1). Returns (horizontals, verticals).

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_snap.text: Merges line positions that are almost the same (within a tiny distance) into one, so a slightly wobbly drawn line counts once.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_snap.tech: Sorts the values and averages each into the previous kept value when within _SNAP (1.6 PDF points); returns the snapped, sorted list.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_veri.text: Checks a table's own arithmetic before it can be trusted. Every count cell must be readable; each column must add up to the printed TOTAL row; a row's total column must equal the values before it; and a grand total spanning several rows must equal those rows. A table counts as verified only if it has a TOTAL row and every check passes; otherwise the reasons are recorded and it must not be published as read.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::_veri.tech: Adds a problem and returns if there are no numeric columns, or if any numeric cell fails parse_count. With total_row: each numeric column's sum over non-shared rows must equal the printed total. Bare one-row total columns are checked against the run of total columns immediately before them, else all earlier plain numeric columns. Spanning total columns are checked group-wise against the latest preceding bare total. Adds a problem when there is no total row. Sets verified = checked and total_row present and no problems; returns the reading (mutated).

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::heade.text: Works out where a table's headings end and its data begins, and for each column lists the stack of headings printed above it (for example 'UR' under 'Zone 1' under 'Post'). A caption spanning the whole table is not treated as a column heading.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::heade.tech: The body starts at the first row whose own (r0==row) non-empty cells are at least half counts and at least two counts; it then moves up over single-row rows holding only counts (a continuation from the previous page). For each column, collects the distinct header cells above body_start, skipping full-width captions, normalising whitespace and joining letters printed one per line ('U R' -> 'UR'). Returns (body_start, paths).

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::parse.text: Reads a table cell as a count: a dash means zero, '11' printed as '1' over '1' means 11, and '2 + 2 cf' means 2 fresh plus 2 carried forward. Anything else is not a count and returns nothing.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::parse.tech: Empty -> Count(0,0,'',blank=True); a lone dash -> Count(0,0,raw). Otherwise removes whitespace and matches ^(\d+)?(\+?(\d+)cf)?\+?$; returns Count(fresh, cf, raw) when at least one number is present, else None.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::read_.text: Reads every table drawn with lines in a PDF, page by page, into cells holding their own text. This avoids the errors of reading a table as a flat run of text, where one blank cell shifts every later number into the wrong column.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::read_.tech: Opens the PDF with pypdfium2; for each page with at least 3 horizontal and 3 vertical rules, collects non-blank characters with their centre, height and x-extent (U+FFFE and soft hyphen become '-'), then for each rule component calls _grid_table. Returns the list of RuledTable objects.

tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::read_.text: Joins tables on consecutive pages that share the same column headings into one logical table, carrying a row that breaks across a page onto the row it continues. It finds the TOTAL row and then checks whether the table's own numbers add up.
tools/exam_builder/ruled_table.py::read_.tech: Returns None for no tables. Uses header_paths of the first table; stops at the first page whose header keys differ. Rows owned by their own r0 are collected; a row with empty first two cells (not a TOTAL label) on a new page is appended cell-wise to the previous row (continued_on). The row labelled TOTAL/GRANDTOTAL in its first three non-value cells becomes total_row. Returns _verify(TableReading(...)).

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: The names of the fields that hold citations for individual facts (such as the vacancy total) and for figures GovOS computed.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Tuple ('factEvidence', 'derivedEvidence'): maps of fact name -> provenance.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: The three kinds of evidence GovOS shows: direct (the value is in the quoted words), reconciled (a later official statement replaced an earlier one) and derived (GovOS calculated it from cited figures).
The names of the fields under which an exam's data objects carry their source citation.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Tuple ('provenance', 'officialProvenance') walked by stamp_exam, evidence_problems and strip_evidence_metadata.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Removes duplicate citations from a list, keeping the first of each.
Collapses extra spaces in a piece of text.

For every exam-pattern figure GovOS computed rather than read (for example marks per question, or a total of questions), attaches evidence saying how it was computed and which printed figures it came from. A computed figure whose inputs cannot be named gets no evidence.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Visits each pattern node depth-first. For each key in node['derived'] present on the node, picks the method and input location from _DERIVATIONS: 'self' (the node's own provenance), 'children' (children's provenances where that key is printed, not derived), 'ancestor' (nearest ancestor with a printed negativeMarking). Skips keys without inputs; otherwise stores node['derivedEvidence'][key] = summary of the first input with id '<id>-derived-<key>', evidenceType DERIVED and derivation {method, inputs (de-duplicated)}. Mutates the tree.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Gives a citation a fixed identity code made from what it cites: the link, the page, the clause and the quoted words. The same words on the same page always get the same code; different words get a different one.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: SHA-1 of the JSON list [officialUrl, pageNumber, whitespace-normalised clauseNumber, whitespace-normalised excerptText]; returns 'ev-' + first 16 hex chars.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Lists every way an exam record's citations break GovOS's evidence rules: a missing or wrong identity code, no evidence kind, 'officially verified' without a source and a place in it, a computed figure that names no inputs, or a replacement that names nothing it replaced. An empty list means the record passes.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Walks the exam like stamp_exam and checks each provenance: evidenceId present and equal to evidence_id(p); evidenceType valid; OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED requires has_evidence; DERIVED requires derivation.inputs; RECONCILED requires supersedes or supersededBy. Returns problem strings prefixed with a path like 'exam.dates[0].provenance'.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Gives the citation for a single fact (such as the total number of vacancies) only when the fact is actually shown and its source is cited; otherwise none.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Returns dict(prov) when value_present is truthy and is_provenance(prov), else None.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Answers whether a citation gives a source a candidate can open and a place in it: a web link plus either a page number or the quoted words.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: True when officialUrl starts with 'http' and either the excerpt text is non-blank or pageNumber is truthy.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Answers whether an object is a source citation (it has a document title and an official link field).
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: True for a dict containing both 'documentTitle' and 'officialUrl' keys.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Links the citation of a replaced entry (for example an old closing date) to the entry that replaced it, both ways, so the evidence panel can show both. Citations are copied first because one citation may be shared by several entries.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: For each (old_id -> new_id) in superseded_by where both rows exist with provenances: copies both provenances, sets old.supersededBy = summary(new) and new.supersedes += [summary(old)], marks both evidenceType RECONCILED, assigns the copies back and sets old['supersededBy'] = new_id. Mutates rows.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Completes a citation, and every citation linked to it: adds the authority's name if missing, labels its kind of evidence, downgrades any 'officially verified' claim that has no link and no page or quote, and gives it its identity code.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Recursively stamps provenances in supersedes, supersededBy and derivation.inputs. Sets authorityName if absent; sets evidenceType when not a valid type (DERIVED if derivation, RECONCILED if supersedes/supersededBy, else DIRECT); changes OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED to UNDER_VERIFICATION when not has_evidence; sets evidenceId = evidence_id(p). Mutates and returns p.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Goes through a whole exam record and completes every citation in it, wherever it sits.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Walks dicts and lists recursively; stamps provenances under PROVENANCE_KEYS and every provenance value inside EVIDENCE_MAPS with the exam's authorityName, and recurses into all other keys. Mutates in place; returns None.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: Returns a copy of an exam record with everything this evidence module added taken out, so a test can prove that adding evidence changed no fact.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Recursively copies dicts/lists, dropping factEvidence and derivedEvidence maps, removing evidenceId, evidenceType, authorityName, supersedes, supersededBy and derivation from provenance dicts, and dropping string supersededBy keys on rows.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.text: A copy of a citation without its links to other citations, i.e. what this one record says on its own.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_evidence.py::.tech: Returns a dict of the provenance minus the 'supersedes', 'supersededBy' and 'derivation' keys.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Cleans a category name by removing a leading 'Category:'.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Strips a case-insensitive leading 'category :' prefix and surrounding whitespace.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Reads a date written as year-month-day at the start of a text, or nothing if it is not a valid date.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Matches ^YYYY-MM-DD and returns a datetime.date, or None on no match or an invalid date.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Lists each fee-exempt category once. A short name that is just the initials of another listed name (for example 'SC' beside 'Scheduled Castes') is dropped as a duplicate.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Takes exemptions with a category, cleans labels, computes initials of multi-word names, and returns [{name (first letter capitalised), exemption}] skipping case-insensitive repeats and 2-5 letter names equal to another name's initials.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Writes where a citation points, such as 'Notice title, page 14 — clause 5'.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Returns documentTitle (default 'the notice') plus ', page N' and ' — clause' when present.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Gives the quoted words of a citation, whole and uncut.
Gives the same calendar day a number of years earlier, using 28 February when the day is 29 February in a non-leap year.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Returns d.replace(year=d.year - years), falling back to day=28 on ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.text: Builds a practice application form for a machine-read exam from the facts its record already holds, with nothing made up. It can include a post and date-of-birth card (warning when a candidate is too young for every post, or older than every post's limit unless a printed relaxation applies), a fee-exemption card (warning when an exemption is claimed with no exempt category), and a submission-date card (warning when the form is dated outside the application window, which runs from the earliest opening to the close that applies now). Each warning quotes the notice and names its page; if no check can be built, there is no form.
tools/exam_builder/runtime_simulator.py:.tech: Reads posts, crucialEligibilityDate and factEvidence.crucialEligibilityDate: with a cited date and integer age bands, adds post/dob fields and DATE_OUTSIDE traps (CRITICAL too-young for the lowest minimum age; WARNING over-age for the highest maximum, listing VERIFIED ageRelaxations). With distinct fee exemptions and a provenance, adds a Fee module and a VALUE_IN_ALL CRITICAL trap. With APPLICATION_OPEN dates and exactly one distinct non-superseded APPLICATION_CLOSE day that is cited and not before the earliest open, adds a Submission module and a DATE_OUTSIDE window trap (quoting superseded wording when present). Returns None if no trap or anchor provenance; otherwise an ApplicationSimulatorSpec-shaped dict (examId, portalName, portalUrl, source document, modelledOnNote, modules, traps, cleanSubmissionNote, provenance = first anchor).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.text: One admit-card release (or city intimation), tied to the stage or paper it admits to: the authority's own name for it, the row it was read from, its year, the release date (or release rule such as '7 days before the exam'), how precisely the date was printed, how long it stays available, the exam date kept separate from the release date, the login portal, a direct download link only if published, login requirements, instructions, regional portals, documents to bring, and what it replaces.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.tech: Dataclass: id, kind (default ADMIT_CARD), scope, official_label, source_label, cycle, released_at, released_precision, available_until, release_rule, exam_date, portal_url, download_url, credentials_required, instructions, alternate_portals, documents_required, supersedes, status, evidence, note; property is_publishable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.text: Answers whether this admit-card notice may be shown: it must be verified, tied to a stage or a year, and backed by words found in an official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.tech: Property: status VERIFIED and (scope.refs or cycle) and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.text: The kinds of notice issued before an exam: an admit card, a city intimation (advance notice of the exam city), an exam intimation, or other. Each is something that may or may not exist.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AdmitCardN.tech: str Enum: ADMIT_CARD, CITY_INTIMATION, EXAM_INTIMATION, OTHER.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRelaxat.text: An extension of the age limit for some group of candidates, as the authority states it: either 'N extra years' or 'the upper limit is N', plus any minimum and any conditions, all kept as printed.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRelaxat.tech: Dataclass: category_label (authority's words), scope, years, absolute_maximum, absolute_minimum (Fact[float]) and conditions (Fact[str]).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRule.text: One age rule: who it applies to, the minimum and maximum ages, the date age is counted on, or a date-of-birth window if that is how the notice puts it, and any category relaxations. It can represent a whole-exam rule, a post-specific rule, different cut-off dates, and rules from different documents.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRule.tech: Dataclass: id, scope, minimum_age, maximum_age (Fact[float]), cutoff_date, born_not_earlier_than, born_not_later_than (Fact[str]), relaxations (list[AgeRelaxation]), note; with is_global and relaxations_for().

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRule.is.text: Answers whether the age rule applies to the whole exam.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRule.re.text: Returns the age relaxations this rule gives for a named category.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AgeRule.re.tech: Returns relaxations whose category_label matches category_label case- and whitespace-insensitively.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerEntr.text: What the authority says the answer is for one question of one paper: the accepted option labels (possibly several), a numerical value if any, its status, the earlier answer it replaced, its proof and a note.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerEntr.tech: Dataclass: question_number, paper (PaperIdentity, default with empty exam_id), accepted (list of labels), value, status (default UNKNOWN), supersedes (Optional[AnswerEntry]), evidence, note; property is_publishable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerEntr.text: Answers whether this answer may be shown: it must be published, revised or a multiple-accepted decision, must actually give an answer, and must be backed by words found in an official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerEntr.tech: Property: status in (PUBLISHED, MULTIPLE_ACCEPTED, REVISED) and (accepted or value) and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKey.text: An answer key tied to the exact paper it answers: its kind, link, publication date, the earlier key it replaces, its state and proof, the answers if the authority publishes them (often it serves them only through each candidate's login), how candidates reach it, and the window for viewing or challenging it.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKey.tech: Dataclass: paper (PaperIdentity), kind (default UNSPECIFIED), url, published_at (Fact[str]), revises (key id), id, status, evidence, note, entries (list[AnswerEntry]), access, window_opens, window_closes, source_status (default None); properties is_publishable and is_attached_to_a_paper.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKey..text: Answers whether the key is tied to a specific paper rather than just an exam and year.
Answers whether the key may be shown: it must name an exact paper and be backed by words found in an official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKey..tech: Property: paper.is_paper_level and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKeyK.text: The kinds of answer key: provisional, final, revised, or not stated.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerKeyK.tech: str Enum: PROVISIONAL, FINAL, REVISED, UNSPECIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerStat.text: What the authority has said about a question's answer: published, not published, dropped, cancelled, several answers accepted, revised, or unknown. Silence is recorded as unknown, never as a cancellation.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AnswerStat.tech: str Enum: PUBLISHED, NOT_PUBLISHED, DROPPED, CANCELLED, MULTIPLE_ACCEPTED, REVISED, UNKNOWN.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.text: One thing an application form asks for, as the source describes it: its label, the type of input, whether it is required, format rules, help text and proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.tech: Dataclass: id, label, input_kind, required (Optional[bool]), constraints (list), help_text, evidence.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.text: How one applies for one exam: the exam, the authority, the application portal, the steps, and the fees.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, authority, portal (Fact[str]), stages (list[ApplicationStage]), fees (list[FeeRule]), note; method stage(id).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.text: Finds an application step by its id.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.tech: Returns the first stage with the given id, or None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.text: One step of applying, exactly as the official source describes it, with its fields, required documents, printed instructions, steps that must come first, whether it is done once only, its proof and state. Nothing assumes a particular sequence such as registration then payment.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Applicatio.tech: Dataclass: id, title, order, description, fields (list[ApplicationField]), documents (list[RequiredDocument]), instructions (list[Fact]), depends_on (stage ids), is_one_time, evidence, status (default NOT_EXTRACTED), note.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::AttemptRul.text: A limit on how many times a candidate may sit the exam, what it applies to, and any conditions.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::CategoryMi.text: A minimum mark or percentage the authority prints for one group of candidates, under the authority's own column heading.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::CutoffMark.text: A cut-off mark, with what it applies to and its basis as printed (such as 'out of 200').

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::DatePrecis.text: How exactly the authority stated a date: to the day, the month, the year, or not at all ('to be notified'). A date is never recorded as more exact than printed.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::DatePrecis.tech: str Enum: DAY, MONTH, YEAR, UNSPECIFIED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::DurationVa.text: A different exam duration printed for a particular group, for example extra time for candidates using a scribe, kept alongside the normal time.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::DurationVa.tech: Dataclass: minutes (Optional[int]), as_printed, applies_to ('' = every candidate).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.text: Every rule about who may apply, each with its own scope and source: age rules, qualifications, nationality, attempt limits, other requirements and other rules.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.tech: Dataclass: age_rules, qualifications, nationality (list[Fact]), attempts (list[AttemptRule]), requirements, other_rules; methods relaxations_for, age_rules_for (most general first), property global_age_rule.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.text: Returns the age rules that apply to a given scope, for example all rules covering a particular post, with the most general rule first and the most specific last.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.tech: Returns age_rules whose scope.covers(scope), sorted stably by len(r.scope.refs) (global rules first).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.text: Returns the age rule that applies to the whole exam, if there is one.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.tech: Property: the first age rule with is_global, or None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.text: Lists every age relaxation the authority published for a category, optionally for one post. If the authority published none, it returns none, rather than applying a standard number.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Eligibilit.tech: Iterates age_rules (skipping rules whose POST scope excludes post_id when given) and their relaxations matching category_label case-insensitively (skipping relaxations whose POST scope excludes post_id). Returns the list of AgeRelaxation.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamIdenti.text: Who runs the exam and what it is called: the exam id, its official name, the authority's name and web address (each recorded with how well it is known), the year, and free-text tags used only for browsing.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamIdenti.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, official_name, authority_name, authority_domain (Fact[str]), cycle, tags (list; never used for extraction).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.text: The whole exam structure as a list of stages, plus any note the authority made about it, the exam it belongs to and the year. A pattern without an exam id cannot be published, so a scheme page shared by several exams cannot feed whichever exam happens to be selected.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.tech: Dataclass: stages (list[PatternNode]), note (Fact[str]), exam_id, cycle; methods walk, of_level, max_depth, find.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.text: Finds a part of the pattern by its id.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.tech: Returns the first node from walk() with the given id, or None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.text: The greatest number of levels in any stage's structure.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.tech: Returns max stage.depth(), or 0 with no stages.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.text: Returns every part of the pattern of a given kind.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.tech: Returns nodes from walk() with the given level.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ExamPatter.text: Goes through every part of every stage.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.text: One piece of exam information: its value, its state (verified, needs review, not published, not extracted), the proof behind it, a confidence figure, a note explaining any doubt, and, if GovOS calculated it, which figures it was calculated from. A value without official word-for-word proof can never be shown as the authority's.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.tech: Generic dataclass Fact[T]: value, status (default NOT_EXTRACTED), evidence list, confidence, note, derived_from (list of input field names; empty for printed values). Properties is_derived, has_value, is_publishable, primary_source; constructors verified, needs_review, not_published, derived, not_extracted.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.deriv.text: Creates a value GovOS calculated from the authority's own figures (for example marks per question from total marks and questions), recording which figures it came from. It is never a way to fill in something the authority did not publish.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.deriv.tech: Classmethod: Fact(value, status VERIFIED, evidence list, confidence 1.0, note, derived_from=list(basis)).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.has_v.text: Answers whether the fact actually holds a value (not empty).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.is_de.text: Answers whether the value was calculated by GovOS rather than printed by the authority.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.is_pu.text: Answers whether the value may be shown as the authority's: it must be verified, hold a value, and have proof quoted word for word from an official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.is_pu.tech: Property: status is VERIFIED and has_value and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.needs.text: Creates a fact that was read but needs a person to check it, with a note saying why.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.needs.tech: Classmethod: Fact(value, status NEEDS_REVIEW, evidence list (possibly empty), confidence default 0.0, note).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.not_e.text: Creates a fact saying GovOS did not manage to read this, which is GovOS's own gap and never a claim that the authority is silent.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.not_e.tech: Classmethod: Fact(value None, status NOT_EXTRACTED, note) with a default note explaining it is a gap in GovOS.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.not_p.text: Creates a fact saying the authority does not publish this thing. Meant only for when the authority's own listing shows it does not exist; any proof attached is proof of that absence.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.not_p.tech: Classmethod: Fact(value None, status NOT_PUBLISHED, evidence list, note).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.prima.text: Returns the first piece of proof for the fact, if any.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.verif.text: Creates a fact marked as verified, with its value and proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Fact.verif.tech: Classmethod: Fact(value, status VERIFIED, evidence as a list, confidence default 1.0).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::FeeRule.text: A fee amount and who it applies to, plus whether some group is exempt, the accepted payment methods, which fee it is (application, exam or total), and the group named in the notice's own words where no standard category fits.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::FeeRule.tech: Dataclass: scope, amount (Fact[float]), currency (default 'INR'), is_exempt (Fact[bool]), accepted_modes (Fact[list]), note, fee_type, stated_group.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::INFRASTRUC.text: A marker recording the rule that a technical failure (a page that would not load, a search outage, an unreadable scan) is never written into an exam's information as if it were a fact about the authority.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::INFRASTRUC.tech: Constant True; documentation-only, kept so the rule is greppable. Such failures are tracked on the build (gate.BuildState) or SourceOutcome instead of a field Status.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone.text: A dated event in an exam's timeline (such as the application window or an exam date), in the authority's own words, with what it applies to, its year, start and end, how precisely it was stated, whether it was postponed or cancelled, whether it is tentative, any alternative dates the authority offered, and links to the event it replaced or that replaced it.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone.tech: Dataclass: id, label, kind (free text), scope, cycle, starts_at, ends_at (Fact[str]), precision (default DAY), state (default ANNOUNCED), is_tentative, alternatives (list[Fact]), superseded_by, supersedes, revision_source_id, status, note; properties is_superseded, is_range, effective_date, is_actionable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone..text: The date this event currently points to: the end date for a window (the deadline), otherwise its single date. A replaced or cancelled event gives none.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone..tech: Property: None if superseded or state CANCELLED; else ends_at.value if set, else starts_at.value if set, else None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone..text: Answers whether this event may trigger a reminder to a candidate: only a verified, still-current, day-exact date that is announced or rescheduled.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone..tech: Property: status VERIFIED and effective_date not None and state in (ANNOUNCED, RESCHEDULED) and precision DAY.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Milestone..text: Answers whether the event has both a start and an end date.
Answers whether a later document replaced this event.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::MilestoneS.text: What has happened to a scheduled event: announced, postponed, rescheduled, cancelled, or awaited (known to be coming but not yet dated).
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::MilestoneS.tech: str Enum: ANNOUNCED, POSTPONED, RESCHEDULED, CANCELLED, AWAITED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::NegativeMa.text: The negative-marking rule for a part of the exam: the sentence as printed, plus where readable the marks lost per wrong answer, marks gained per right one, whether unanswered questions are penalised, and a share of the question's marks if the rule is stated that way.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::NegativeMa.tech: Dataclass: as_printed, deducted_per_wrong, awarded_per_correct (Optional[float]), applies_to_unattempted (bool), fraction_of_marks (Optional[float]); property is_none.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::NegativeMa.text: Answers whether the authority actually states there is no penalty for wrong answers, which is different from GovOS not knowing.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::NegativeMa.tech: Property: deducted_per_wrong == 0 and as_printed is non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialPa.text: A question paper the authority itself published: its identity, link, title, publication date, its contents (left as 'not extracted' when it is a scan GovOS cannot read), state, proof and a note.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialPa.tech: Dataclass: identity (PaperIdentity), url, published_at (Fact[str]), title, contents (Fact[list]), status (default NOT_EXTRACTED), evidence, note.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialQu.text: One question of one paper, tied to the exact paper it was printed in: its number, wording, type, options, marks and negative marks where printed, language, any shared reading passage, section, subject, answer, and its source state and proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialQu.tech: Dataclass: paper (PaperIdentity), number, text, format (default OTHER), options, marks, negative_marks (Fact[float]), language, passage_id, passage_text, section, subject, answer (Optional[AnswerEntry]), source_status (default NOT_EXTRACTED), status, evidence, note; identity_key() and is_publishable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialQu.text: The key that identifies a question: its exact paper plus its number, never its wording.
Answers whether the question may be shown: it needs an exact paper, a number, wording, an officially verified source and word-for-word official proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::OfficialQu.tech: Property: paper.is_paper_level and number and non-blank text and source_status is OFFICIAL_VERIFIED and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.text: Identifies exactly which question paper something refers to: exam, year, stage, paper, subject, language, booklet set and shift. Only the parts the authority printed are filled. It cannot be changed once made, because it decides whether an answer key may be attached to a paper.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.tech: Frozen dataclass: exam_id, cycle, stage, paper, subject, language, set_code, session (all str, optional beyond exam_id); methods key(), is_paper_level, describe(), matches().

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.text: Writes the paper's identity in readable form, such as '2026 · Main · Paper-I · English'.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.tech: Joins non-empty cycle, stage, paper, subject, language, set_code, session with ' · '; falls back to exam_id.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.text: Answers whether this identifies a specific paper rather than just an exam and year. It needs an exam plus at least a stage, paper or subject.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.tech: Property: bool(exam_id and (stage or paper or subject)).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.text: Turns the paper's identity into one comparable text key.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.tech: Returns the eight parts, each stripped, lower-cased and whitespace-collapsed, joined with '|'.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.text: Decides whether two identities are the same paper. One may leave out a detail the other has, but two different stated values for the same detail (for example Shift 1 and Shift 2) mean different papers, and different exams never match.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PaperIdent.tech: False if exam_id differs; otherwise False if any of the seven other parts are both non-empty and differ case-insensitively after stripping; else True.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternLev.text: What a part of the exam's structure is: a stage, paper, subject, section, part, other, or a heading above the structure. It deliberately has no 'Tier 1' or 'Prelims', since those are one authority's names; the authority's own word is kept separately.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternLev.tech: str Enum: STAGE, PAPER, SUBJECT, SECTION, PART, OTHER, HEADING.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.text: One part of the exam's structure (a stage, paper, section and so on) at whatever depth the authority uses, with its own sub-parts. Each measurable detail (number of questions, marks, duration, negative marking, qualifying rule, languages, mode, question type, marks per question, separate section timing) is kept as a fact, so 'not printed' is never lost.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.tech: Dataclass: id, level (PatternLevel), level_label, name, order, children, Fact fields questions, marks, duration_minutes, negative_marking, qualifying, languages, mode, remarks, question_type, marks_per_question, sectional_timing; code, duration_variants, evidence, status. Methods walk, of_level, depth, path_labels.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.text: Counts how many levels deep the structure goes from this part.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.tech: Returns 1 + the maximum child depth (0 when there are no children).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.text: Returns every part at or below this one that is of a given kind, for example all papers.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.tech: Returns [n for n in walk() if n.level is level].

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.text: Gives the name of this part's level, using the authority's own word if known.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.tech: Returns [level_label or level.value] (a single-element list for this node only).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.text: Goes through this part and all the parts beneath it, one by one.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::PatternNod.tech: Generator: yields self then recursively each child's walk() (pre-order).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Post.text: One post or service an exam recruits to, with everything stated about it kept as facts: department, group or class, pay, vacancies, qualifications, other requirements, proof, its own post code where printed, and its printed age band. Only an id and a name are required.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Post.tech: Dataclass: id, name, department, classification, pay (Fact[str]), vacancies (list[VacancyCount]), qualification (list[QualificationRule]), other_requirements (list[Fact]), evidence, status, note, code, age_band (Fact[str]).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Qualificat.text: An educational or professional requirement, what it applies to, the date by which it must be held, and whether it is essential.
What a result says happened to the candidates it names: qualified, not qualified, shortlisted, selected, recommended, waitlisted, or not stated. Recorded only where the source says it.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Qualificat.tech: str Enum: QUALIFIED, NOT_QUALIFIED, SHORTLISTED, SELECTED, RECOMMENDED, WAITLISTED, UNSTATED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Qualifying.text: Whether a part of the exam counts towards the final ranking or only needs to be passed, and what passing takes, with separate minimums per category where printed.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Qualifying.tech: Dataclass: as_printed, is_qualifying_only, minimum_marks, minimum_percent, counts_towards_merit (all Optional) and by_category (list[CategoryMinimum]).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::QuestionFo.text: The kinds of question a paper can contain: multiple choice, multiple select, numerical, descriptive, assertion-reason, matching, passage-based or other. Kept open so a descriptive paper is never given fake answer options.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::QuestionFo.tech: str Enum: MULTIPLE_CHOICE, MULTIPLE_SELECT, NUMERICAL, DESCRIPTIVE, ASSERTION_REASON, MATCHING, PASSAGE_BASED, OTHER.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::QuestionOp.text: One answer choice of a question, with the label printed beside it, such as '(b)' or '2'. The label is kept so an answer key is matched by label, never by position.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::RequiredDo.text: A document or upload an application step requires (such as a photo or signature), with whatever specifications were printed (size, format, ink colour) and proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::RequiredDo.tech: Dataclass: id, name, specifications (list as printed), required (Optional[bool]), evidence.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Requiremen.text: Any other condition on who may apply, beyond age and qualification (experience, domicile, medical or physical standards, a licence, a language), with the authority's own wording, what it applies to and whether it is essential.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Requiremen.tech: Dataclass: kind (open string), statement (Fact[str]), scope, is_essential (Optional[bool]), note.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultDecl.text: One result announcement by the authority, tied to a stage or paper: its own wording, the row it came from, its kind and year, the declaration date or (for a scheduled result) the expected date kept separate, how precise those dates are, the document link, the login portal, the number who cleared, what happened to them, the next step, cut-offs, its revision history, and proof.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultDecl.tech: Dataclass: id, label, source_label, kind (default OTHER), scope, cycle, published_at/published_precision, expected_at/expected_precision, document_url, portal_url, qualified_count, qualification (default UNSTATED), next_step, next_stage_ref, cutoffs, lifecycle (default ORIGINAL), supersedes, status, evidence, note; properties is_declaration and is_publishable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultDecl.text: Answers whether this is an actual declared result rather than a scheduled one.
Answers whether this result may be shown: it must be verified, tied to a stage or a year, and backed by words found in an official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultDecl.tech: Property: status VERIFIED and (scope.refs or cycle) and any evidence is_official_verbatim.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultKind.text: The kinds of result an authority publishes: result, written result, stage result, final result, shortlist, qualified list, merit list, scorecard, marks, selection, waitlist, document-verification or interview shortlist, recommendation, other, and 'scheduled', which is a future date for a result not yet declared and is never shown as declared.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultKind.tech: str Enum of 16 values including SCHEDULED and OTHER; property is_declaration.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultKind.text: Answers whether this kind is an actual declared result, rather than a scheduled date or 'other'.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultLife.text: Where a result declaration stands in its revision history: original, revised, cancelled, or superseded by a later one.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ResultLife.tech: str Enum: ORIGINAL, REVISED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Revision.text: A correction the authority published (a corrigendum), recording exactly which detail it changed, the value before and after, when it was published and took effect, the document that made it and the one it applies to. If two documents disagree and nothing settles it, it is marked for review and blocked rather than guessed.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Revision.tech: Dataclass: id, field_path (dotted path into the record), scope, previous_value, revised_value, published_at, effective_from (Fact[str]), evidence, supersedes_source_id, summary, status (NEEDS_REVIEW for unsettled disagreements), note.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.text: What a rule applies to, as a set of conditions that must all hold. Empty means the whole exam; one post means just that post; a post plus a category means that post for that category.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.tech: Dataclass with refs: list[ScopeRef] (a conjunction), plus is_global, of(kind), covers(other) and __str__.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.__st.text: Writes the scope as text, or 'EXAM (global)' for the whole exam.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.__st.tech: Joins str(ref) with ' & ', or returns 'EXAM (global)' when empty.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.cove.text: Answers whether this rule's scope includes another, more specific scope; a whole-exam rule covers everything.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.cove.tech: Returns True when every ref of self is in other.refs.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.is_g.text: Answers whether the rule applies to the whole exam (no conditions).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.of.text: Returns only the conditions of one kind, for example only the posts.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Scope.of.tech: Returns refs whose kind is the given ScopeKind.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ScopeKind.text: The things a rule can be limited to: the whole exam, a post, a category of candidate, a stage, a paper, a subject, a section, a cycle, or some other grouping the authority uses.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ScopeKind.tech: str Enum: EXAM, POST, CATEGORY, STAGE, PAPER, SUBJECT, SECTION, CYCLE, OTHER.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ScopeRef.text: One 'this applies to ...' condition, such as a particular post or category, keeping the authority's own wording and, where possible, a link to an item in the record.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ScopeRef.tech: Frozen dataclass: kind (ScopeKind), ref (id inside the record), label (the authority's wording).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::ScopeRef._.text: Writes the condition as text, like 'POST:Inspector'.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceDocu.text: Describes one source document once (its id, link, kind, title, authority, publication and access dates, a fingerprint of its content, and the exam it belongs to), so every fact can point to it. The fingerprint lets a later build notice that the document changed.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceDocu.tech: Dataclass: id, url, kind (SourceKind, default OTHER_OFFICIAL), title, authority, published_at, accessed_at, content_hash, exam_id (never assumed), notes list.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.text: Records exactly where a value came from, precisely enough for a person to check it by hand: the document, its link, title, authority, page and section, the exact words quoted, whether those words were found in the document, and what kind of source it is (official or secondary).
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.tech: Dataclass, the contract's single evidence shape: source_id, url, document_title, authority, document_type, published_at, accessed_at, page, section, span (verbatim words), content_hash, span_status (EvidenceStatus, default UNCHECKED), reading, source_class ('' = the pipeline's own official reading). Properties span_digest, is_verbatim, is_official, is_official_verbatim; locator(); classmethod from_evidence.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.text: Converts proof produced by the text-reading layer into this standard form, keeping its record of whether the quoted words were verified and filling details from the source document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.tech: Classmethod: builds SourceEvidence from an Evidence (source_url, document_title, page, span, status, reading), filling source_id, url, title, authority, document_type, published_at, accessed_at and content_hash from the optional SourceDocument; span_status = ev.status.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.text: Answers whether this proof comes from an official source rather than a secondary one.
Answers whether the quoted words were found in an official document. Only this kind of proof lets a value be shown as the authority's own; a trusted secondary site's words can only back it up.
Answers whether the quoted words were actually found in the document.
Writes a short readable 'where' for this proof, such as 'Notice title · p.14 · Section 5', for reports or tooltips.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.tech: Joins document_title (or url, or source_id), 'p.<page>' when set and section when set with ' · '.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.text: A short fingerprint of the quoted words, used to tell whether two pieces of proof quote the same text.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceEvid.tech: Property: first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of normalise_ws(span).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceKind.text: The kinds of document an authority publishes, by the role they play: notification, application page, corrigendum, syllabus, question paper, answer key, admit card notice, result, exam page, cut-off, or other official document.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceKind.tech: str Enum: NOTIFICATION, APPLICATION_PAGE, CORRIGENDUM, SYLLABUS, QUESTION_PAPER, ANSWER_KEY, ADMIT_CARD_NOTICE, RESULT, EXAM_PAGE, CUTOFF, OTHER_OFFICIAL.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceOutc.text: What happened when GovOS tried to read a source: read, could not fetch, network down, unreadable, build paused, or identity refused. These describe GovOS's run, never what the authority published, so they can never become 'not published'.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceOutc.tech: str Enum: READ, SOURCE_FETCH_FAILURE, NETWORK_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_UNREADABLE, BUILD_PAUSED, IDENTITY_REFUSED. Recorded on reports, never on a field Status.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceStat.text: How good the source behind an item is, in a candidate's terms: officially verified, secondary and unverified, needs review, not published, or not extracted. Only the first may be shown as official.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SourceStat.tech: str Enum: OFFICIAL_VERIFIED, SECONDARY_UNVERIFIED, NEEDS_REVIEW, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_EXTRACTED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.text: The four states any piece of exam information can be in: verified, needs review, not published by the authority, or not extracted (GovOS failed to read it). The last two are kept strictly apart, because 'the authority published nothing' and 'GovOS could not find it' are very different claims.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.tech: str Enum: VERIFIED, NEEDS_REVIEW, NOT_PUBLISHED, NOT_EXTRACTED, with properties is_about_the_authority and carries_value.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.car.text: Answers whether this state comes with an actual value (verified or needs review).
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.car.tech: Property: True for VERIFIED and NEEDS_REVIEW.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.is_.text: Answers whether this state says something about what the authority published (true for verified, needs review and not published; false for GovOS's own reading gap).
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Status.is_.tech: Property: True for VERIFIED, NEEDS_REVIEW and NOT_PUBLISHED; False for NOT_EXTRACTED.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.text: The full syllabus as the authority structured it, as one or more top-level entries, plus a note about its source.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.tech: Dataclass: roots (list[SyllabusNode]), source_note (Fact[str]); methods walk, max_depth, level_labels, find.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.f.text: Finds a syllabus entry by its id.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.f.tech: Returns the first node from walk() with the given id, or None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.l.text: Lists every word the authority used for its syllabus levels (such as 'Paper', 'Unit', 'Topic'), in the order they first appear.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.l.tech: Returns de-duplicated non-empty level_label values from walk(), in first-seen order.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.m.text: The greatest number of levels in the syllabus.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.m.tech: Returns max root depth, or 0 with no roots.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::Syllabus.w.text: Goes through every entry of the syllabus.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.text: One syllabus entry (a paper, section, unit, topic and so on) at whatever level the authority placed it, with its sub-entries, the authority's own word for the level, what part of the exam it belongs to, its proof, and any figures GovOS calculated (kept separately from the authority's).
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.tech: Dataclass: id, title, level_label, scope, order, children, evidence (for this node's existence and wording), status, derived (dict of GovOS-derived values), note; methods walk, depth, leaves.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.text: Counts how many levels deep the syllabus goes under this entry.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.tech: Returns 1 + max child depth (0 with no children).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.text: Returns the lowest-level entries under this one, those with nothing beneath them.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.tech: Returns nodes from walk() without children.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.text: Goes through this entry and every entry beneath it.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::SyllabusNo.tech: Pre-order generator: yields self then each child's walk().

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.text: The complete record of one exam, and only one: its identity, source documents, application process, timeline, posts, eligibility, pattern, syllabus, question papers, answer keys, admit cards, results, corrections, the build's technical state (kept off every fact) and a log.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.tech: Dataclass: identity, sources, application, milestones, posts, eligibility, pattern, syllabus, papers, answer_keys, admit_cards, results, revisions, build_state (gate.BuildState string), log; exam_id property, source(), keys_for(), all_facts(), unsourced_facts().

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.text: Goes through every piece of information in the exam record, with the path to where it sits. Used by audits and the publication gate.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.tech: Generator delegating to _walk_facts(self, ''), yielding (dotted path, Fact).

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.text: Returns every answer key published for exactly a given paper.
Finds one of the exam's source documents by its id.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.tech: Returns the first SourceDocument with the id, or None.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.text: Lists every piece of information that claims to be verified but has no word-for-word official proof. This list should always be empty; it is the check that GovOS's central rule held.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::UniversalE.tech: Returns paths from all_facts() where status VERIFIED and has_value but not is_publishable.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::VacancyCou.text: A number of vacancies, for whatever the notice breaks it down by (post, category, year), with any printed qualifier such as 'provisional'.

tools/exam_builder/schema.py::_walk_fact.text: Searches through any nested structure (records, lists, dictionaries) and finds every piece of information in it, along with its location.
tools/exam_builder/schema.py::_walk_fact.tech: Recursive generator: yields (path, obj) for a Fact without descending into it; skips scalars/None; recurses into dicts ('a.b'), lists/tuples/sets ('a[i]') and dataclass fields; an id-based seen set prevents cycles.

tools/exam_builder/search.py::Hit.text: One search result: page title, link, a snippet of its content, and its trust level.
tools/exam_builder/search.py::Hit.tech: Dataclass: title, url, content, trust; property host.

tools/exam_builder/search.py::Hit.host.text: The website name of the result, without 'www.'.
tools/exam_builder/search.py::Hit.host.tech: Property: lower-cased urlparse(url).hostname with 'www.' removed ('' if none).

tools/exam_builder/search.py::SearchUnav.text: An error raised when web discovery through the Claude command-line tool cannot run (turned off, not installed, not signed in). GovOS then reports it cannot identify the authority, rather than guessing.
tools/exam_builder/search.py::SearchUnav.tech: RuntimeError subclass raised by search() when tools.claude_cli.discovery.discover raises DiscoveryUnavailable.

tools/exam_builder/search.py::classify.text: Decides how trustworthy a web address is (for example official for Indian government domains).

tools/exam_builder/search.py::search.text: Finds candidate web pages for a query using Claude's web discovery, then applies GovOS's own filter: when only official results are wanted, it keeps only addresses GovOS itself classifies as official, whatever Claude said. Results are remembered so the same query is not repeated. If discovery cannot run, it raises an error instead of guessing.
tools/exam_builder/search.py::search.tech: Memo key (lower-cased query, max_results, official_only); uses memo_get/memo_put only when no gateway is passed. Calls discovery.discover(query, max_results=min(max_results, 12), official_only, gateway); DiscoveryUnavailable -> SearchUnavailable with setup guidance. Builds Hit(title, final_url or url, snippet or why_relevant, trust) for each candidate, filtered to classify_url == 'OFFICIAL' when official_only. Returns list[Hit].

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's article about the invented commission's Group 1 notification.
Test fixture: the base web address of the invented portal.
Test fixture: the made-up web address of an invented education portal used in the tests for reading secondary sources.

Test data only: the official record of a made-up exam (Group-I Services 2026 of an invented commission), shaped like a real GovOS exam record. Tests compare what the made-up news site says against these official dates, vacancy count and result.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture dict shaped like a runtime registry record: id exam-epsc-group-i-2026, cycle 2026, vacanciesTotal '120' with factEvidence, dates (notification, application open, an extended close plus the SUPERSEDED original close, edit-window open/close, a May/June Prelims with displayWhen, a Mains range, a result) each with _prov provenance, and one resultDeclarations entry. Input to ingest_secondary/official_claims in tests.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: a deliberately planted piece of text, addressed to an AI, that tries to get the portal's page treated as official. The tests use it to prove that GovOS ignores such text and never treats a secondary site as official.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Constant adversarial string embedded as a paragraph in the ARTICLE fixture page; test_secondary_ingestion's test_text_addressed_to_an_ai_changes_nothing checks that it is present in the page's visible text yet no claim quotes it and no claim is PRIMARY_OFFICIAL.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's answer-key article for the invented Group 1 2026 exam.
Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's list of notifications for the invented commission.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Constant f'{BASE}/sourceview/EPSC/Notification/notification-list'; a key of the in-memory PAGES map and a configured ingestion entry point.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: a made-up address of the invented commission's own official notice, which the portal links to.

Test data only: the HTML pages of a made-up exam-news website, kept in memory so the tests that check how GovOS reads 'reviewed outside' websites never touch the real internet. The pages deliberately include tricky cases: a date the commission later changed, a table about a different exam, a list showing only part of its papers, and a paragraph that tries to give orders to an AI.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture. Dict mapping fixture URLs (NOTIFICATIONS, RESULTS, PAPERS, ARTICLE, RESULT_PAGE, KEY_PAGE) to HTML built with _html/_row: link lists (including an off-site link and a link to the authority root), a paper list of ul/li blocks with Label : Value tables and viewer links carrying DocUrl=, a commented-out link, a '1 - 2 of 9' pager, an article with Label | Value tables (one for a sibling Group 2 exam), a prompt-injection paragraph (INJECTION) and a result page with an 'Exam Name' row. Consumed by SecondarySite.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's question-paper list.

Test fixture: the review record for the invented portal, saying it is a reviewed trusted-secondary source for the invented commission, which kinds of document it is trusted for, who reviewed it and when, and which of its listings to read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Dict shaped like a source_trust_profiles.json entry: domain, source_class TRUSTED_SECONDARY, authority_coverage, permitted_roles (NOTIFICATION, RESULT, ANSWER_KEY, QUESTION_PAPER, CALENDAR), review_status REVIEWED, last_reviewed, reviewed_by, notes, evidence, and ingestion {maxItemPages 8, entryPoints for NOTIFICATIONS, RESULTS, PAPERS with authority and estates}.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's results list.
Test fixture: the address of the invented portal's results article for the invented Group 1 exam.

Test helper that pretends to be the made-up exam-news website. When the code under test asks for a page, it hands back the stored page (or an error), and it keeps a list of every address that was asked for.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Test fixture: a callable fetch stub over PAGES returning authority_fixture_site.FakeResponse objects. Records requested URLs in self.calls; supports extra pages and a set of URLs that fail.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Answers one page request from the code under test. It records the address, then returns a timeout for addresses set to fail, a redirect to another site for one special 'moved' page, the stored page if there is one, and 'page not found' otherwise.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Appends url to self.calls. failing -> FakeResponse(ok=False, status=0, error='connection timed out'); URLs ending '/results/moved.asp' -> a response whose final_url is off-site (elsewhere.example.com); known pages -> FakeResponse(final_url=url, text, content_hash = first 24 hex of SHA-256); anything else -> ok=False, status 404.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Sets up the pretend website for a test: starts an empty list of requested addresses, loads the stored pages plus any extra pages the test adds, and notes which addresses should fail.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Initialises calls=[], pages = PAGES merged with optional `extra` dict, and failing = set(failing). Keyword-only arguments.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture helper: wraps a title and body into a simple web page.
Test helper that builds a citation record (which official document, page and quoted words a fact came from) for the made-up exam.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.tech: Returns a provenance dict: documentTitle '05/2026 - GROUP-I SERVICES', officialUrl (default OFFICIAL_NOTICE), pageNumber '1', excerptText, verificationLevel (default OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED) and evidenceType (default DIRECT). Used to build EXAM.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_fixture_sit.text: Test fixture helper: makes one two-column table row (label and value) for a fixture page.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Describes one list page on a reviewed outside website that GovOS is allowed to read: its address, what kind of documents it lists (notices, results, papers...), and which exam authority it covers.
