tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Dataclass: url, lists (DocKind), authority name (default ''), estates (list of authority domains). Built by load_reviewed_sources from a profile's ingestion.entryPoints.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Plain-English names for each fact the tool compares, such as 'Last date to apply' or 'Main examination begins', used in its report.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Constant dict mapping internal field names (vacancies_total, notification_date, application_open/close, edit_window_start/end, exam_stage_1/2 _start/_end/_months, result_release) to display labels. Used by _cross_check; unknown fields fall back to a prettified name.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: The error raised when an outside website may not be read for an exam, for example because its review does not cover that authority or because it is actually the authority's own site.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Exception subclass with no extra behaviour; raised by ingest_secondary and caught by main() (exit code 3).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: One outside website that a person has reviewed and approved, together with the list pages GovOS may read on it and a cap on how many article pages to open.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Dataclass: profile (SourceTrustProfile), entry_points (list of EntryPoint), max_item_pages (default 8). Provides domain, review_record() and entry_points_for().

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: The website's plain address (for example 'example.in'), without 'www.'.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Property returning bare_host(self.profile.domain): lower-cased host with any leading 'www.' removed.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Picks out the list pages on this website that are about a given exam authority, matched by the authority's name or its official web address.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns entry points whose authority equals `authority` (case-insensitive) or whose estates intersect the given estates (lower-cased). Empty list if none match.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: A short summary of the human review of this website: its address, its trust level, whether it was reviewed, when, by whom, and which kinds of document it is trusted for.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns dict {domain, sourceClass, reviewStatus, lastReviewed, reviewedBy, permittedRoles} from the profile. Attached to the ingestion report and to every resource row.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: A fixed label stamped on everything this tool produces. It says the information came from a reviewed outside website, was read only from the command line, and is not published to candidates or stored by the app.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Constant dict: sourceClass TRUSTED_SECONDARY, availability COMMAND_LINE_ONLY, publication NOT_PUBLISHED, plus an explanatory note. Copied into SecondaryIngestion.as_dict()['status'], into each claim row (_claim_row) and resolution row (_cross_check), and printed by main().

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: The full report of one reading of an outside website for one exam: which list pages were read, which items were found, every claim the site makes, how each claim compares with the official record, links back to the authority's own site, and anything that could not be read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Dataclass with source, review, exam_id, exam_title, authority, cycle, started_at/ended_at, and lists listings, resources, claims, resolutions, pointers (links to the authority's estate, leads only), refused, unexplored and notes. Has counts() and as_dict(). Returned by ingest_secondary.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Turns the report into plain data ready to save as a JSON file, with the 'not published, command line only' label at the top.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns a dict with status (copy of STATUS), source, review, examId, examTitle, authority, cycle, startedAt, endedAt, counts(), listings, resources, claims, resolutions, pointers, refused, unexplored and notes.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Totals for the report: how many list pages were read, items found, claims made and compared, results by comparison outcome, links back to the authority, refusals and unread places.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns {listingsRead (listings with ok), resources, claims, claimsCompared, resolutions (count per resolution state), pointers, refused, unexplored}.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: One table found on a web page: the heading it sits under and its rows of cell text.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Dataclass: heading (str, the last h1-h6/caption seen before the table) and rows (list of lists of cell strings). Produced by _TableParser/read_tables. Distinct from tables.Table.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads the way many exam portals lay out a list of papers: a list whose first item is a title, followed by a small 'Label : Value' table and a download link. For every link it records the list's title and those label/value pairs.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: HTMLParser subclass keeping a stack of ul/ol blocks {title, fields, links}. The first li without a link becomes the title; two-cell tr rows (ignoring ':' cells) become fields; a hrefs (excluding #, javascript:, mailto:) are resolved with urljoin. On closing a list it emits one record {url, text, title, fields} per link into self.records.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Prepares the list-block reader for one page, remembering the page address so relative links can be made full.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Stores base_url; initialises records, _blocks, _li_buf, _li_has_link, _row, _cell, _a and _skip.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Adds a piece of text to whatever is being read: a link's words, a table cell, or a list item.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Unless skipping, appends data to the open link buffer, cell buffer and li buffer (any that are open).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: On a closing tag: saves the finished link (as a full address), a 'Label : Value' pair, the list's title, or, when the whole list closes, one record per link carrying the list's title and pairs.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: a: appends (urljoin(base, href), collapsed text) to the innermost block unless href is empty or starts with #, javascript:, mailto:. td/th: appends cell text. tr: if exactly two non-empty, non-':' cells, stores fields[label.rstrip(':')] = value. li: the first link-free non-empty li text becomes the block title. ul/ol: pops the block and emits records.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: On an opening tag: begins a new list block, a list item, a table row or cell, or a link, and skips hidden code.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Script-like tags increment _skip. ul/ol push a new block; li (inside a block) resets _li_buf and _li_has_link; tr starts _row; td/th starts _cell; a records its href and sets _li_has_link.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads every table on a web page as rows of cell text, remembering which heading each table was under. Tables inside tables are read as separate tables, and hidden or commented-out parts are not read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: HTMLParser subclass keeping a stack of open Table objects, the current row/cell buffers, the last heading text and a skip counter for script/style/noscript/template. Comments are ignored by default (no handle_comment). Completed tables accumulate in self.tables.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Prepares the table reader with nothing read yet.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Initialises tables=[], _stack=[], _row/_cell/_hbuf=None, _heading='', _skip=0; convert_charrefs=True.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Adds a piece of text to the heading or table cell currently being read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Unless skipping, appends data to _hbuf and/or _cell when they are open.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: On a closing tag: finishes the heading, cell, row or table being read and files it in the right place. Empty rows are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Closing heading/caption sets _heading to the collapsed text (if non-empty); td/th appends collapsed cell text to _row; tr appends the row to the innermost table if any cell is non-empty; table pops the stack into self.tables (so inner tables are appended before outer ones).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: On an opening tag: starts ignoring hidden code, starts collecting a heading, opens a new table under the current heading, or starts a new row or cell.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: script-like tags increment _skip; while skipping, returns. h1-h6/caption start _hbuf; table pushes Table(heading=_heading); tr (inside a table) starts _row; td/th (inside a row) starts _cell.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads a web page and keeps only the words a person would see, skipping hidden code and styling.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: HTMLParser subclass collecting text into self.parts, skipping script/style/noscript/template content (nesting counter) and inserting line breaks at block tags. Used by visible_text.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Prepares the page-text reader with an empty text buffer.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Calls HTMLParser.__init__(convert_charrefs=True); sets parts=[] and _skip=0.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Keeps a piece of page text unless it is inside hidden code.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Appends data to parts when _skip is 0.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: When a closing page tag is met: stop ignoring text after hidden code ends, and put a space after each table cell so cell words do not run together.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Closing script/style/noscript/template decrements _skip (not below 0); closing td/th appends a space.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: When an opening page tag is met: start ignoring text if it is hidden code or styling, or start a new line if it is a paragraph, list item, table cell, heading and similar.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: script/style/noscript/template increments _skip; br, p, div, li, tr, td, th, h1-h6 and title append a newline to parts.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Turns one claim from the outside website into a report row, adding the 'not published' label, the year it is about, the exact words printed, where it came from, and whether it was compared with the official record (and if not, why).
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns c.as_dict() updated with publication, availability (from STATUS), cycle, printed, origin, rowLabel, compared and whyNotCompared (default reason when not compared). Keeps the SourceClaim object under '_claim' for _cross_check, which removes it.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads one article page from the outside website and collects what it claims about the exam. It skips the page if its title names another exam, records links back to the authority's own site as leads, reads 'Label | Value' table rows (ignoring tables about other exams) for dates and counts, and reads sentences stating a number of vacancies. Each claim keeps its exact words, and is checked against the page text.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Mutates `out` and `res`. Reads visible text and <title>; relation_of on the title (OTHER_EXAM -> note and return); page cycle falls back to the listing's cycle. Inner add() de-duplicates (field, value, quotation), builds a SourceClaim, calls check_quotation(text) and appends a _claim_row with compared = claim cycle equals exam cycle. Tables: skip headings/one-cell rows naming another exam, 'Exam Name' rows set the cycle and a Prelims/Mains stage hint for an 'Exam Date' row, _row_field maps labels; COUNT via _count, DAY via parse_when (DAY only), SPAN via _span_values. Sentences matching _VACANCY_SENTENCE (excluding year-like numbers) that relate to this exam add vacancies_total.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads a cell as a plain whole number (such as '563' or '12,256'), or gives nothing if the cell is anything else.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns int with commas removed when the stripped text fully matches comma-grouped thousands or 1-6 digits; otherwise None.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Compares each fact the outside website stated (for this exam's year) with the official record, using GovOS's single rule for weighing sources: the official value always wins, agreement is noted as support, disagreement is recorded but never used. It adds plain notes, for example that the site is repeating a date the authority later changed, or that nothing official states a claim so it is only a lead.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Builds official claims via official_claims and _official_listed, groups by field; for each field with compared secondary claims calls claims.reconcile(field, officials + secondary) and appends resolution.as_dict() plus publication/availability, label (FIELD_LABELS), officialPrinted and notes (OFFICIAL_CONTESTED conflicts matched against superseded values or described as differing; SECONDARY_ONLY/UNSUPPORTED get the listing note; SECONDARY_ONLY gets a 'lead only' note). Strips '_claim' from claim rows and adds a note counting claims not compared. Mutates `out`.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Works out where to save the report file by default: a file named after the website and exam inside the project's exam_data/secondary folder.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns <repo root>/exam_data/secondary/<domain>__<exam_id>.json, with the root derived from this file's location.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Some portals show a PDF through a viewer page whose address carries the real file address inside it. This pulls out that inner file address, exactly as written.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Parses the URL query and returns the first value of a key named docurl, qpurl, file or pdf (case-insensitive); '' if none.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Makes a short fingerprint of a page's text, so two addresses showing the same page can be spotted.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: First 24 hex characters of SHA-256 over the UTF-8 text ('' treated as empty).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Builds a standard date (year-month-day) from three numbers, or gives nothing if they are not a real calendar day (31 February is refused).
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Casts y, m, d to int (None on failure); requires 1900 < y < 2100 and that datetime.date(y, m, d) is valid (days per month and leap years); returns 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Turns a month name or abbreviation ('Oct', 'October') into its number (10).
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Lower-cases the name and returns the 1-based index of the first month whose full name starts with its first three letters; raises StopIteration if none (callers catch it).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Gathers official evidence that a document (an answer key, a paper, a result) exists for this exam: items on the authority's own list pages from a walk of its site, and the record's own result announcement. It also adds notes explaining what the walk of the authority's site found, or that no walk was done.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns (claims, notes). From official_listing.repositories items with relation THIS_EXAM and a role in _LISTED_ROLES, builds 'listed:<role>' PRIMARY_OFFICIAL SourceClaims marked VERIFIED; adds at most one 'listed:RESULT' claim from the first OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED resultDeclaration with an excerpt and URL. notes maps 'listed:<role>' to the walk's search state and reason, or, with no official_listing, to 'not walked' for each listed role.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Turns a page number into a whole number, or nothing if it is not one.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: int(value), returning None on TypeError/ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Looks at a table row's label (like 'Online Application Last Date') and says which fact it states and what kind of value to expect (a count, a day, or a span of dates). Returns nothing for labels it does not recognise.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Strips ' :' and fullmatches the label against _ROW_FIELDS in order; returns (field_name, kind) where kind is COUNT/DAY/SPAN, or None.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Splits a date reading into the facts it actually states: a range gives a start and an end, a single day gives only a start (an exam 'on 21 October' does not say when it ends), and a month gives only the month.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: For when['kind'] RANGE returns [(field_start, start), (field_end, end)]; DAY returns [(field_start, start)]; otherwise [(field_months, start)].

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Rewrites a portal's 'Group 1' or 'Gp-2' as 'Group-I' / 'Group-II', the way commissions write it, so GovOS's existing exam matcher can recognise it. It deliberately leaves 'Gr-1' alone, because that is a grade of a post, not a recruitment group.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Regex substitution of (group|gp)[\s.-]*[1-4] (not followed by a digit, case-insensitive) with 'Group-' plus the Roman numeral I-IV. Returns '' for empty input.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: The main routine for checking a reviewed outside website against GovOS's official record for one exam. It first refuses if the site is the authority's own, or its review does not cover this authority. It then reads the approved list pages, finds the items about this exam, opens a limited number of this exam's article pages, and collects every date, count and 'a key is listed' statement with its exact words. Finally it compares each claim with the official record. Nothing it finds is ever treated as official.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Args: ReviewedSource, exam record dict, optional fetch (default fetch_checked, 20 s, 3 MB), registry, official_listing (a project_for_exam projection), max_item_pages. Raises IngestionRefused (same estate as the authority, profile.covers false, no entry points, no exam words from exam_words_for). For each entry point: fetches (redirects off the source domain are refused), records hash, notes a 'x - y of z' pager as unexplored, reads blocks and extract_links; off-domain links to the authority estate become pointers; items are judged by relation_of on block title/fields/link text, role by classify_link (fallback to the listing's role), class by classify_source with PRIMARY_OFFICIAL forcibly downgraded to SECONDARY; THIS_EXAM listed answer keys/papers/results become 'listed:<ROLE>' SourceClaims. Then reads THIS_EXAM/CYCLE_UNSTATED item pages (skipping file viewers and PDFs) within the budget, de-duplicating by content hash, via _claims_from_page; finally _cross_check. Returns SecondaryIngestion.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Loads the file of human-reviewed outside websites and keeps only those GovOS is allowed to read: reviewed, marked as trusted, and with a list of pages to read that all sit on that same website. Any website whose review has a problem anywhere is left out entirely and the problem is reported, rather than half-used.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Reads the JSON registry at `path` (default DEFAULT_PROFILE_PATH); returns ({bare domain: ReviewedSource}, [problem dicts]). Each profile is validated via TrustRegistry; profiles without an `ingestion` block are skipped silently. Refuses a profile (problem recorded) if not REVIEWED, not TRUSTED_SECONDARY, any entry point fails validate_url_syntax, is off the profile's domain, or names an unknown DocKind, or if no entry point remains. maxItemPages is clamped to 1..25 (default 8). An unreadable file returns ({}, [one problem]).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: The command-line entry point. Given a website and an exam id, it loads the exam from the database, finds the website among the reviewed ones, optionally walks the authority's own site too, runs the comparison, saves the report as a JSON file and prints a summary. It writes nothing else.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: argparse: --source, --exam (required), --db, --walk, --max-items, --out. Loads the exam via claude_cli.context.ExamStore (default govos.db), registry problems to stderr, source via load_reviewed_sources; --walk runs authority_discovery.discover_authority + project_for_exam. Calls ingest_secondary; writes result.as_dict() to --out or _default_out; prints STATUS, counts and one line per resolution. Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 unknown exam or source, 3 IngestionRefused.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Pulls the official side of the comparison out of GovOS's exam record: every date and the vacancy count that the record holds as officially verified, with the exact quoted words and document. Dates that were later replaced are kept apart, so if the outside site repeats an old date the report can say so.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Returns (claims, superseded): claims is a list of (SourceClaim PRIMARY_OFFICIAL with quotation_status VERIFIED, printed) and superseded maps field -> [{value, quotation, url, printed}]. take() needs excerptText, officialUrl and a value; SUPERSEDED (level, or date status) goes to superseded; only OFFICIALLY_VERIFIED becomes a claim. CORRECTION_WINDOW dates map to edit_window_start/end by 'open'/'close' in the label; EXAM_TIER1/2 read displayWhen via parse_when (or the bare day) and expand with _span_values; other mapped types (_OFFICIAL_TYPES) take the day only when no displayWhen. vacanciesTotal is read with _count and cited from factEvidence.vacanciesTotal.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads a table cell as a date only if the whole cell is a date: a single day, a range of days, or only a month (such as 'May/June 2026'). A cell that says anything more than a date is not treated as one.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Normalises spacing/commas and strips ' .', then tries _WHEN_PATTERNS with fullmatch in order (numeric range, 'd Mon to d Mon yyyy', 'd to d Mon yyyy', numeric day, 'Mon d, yyyy', 'd Mon yyyy', 'Mon/Mon yyyy', 'Mon yyyy'). Returns {'kind': RANGE|DAY|MONTHS, 'start', 'end'} (MONTHS start is 'YYYY-MM' or 'YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM'), skipping matches with an invalid start or a range without an end. None if nothing matches.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Reads a list page's title-plus-details blocks and returns them keyed by each link's tidied address, keeping only blocks that have a title.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Runs _BlockParser(base_url) over html (exceptions swallowed); returns {normalize_url(record.url): record} for records whose title is non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Gives back every table on a web page, each with its heading and rows. A badly formed page yields whatever tables could be read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Runs _TableParser over html (exceptions swallowed) and returns its list of Table objects.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Decides how one listed item relates to the exam being checked: this exam this year, this exam but the year is not stated, this exam in another year, another exam, or not this exam. It reuses GovOS's existing exam matcher on the item's own words.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Normalises text with designation_text, runs discover.gate(...) with the exam words and sibling words, and reads the cycle via pyq.identity_from_text. If not REJECTED and words exist: returns ('THIS_EXAM_CYCLE_UNSTATED', '') with no cycle, else ('THIS_EXAM' if cycle empty or equal, else 'THIS_EXAM_OTHER_CYCLE', item_cycle). Otherwise ('OTHER_EXAM' if gate reported a foreign match, else 'NOT_THIS_EXAM', item_cycle).

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: For an exam named by its group (like 'Group I'), lists the other groups ('group ii', 'group iii', 'group iv'), so items about those sister exams can be told apart.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Collects Roman numerals from words that fully match 'group <roman>'; returns ['group ii', ...] for the I-IV numerals not owned; [] if the exam words name no group.

tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.text: Turns a web page into the plain text a reader sees, one tidy line per block, with empty lines removed. A badly formed page still gives whatever text could be read.
tools/exam_builder/secondary_ingestion.p.tech: Feeds html to _TextParser (swallowing any parser exception), joins parts, splits on newlines, collapses whitespace per line and drops blank lines. Returns a newline-joined string.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::CueSet.text: Describes the kinds of words that signal a fact (such as a fee): words that must appear, words that make it more likely, and words that suggest the passage is about something else.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::CueSet.tech: Dataclass of regex tuples: anchors (at least one required), supporting (each +0.6) and against (each -1.2). score() rates a passage. Also used by stages.PROCEDURE.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::CueSet.s.text: Rates how strongly a passage looks like it states the fact. No signal word means zero; supporting words raise the score and warning words lower it sharply.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::CueSet.s.tech: Lower-cases the passage; returns (0.0, []) if no anchor regex matches; otherwise score = 1.0 + 0.6*supporting hits - 1.2*against hits, floored at 0, and the list of matched anchor and supporting patterns.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::FieldSpe.text: Describes one fact GovOS reads from a notice (fee, age limits, vacancies, attempts, qualification, exam pattern): its signal words, how to turn a passage into a tidy value, and whether the value must be a whole sentence.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::FieldSpe.tech: Dataclass: name, cues (CueSet), normalise (passage -> value or None), optional evidence_from, purpose, and unit ('sentence' means the value's text is re-read to its sentence end in the full document by _whole_sentence).

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::SPEC_BY_.text: A lookup from a fact's name (such as 'fee') to its description of how to read it.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::SPEC_BY_.tech: Dict {spec.name: FieldSpec} built from SPECS (fee, ageLimits, vacancies, attempts, qualification, examPattern). Used by extract.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_age.text: Reads an age limit however it is worded ('between 18 and 27 years', 'not below 21 and not above 30', 'must have attained the age of 21...'), plus the date age is counted on and any 'born between' dates.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_age.tech: Tries five regex phrasings; the first giving 10 <= min < max <= 70 wins. Returns {minAge, maxAge, asOn, bornBetween, [asOnText]}: asOn is parsed by _iso_date from the 48 chars after a cue ('as on', 'on the', 'crucial date', 'reckoned'), bornBetween from a 'born not earlier than / on or after ... not later than / on or before' phrase. None if no phrasing fits.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_attempt.text: Reads any limit on how many times a candidate may sit the exam, including the case where the notice says there is no limit.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_attempt.tech: Returns {limited: False, count: None} for 'no restriction/limit/bar on the number of attempts' or 'attempts are unlimited'; otherwise the number from 'permitted/allowed/eligible for/restricted to ... N attempts', else from a bare 'N attempts', as {limited: True, count}. None if nothing matches.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_bound_c.text: Finds a number written just before the word 'vacancies' or 'posts', skipping numbers that are only a part of the total (as in 'which include 33 vacancies reserved').
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_bound_c.tech: Iterates _COUNT_BEFORE matches and returns the first whose preceding 30 chars do not end in a 'part of' phrase (_PART_OF: including, of which, among them...); None if none.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_fee.text: Reads an application fee from a passage: the rupee amounts, whether an amount is written in words, which categories (women, SC, ST, PwBD and others) are exempt, and which payment methods are named.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_fee.tech: Returns None unless a Rs/INR/rupee-symbol amount or a worded amount ('one hundred rupees') is found. Exempt categories are read from up to 220 chars after an exemption cue (exempt, remission, not required to pay, no fee), or from 200 chars before it if none follow. Payment modes from a fixed word list. Returns {amounts (max 3, commas removed), amountInWords, exemptCategories, paymentModes}.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_iso_dat.text: Turns a date phrase into a standard year-month-day date, or gives nothing if it cannot.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_iso_dat.tech: Calls exam_authoring.extract.parse_date(text); returns its result or '' (also '' on any exception).

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_narrowe.text: Picks the shortest sentence in a chunk that states the very value that was read, so a reviewer sees the claim rather than a whole paragraph, and never a nearby sentence stating a different figure.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_narrowe.tech: Returns the shortest sentence (>= 25 chars) of the chunk for which spec.normalise(sentence) == value, else the chunk. Normaliser exceptions are ignored. It used to accept any sentence yielding some value.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_pattern.text: Reads the exam pattern from a passage: each paper, tier or stage with its marks, and where nearby its duration and number of questions, plus any negative-marking rule. A figure printed as a stage's 'Total' is not taken as one paper's marks.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_pattern.tech: Regex over 'paper/tier/stage <ordinal> ... N marks' (skipping rows whose middle text ends in 'Total'); each row {label, name, marks, [duration from 120 chars after], [questions from 80 before to 120 after]}, de-duplicated. negativeMarking is the first 160 chars of a 'negative marking ...' fraction/amount phrase. Returns {papers (max 12), [negativeMarking]} or None if neither found.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_qualifi.text: Reads the minimum education requirement, starting from 'must hold / should possess' or from a degree word, up to the end of its sentence. If it started on a degree word in the middle of a sentence, it is marked so the full sentence is read from its start later.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_qualifi.tech: Finds the first match of a requirement phrase or a qualification word; text runs to units.sentence_end within the passage if found. Returns None if no qualification levels are present; otherwise {text, levels} plus internal flag _starts_inside_sentence when the text does not begin with must/should/shall (removed by _whole_sentence).

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_qualifi.text: Lists the education-level words found in a text, such as bachelor's, degree, diploma or 10+2.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_qualifi.tech: Returns the sorted set of lower-cased matches of a fixed regex of qualification words (bachelor, master, graduate, post-graduate, degree, diploma, matriculation, 10+2, intermediate, doctorate, PhD).

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_vacanci.text: Reads the number of vacancies from a passage, preferring a total stated in so many words ('the number of vacancies is expected to be approximately 933'), and notes whether the number is approximate.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_vacanci.tech: Tries _COUNT_STATED, then _bound_count, then _COUNT_AFTER; strips commas and accepts 1..2,000,000. Returns {count (string), isApproximate (approx/about/tentative/expected/likely anywhere in the passage)} or None.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_whole_s.text: Makes sure a quoted requirement ends where its sentence really ends in the whole document, not where the search chunk happened to stop. If no sentence end is found before the next clause or heading, the reading is dropped instead of being published cut short.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::_whole_s.tech: Locates the first 60 chars of value['text'] in the chunk and the flattened document (with a fallback search near the offset); end = units.sentence_end(flat, start, next_structural_boundary(flat, start+1)). Returns None if not found or no end. If _starts_inside_sentence was set, start moves to units.sentence_start. Returns a copy with text = flat[start:end]; for 'qualification' recomputes levels and returns None if empty.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::extract.text: Reads one fact from a document however the authority worded it. It scores overlapping chunks by their signal words, tries the best ones, turns each into a tidy value, picks the shortest quote that supports it, and accepts the value only if that quote really appears word for word in the document. Getting nothing back means 'could not read it', never 'the authority did not publish it'.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::extract.tech: Looks up SPEC_BY_NAME[field_name]; scores passages() with spec.cues.score, keeps those >= min_confidence (default 1.0), and tries up to the top 25. For unit='sentence' specs the value is extended by _whole_sentence and its text is the span; otherwise the span is _narrowest_span. Builds Evidence (page from page_of or 1) and Extracted(confidence = min(1, score/3), cues_matched) and returns the first that evidence.verified_or_none accepts against document_text. None otherwise.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::extract_.text: Reads every fact this module knows (fee, age, vacancies, attempts, qualification, pattern) from one document, or only the ones asked for, keeping each that has a verified quote.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::extract_.tech: For each SPECS entry in `only` (or all), calls extract(...) and returns {name: Extracted} for non-None results.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::passages.text: Cuts a document's text into overlapping chunks (about 320 characters, moving 160 at a time) for searching. The chunks overlap so a fee sentence and its exemption clause are not split apart, and a chunk never starts or ends in the middle of a word or number, which once turned '12,256 vacancies' into '122'.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::passages.tech: Normalises whitespace, then for start in range(0, len, stride) takes [start, start+window], moving the begin forward to the next space if it falls mid-token and the end forward (up to 60 chars) to the next space. Stops when a trailing chunk is under 40 chars. Returns [(offset, chunk)]; [] for empty text.

tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::sentence.text: A rough split of text into sentences, used to trim a chunk down to the sentence that holds a fact.
tools/exam_builder/semantic.py::sentence.tech: Normalises whitespace and splits after '.', ';' or ':' followed by whitespace and an uppercase letter or '('. Returns non-empty parts.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::AUTH.text: The kinds of service that belong to the whole authority rather than one exam: the one-time registration portal, the application portal and the official portal.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::AUTH.tech: frozenset {OTR_PORTAL, APPLICATION_PORTAL, OFFICIAL_PORTAL}. Excluded from exam-level checks in unsearched and role_search_state.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::CAND.text: The plain labels shown to candidates for each trust level: 'Official source', 'Trusted secondary source', 'Third-party source - not verified', 'Community lead - not verified', and nothing for refused addresses.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::CAND.tech: Dict SourceClass -> display string; UNVERIFIED maps to ''.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::CLAU.text: The note attached to a source when its role was guessed by Claude rather than by GovOS's own rules, so it can always be treated as a reading, not as proof.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::CLAU.tech: Constant string beginning 'classified by Claude'; role_by_claude checks the prefix.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.text: The fixed limits of one walk of an authority's website, so it never turns into an open-ended crawl: 2 links deep, 25 pages, 600 sources, 40 files, about 1.5 MB per file, a 12-second timeout, 4 redirects, and at most 25 unclear links sent to Claude.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.tech: Frozen dataclass: max_depth 2, max_pages 25, max_nodes 600, max_documents 40, max_content_bytes 1,500,000, timeout_seconds 12.0, max_redirects 4 (informational; fixed in fetch_checked), max_claude_links 25. as_dict().

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.text: Turns the limits into plain data for the report.

The record of one bounded walk of an authority's website: which domains count as the authority's own, where it started, its limits, the map it built, how many pages and files it fetched, what it left unexplored and why, failures, leads from social posts, Claude usage, and notes.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.tech: Dataclass: id ('run-' + 12 hex), authority_name, estates, roots, limits, graph, started_at/ended_at, pages_fetched, documents_fetched, frontier, skipped_out_of_scope, fetch_failures, leads, claude, cancelled, notes. as_dict/from_dict with camelCase keys. Stored by SourceGraphStore.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.text: Turns the walk's record into plain data for saving.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.tech: Returns a camelCase dict including limits.as_dict() and graph.as_dict(); lists and dicts are copied.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.text: Rebuilds a walk's record from saved data.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Disc.tech: Classmethod reading camelCase keys with defaults; DiscoveryLimits built only from known fields, graph via SourceGraph.from_dict.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Edge.text: How GovOS reached a source: linked from an official page, from an official archive page, as an item of an official list, as the place an official page sends people to apply, linked from a non-official page, from a search engine, cited by an outside source, or pointed at by a social post.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Edge.tech: str Enum: OFFICIAL_LINK, OFFICIAL_ARCHIVE_LINK, REPOSITORY_ITEM, APPLICATION_LINK, REFERENCE_LINK, DISCOVERED_BY_SEARCH, SECONDARY_REFERENCE, DISCOVERY_SIGNAL. is_official property.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Edge.text: Whether this way of reaching a source came from the authority's own pages.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Edge.tech: True for OFFICIAL_LINK, OFFICIAL_ARCHIVE_LINK, REPOSITORY_ITEM and APPLICATION_LINK.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Node.text: What happened when GovOS looked at a source: only seen as a link, read, read but had no links, file downloaded, unreadable (such as a scan), could not be fetched, address refused, or skipped because a limit was reached.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Node.tech: str Enum: DISCOVERED, READ, READ_NO_LINKS, FETCHED, UNREADABLE, FETCH_FAILED, BLOCKED, SKIPPED_LIMIT.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Node.text: What kind of thing a found address is: the site's home, an ordinary page, a list page of many documents, a file, a service such as a registration portal, a video, a social account, or a link not yet looked at.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Node.tech: str Enum: SITE_ROOT, PAGE, REPOSITORY, DOCUMENT, PORTAL, VIDEO, SOCIAL, LINK.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sear.text: What GovOS can honestly say after looking for one kind of document: found and identified, found but unclear, found but unreadable, not found after reading everything relevant, search incomplete (some places could hold it but were not read), or not searched at all. 'Not found' is allowed only when every relevant place found was actually read.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sear.tech: str Enum: FOUND_VERIFIED, FOUND_AMBIGUOUS, FOUND_UNREADABLE, NOT_FOUND_AFTER_DISCOVERY, SEARCH_INCOMPLETE, NOT_SEARCHED. Produced by role_search_state.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Skip.text: Why a source was not read, recorded on it: a budget of files, pages or items ran out, it was too deep, the page is built by script, it could not be fetched, its address was refused, it was never opened, or its links were not followed. An unread source is a place GovOS did not look, never proof something is missing.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Skip.tech: str Enum: FILE_BUDGET, PAGE_BUDGET, ITEM_BUDGET, DEPTH_LIMIT, SCRIPT_RENDERED, FETCH_FAILED, REFUSED_ADDRESS, NOT_OPENED, LINKS_NOT_FOLLOWED. coverage_key property.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Skip.text: The name used for this reason in the coverage report, such as 'skipped_due_to_file_budget'.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Skip.tech: 'skipped_due_to_' + a mapped suffix: depth for DEPTH_LIMIT, script_rendering for SCRIPT_RENDERED, refused_address for REFUSED_ADDRESS, otherwise the lower-cased value.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: The trust levels GovOS gives to any source it finds: official (the authority itself), trusted outside source (reviewed by a person, for named kinds of document), other outside source (unreviewed), community lead (such as a social post, used only to go looking), and unverified (a refused address).
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: str Enum: PRIMARY_OFFICIAL, TRUSTED_SECONDARY, SECONDARY, DISCOVERY_ONLY, UNVERIFIED, in strength order. Properties rank, may_state_official_fact, may_corroborate, candidate_visible, candidate_label.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: The plain words a candidate sees for this trust level, such as 'Official source'.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Returns CANDIDATE_LABELS[self].

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Whether a candidate may be shown a source of this level at all (with its label). Community leads and refused addresses are not shown.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: True for PRIMARY_OFFICIAL, TRUSTED_SECONDARY and SECONDARY.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Whether a source of this level may back up (agree with) an official fact: official and person-reviewed trusted sources may.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: True for PRIMARY_OFFICIAL and TRUSTED_SECONDARY.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Whether a source of this level may state an official fact. Only the authority's own sources may.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: True only for PRIMARY_OFFICIAL.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: A number for how strong a trust level is (0 is strongest), used to keep the stronger reading when the same address is found twice.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Index of the member in declaration order (PRIMARY_OFFICIAL=0 ... UNVERIFIED=4).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: One record of how GovOS got from one source to another: which page linked to which, in what way, with the link's words and the heading it sat under. This is the trail an auditor follows.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Dataclass: source_id ('' for roots, search results or signals), target_id, kind (EdgeKind), anchor_text, context, method (crawl|seed|search|social|claude-classified, default crawl), discovered_at. as_dict/from_dict.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Turns the link record into plain data for saving.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: asdict with kind as its string value.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Rebuilds a link record from saved data.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Classmethod: kind converted to EdgeKind (required; raises if missing/invalid), unknown keys dropped.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: The map of everything one walk found: each source once, however many ways it was reached, plus every link between them.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Holds nodes {id: SourceNode}, edges list, a set of (source, target, kind) edge keys and a content-hash index. Methods: get, add, add_edge, record_content, parents, children, provenance, of_role, as_dict, from_dict; len() is the node count.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Starts an empty map.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Initialises nodes={}, edges=[], _edge_keys=set(), _by_hash={}.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: How many sources the map holds.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: len(self.nodes).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Adds a source to the map, or updates it if already there. When a source is reached again, the stronger reading is kept: a higher trust level with its reason, a known role over 'unknown', a known kind over 'just a link', and a title over none. Being linked again from an official page is noted, but does not raise its trust.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Returns (node, created). New: SourceNode with normalised URL, first_seen_at, attrs applied, host derived. Existing: source_class replaced only if attrs class has a lower rank (with class_reason/relationship); otherwise relationship upgraded to LINKED_FROM_OFFICIAL from ''/INDEPENDENT; owner, role (from UNKNOWN), node_type (from LINK), title/context/video_kind/authority filled only when empty; depth = min.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Records that one source led to another, once per pair and kind of link, and never a source linking to itself.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Returns the new SourceEdge, or None if (source_id, target_id, kind) already exists or source_id == target_id. discovered_at defaults to now_iso(); other attrs passed to SourceEdge.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Turns the whole map into plain data for saving.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: {'nodes': [node.as_dict()], 'edges': [edge.as_dict()]}.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Lists the links that lead out from a given source.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Edges whose source_id equals node_id (linear scan).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Rebuilds the map from saved data, including the indexes used to spot duplicates.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Classmethod: loads nodes via SourceNode.from_dict (re-registering content hashes of non-duplicates) and edges via SourceEdge.from_dict (re-registering edge keys).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Finds the record for a web address in the map, if it is there.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: self.nodes.get(node_id_for(url)).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Lists all sources of one kind of role, for example every answer key.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Nodes whose role is the given DocKind.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Lists the links that led to a given source.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Edges whose target_id equals node_id (linear scan).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Traces back how a source was first reached, step by step from the starting page, so a reviewer can check where it came from.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Follows the first inbound edge repeatedly (cycle-safe, max_hops 8), collecting {from (parent URL), kind, anchorText, context, method}; returns the chain reversed (root first).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Notes the fingerprint of a downloaded file. If another address already served exactly the same file, this one is marked as a copy so the file is counted once.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Sets node.content_hash (and content_type if given). If the hash was first seen on another node, sets duplicate_of to that node id; otherwise registers this node in _by_hash. Empty hash: nothing further.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Saves each website walk as one row in GovOS's SQLite database and reads them back. A saved walk is never overwritten; it stays as the record of what that walk saw.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Wraps a SQLite file (table source_discovery_runs, created on init). Methods: save, get, latest_id, latest, list. Each operation opens, commits and closes its own connection.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Connects to the database file and makes sure the table for walks exists.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Stores db_path and calls init_source_tables inside _conn().

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Opens a database connection for one task, saves the changes, and always closes it, because a connection left open locks the file on Windows.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Context manager: sqlite3.connect(timeout=30), row_factory=sqlite3.Row, yields inside 'with conn' (commit/rollback), closes in finally.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Loads one saved walk by its id, or nothing if there is none.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: SELECT run_json by id; returns DiscoveryRun.from_dict or None.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Loads the most recent walk of an authority's site.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Same ordering as latest_id but returns DiscoveryRun.from_dict(run_json) or None.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Finds the id of the most recent walk of an authority's site, without loading the whole walk.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: SELECT id WHERE estate = ? ORDER BY ended_at DESC, rowid DESC LIMIT 1; None if none.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Lists recent walks with a few summary facts each: site, authority, times, how many sources, whether it was complete, and how many official list pages it found.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Newest first by rowid, limit clamped to 1..100 (default 20); returns dicts {id, estate, authorityName, startedAt, endedAt, jobId, nodes, exhaustive, repositories} read from coverage_json.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Saves one walk with its coverage summary and returns its id.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: INSERTs id, estate (first of run.estates or ''), authority_name, times, job_id, node count, run JSON and coverage JSON (given or coverage_report(run)). Returns run.id. A duplicate id raises from SQLite.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Everything GovOS records about one found source: its address and title, what it is, what role it plays (notice, paper, result...), how far it is trusted, what happened when it was looked at, who runs the site, how it relates to the authority, and why it was skipped if it was.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Dataclass keyed by node_id_for: url, title, node_type, role (DocKind), source_class, status, host, authority, content_type, content_hash, duplicate_of, depth, context, class_reason, role_reason, video_kind, identity, listed_without_link, skipped (SkipReason value), owner, relationship, notes, first_seen_at, checked_at. as_dict/from_dict serialisation.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Turns the source's record into plain data for saving.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: dataclasses.asdict with node_type, role, source_class and status replaced by their string values.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.text: Rebuilds a source's record from saved data, tolerating unknown roles and extra fields.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::Sour.tech: Classmethod: converts node_type/source_class/status to enums (with defaults LINK/UNVERIFIED/DISCOVERED), role via _role (unknown -> UNKNOWN), drops keys that are not dataclass fields.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_is_.text: Says whether a source counts as a list page (a place that may hold many documents), excluding pages the walk went no further than.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_is_.tech: node_type in (SITE_ROOT, PAGE, REPOSITORY) and not links_not_followed(run, node).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_rea.text: Says whether a page links to a file that GovOS actually downloaded (even if it could not read it).
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_rea.tech: True if any child edge targets a DOCUMENT node with status FETCHED or UNREADABLE.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_rel.text: Finds the official list pages that could hold a given kind of document. For example, a question paper can sit on a page of answer keys or results too.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_rel.tech: PRIMARY_OFFICIAL nodes of hub types (SITE_ROOT, PAGE, REPOSITORY) whose role is in _HUB_AFFINITY[role] (or {role}).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_rol.text: Turns a saved role name back into a role, or 'unknown' if the name is not recognised.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_unr.text: Writes a short phrase counting why places were not read, such as '3 file budget, 1 built by script'.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::_unr.tech: Counts SkipReasons in `missing` and joins '<n> <_SKIP_WORDS[reason]>' ordered by count descending.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::cove.text: Summarises a walk: what it looked at, the official list pages and their item counts, what it found by trust level and role, unreadable files, failures, unclear items, leads, what it did not get to and why, whether the walk was complete, and the honest search state for each important kind of document. It keeps 'not found' and 'never looked in the right place' clearly apart.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::cove.tech: Returns a dict: runId, authorityName, times, rootsInspected, pagesFetched, officialRepositories (url, title, role, REPOSITORY_ITEM count, listedWithoutLink, status), officialResources, officialByRole, bySourceClass, trustedSecondaryConsulted, documentsFetched/Read, unreadable, fetchFailures, pagesWithoutLinks, ambiguous (official UNKNOWN non-hubs), identityMismatches, listedWithoutLink, remainingUnexploredOfficialLinks, skippedOutOfScope, skipped (counts per coverage_key incl. item budget from frontier), leads, exhaustive (no frontier, failures, link-less pages, cancellation or skips), searchStates (role_search_state per role, default 10 roles, with notRead counts for incomplete/not searched), limits, claude.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::init.text: Creates the database table for website walks (and an index by site) if it does not exist yet.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::init.tech: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS source_discovery_runs (id PK, estate, authority_name, started_at, ended_at, job_id, node_count, run_json NOT NULL, coverage_json) and index idx_source_runs_estate on estate. Does not commit itself.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::link.text: Says whether a page was opened but the walk went no further from it, either because it was marked that way or because nothing on it was kept. Such a page is never counted as a list read in full.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::link.tech: True only for PAGE nodes with status READ that are marked skipped=LINKS_NOT_FOLLOWED or have no child edges in run.graph.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::node.text: Makes a short, stable id for a web address.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::node.tech: 'n-' + first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of url_key(url).

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::norm.text: Tidies a web address so the same page is recognised however it was written: removes the '#' part, a default port, tracking tags (like utm_source) and a trailing slash, while keeping the path's capital letters, because some servers name files that way.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::norm.tech: For http/https only (others returned stripped): lower-cases scheme and host, drops default ports, strips trailing '/' from non-root paths (empty path becomes '/'), drops query params matching _TRACKING (utm_*, fbclid, gclid, mc_cid, mc_eid, igshid, ref_src) and the fragment. Path and query case preserved.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::now_.text: The current time in standard UTC format, for timestamps.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::role.text: Says whether a source's role came only from Claude's reading.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::role.tech: True when node.role_reason starts with 'classified by Claude'.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::role.text: Decides, for one kind of document (say, question papers), what GovOS can honestly say after a walk: found and identified as this exam, found but unclear (for example only Claude thought it was that kind, or the year is not stated), found but listed without a link, not found after reading everything relevant, search incomplete, or not searched. 'Not found' is only said when every relevant list and item discovered was read; any skipped place makes it 'incomplete' or 'not searched', with a reason in words.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::role.tech: Returns (SearchState, reason). Exam-level mode when `identified` is given and the role is not authority-wide. Order: (exam level) items on relevant hubs naming the exam under another role -> FOUND_AMBIGUOUS; `unlinked` items -> FOUND_UNREADABLE; official non-hub nodes or this exam's pages: rule-identified -> FOUND_VERIFIED, Claude-only -> FOUND_AMBIGUOUS, cycle-unstated -> FOUND_AMBIGUOUS, identified PAGE nodes -> FOUND_VERIFIED (noting unreached files), thin wording -> FOUND_AMBIGUOUS; (authority level) all unreadable -> FOUND_UNREADABLE, Claude-only -> FOUND_AMBIGUOUS, else FOUND_VERIFIED. Then unsearched(): with read hubs -> SEARCH_INCOMPLETE, else NOT_SEARCHED. With nothing unsearched and read hubs -> NOT_FOUND_AFTER_DISCOVERY; otherwise NOT_SEARCHED.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::skip.text: Works out why a source was not read: the reason recorded on it, or one inferred from what happened (script-built page, failed fetch, refused address), or simply 'not opened'.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::skip.tech: Returns SkipReason(node.skipped) when valid; else maps status via _STATUS_SKIP (READ_NO_LINKS -> SCRIPT_RENDERED, FETCH_FAILED/UNREADABLE -> FETCH_FAILED, BLOCKED -> REFUSED_ADDRESS); default NOT_OPENED.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::unse.text: Lists every relevant official place the walk found but did not read for a given kind of document, with the reason: a list page not read in full, or an item that could be it and was not opened. An item whose own words clearly name another exam or year is ruled out; a list page is never ruled out by its title. Items that did not even fit in the item budget are counted too.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::unse.tech: Returns [(node or frontier dict, SkipReason)]. Considers PRIMARY_OFFICIAL, non-duplicate nodes whose status is in _UNREAD or that are links_not_followed; excludes SOCIAL/VIDEO/PORTAL and AUTHORITY_WIDE_ROLES; keeps nodes whose role is in the affinity set or that are children of relevant hubs; drops non-listings whose relation is OTHER_EXAM/NOT_THIS_EXAM/THIS_EXAM_OTHER_CYCLE. Adds frontier entries with skip ITEM_BUDGET and a matching role.

tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::url_.text: Gives one identity for a web resource that ignores http vs https and a leading 'www.', used to avoid counting the same page twice.
tools/exam_builder/source_graph.py::url_.tech: From normalize_url: host lower-cased without 'www.' + path + '?query' if any (scheme dropped).

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::DEFA.text: Where the file of human-reviewed outside websites lives: source_trust_profiles.json next to this code.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::RELA.text: The ways a source can stand to an exam authority: owned by the authority, a government site the authority links to, someone else's site the authority links to, or independent. Being linked is not the same as being owned.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::REVI.text: The allowed states of a website review: reviewed, pending, or revoked.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::SOCI.text: The social-media websites (Twitter/X, Facebook, Instagram, Telegram, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, Threads, Koo) whose pages are accounts and posts, not publications.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::SOCI.tech: frozenset of bare host names; matched (including subdomains) by is_social.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.text: A person's recorded decision about an outside website: its address, the trust level it gets (never 'official'), which authorities and which kinds of document it is trusted for, whether the review is done, when and by whom, and on what basis.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.tech: Dataclass: domain, source_class (default TRUSTED_SECONDARY), authority_coverage, permitted_roles, review_status (default PENDING), last_reviewed, reviewed_by, notes, evidence. Methods problems, matches, covers, as_dict.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.text: Turns the review record into plain data.
Says whether this review covers a given exam authority, by its name or its official site. A review that lists no authorities covers all of them.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.tech: True if authority_coverage is empty; otherwise case-insensitive membership of the authority name or any estate in authority_coverage.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.text: Says whether a website name is this reviewed site or one of its sub-sites.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.tech: Compares bare_host(host) to bare_host(domain): equal or endswith '.' + domain; False if domain is empty.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.text: Checks a review record for mistakes: the address must be a plain site name, the trust level may not be 'official', the review state must be valid, the document kinds must be known, a trusted site must name what it is trusted for, and a finished review must say when, by whom and why.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Sour.tech: Returns a list of problem strings: domain empty or containing '/' or space; source_class not in TRUSTED_SECONDARY/SECONDARY/DISCOVERY_ONLY; review_status not in REVIEW_STATUSES; unknown DocKind values in permitted_roles; TRUSTED_SECONDARY with no roles; REVIEWED without last_reviewed, reviewed_by and notes or evidence.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.text: The collection of reviewed outside websites, loaded from a file. Any review record with mistakes is refused and listed, never partly used.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.tech: Holds profiles (valid SourceTrustProfile list) and rejected ({domain, problems}). Methods add, load (classmethod), for_host.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.text: Builds the collection from a list of review records, checking each one.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.tech: Initialises profiles=[] and rejected=[]; calls add() for each given profile.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.text: Adds one review record if it has no mistakes; otherwise records why it was refused.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.tech: Accepts a SourceTrustProfile or dict (unknown keys dropped); if problems() is non-empty appends to rejected and returns False, else appends to profiles and returns True.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.text: Finds the review that applies to a website, ignoring revoked ones. If several match, the most specific one wins (a sub-site's own review over its parent site's).
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.tech: Among non-REVOKED profiles that match(host), returns the one with the longest domain string, or None.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.text: Loads the collection from the review file. If the file cannot be read, the collection is simply empty.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::Trus.tech: Classmethod: reads JSON at path (default DEFAULT_PROFILE_PATH) and builds from data['profiles']; returns an empty registry on OSError/ValueError.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::VIDE.text: The video websites GovOS recognises: YouTube and its short links.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::_hos.text: Checks whether a website name is one of a set of sites, or a sub-site of one.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::_hos.tech: host in hosts or host endswith '.' + any member.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::_off.text: Says whether a source was reached through an official link from an official page.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::_off.tech: parent_class is PRIMARY_OFFICIAL and via is not None and via.is_official.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::bare.text: Gets the plain website name from an address or host, in lower case and without 'www.'.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::bare.tech: Uses urlparse().hostname when the input contains '//', else the input itself; lower-cases, strips dots at the ends and a leading 'www.'.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::clas.text: Decides, by fixed rules a person can read, how far to trust a source, with the reason in words. Only the authority's own site, or a government site the authority itself links to, counts as official. Anything else that the authority links to stays someone else's: a person-reviewed site keeps its reviewed trust (and only for the kinds of document it was reviewed for), a social post is only a lead, and everything else is 'third-party'. Claude has no say in this.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::clas.tech: Returns (SourceClass, reason). validate_url_syntax failure -> UNVERIFIED; same estate -> PRIMARY_OFFICIAL; officially linked (parent PRIMARY_OFFICIAL via an official EdgeKind) and classify_url OFFICIAL -> PRIMARY_OFFICIAL. Then registry.for_host (default empty TrustRegistry): REVIEWED and covers(authority, estates) -> the profile's class if not TRUSTED_SECONDARY, TRUSTED_SECONDARY if role in permitted_roles, else SECONDARY. Then is_social -> DISCOVERY_ONLY; otherwise SECONDARY with a reason (officially linked / other government site / no profile). is_document is accepted but unused.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::is_s.text: Says whether an address is on a social-media site.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::is_v.text: Says whether an address is on YouTube.

tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::sour.text: Works out who runs a source's website and how it stands to the authority: on the authority's own domain, a government site the authority links to, someone else's site the authority links to, or independent.
tools/exam_builder/source_trust.py::sour.tech: Returns (owner = estate_of(host), relationship): OWNED_BY_AUTHORITY if same_estate with any estate; GOVERNMENT_HOST if officially linked and claude_cli.discovery.classify_url(url) == 'OFFICIAL'; LINKED_FROM_OFFICIAL if officially linked; else INDEPENDENT.

tools/exam_builder/sources_compat.py::sa.text: Fetches a web page but returns nothing instead of crashing if it cannot be reached. Used when trying several possible official addresses, most of which will not exist; the caller reports such an address as 'could not fetch', never as 'not official'.
tools/exam_builder/sources_compat.py::sa.tech: Wraps exam_authoring.sources.load_html(url, **kw); returns its result, or None on FetchError or any other Exception.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::PROCEDURE.text: The signal words for a part of a notice that explains how to apply, such as 'how to apply' or 'procedure for filling online application', with supporting words like 'online', 'portal', 'upload', and warning words like 'syllabus'.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::PROCEDURE.tech: CueSet with application-procedure anchors, supporting words (online, website, portal, registration, candidate, form, submit, upload) and against words (syllabus, scheme of examination). Used by procedure_regions.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::REGION_LEN.text: How much text (9000 characters) is examined after each 'how to apply' signal.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::REGION_LEN.tech: Integer 9000; region width in procedure_regions and the minimum spacing (a third of it) between kept regions.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::StageCandi.text: One application step the document appears to describe: its title, its text, how it was laid out, its order and position, and the action words (register, upload, pay...) that show it tells a candidate to do something.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::StageCandi.tech: Dataclass: title, body, structure, order (default 0), offset (default 0), action_cues (default None -> []). confidence property.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::StageCandi.text: Makes sure the list of action words starts empty rather than missing.
How sure GovOS is that this is a real step: based on how strong its layout is (explicit labels highest, bullets lowest), plus a little for each action word, up to two.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::StageCandi.tech: Base by structure (0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5) + 0.05 * min(len(action_cues), 2), capped at 1.0 and rounded to 3 decimals.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::Structure.text: The ways an authority can lay out its application steps: explicit 'Step 1 / Part-A' labels, table rows, headings, lettered lists, numbered clauses, or bullets. It is reported so a reader can judge how the steps were found.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::Structure.tech: str Enum: EXPLICIT_MARKER, TABLE_ROW, HEADING, LETTERED_LIST, NUMBERED_CLAUSE, BULLET (strongest first).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_actions_i.text: Lists the action words (register, apply, submit, upload, pay, click...) in a passage, but only if the passage actually tells someone to act. Otherwise a glossary or a heading that merely mentions 'register' would look like a step.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_actions_i.tech: Returns [] if _directing_sentences(body) is empty; otherwise the _ACTION regexes found anywhere in the lower-cased body.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_headin.text: Splits a passage into steps at headings that introduce real text. The first line is skipped because it names the whole procedure. A heading counts only if the line before it ended a sentence, and it has enough sentence text under it, so a menu is not mistaken for steps.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_headin.tech: Skips line 0; a line qualifies if _is_heading, the previous non-empty line ends in . : ; ? (or is furniture), and the next 5 lines hold >= 80 chars including a _looks_like_prose line. Needs >= 2 starts; bodies run to the next start, skipped if < 60 chars. Returns HEADING StageCandidates.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_marker.text: Splits a passage into steps wherever a given kind of label begins a line (such as 'Step 2', '(B)', '9.1' or a bullet). Each step runs to the next label. It needs at least two labels, and skips steps with a bad title or too little text.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_marker.tech: Finds pattern matches; returns [] if fewer than 2. Each candidate's body is from its match to the next (or region end); title via _clean_title(group 'title'); skipped if not _valid_title or body < 25 chars. Returns StageCandidates with offset and _actions_in(body).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_table.text: Reads steps from a table whose rows start with a number, roman numeral, letter or 'Step N', and whose next cell names the activity. At least two such rows are needed.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_by_table.tech: Rows from _TABLE_ROW (pipe-separated lines); keeps rows with >= 2 cells whose first cell fullmatches an ordinal; title = _clean_title(cells[1]), body = cells joined by spaces, offset = region.find(row). Returns [] unless >= 2 candidates.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_clean_tit.text: Tidies a title: collapses spaces, trims stray dashes and punctuation, removes brackets wrapped around the whole title, and drops a dangling unmatched bracket.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_clean_tit.tech: Collapses whitespace, strips ' -–—:.;,'; if wrapped in (...) removes them; else if paren counts differ strips trailing ')' and '('.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_directing.text: Picks out the sentences in a passage that tell someone to do something, either 'candidates must/should...' or an instruction like 'Upload...', 'Click...'.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_directing.tech: Splits on sentence punctuation or newlines; keeps parts matching _DIRECTED (candidate/applicant + modal within 80 chars) or _IMPERATIVE (line-start imperative verb, optionally after a bullet or marker).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_has_words.text: Says whether a piece of text is made of real words, at least two words of three or more letters, or one word of five or more letters, so fragments like 'Hours)]' are not taken as titles.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_has_words.tech: Counts alphabetic words longer than 2 chars; True if >= 2, or exactly 1 with length >= 5.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_is_furnit.text: Says whether a line is just page decoration, such as a page number, 'Annexure-II', 'contd.' or 'Table 3', rather than content.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_is_furnit.tech: Matches the stripped line against _FURNITURE (page N of M, bare numbers, short roman numerals, annexure/appendix/schedule labels, contd/continued, table N).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_is_headin.text: Says whether a line looks like a heading: short, capitalised (all caps or title case), no full stop at the end, not website navigation, code or page decoration, not a statement, with balanced brackets and at most ten words.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_is_headin.tech: Rejects lines outside 3..70 chars, ending in . ; ,, matching _NAVIGATION or _MARKUP, furniture or without words (_has_words), _reads_as_a_clause, unbalanced () or [], or over 10 words; requires a capital or opening bracket first and either >55% upper-case letters or _title_case(words).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_looks_lik.text: Says whether a line looks like ordinary sentence text: long, or ending with a full stop or semicolon.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_looks_lik.tech: len(line) > 70 or line ends with '.' or ';' after rstrip.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_reads_as_.text: Says whether a supposed title is really a statement, because it contains joining words like 'which', 'because', 'that' or 'strives'. A step is called something like 'Registration'; a policy banner reads as a sentence.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_reads_as_.tech: True if _CLAUSE_MARKER (a closed list of subordinators/connectives plus strive/seek) matches.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_support.text: Scores how believable a set of found steps is, to choose between parts of a document: mainly how strong the layout is, then how many steps were found (up to eight), then how many clearly describe an action.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_support.tech: 0 for no candidates; else candidates[0].confidence + 0.15 * min(n, 8)/8 + 0.25 * (share with action_cues).

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_title_cas.text: Says whether most of the significant words in a line start with a capital letter.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_title_cas.tech: Among words longer than 3 chars, True if at least 60% start upper-case; False if there are none.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_valid_tit.text: Says whether a title is a real title rather than a scrap of a sentence: real words, not page decoration, not starting in lower case or with punctuation, not a statement, and with balanced brackets.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_valid_tit.tech: False if empty, furniture, lacks words, starts lower-case or with ) ] } , . ;, or _reads_as_a_clause; else requires balanced () and [].

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_whole_ste.text: Makes sure each step ends where the document ends it. A step that ran to the edge of the search window is re-read further into the document; if its real end cannot be found it is left out rather than published cut short. A step is also cut at any higher-level heading it ran into.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::_whole_ste.tech: For steps whose body runs to a truncated region's edge, re-runs `segment` on text from the step's absolute start and takes its first body if it matches the title (>= 2 results, offset 0); else uses units.unit_end (clauses=True only for NUMBERED_CLAUSE), dropping the step on None. Then trims the body at next_structural_boundary(body, 1, clauses=False); drops bodies < 25 chars; rebuilds changed candidates with fresh _actions_in. Returns the list.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::discover_s.text: Finds the application steps a document describes, or none. It looks at up to six 'how to apply' passages, tries each layout from strongest to weakest, and believes a layout only if at least two steps, and at least half of them, tell the candidate to do something. The best-supported set is kept, completed to its real ends and numbered. Finding nothing is preferred to inventing steps.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::discover_s.tech: For each of the first 6 procedure_regions (skipping those with markup in the first 400 chars), tries _SEGMENTERS in order; the first segmenter yielding >= 2 candidates of which >= 2 and >= 50% have action_cues is that region's structure. Keeps the region with the highest _support, sorts by offset, applies _whole_steps, then sets order 1..n. Returns [] if none.

tools/exam_builder/stages.py::procedure_.text: Finds the parts of a document that explain how to apply, starting exactly where the document says so, best first. A signal that stands on its own line as a heading scores higher, and regions too close to a better one are dropped.
tools/exam_builder/stages.py::procedure_.tech: For every PROCEDURE anchor match takes text[m.start(): +REGION_LENGTH], scores it with PROCEDURE.score (skips <= 0), adds 1.5 when the anchor starts its line; sorts by score desc then offset, and keeps regions whose start is at least REGION_LENGTH//3 from an already kept one. Returns [(offset, region)].

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_clause_.text: Joins each numbered clause of a syllabus back into one piece of text, however many lines the PDF broke it across, so titles whose colon fell on the next line stay whole.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_clause_.tech: Over lines start..end, skipping blanks and _FURNITURE: a _CLAUSE match starts a new block (number, first text); other lines append to the current block. Returns [(number, joined text, line index)].

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_clean_h.text: Removes a leading clause number or list marker from a syllabus heading and trims stray punctuation.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_clean_h.tech: Strips a leading '13.10.' style number, '(a)' or 'A.' marker via regex, then strips ' :.'.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_covers.text: Checks whether a quote covers a whole syllabus entry (ignoring spacing and page numbers printed inside it).
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_covers.tech: True if ev is not None and normalised ev.span equals normalised span, or _only_page_numbers_between(ev.span, span).
