tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_depth.text: Counts how many levels deep a syllabus tree goes.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_depth.tech: 0 for an empty list; else 1 + the maximum _depth of the nodes' children.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_depth_o.text: Counts the levels in a clause number: '13.11.1' has three.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_ends_sy.text: Says whether a line marks the end of a syllabus: a heading for something else in the notice (how to apply, fees, important dates, instructions, centres...), an annexure heading, or (only if the syllabus itself opened with a section heading) the next section heading. A line that mentions the syllabus never ends it.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_ends_sy.tech: False if _SYLLABUS_HEADING matches; True if _NAMED_SECTION or _ANNEXURE_HEADING matches; otherwise opened_in_section and _SECTION_HEADING matches.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_entry_c.text: Counts all nodes in a set of syllabus trees.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_entry_c.tech: Sum over node.walk() for each node (includes the node itself and descendants).

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_entry_e.text: Finds the quote that proves a syllabus entry: the whole entry as printed across all its lines; if it ran over a page, the printed text including the page number; and if neither can be found, just its first line (the caller then marks it for review).
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_entry_e.tech: Tries pattern._evidence(entry); else locates the normalised first line and the entry's last 40 chars in the flattened text and, if the span between passes _only_page_numbers_between, evidences that span; falls back to _evidence(first_line). May return None.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_in_anne.text: Says whether a line is one entry in a list of annexures (a table of contents), such as 'Annexure-II Scheme and Syllabus' between other annexure lines.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_in_anne.tech: True if the line matches _ANNEXURE_REFERENCE and the nearest non-blank line above or below also matches it.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_level_l.text: Names the level of a syllabus node using the authority's own word if its heading has one ('Paper', 'Section', 'Unit'...), otherwise by depth: Subject, Topic, Subtopic, Detail.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_level_l.tech: Returns the title-cased label from _LEVEL_HEADING if matched; else ['Subject','Topic','Subtopic','Detail'][relative_depth clamped to 0..3].

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_make_id.text: Gives every syllabus node an id no other node has. When papers restart their numbering, the same id can repeat; the first keeps its id and later repeats are qualified by their parent's id (with a counter if needed).
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_make_id.tech: Depth-first visit; a seen id becomes '<parent_id>-<last segment of id>' (or unchanged base for roots), then '-2', '-3'... until unique. Mutates node ids in place.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_only_pa.text: Checks whether a printed piece of text is exactly an entry's own words in order, with nothing added except bare page numbers (which appear when an entry runs across a page).
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_only_pa.tech: Walks whitespace-normalised words of `printed`, matching `entry` words in order and allowing only 1-3 digit tokens extra; True if all entry words were matched.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_cl.text: Reads a syllabus whose structure is its own clause numbering: '13.11.1.1' sits under '13.11.1', which sits under '13.11'. Each entry gets its name, its description, the paper or section it belongs to, and a quote proving it; an entry whose quote does not cover it is marked for review. A clause that is a long sentence (a rule about the syllabus) is kept as a note on the entry above, not as an entry.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_cl.tech: Iterates _clause_blocks; depth = _depth_of(number) relative to the first clause's depth; _split_title; statement titles over 8 words are appended to the parent's note. Node id prefix-slug(number), level_label via _level_label, evidence via _entry_evidence (VERIFIED if _covers else NEEDS_REVIEW; missing evidence adds a note). A stack places nodes under the nearest shallower clause; scope via _scope_of. Returns root SyllabusNodes.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_he.text: Reads a syllabus written as headings (Part, Section, Paper, Unit...) with bullet points under them. Each bullet is kept whole as one topic of the heading above it, even when it wraps over lines. A heading must carry a number or be clearly marked, so the wrapped end of a bullet is not mistaken for one. Notes are attached to the current heading, and each item gets a quote.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_he.tech: Ranks labels (part 0, section 1, paper 2, unit/module/group 3, subject 4, topic 5) for nesting. Bullets (_BULLET) accumulate in `pending` (wrapped lines appended) and flush_bullet creates a 'Topic' child of the stack top with _split_title, _entry_evidence and VERIFIED/NEEDS_REVIEW via _covers. Headings: _LEVEL_HEADING with an ordinal or _is_marked, < 110 chars, not a statement; title 'Label ORD — rest'; evidence of the line (VERIFIED or NEEDS_REVIEW); placed by rank with _scope_of. _NOTE_LINE lines append to the stack top's note; furniture skipped. Returns roots.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_ou.text: Reads the most common syllabus layout: headings with numbered lists that restart at '1.' under each heading. Headings are recognised by what they are (a labelled paper or section, a Roman-numbered heading, or a short title line followed by a list or another heading) and ranked stage, then paper, then section, then topic. A number that does not continue its list is treated as part of the topic before it, a bracketed line under a heading is its note, and a heading with nothing under it is dropped (unless it is a paper).
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_read_ou.tech: Pre-collects non-blank, non-furniture, non-page-number lines, merging wrapped bracketed notes. Inner helpers: next_kind (first/item/heading/text/end lookahead), _short_title, _labelled (paper/section/part/unit/module with ordinal), title_line, evidence_for, close_entry (final title/note via _split_title, _entry_evidence, VERIFIED only if single-line or _covers), attach (rank-based stack, _scope_of). An _OUTLINE_ITEM whose number equals the parent's expected next number opens a Topic (rank 3). Headings (labelled: Paper rank 1, others 2; Roman: Subject rank 2; title line: Stage rank 0 if stage words and followed by a heading, else Subject rank 1) take up to 3 wrapped lines plus bracketed notes. Other lines extend the open entry. prune() drops childless nodes except Topic/Paper and renumbers order.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_region_.text: Finds where a syllabus stops: at a line that ends it, or at another syllabus heading numbered at the same or a higher level (so 'Syllabus (Tier-I)' does not swallow 'Syllabus (Tier-II)').
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_region_.tech: From start, returns the index of the first non-blank line where _ends_syllabus is true, or (when opening_depth > 0) a _SYLLABUS_HEADING line whose clause number depth <= opening_depth; else len(cur.lines).

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_scope_o.text: Works out which paper, stage or section a syllabus heading ties its topics to. A heading like 'Part A of Section-I of Paper-I' names all three, and all are kept; a heading that names none simply passes on its parent's.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_scope_o.tech: Starts from inherited.refs and appends ScopeRef(kind, slug, label) for each 'paper/tier/phase/stage/part/section <ordinal>' found in the title (label like 'Paper-I'), skipping duplicates. Returns a new Scope.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_split_t.text: Splits a syllabus entry into its name and its description, at a colon if there is one, else at a dash, exactly where the authority punctuated it. If there is neither, the whole line stays the name.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_split_t.tech: Uses _TITLED (title 3-90 chars before ':'), else a dash pattern (title 3-70 chars, then an en/em dash or hyphen followed by a space); returns (title stripped of ' .;,:', body) or (cleaned text, '').

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_syllabu.text: Finds every stretch of a notice that is a syllabus, with the heading that opens it. A notice may have several. It ignores a table-of-contents line that only names the syllabus, sentences that merely mention it, and, under a 'Scheme and Syllabus' heading, starts at the inner 'SYLLABUS' heading so the scheme table is not read as topics.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::_syllabu.tech: Scans cursor lines <= 120 chars matching _SYLLABUS_HEADING, not _in_annexure_list, that are marked, clause-numbered or short capitalised titles (<= 8 words), not statements (unless clause-numbered) and <= 12 words; end via _region_end (with the clause depth and section flag); keeps regions longer than 2 lines. Then drops regions nested in another (unless the outer is a 'scheme' heading and the inner a bare SYLLABUS heading) and drops a 'scheme' region that contains such an inner one. Returns [(start, end, heading)].

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::describe.text: Summarises a read syllabus with counts: top-level parts, total nodes, end topics, how deep it goes, which level names were used, how many have quotes, how many are verified or need review, and how many are tied to a paper or stage.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::describe.tech: Returns {roots, nodes, leaves, maxDepth (syllabus.max_depth()), levelLabels (syllabus.level_labels()), withEvidence, states (count per status), scoped (nodes with scope refs)}.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::extract_.text: Reads the syllabus a document publishes, for the exam asked about and no other. For each syllabus region it tries the three readings (numbered clauses, headings with bullets, headings with restarting numbered lists) and keeps the one that recovers the most structure, never mixing them. Each region becomes a top node with its heading's quote. Ids are made unique, and a source note is added. A document with no syllabus gives an empty result.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::extract_.tech: Returns schema.Syllabus; empty if no text or exam_id, or no _syllabus_regions. Per region: prefix 'syl-<slug>', scope from the heading; children = clause reading if its _entry_count >= the bullet reading's, else bullets; replaced by _read_outline when deeper and >= 90% of the entry count. Root SyllabusNode(level 'Syllabus') VERIFIED if the heading has verbatim _evidence else NEEDS_REVIEW. Then _make_ids_unique and source_note (Fact.verified with the first root's evidence, else Fact.needs_review). exam_id and cycle are only used as a guard; gating is may_supply_syllabus's job.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::may_supp.text: Decides whether a document's syllabus may be used for this exam and this year. It uses the same check as the exam-pattern reader, so a syllabus for another exam or a previous year contributes nothing.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus.py::may_supp.tech: Delegates to pattern.may_supply_pattern(text, target); returns (bool, reason).

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::ID.text: The score (0.85) two topics must reach to be treated as the same topic. Below it, nothing is merged.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::ID.tech: Float 0.85 used by merge_syllabus and unsupported_topics.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::No.text: The merge's decision about one topic (unchanged, confirmed, conflicting, replaced, or added), with its reasons, its per-field decisions, its match score and any old wording it replaces.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::No.tech: Plain class: action (MergeAction), title, topic_id, fields (FieldDecision list), reason, identity, superseded. field(name) lookup.
Stores the given action, title, topic_id, fields (default []), reason, identity and superseded.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::No.text: Finds this decision's ruling on one named field, if any.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::No.tech: First FieldDecision whose .field equals name, else None.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.text: The full list of topic decisions from one syllabus merge, with helpers to filter and count them.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.tech: Holds decisions (list of NodeDecision); methods of, summary, fields_of.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.text: Lists every field decision with a given outcome, together with the topic it belongs to.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.tech: [(decision, field_decision)] for field decisions whose outcome is the given FieldOutcome.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.text: Lists the decisions of one kind, for example all added topics.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::Sy.tech: Decisions whose action is the given MergeAction.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::_w.text: Gets the distinctive words of a topic title, ignoring short words and common syllabus words like 'general', 'paper' or 'topics'.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::_w.tech: Lower-cases, splits on non-alphanumerics, keeps words longer than 2 chars not in _GENERIC. Returns a set.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::me.text: Works out how a syllabus read from a document would fold into the topics a record already holds, without changing anything. Each existing topic is matched to its best document entry: no confident match leaves it unchanged; two equally good matches, or one entry that is the best match of several record topics, are a conflict; same wording confirms it; different wording is a conflict unless the document says it revises the syllabus, in which case the new wording replaces the old and the old is kept as superseded. Document entries with no match (and no sub-entries) are reported as new topics.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::me.tech: existing: list of SyllabusTopic dicts (topicName, id); incoming: Syllabus. First scores every row against all titled nodes with topic_identity and counts how many confident rows claim each node. Then per row: best < IDENTITY_THRESHOLD -> UNCHANGED; runner-up >= threshold -> CONFLICTED; a node claimed by more than one row -> CONFLICTED (node marked used); otherwise marks the match used with a topicName KEPT FieldDecision; differing _words with revises(document, revision_span) -> SUPERSEDED; differing without revision -> CONFLICTED with an UNDER_REVIEW field; same words -> CONFIRMED. Unused leaf nodes -> ADDED. Returns SyllabusMergeReport; writes nothing.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::re.text: Decides whether a document says it changes an earlier syllabus: either it is a corrigendum, or the given passage both uses revising words (amended, revised, in supersession of, read as...) and mentions the syllabus, topics or papers. Being newer is not the same as revising.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::re.tech: True if document.kind is SourceKind.CORRIGENDUM; otherwise requires _REVISION_WORDS in text_span and a syllab/curricul/topic/paper word in the same span.

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::to.text: Scores how sure GovOS is that a topic in the existing record and a topic read from the document are the same topic, using their distinctive words as printed. 'Number Systems' and 'Systems: Number' match; 'Number Systems' and 'Number Series' do not just because they share 'number', and a plural and its singular are left for a person.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::to.tech: Returns 0.0 if either _words set is empty or they share nothing; 1.0 if equal; if one is a subset of the other, 0.9 when >= 2 words are shared else 0.55; otherwise round(0.8 * shared / max size, 3). No stemming: 'Number Systems' vs 'Number System' scores 0.4, below IDENTITY_THRESHOLD (0.85).

tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::un.text: Lists the topics a record holds that the published syllabus does not contain. This is not a deletion or an error, just a list for a person to check, and it lets the app say which topics are the authority's own words and which are GovOS's reading.
tools/exam_builder/syllabus_merge.py::un.tech: Returns ids (or titles when no id) of existing rows whose best topic_identity against any titled node is below IDENTITY_THRESHOLD.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Column.text: One column of a rebuilt table: what kind it is, the header words it was named by, and its position.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::ColumnKind.text: The kinds of column GovOS recognises in a notice's table, from the words in its header: serial number, post name, department, group, pay, age, vacancies, qualification, and, for exam-scheme tables, stage, paper, section, subject, number of questions, marks, duration, language and qualifying marks.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::ColumnKind.tech: str Enum: SERIAL, NAME, DEPARTMENT, CLASSIFICATION, PAY, AGE, VACANCY, QUALIFICATION, STAGE, PAPER, SECTION, SUBJECT, QUESTIONS, MARKS, DURATION, LANGUAGE, QUALIFYING_MARKS, OTHER.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Row.text: One rebuilt table row: its values by column, the original text it came from (for quoting), its row number, and whether it could be rebuilt. A row that could not be matched to the columns is kept, unassigned, with a note.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Row.tech: Dataclass: cells {ColumnKind: str}, span, ordinal, reconstructed (default True), note, raw_cells.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Table.text: One table rebuilt from a PDF: its columns, rows, the heading above it, any value that heading states for all rows (such as a pay level), and its 'TOTAL' line if printed.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Table.tech: Dataclass: columns, rows, heading, heading_values, total_line. kinds property.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::Table.kind.text: Lists the kinds of the table's columns, in order.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_assign.text: Places a row's cells into the table's columns, or says it cannot. First by position when the counts match (unless a recognisable value like a vacancy number or age sits in the wrong column); then by placing the recognisable values and giving the leftover text to the one remaining column; then by cutting a run-together row at its recognisable values. It never splits text between columns on a guess.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_assign.tech: Returns (assigned {ColumnKind: str}, ok, note). Ignores SERIAL columns. Positional assignment is accepted unless a typed column's shape fails while another cell matches that shape, or a _SHAPE_REQUIRED column (VACANCY, AGE) holds a non-matching value. Second attempt: every typed column matched to some cell and exactly one untyped column left gets the rest. Third: _split_on_values. Otherwise ({}, False, explanatory note).

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_columns_i.text: Reads a header line and lists the columns it names, in left-to-right order, one per kind. Words that are part of a longer heading phrase (like 'as specified in the Service Rules of the department') do not create extra columns.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_columns_i.tech: For each _HEADER_CUES (kind, regex) takes the first match that does not overlap an earlier one and is not preceded within 30 chars by _INSIDE_A_PHRASE; sorts by position and keeps the first column per kind. Returns [Column(kind, label, order)].

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_heading_v.text: Picks out a value stated in the heading above a table that applies to every row, currently a pay level, when the table has no pay column of its own.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_heading_v.tech: For each _HEADING_VALUE (PAY: 'pay level N...' up to 40 more chars), returns {kind: matched text} when the kind is not among the declared columns.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_introduce.text: Checks whether the lines just above a numbered list say that it lists posts or services (for example 'the following posts').
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_introduce.tech: Joins up to 8 non-blank lines above first_item (in document order) and searches _LISTS_POSTS (posts/services/cadres/designations near below/following/as under/namely/as follows).

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_is_next_s.text: Checks whether one numbered heading directly follows another at the same level, like '2.4' after '2.3'.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_is_next_s.tech: Both must match _SECTION_NUMBER (dotted numbers with at least two parts); same length, same parent parts, and last part = previous + 1.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_next_nonb.text: Finds the next line that is not empty.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_next_nonb.tech: Returns (index, stripped line) of the first non-blank line from `index`, or (len(lines), '').

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_row_block.text: Splits the lines after a table header into rows, at the numbers that start each row, but only when the number continues the sequence (1, 2, 3...), so a count inside a cell does not start a new row. It stops at the next section heading, at a repeat of the header, or at the TOTAL line, and skips page decoration.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_row_block.tech: Returns ([(ordinal, lines)], stop index). Inner ordinal_value parses digits or roman numerals; continues_the_sequence requires the first ordinal <= 2 and later ones to be previous + 1. Stops at _SECTION_HEADING, a line equal to a header line (popping trailing <= 4-char fragments), or _TOTAL_LINE once a row has started; skips _FURNITURE; _ORDINAL or _LEADING_ORDINAL lines continuing the sequence open rows (a leading ordinal's rest of line becomes the first line). The returned index is where collection stopped (len(lines) if it ran to the end).

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_split_on_.text: Cuts a row whose cells ran together at the values that can be recognised on sight (pay, age, marks...), giving the text between them to the columns in header order. If two text columns have to share one stretch of text, the row is flagged for review. A row that yields fewer than two values is not kept.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_split_on_.tech: Finds each typed column's shape in order (cursor advances); for each cut assigns the preceding text to the single preceding column, or splits name + trailing whole number when the two preceding columns are an untyped one then VACANCY/QUESTIONS, or gives it to the first and sets a review note. The tail goes to the next remaining column. Returns ({}, '') if no typed columns/cuts or fewer than 2 non-empty values.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_starts_ro.text: Says whether a line starts a table row: a bare number or roman numeral on its own, or a number followed by the row's first words.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::_starts_ro.tech: True if the stripped line matches _ORDINAL or _LEADING_ORDINAL.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::blocks_con.text: Decides whether rows starting at a line belong to the table above. A bare row number on its own line always does. A number followed by row text does too if its section heading is the next numbered sibling of the previous one (such as '2.4' after '2.3').
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::blocks_con.tech: True if lines[index] matches _ORDINAL; else True if it matches _LEADING_ORDINAL and _is_next_sibling(heading, previous).

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::find_heade.text: Finds the first table header in a list of lines and the columns it names. Because headers wrap over several lines, lines are joined until at least two column names appear together. Section headings, sentences, dated or government-order references are not taken as headers, a header may keep growing with short fragments, and it must be followed by a first row.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::find_heade.tech: For each start line (skipping _SECTION_HEADING/_PROSE_LINE), joins up to `lookahead` (6) lines (resetting on headings/prose), tracking the join with the most (>= 2) columns, stopping at an ordinal. Rejects candidates with _PROSE_IN_HEADER; extends with short fragments (<= 40 chars, up to 8 lines) until a row start, keeping the grown columns if not fewer; requires the next non-blank line to _starts_row. Returns (last header line index, columns) or None.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::reconstruc.text: Rebuilds every table in a PDF's flattened text, as far as its structure allows. It finds a header, splits the rows, groups each row's lines into cells and assigns them to columns; a row that cannot be assigned is kept but marked. When a document states one header and then several sections under it, each section becomes its own table carrying the value its heading states.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::reconstruc.tech: Loop until lines or max_tables (40) run out: optional _SECTION_HEADING line as heading; if the next line starts a row, columns exist and blocks_continue, reuses the previous columns; otherwise find_header (stops if None), records header_text for repeat detection and uses the 6 lines above as heading when none. Builds Table with _heading_values, gets _row_blocks, records a TOTAL line, and for each block: split_cells, _assign, Row(span <= 900 chars, reconstructed, note, raw_cells). Advances the cursor to the stop index. Returns the tables.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::reconstruc.text: Finds numbered lists of posts in a document, such as '(i) Assistant Section Officer'. A list counts only if it has at least three items that look like names and the text above says it lists posts. If an item contains a recognisable value like a group or pay level, that value becomes its own column and the rest is the name.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::reconstruc.tech: Collects runs of _LIST_ITEM lines; flush() keeps a run if it has >= 3 items, _introduces_posts is true, and >= 3 items pass names_a_thing (capitalised, >= 4 chars, not ending in punctuation or 'or'/'and'). Each row: first _VALUE_SHAPES match except VACANCY becomes that kind's cell, the text before it the NAME; span = raw line. Columns SERIAL, NAME, plus CLASSIFICATION 'inline' if any typed value was found. Returns up to max_lists (12) Tables.

tools/exam_builder/tables.py::split_cell.text: Groups a row's lines into cells using only how the PDF wrapped them: a cell continues while its line ended with a trailing space, while a bracket is still open, or when the next line starts with an opening bracket.
tools/exam_builder/tables.py::split_cell.tech: Iterates non-blank lines, appending to the current cell; ends the cell unless the raw line had trailing whitespace, brackets ()/[] in the cell are unbalanced, or the next non-blank line starts with '('. Returns non-empty joined cells.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::CLAUSE_NUMB.text: A pattern for the start of a numbered clause, such as '10.3 If the...', which means the previous clause has ended.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::CLAUSE_NUMB.tech: Regex: 1-2 digits '.' 1-2 digits (optional third part) followed by whitespace and a capital, bracket or quote, at start or after whitespace.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completenes.text: The answer to 'is this quoted text a whole sentence or clause of its document?': yes, no (it was cut), or cannot tell, plus the reason.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completenes.tech: Frozen dataclass with complete: bool | None (True whole, False demonstrably cut, None uncheckable because the value is not verbatim in the document) and reason: str. Returned by check_value.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completenes.text: A yes/no shortcut that is true only when the text was definitely cut off.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completenes.tech: Property: returns self.complete is False (None, the uncheckable case, is not 'cut').

tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completion.text: The result of trying to repair a cut-off quotation from its source: the full text if it could be found, and what happened (unchanged, extended, trimmed, not checkable, or unresolved).
tools/exam_builder/units.py::Completion.tech: Frozen dataclass: text (the whole unit as printed, or None), kind ('unchanged' | 'extended' | 'ended' | 'unchecked' | 'unresolved') and reason. Returned by complete_from_source.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::SIGNATURE.text: A pattern for the 'Sd/-' signature mark that closes an order or notice; anything after it is the signatory, not the last clause.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::SIGNATURE.tech: Compiled case-insensitive regex for 'Sd /' (optional '-') at start or after whitespace.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::STRUCTURAL_.text: A pattern for a higher-level heading in a notice, such as 'PARA-9', 'SECTION 2', 'ANNEXURE-VI', written in capitals. When one starts, every quote above it has ended.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::STRUCTURAL_.tech: Compiled regex: (PARA|SECTION|CHAPTER|PART|ANNEXURE|ANNEXE|APPENDIX) + optional separator + 1-2 digits or roman numerals, at start or after whitespace; case-sensitive. Used by next_structural_boundary and sentence_start.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::UNIT_FIELDS.text: The candidate-facing facts whose values quote whole pieces of a document: qualification, how to apply, the exam-day checklist, FAQs and the syllabus.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_heading_en.text: Finds where a heading's own capitalised title ends, such as the end of 'PARA-5 EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATIONS:'.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_heading_en.tech: m.end() plus the length of a following run of upper-case words (allowing & / , ( ) -) and an optional trailing separator; m.end() if none.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_figure.text: Decides whether something shaped like a clause number (such as '86.3') is really a measurement inside a sentence, because it follows words like 'than' or 'minimum', or is followed by a unit like 'Cms', 'years' or '%'.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_figure.tech: True if the word before the match (lower-cased, stripped of '(' ',') is in _BEFORE_FIGURE, or _UNIT_AFTER matches right after the number.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_heading.text: Checks that a heading-like word really starts something new: the text before it ends a sentence or stands alone, rather than ending in a lower-case word or a comma (which would make it a reference inside a sentence).
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_heading.tech: True if nothing precedes `at`, or the last non-space char before it is not lower-case and not one of , ; ( or an opening quote.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_sentenc.text: Decides whether a full stop (or ? or !) really ends a sentence, rather than belonging to an abbreviation like 'Rs.' or 'G.O.Ms.No.', a serial number like '5.', or an initial; and it must be followed by something that can start a new sentence.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_is_sentenc.tech: '?' and '!' are always ends. For '.', False if the preceding word is in _ABBREVIATIONS (with or without trailing dots), contains an inner dot, or is 1-3 digits or one letter; otherwise True only if _NEXT_OPENS matches after it (end of text, capital, digit, bracket, quote, list marker or dash).

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_locate.text: Finds where a piece of text is printed in a document, first exactly and then ignoring upper/lower case.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_locate.tech: _locate(value_flat, doc_flat) -> int: str.find of the value in the already whitespace-normalised document; if not found, a case-insensitive find; -1 when absent.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_markup_as_.text: When the source is a web page, removes its HTML tags but leaves a hidden marker wherever a heading, paragraph, table cell or list item ended, so later checks still know where one block of text stopped.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_markup_as_.tech: If the text contains no tag, returns it unchanged. Otherwise replaces block-level tags (h1-h6, p, div, li, ul, ol, td, th, tr, table, br, section, article, dd, dt) with ' _BLOCK ' (a private-use character) and then strips all remaining tags.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_syllabus_n.text: Walks a syllabus tree (subjects, papers, topics nested inside each other) and returns every entry in it as one flat list.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_syllabus_n.tech: Depth-first pre-order walk over a list of root dicts, following each node's 'children' list; returns all dict nodes. A non-list tree yields []; non-dict children are ignored.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_within.text: Checks whether a short piece of text (such as a syllabus entry's title) really appears inside the longer quotation that is supposed to back it up. It tolerates a stray page number printed in the middle of the words and small differences in trailing punctuation.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_within.tech: _within(value, quoted) -> bool. Normalises whitespace (normalise_ws), strips ' .;,:' from the value; empty or plain substring -> True. Otherwise compares word lists with trailing '.,;:' removed, scanning for a run starting at want[0] where intervening tokens that are 1-3 digit numbers (page numbers) are skipped; any other mismatching token breaks that attempt. True if all wanted words are matched in order.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::_word_befor.text: Gets the word that ends just before a given position, in lower case and without brackets or quotes around it.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::_word_befor.tech: Scans back from `stop` to the previous whitespace; returns flat[i:stop] stripped of opening brackets/quotes and lower-cased.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::check_value.text: Decides whether a quotation GovOS stored is a complete unit of its official document — a whole sentence, clause or list item — rather than a fragment cut off at an arbitrary length. It says whether it is whole, cut, or cannot be checked (because the words are not printed exactly in the document), and why. It never fills in missing words.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::check_value.tech: check_value(value, document_text) -> Completeness. Both sides are whitespace-normalised (document also via _markup_as_boundaries). Order: empty -> False; not found by _locate -> False if it ends in '…', else None; begins or ends inside a word -> False; next_structural_boundary(clauses=False) inside the value -> False (runs past a heading); terminal punctuation that _is_sentence_end confirms -> True; then True if the document ends, a block marker follows, nothing but whitespace precedes the next structural boundary, or a list marker ((i), (a), 1), bullet) follows; else False, distinguishing 'stops mid-sentence' (ends in :;, or no closing punctuation) from 'stops before the unit ends'.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::complete_fr.text: Repairs a stored quotation that was cut off at a character count by reading the rest of the same sentence or clause from the original document. It only accepts the result if the document's own words continue the stored words exactly (or if the stored words ran past a heading and need trimming). If anything is uncertain it leaves the value as it was and reports it as unresolved, so a person can review it; it never writes new words.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::complete_fr.tech: complete_from_source(value, document_text, unit) with unit 'sentence' or 'clause' (anything else raises ValueError). Runs check_value first: complete -> 'unchanged'; uncheckable and not ending in '…' -> 'unchecked'. Otherwise locates the value minus a trailing ellipsis; not found or starting mid-word -> 'unresolved'. The end is sentence_end(doc, at, next_structural_boundary) for 'sentence', or the next boundary (trailing whitespace trimmed) for 'clause'. Returns 'extended' when the document unit starts with the stored words, 'ended' when the stored words start with the unit and a heading boundary lies inside them, else 'unresolved' (including when the unit equals the stored words yet the check found them cut).

tools/exam_builder/units.py::next_struct.text: Finds where the next structural break is after a position: a higher-level heading, a signature mark, or (optionally) a new numbered clause that is not just a measurement. If there is none, it is the end of the text.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::next_struct.tech: Collects the first STRUCTURAL_HEADING or SIGNATURE match from `start` that is followed by a capitalised title (headings only) or passes _is_heading; and, if clauses=True, the first CLAUSE_NUMBER that is not _is_figure. Returns the minimum of those and len(flat).

tools/exam_builder/units.py::sentence_en.text: Finds where the sentence starting at a position ends, searching only up to an optional limit. If no real sentence end appears in time, it says so (nothing), because the text was cut or never ended in a sentence.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::sentence_en.tech: Iterates _TERMINAL matches in [start, limit or len) and returns m.end() for the first where _is_sentence_end is true; None otherwise.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::sentence_st.text: Finds where the sentence containing a position begins: just after the nearest previous sentence end, numbered clause, or heading (and its capitalised title), or the start of the text.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::sentence_st.tech: Takes the last _TERMINAL sentence end before pos, then advances past any STRUCTURAL_HEADING (to _heading_end) or non-figure CLAUSE_NUMBER between it and pos; skips leading whitespace. Returns the index.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::syllabus_pr.text: Explains why a machine-read syllabus is not safe to publish, or returns nothing if it is fine. For each verified entry it checks that the entry's title and note are actually inside the official words it quotes, and that the quotation was not cut off mid-word or marked with '…'.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::syllabus_pr.tech: syllabus_problems(tree, document_text) -> list[str]. Flattens the document with _markup_as_boundaries + normalise_ws. For every VERIFIED node: title and note must pass _within against provenance.excerptText; a quotation ending in '…' is reported as cut; otherwise the quotation is located with _locate and reported if the next document character is alphanumeric while the quotation ends in an alphanumeric (stops inside a word). Nodes with another status are skipped.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::unit_end.text: Finds where a quoted piece of a document that begins at a position ends: the last sentence end before the next structural break (or before a known end the caller gives). For a section that contains its own numbered clauses, only a heading, annexure or signature ends it. If there is no sentence end at all before that break, it says the piece is incomplete (nothing), so nothing gets filled in.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::unit_end.tech: bound = next_structural_boundary(flat, start+1, clauses=clauses), capped by `stop`; repeatedly calls sentence_end from the last end up to bound and returns the last end found, or None.

tools/exam_builder/units.py::units_of.text: Lists every piece of quoted official text that one exam field shows to candidates, each with a short label so a reviewer knows which item it is. It covers qualifications, how-to-apply steps, exam-day checklist items, FAQ answers and syllabus entries. It only collects the text; it never changes it.
tools/exam_builder/units.py::units_of.tech: units_of(field_name, value) -> list[(label, text)]. 'qualification': value['text'] or the value itself if a string; 'howToApply': the string itself and/or each list step's description (label 'step i (title[:40])'); 'examDayChecklist': each item's title and description; 'syllabus': the provenance.excerptText of every node (via _syllabus_nodes) whose status is VERIFIED (default) and whose excerpt is non-empty; 'faqs': each answer labelled by officialClause[:30]. Blank texts are skipped; unknown field names return [].

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.text: Works out, from a vacancy table's own contents, which column is the serial number, which holds the post names, which holds a short zone or region label, which columns are counts and which are totals.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.tech: _columns(reading) -> (serial, name, zone, counts, totals) column indexes. Uses _numeric_columns; among the other columns, serial is the first whose non-shared, non-empty cells all parse as integers; name is the remaining column with the longest average cell text; zone is the first other remaining column whose longest cell is at most 12 characters; totals are numeric columns whose header _is_total_column; counts are the remaining numeric columns. Any may be None/empty.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.text: Reads a table cell as a whole number if it is only digits (spaces allowed), otherwise gives nothing.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.tech: Removes all whitespace; returns int(digits) if the remainder is all digits, else None (empty input gives None).

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.text: Asks whether two post names refer to the same post, using the same name-matching rule GovOS's eligibility reader uses.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.tech: Thin wrapper that lazily imports and calls eligibility._names_agree(a, b), so this module shares one name-matching definition.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.text: Checks whether a table mentions any of the exam's posts at all, so that only relevant tables get a 'why it was refused' note.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.tech: True if any non-empty cell among the first three cells of any row _names_agree with any post's postName.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.text: Picks out the distinctive words of a post name (three letters or more), dropping common words like 'officer', 'assistant' or 'grade' that appear in many post names and so identify nothing.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::_.tech: Returns the set of lower-case [a-z]{3,} tokens of the name minus _GENERIC_WORDS; empty name gives an empty set.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::a.text: Takes one official vacancy table and ties each of its rows to one post in GovOS's record of the exam, so candidates can see the category-wise break-up for each post. It only does this if the whole table adds up to its own printed totals, every row matches exactly one post (by name, or else by serial number plus total plus a shared word), and each post's total equals the vacancy count already on record. If any check fails, nothing is attached and the reason is returned.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::a.tech: attach(reading: TableReading, posts) -> (breakup dict, '') or (None, reason). Refuses unverified readings and tables without a name column or count columns. Groups rows into post groups (a new group whenever the name cell is not row-spanned/shared). Group total comes from a row-spanning total column, else the sum of the last total column, else the sum of all count cells (parse_count). Each group joins by _names_agree when exactly one post matches, else by postCode == serial, vacancies == printed total and a shared _words term; refuses no/multiple matches, two groups on one post, or a vacancy mismatch. Output: columns, pages, rows (postId, postCode, printedName, zone, counts with fresh/carriedForward/asPrinted, rowTotal, page, joinedBy; postTotal on each group's last row), tableTotal, checks, postsCovered. The final coverage check (used < posts and used < groups) cannot trigger because each group adds exactly one post.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::b.text: Reads every ruled table in one official PDF and returns the ones that are verified vacancy break-ups of the exam's posts, plus a note for each table that named the posts but could not be safely attached.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::b.tech: breakups_in(pdf_source, posts) -> (found, refused). read_ruled_tables -> logical_tables -> read_table per group (empty readings skipped) -> attach. A refusal is recorded as 'pages [..]: reason' only when _names_any says the table names one of the posts, so unrelated tables add no noise.

tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::l.text: Joins table pieces that continue across pages: if a table on the next page has exactly the same column headings, it is treated as the same table carried over.
tools/exam_builder/vacancy_breakup.py::l.tech: logical_tables(tables: list[RuledTable]) -> list[list[RuledTable]]. A table is appended to the previous group when its page is the last table's page + 1 and its header paths (header_paths(...)[1], normalised by _key) equal those of the group's first table; otherwise it starts a new group.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: From a line of cut-off marks like '92.66 (General) 89.34 (EWS)', cuts out the small piece around the category being asked about, so the mark beside that category is what gets checked.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: Case-insensitive regex for up to ~25 characters ending with the category token (optionally in parentheses); falls back to a bare match of the category; returns excerpt from 8 characters before the match start to its end, stripped. Returns '' when excerpt or category is empty or the category is not found.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns one cut-off mark (for one category and stage, such as the General category's Prelims cut-off) into a checkable claim. Because a cut-off sheet lists many categories' marks on one line, it narrows the supporting text to the part next to the claimed category so the checker looks at the right number.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_cutoff(entry, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, tier='prelim', source_text='') -> Claim. value = tier2Cutoff if tier == 'mains' else tier1Cutoff; field 'cutoff:<tier>:<category>'; cycle = entry year; source_text defaults to documentTitle + excerpt; evidence_span = _focus_on_category(excerpt, category) or the excerpt or the title; requires_value when the mark is not None.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns one exam-day instruction (such as what to bring or when to report) into a checkable claim against the exam's official clause. The instruction's category and stage are part of the claim, so a rule about documents cannot confirm a rule about timing, and a Prelims rule cannot confirm a Mains one.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_exam_day(instruction, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, cycle='', stage='', source_text='') -> Claim. field 'examday:<category>[:<stage>]'; value = text or title or description; evidence = evidenceSpan/evidence or the text itself; source_url = sourceUrl; source_text defaults to sourceTitle + excerpt; requires_value when text exists.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns one FAQ answer into a checkable claim that the official clause it cites really supports it.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_faq(faq, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, cycle='', stage='', source_text='') -> Claim. value = answer (or claim); field 'faq:<slug of officialClause or question, max 36>[:<stage>]'; evidence = evidenceSpan or provenance excerpt, else the answer; title = documentTitle or the clause; source_url = provenance.officialUrl; requires_value when the answer exists.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns any single fact the exam builder read from a document (with its citation) into a checkable claim, so the same verification can run over whatever the builder extracted.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_field(field, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, cycle='') -> Claim. Duck-typed on field.name, field.value and field.citation (excerpt, document_title, url); field 'field:<name>'; source_text = document_title + excerpt; requires_value unless the value is None, '', [] or {}.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns a link into a checkable claim that this specific website is the portal for a specific purpose (applying, downloading the admit card, results and so on) for this exam and cycle. This stops a plain homepage from being presented as a 'Download Admit Card' link just because it exists.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_portal(link, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, purpose='OTHER', cycle='', stage='', source_text='') -> Claim. value = '<host> is the <_PORTAL_LABEL[purpose]> for <official_name> [cycle]'; field 'portal:<purpose>[:<stage>]'; evidence = evidenceSpan / note / title; source_url = the link's url; requires_value when a host could be parsed. Officiality is left to portal_officiality.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns one official previous-year question into a checkable claim that it really appears in that exam's paper for that year. A question GovOS wrote itself has no official source, so it can never pass this check.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_question(q, *, official_name, authority, source_text='') -> Claim. exam_id and cycle (paperYear) come from the question; field 'pyq:<stage>:<paper slug[:40]>:q<number>'; value and evidence_span are the prompt (promptEnglish or prompt); source_url = provenance.officialUrl; source_text defaults to documentTitle (or paper name) + excerpt; requires_value when the prompt is non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns a study resource or official document in the record into a checkable claim that it belongs to this exam and cycle and is the kind of resource it says it is (for example 'an official document for SSC CGL 2026'). Whether it is official is decided separately, from its web address.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_resource(resource, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, cycle='', source_text='') -> Claim. value is a scope phrase '<label> for <official_name> [cycle]' using _RESOURCE_LABEL by resource type (default 'resource'), not the title; field 'resource:<type lower>'; evidence = description or provenance excerpt or title; source_url = url / directPdfUrl / provenance.officialUrl; requires_value when a title exists.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns one result announcement from an exam's record (for example 'Prelims result declared on this date') into the standard checking form used by GovOS's verifier: the value, the official words that support it, and the source document.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_result(row, *, official_name, authority, source_text='') -> Claim. value = declaredAt or expectedAt; field = 'result:' + kind lower-cased; cycle from row; evidence_span = provenance.excerptText or label; source_url = provenance.officialUrl / documentUrl / portalUrl; source_title = documentTitle or label; requires_value only when a date is present. Shapes input only; verifies nothing.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Turns a correction notice (a corrigendum that changes, say, the last date) into a checkable claim that the new value is really stated by the correction document. The changed field is part of the claim, so a notice changing one date cannot be used to confirm a change to another.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: claim_from_revision(rev, *, exam_id, official_name, authority, source_text='') -> Claim. field 'revision:' + (affected or fieldPath or 'field'); value = newValue (or revisedValue); evidence = evidenceSpan/evidence, falling back to the title; source_url = sourceUrl or pdfUrl; source_text defaults to title + excerpt; requires_value when the new value is non-empty.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Decides whether a portal link is official by checking it against all of the authority's own website addresses (an authority can have several, such as UPSC's main site and its separate online application site). Look-alike or coaching sites are always unofficial.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: portal_officiality(url, authority_domains='') -> 'OFFICIAL' | 'UNOFFICIAL'. Accepts a single domain, a comma/space-separated string, or an iterable; returns OFFICIAL if resource_officiality(url, d) is OFFICIAL for any domain d.

tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.text: Decides whether a link is official, purely from its web address: it is official only if it is on the exam authority's own website or one of its sub-sites. Anything else, including useful coaching or news sites, is unofficial.
tools/exam_builder/verification/adapters.tech: resource_officiality(url, authority_domain='') -> 'OFFICIAL' | 'UNOFFICIAL'. Parses both with urlsplit (adding '//' when no scheme), lower-cases, drops the port and a leading 'www.'; OFFICIAL when the host equals the base domain or ends with '.' + base. No domain, or no host, gives UNOFFICIAL.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: The exact set of answers Claude must give when asked about a date.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: Tuple ('role', 'supports_date', 'evidence_span', 'is_reference', 'confidence', 'conflicts'); validate_date requires exactly these keys.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: The list of event types a date can be (application opens, exam date and so on) plus 'not a date' and 'just a reference date', shared with the date reader so both use the same words.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: tuple(tools.claude_cli.schemas.DATE_ROLES); offered to Claude in classify_date and used by validate_date to reject roles outside the list.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: The exact set of answers Claude must give when asked what a piece of supporting text is doing.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: Tuple ('role', 'supports_value', 'scope', 'evidence_span', 'confidence', 'conflicts'); validate requires the reply's keys to be exactly this set.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: For each kind of fact (vacancies, qualification, fee, fee exemptions, posts, exam pattern), the job the supporting text must be doing, and the other jobs similar text often does instead. For example, a number backing 'total vacancies' must be the total, not one category's count or a row number.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: Dict field_name -> (required role, tuple of alternative roles); e.g. 'vacancies' -> ('total_vacancies', ('category_count', 'post_count', 'row_serial', 'other_number')). The full list is offered to Claude and validate accepts only the required role.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: Asks Claude what job a piece of official text is doing for a fact (for example, whether a number is the total vacancies or one category's count). The answer is only used later to hold a fact back, never to supply a value.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: classify(field_name, value, evidence, context, gateway=None) -> (output | None, status, detail). Runs Operation.CLASSIFY_ATTRIBUTION through the gateway with field, value_json, the ROLES list for the field, and whitespace-normalised evidence and context. Returns (result.output, 'OK', '') on success, else (None, result.status.value, result.message). Raises KeyError for a field not in ROLES.

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: Asks Claude what a date in an official document is for — which event it schedules, whether it is just the notice's own date, or not a date at all.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: classify_date(item, context, gateway=None) -> (output | None, status, detail). Runs Operation.CLASSIFY_DATE with the item's ISO date (dateTimeStr[:10]), label (rawLabel or label), stated text (rawValue or provenance excerpt), all DATE_ROLES and the context, all whitespace-normalised. Returns (output, 'OK', '') or (None, status value, message).

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: Decides whether Claude's answer about a piece of supporting text lets the fact be published. It does only if the answer is well-formed, the quoted text really is in the document, Claude says the text plays the required role and supports the value, and it reports no conflict. Anything else keeps the fact for human review.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: validate(field_name, raw, source_text) -> (bool, reason). Fails if raw is not a dict with exactly KEYS; role not in the field's list; supports_value not bool or conflicts not a list; evidence_span empty or not in normalise_ws(source_text); role != required role; supports_value False; or any non-empty conflict string. Otherwise (True, 'Claude confirms the role ...').

tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.text: Decides whether Claude's reading of a date lets that date stand. The quoted text must be in the document and actually contain the date; a 'not a date' answer, a conflict, no support, or a different event type than the one published all hold the date back. A notice's own dateline is accepted only where that is the role being checked.
tools/exam_builder/verification/attribut.tech: validate_date(item, raw, source_text, need_role) -> (bool, reason). need_role is a callable role -> bool, or None. Requires exactly DATE_KEYS, a role in DATE_ROLES, boolean supports_date/is_reference and a list conflicts; the span must be in the source and read_dates(span) must yield the item's ISO date (or the same month when the read precision is not DAY). NOT_A_DATE fails; is_reference or REFERENCE passes only if need_role('REFERENCE'); then supports_date must be True, no conflicts, and need_role(role) must hold when given.

tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.text: A short-term memory of checking results so the exact same fact with the exact same evidence is not sent to Claude twice. Failures such as Claude being unavailable are never remembered, so the next run tries again.
tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.tech: In-memory dict keyed by Claim.fingerprint (which includes the verifier version). Not persistent; one instance per caller.

tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.text: Looks up a remembered result for a fact, if there is one.
tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.tech: Returns self._store.get(fingerprint) — a VerificationResult or None.

tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.text: Remembers a result, but only if Claude actually gave a decision rather than failing to run.
tools/exam_builder/verification/cache.py.tech: Stores result under fingerprint only when result.infra is InfraStatus.OK; infrastructure failures are dropped.

tools/exam_builder/verification/claude_v.text: Prepares exactly what Claude is shown when asked to check a fact: the exam, cycle, field, value, the source's title and address, the authority, and the quoted supporting words — never the whole document.
tools/exam_builder/verification/claude_v.tech: claim_payload(claim) -> dict with exam (official_name or exam_id), cycle, field, value, source_title, source_url, authority and evidence (evidence_span stripped). These are the VERIFY_CLAIM operation's schema fields.

tools/exam_builder/verification/claude_v.text: Asks Claude whether the quoted official words support a fact, and returns its answer in a strict, checked form. If Claude is off, missing, slow or answers in the wrong shape, the result is an error state that can never count as 'supported'.
tools/exam_builder/verification/claude_v.tech: run_claude(claim, gateway=None) -> VerificationResult. Calls gateway.run(Operation.VERIFY_CLAIM, claim_payload(claim)) (default gateway from get_gateway()); a failed result becomes VerificationResult.error(status, message, ENGINE), otherwise VerificationResult.from_claude_output(output).

tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.text: The exact set of answers Claude must give when asked whether a quotation is complete.
tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.tech: Tuple ('complete', 'continues_after', 'starts_mid_unit', 'confidence', 'reason'); validate requires exactly these keys.

tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.text: For each kind of quoted text (qualification, application step, exam-day rule, FAQ clause, syllabus entry), a plain description of what a complete piece looks like, used when asking Claude.
tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.tech: Dict field_name -> description string sent as unit_kind in CHECK_COMPLETENESS; classify falls back to 'a complete quoted unit' for other fields.

tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.text: Shows Claude a quotation and the text around it and asks whether the quotation starts and ends where the document's own sentence or clause does.
tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.tech: classify(field_name, quotation, context, gateway=None) -> (output | None, status, detail). Runs Operation.CHECK_COMPLETENESS with unit_kind (UNIT_KIND lookup) and whitespace-normalised quotation and context; returns (output, 'OK', '') or (None, status value, message).

tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.text: Decides whether Claude's answer lets a quotation be published as a whole unit. It passes only if the answer is well-formed and Claude says it is complete, does not continue afterwards, does not start mid-sentence, and is not low-confidence. Claude's words are never used as the text itself.
tools/exam_builder/verification/complete.tech: validate(raw) -> (bool, reason). Fails for a non-dict or keys other than KEYS, non-boolean flags, confidence not in high/medium/low, complete False, continues_after True, starts_mid_unit True, or confidence 'low'. Reason text includes Claude's reason truncated to 160 characters.

tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.text: Asks Claude whether a particular document is about the same recruitment (same exam and year) as the one GovOS holds. The answer can only stop a match, never create one.
tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.tech: confirm_same_recruitment(designation, cycle, components, document_block, gateway=None) -> (output | None, status, detail). Runs Operation.CONFIRM_RECRUITMENT with the normalised designation, cycle, component list and normalised document block.

tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.text: Asks Claude to point at the words in a notification's title that name the recruitment, its qualifiers, its year and its parts, each with the exact quoted words. What it returns is still checked elsewhere before anything is used.
tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.tech: extract_designation(title_block, gateway=None) -> (output | None, status, detail). Runs Operation.EXTRACT_DESIGNATION with the whitespace-normalised title block; output is unverified and must go through designation.validate_extraction.

tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.text: Checks Claude's 'same recruitment?' answer. If the answer is malformed, or the words Claude quotes as proof are not actually in the document, the answer is treated as unusable either way.
tools/exam_builder/verification/designat.tech: validate_confirmation(raw, document_text) -> (bool | None, span, reason). None when raw is not a dict, has keys outside {same_recruitment, evidence_span, reason}, same_recruitment is not a bool, or the normalised evidence_span is empty or absent from the document. Otherwise returns the boolean, the span, and the reason normalised and capped at 300 characters.

tools/exam_builder/verification/determin.text: A simple check that the claimed exam year appears somewhere in the source text.
tools/exam_builder/verification/determin.tech: True when the stripped cycle is empty or is a substring of the text; relies on identity.verify having already rejected conflicting years.

tools/exam_builder/verification/determin.text: Runs GovOS's own fixed checks on a fact before Claude is ever asked: there must be a source link, quoted supporting words, those words must be printed in the fetched document, a value must be present when needed, and the document must belong to this exam and this year. If any check fails, the reason is recorded and Claude is not consulted.
tools/exam_builder/verification/determin.tech: run_deterministic(claim) -> DeterministicResult. Sets source_ok, span_present, span_in_source (normalise_ws membership; False with a reason when no source_text), value_present (unless requires_value is False). Identity via identity.verify on source_text (or the span): MISMATCH fails; MATCH passes; AMBIGUOUS fails outright when designation_mode(target), else passes only if the first 3000 characters MATCH or have matches. cycle_ok = identity_ok and (_cycle_present when a cycle is claimed). Reasons accumulate in r.reasons.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: The label stamped on every study roadmap order to mark it as GovOS's own suggestion, not an official recommendation.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Constant 'GOVOS_GUIDANCE', the default and only value of RoadmapGuidance.source.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: A suggested study order for one exam, always labelled as GovOS guidance, with a disclaimer, who produced the order (Claude or GovOS's fixed rule), and why no guidance exists if none could be made.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Dataclass: exam_id, source (always GOVOS_GUIDANCE), generated_by ('claude' | 'deterministic'), steps (list of RoadmapStep), disclaimer, unavailable_reason, infra (InfraStatus value string, default OK).

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Converts the guidance into the plain data form the app sends and stores.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Returns a camelCase dict: examId, source, generatedBy, disclaimer, unavailableReason, infra, and steps as a list of {topicId, topicName, subject, rationale}.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: True when there is actually a study order to show.
One step of a suggested study order: a syllabus topic, its subject, and a short reason for its place in the order.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Dataclass with topic_id, topic_name, subject and rationale (default '').

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Writes the note saying the study order is GovOS's suggestion and not an official recommendation of the named authority.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Uses the authority name up to ' (' (or 'the authority' when empty) in a fixed sentence.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Cleans up the list of verified syllabus topics, keeping only what is needed to order them and dropping any topic without an id or a name.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: Maps each topic dict to {id (id or topicId), name (topicName or name), subject, weightage (float of weightagePercentage, default 0), high_yield (bool isHighYield)}; skips entries missing id or name.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Checks the study order Claude proposed. It is accepted only if Claude used exactly the topics it was given — each one once, none invented, none dropped; otherwise it is rejected entirely.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: _parse_order(data, norm) -> list[RoadmapStep] | None. Requires a dict with a non-empty list 'order' of dicts whose 'id' is a known, not-yet-seen topic id; the set of seen ids must equal all input ids. Topic names and subjects come from the input; Claude's 'why' (string only) is capped at 200 characters.

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Builds a default study order from verified data alone, with no AI: high-yield topics first, each subject's topics kept together, heavier-weighted topics earlier, and otherwise the syllabus's own order. Each step's reason states what actually decided its place.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: deterministic_sequence(topics) -> list[RoadmapStep]. Sort key: (not high_yield, subject's first-appearance rank, -weightage, original position). Rationale is 'High-yield; scheduled early.', 'Scheduled by weightage within its subject.' when weightage > 0, else 'In the order the official syllabus lists it.'

tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.text: Produces the suggested study order for one exam from its verified syllabus. A rule-based order is always prepared first; if Claude is switched on and returns a valid reordering, that is used instead, otherwise the rule-based order is returned. With no verified syllabus it returns no order and says why. The result is always labelled GovOS guidance.
tools/exam_builder/verification/roadmap_.tech: generate(exam_id, topics, *, authority='', exam_label='', gateway=None) -> RoadmapGuidance. Empty normalised topics -> unavailable_reason 'NOT_EXTRACTED: ...'. Otherwise computes deterministic_sequence; if gateway.is_enabled() is False returns it with infra CLAUDE_DISABLED; runs Operation.ORDER_ROADMAP with exam_label and topics (id, subject, name, high_yield); a failed run returns the baseline with that status; an order rejected by _parse_order returns the baseline with CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED; else generated_by 'claude'. Writes nothing.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: One fact to be checked, packaged with everything needed to check it: which exam and year it is for, what field and value it states, the quoted official words supporting it, and the source document's link, title and full text.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Dataclass: exam_id, field, value, evidence_span, and optional source_url, cycle, source_title, authority, official_name, source_text (the fetched document, needed to confirm the span) and requires_value (default True). Built by the adapters module.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Makes a unique code for a fact plus its evidence and source, so the same check is not repeated; any change in the evidence or the rules version gives a new code.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: SHA-256 hex of exam_id, cycle, field, stripped value, whitespace-collapsed evidence_span, source_url and verifier_version joined with a unit-separator symbol. source_text is not included.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: The results of GovOS's own fixed checks on a fact (source link present, supporting words present and found in the document, right exam, right year, value present), with the reasons for any failure.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Dataclass of booleans source_ok, span_present, span_in_source, identity_ok, cycle_ok, value_present, cross_exam_ok (all default False) plus a reasons list. Filled by run_deterministic.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: True only when every one of the fixed checks passed.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Property: logical AND of all seven boolean checks.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: The name recorded on each check result to say it was produced by the Claude command-line tool.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Constant 'claude-cli', the default engine of VerificationResult.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: The version name of the fact-checking rules. Changing it makes every fact be checked again rather than reusing old results.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Constant 'gov-verify-2'; part of Claim.fingerprint and stored on each VerificationResult.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: The final publishing decision for one fact: either VERIFIED (shown to candidates as verified) or NEEDS_REVIEW, with the results of both the fixed checks and Claude's check and the reason.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Dataclass: publishable, status ('VERIFIED' | 'NEEDS_REVIEW'), deterministic (DeterministicResult), claude (VerificationResult | None), infra, reason, fingerprint. VERIFIED only when deterministic passed and Claude returned SUPPORTED.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Converts the publishing decision and everything behind it into plain data.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Returns {status, publishable, reason, infra, fingerprint, deterministic: {passed, sourceOk, spanPresent, spanInSource, identityOk, cycleOk, valuePresent, crossExamOk, reasons}, claude: claude.as_dict() or None}.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Claude's possible verdicts on whether the evidence backs a fact: supported, contradicted, not enough evidence, or error (which means the check did not run properly, not a judgement about the fact).
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: str Enum: SUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED, INSUFFICIENT, ERROR; ERROR is non-factual and is paired with a non-OK infra status.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Claude's checked answer about one fact: its verdict, whether it found the exam identity, the evidence and the claim supported, its reason, and whether the check ran properly.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Dataclass: decision (VerificationDecision), identity_supported, evidence_supported, claim_supported, reason, engine, verifier_version (default VERIFIER_VERSION), infra (InfraStatus, default OK).

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Converts Claude's checked answer into plain data for storage or display.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Returns a camelCase dict: decision, identitySupported, evidenceSupported, claimSupported, reason, engine, verifierVersion, infra (enum values as strings).

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Builds a 'the check could not run' result (for example Claude was off or timed out). Such a result can never count as the fact being supported.
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Classmethod error(infra, reason, engine=ENGINE): decision ERROR, all three support booleans False, the given infra status and reason.

tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..text: Turns Claude's reply into a result, refusing any reply that is malformed or contradicts itself (for example saying 'supported' while also saying the evidence does not support it).
tools/exam_builder/verification/schemas..tech: Classmethod from_claude_output(raw, *, engine=ENGINE). Non-dict -> error CLAUDE_INVALID_OUTPUT; decision missing, unknown or 'ERROR' -> CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED; any of identity_supported/evidence_supported/claim_supported not bool -> CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED; SUPPORTED without both evidence_supported and claim_supported -> CLAUDE_SCHEMA_REJECTED. Otherwise a result with the decision and booleans; a non-string reason becomes '' and the reason is capped at 600 characters.

tools/exam_builder/verification/verifier.text: Decides whether one fact may be published as verified. GovOS's own fixed checks run first; if any fails, the fact needs review and Claude is never asked. If they pass, Claude is asked whether the evidence supports the fact (reusing a remembered answer when available). Only a 'supported' answer makes it VERIFIED; anything else, including Claude being unavailable, means it needs review.
tools/exam_builder/verification/verifier.tech: verify(claim, *, gateway=None, cache=None) -> Verdict. Computes claim.fingerprint and run_deterministic; on failure returns NEEDS_REVIEW with claude=None. Otherwise gets a cached VerificationResult or calls run_claude (and cache.put, which keeps only infra OK results). Non-OK infra -> NEEDS_REVIEW carrying that infra; SUPPORTED -> VERIFIED/publishable; CONTRADICTED or INSUFFICIENT -> NEEDS_REVIEW.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::CHILD_MEMORY_.text: The most memory the separate file-reading process may use (2.5 GB), set with headroom over the largest real scorecard photo.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::CHILD_MEMORY_.tech: 2560 MB; passed to _WindowsJob (ProcessMemoryLimit) or _limit_this_process (RLIMIT_DATA/AS) by decode_isolated.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::CHILD_TIMEOUT.text: How long the file-reading process may run (90 seconds) before it is stopped; a normal read takes about 5 seconds.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::CHILD_TIMEOUT.tech: 90; communicate() timeout in decode_isolated and the POSIX RLIMIT_CPU soft limit.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::IMAGE_FORMATS.text: The only photo formats accepted: PNG, JPEG and WEBP. Other formats are refused to reduce risk from untrusted uploads.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::IMAGE_FORMATS.tech: ('PNG', 'JPEG', 'WEBP'), passed as formats= to PIL Image.open.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::INFLATE_STREA.text: The most data any single compressed part of an uploaded PDF may expand to (48 MB), so a small file cannot balloon into a huge one.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::INFLATE_STREA.tech: 48 MB cap on one zlib stream's decoded size in preflight_pdf; sized for a large lossless page image.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::INFLATE_TOTAL.text: The most data all compressed parts of one uploaded PDF may expand to together (96 MB).
tools/scorecard_decode.py::INFLATE_TOTAL.tech: 96 MB cap on the summed decoded size of all zlib streams in preflight_pdf.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::InflateDataEr.text: Signals that compressed data was damaged part-way through, while remembering how much had already been expanded so that work still counts toward the size limit.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::InflateDataEr.tech: Subclass of zlib.error with a decoded attribute (bytes produced before the error); preflight_pdf adds it to the running total.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::InflateDataEr.text: Stores the error message and how much data was produced before the damage.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::InflateLimitE.text: Signals that a compressed part expanded past its allowed size, so reading stopped.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::InflateLimitE.tech: Plain Exception raised by inflate_bounded with the decoded size so far as its argument.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_ASPECT.text: How much longer than wide (or wider than long) an image or page may be (20 to 1), which blocks extreme strip images designed to blow up when enlarged.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_CONCURREN.text: How many uploaded files may be read at the same time (2), so many uploads at once cannot multiply memory use.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_CONCURREN.tech: 2; size of the _SLOTS BoundedSemaphore used by decode_isolated.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_OCR_PAGES.text: How many pages of a scanned PDF are read by text recognition (3), since a scorecard is on its first page or two.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_OCR_PIXEL.text: The largest image size allowed after GovOS enlarges a narrow photo for text recognition (32 million pixels), checked before the enlargement happens.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_OCR_PIXEL.tech: 32,000,000; check_image_size computes the 1600-px-wide upscale target and refuses above this.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_PDF_STREA.text: The most compressed parts GovOS will examine in one uploaded PDF (2000); a real scorecard has a few dozen.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_PDF_STREA.tech: 2000; preflight_pdf raises 413 TOO_MANY_PARTS once more stream-start matches than this are examined.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_RENDER_PI.text: The largest page image GovOS will create when turning a PDF page into a picture; bigger pages are rendered less sharply to stay within it.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_RENDER_PI.tech: 32,000,000 pixels; _render_dpi lowers the dpi so the bitmap fits.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_SOURCE_PI.text: The largest image size allowed (50 million pixels), checked before the image is opened; a 48-megapixel phone photo fits.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_SOURCE_PI.tech: 50,000,000; enforced by check_image_size and for embedded page images in pdf_ocr_lines.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_TEXT_CHAR.text: The most text (one million characters) passed on to the scorecard reader.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_TEXT_CHAR.tech: 1,000,000 characters; caps text from pdf_text, _pdf_text_fallback and OCR output in decode.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_TEXT_PAGE.text: How many pages of a text PDF are read (20).
tools/scorecard_decode.py::MAX_TEXT_PAGE.tech: 20 pages for PyMuPDF text extraction in pdf_text.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::MB.text: One megabyte, used to state the size limits below.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::RENDER_DPI.text: The sharpness (200 dots per inch) at which a scanned PDF page is turned into an image for text recognition.
