tools/scorecard_decode.py::TEXT_STREAM_L.text: How much one part of a PDF may expand to when GovOS reads its text without a PDF library (4 MB); anything bigger is not a page of text and is skipped.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::TEXT_STREAM_L.tech: 4 MB inflate cap used by _pdf_text_fallback per stream.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::UploadRejecte.text: The error used when an uploaded scorecard will not be read, carrying the web error number, a short code the app shows, and the message for the candidate.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::UploadRejecte.tech: Exception with status (HTTP code), reason (stable code) and message (candidate-facing text); str(exc) is the reason.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::UploadRejecte.text: Stores the error number, code and message.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::UploadRejecte.tech: Calls Exception.__init__(reason) and sets self.status, self.reason, self.message.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.text: On Windows, a container for the separate file-reading process that caps its memory, stops it from starting further processes, and kills it when GovOS is done with it.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.tech: Wraps a Win32 job object via ctypes (kernel32 CreateJobObjectW, SetInformationJobObject, AssignProcessToJobObject, CloseHandle).

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob._.text: Creates the Windows container and sets its memory cap and safety rules.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob._.tech: Creates the job and sets JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION (info class 9) with LimitFlags PROCESS_MEMORY | KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE | DIE_ON_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION | ACTIVE_PROCESS, ActiveProcessLimit 1 and ProcessMemoryLimit = memory. Raises OSError (closing the handle) if creation or configuration fails.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.a.text: Puts the file-reading process into the container so the limits apply to it.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.a.tech: AssignProcessToJobObject(handle, proc._handle); raises OSError on failure.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.c.text: Closes the container, which also kills the process if it is still running.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_WindowsJob.c.tech: CloseHandle on the job handle once (sets handle to None); KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE terminates any remaining process.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_child_main.text: The entry point of the separate file-reading process: it reads the request, does the reading, and sends back one answer, keeping any stray output from the reading libraries out of that answer.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_child_main.tech: Reads one JSON request from stdin, duplicates fd 1 for the answer and redirects fd 1 to stderr (so C-library prints cannot corrupt it), runs decode(kind, base64-decoded raw, ocr), writes the JSON answer fully to the saved fd and returns 0. Run via __main__.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_declares_fla.text: Checks whether a PDF part says of itself that it is compressed with the standard method (FlateDecode), even if that name is disguised with escape codes.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_declares_fla.tech: Decodes #xx hex escapes in the dictionary bytes, then regex-searches for /Filter followed (optionally inside an array, as the first entry) by /FlateDecode or /Fl.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_is_zlib_head.text: Checks whether two bytes look like the start of standard compressed data.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_is_zlib_head.tech: True when the compression method nibble is 8 (deflate), CINFO <= 7, and the 16-bit header is divisible by 31 (the zlib FCHECK rule).

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_limit_this_p.text: On Linux or Mac, caps the memory and processor time of the separate file-reading process before it starts reading.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_limit_this_p.tech: POSIX-only, called via preexec_fn in the child: setrlimit on RLIMIT_DATA (or RLIMIT_AS if unavailable) to `memory`, and RLIMIT_CPU to (CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, +5).

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_ocr_engine.text: Loads the text-recognition engine the first time it is needed and reuses it afterwards.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_ocr_engine.tech: Lazy module-level singleton: imports rapidocr_onnxruntime.RapidOCR and caches the instance in _OCR_ENGINE.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_ocr_image.text: Reads the text lines out of one image (a photo or a rendered scan page) with text recognition, after checking its size. Narrow images are enlarged first, and the lines are returned in reading order, top to bottom and left to right.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_ocr_image.tech: _ocr_image(pil_image) -> list[str]. check_image_size, convert to RGB, resize to 1600 px wide if narrower; runs the RapidOCR engine on a 1.2x contrast-enhanced copy, and on the plain image if that raised or found nothing. Sorts results by (top-left y rounded to 15 px bands, x) and returns non-blank texts; [] if nothing found.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_pdf_text_fal.text: A basic way to pull the visible text out of a PDF without a PDF library, used when the library fails. Each part is expanded with a size cap, parts that are too large or contain no text commands are skipped, and the text strings inside are collected.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_pdf_text_fal.tech: Iterates regex 'stream ... endstream' blocks; inflate_bounded with TEXT_STREAM_LIMIT (over-limit blocks skipped; invalid zlib uses the raw bytes). Keeps blocks containing Tj/TJ, decodes latin-1, extracts parenthesised string literals with escaped parens/backslashes unescaped, adds a newline per block, stops once MAX_TEXT_CHARS is passed. Returns the joined text truncated to MAX_TEXT_CHARS.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_render_dpi.text: Chooses how sharply to turn a PDF page into an image: normally 200 dots per inch, lower for very large pages so the image stays within the limit. Pages with no size or an extreme shape are refused.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::_render_dpi.tech: _render_dpi(width_pt, height_pt) -> float. Non-positive size -> 422 PDF_UNREADABLE; aspect > MAX_ASPECT -> 413 PAGE_TOO_LARGE. Returns RENDER_DPI if the pixel count at 200 dpi is within MAX_RENDER_PIXELS, else RENDER_DPI * sqrt(MAX_RENDER_PIXELS / pixels).

tools/scorecard_decode.py::_too_large.text: Builds the 'this file expands to far too much data' refusal, saying what was too large.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::check_image_s.text: Refuses an image that is too big, too oddly shaped, or that would become too big when GovOS enlarges it for text recognition — all worked out from its width and height before any pixels are loaded.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::check_image_s.tech: check_image_size(width, height, *, upscale_to=1600) -> None. Raises UploadRejected 422 IMAGE_UNREADABLE for non-positive sizes; 413 IMAGE_TOO_LARGE when width*height > MAX_SOURCE_PIXELS, aspect > MAX_ASPECT, or (width < upscale_to) the upscaled size upscale_to x height*(upscale_to/width) exceeds MAX_OCR_PIXELS.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::decode.text: The actual reading work done inside the separate safe process: for a PDF it runs the size pre-check, reads its text, and uses text recognition if the PDF is a scan and that is allowed; for a photo it checks its size and reads it with text recognition. Problems become a clear error answer rather than a crash.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::decode.tech: decode(kind, raw, *, ocr) -> dict. PDF: preflight_pdf, pdf_text; returns method TEXT_LAYER if text has >= 30 non-whitespace-trimmed characters or ocr is False, else method OCR with pdf_ocr_lines joined. Image: image_header_size, check_image_size, open with IMAGE_FORMATS, _ocr_image. Output text capped at MAX_TEXT_CHARS. UploadRejected -> {ok: False, status, reason, message}; MemoryError -> 413 TOO_COMPLEX; any other exception -> status 200 with OCR_FAILED (image) or PDF_UNREADABLE (pdf).

tools/scorecard_decode.py::decode_isolat.text: Reads an uploaded scorecard in a separate, walled-off process with a memory cap and a time limit, so a malicious or broken file can at worst get that process killed rather than taking down the GovOS server. Only two files are read at once; if both slots stay busy for 15 seconds the candidate is told to try again. Any crash, timeout or memory overrun becomes a polite 'too complex' answer.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::decode_isolat.tech: decode_isolated(kind, raw, *, ocr, memory=CHILD_MEMORY_LIMIT, timeout=CHILD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) -> dict. Acquires _SLOTS (15 s, else 503 BUSY). Spawns 'python -m tools.scorecard_decode' in the repo root with a whitelisted environment (PATH, SYSTEMROOT, TEMP, TMP, HOME, USERPROFILE, LANG, LC_ALL, plus PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE) and stderr discarded; on Windows assigns a _WindowsJob, on POSIX sets limits via preexec_fn. Sends {kind, ocr, raw base64} on stdin only after limits are set. Timeout, non-zero exit, empty or non-JSON or non-dict output -> 413 TOO_COMPLEX; OSError -> 503 DECODER_UNAVAILABLE. Always closes the job and releases the slot.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::image_header_.text: Reads only the header of an uploaded photo to learn its width, height and format, without decoding the picture. Unreadable or suspiciously huge images are refused.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::image_header_.tech: image_header_size(raw) -> (width, height, format). Opens with PIL Image.open(formats=IMAGE_FORMATS) lazily; DecompressionBombError -> UploadRejected 413 IMAGE_TOO_LARGE; any other exception -> 422 IMAGE_UNREADABLE.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::inflate_bound.text: Expands one compressed block of data piece by piece, stopping the moment it would exceed a size limit. It can just measure the size without keeping anything, which is how uploads are checked safely.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::inflate_bound.tech: inflate_bounded(data, limit, *, keep=True, start=0) -> (bytes | None, size, reached_eof). Uses zlib.decompressobj fed 64 KB input chunks with max_length min(1 MB, limit - size + 1); handles unconsumed_tail; stops at end of stream or end of input. Raises InflateLimitExceeded when size > limit and InflateDataError (with bytes decoded so far) on invalid data. keep=False returns None for the bytes.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::ocr_available.text: Checks whether the optional text-recognition software is installed, without loading it.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::ocr_available.tech: True when importlib.util.find_spec finds rapidocr_onnxruntime, PIL and numpy.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::pdf_ocr_lines.text: Reads a scanned PDF scorecard (pictures of pages, no real text) by turning its first few pages into images and running text recognition on each. Page sizes and any embedded images are checked before rendering.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::pdf_ocr_lines.tech: pdf_ocr_lines(blob, max_pages=MAX_OCR_PAGES) -> list[str]. With PyMuPDF and PIL importable and the PDF openable: for each page, refuses embedded images over MAX_SOURCE_PIXELS (413), renders at _render_dpi, converts to a PIL image and extends with _ocr_image, appending '' between pages. Otherwise uses pypdfium2 (render scale = dpi/72, to_pil). Documents are closed in finally blocks.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::pdf_text.text: Gets the visible text of a PDF scorecard that has real text in it, using the PyMuPDF library on the first 20 pages, and falls back to the basic reader if that gives nothing or fails.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::pdf_text.tech: pdf_text(blob) -> str. fitz.open(stream=blob) and get_text('text') per page up to MAX_TEXT_PAGES, stopping past MAX_TEXT_CHARS; returns the stripped, truncated text if non-empty. UploadRejected propagates; other exceptions print a note to stderr. Falls back to _pdf_text_fallback.

tools/scorecard_decode.py::preflight_pdf.text: Before any PDF library touches an uploaded scorecard, measures how big every compressed part would become, without keeping the data. It refuses files with too many parts, any part or all parts together expanding too far, or parts that claim to be compressed but are damaged — giving the candidate a clear message instead of letting the server run out of memory.
tools/scorecard_decode.py::preflight_pdf.tech: preflight_pdf(blob) -> {'streams', 'decodedBytes'}. Iterates _STREAM_START matches; over MAX_PDF_STREAMS -> 413 TOO_MANY_PARTS; total at or over INFLATE_TOTAL_LIMIT -> 413. The stream's dictionary is the up-to-4096 bytes before 'stream', after the last 'obj'. Non-zlib-header data: 422 MALFORMED_COMPRESSED_DATA if the dictionary declares Flate, else skipped. zlib data is measured with inflate_bounded(keep=False) from right after the keyword (ignoring /Length and endstream) with limit min(stream limit, remaining total); InflateLimitExceeded -> 413 (total or per-stream message); invalid data -> 422 if declared, else its partial decoded size is counted and it is skipped.

tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.text: Makes sure that when many requests ask for the same slow thing at once (such as checking the Claude tool or fetching a feed), it runs only once and everyone gets the same answer. Nothing is remembered afterwards, so the next request starts fresh.
tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.tech: Thread-safe per-key call deduplication: a Lock-guarded dict of key -> _Flight. No caching of results or failures beyond the in-flight call.

tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.__i.text: Sets up an empty list of running operations.
tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.__i.tech: Creates the lock and an empty _flights dict.

tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.do.text: Runs an operation for a given key, or, if the same operation is already running, waits for it and returns its result (or the same error). A failure is shared with everyone waiting rather than retried by each of them.
tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.do.tech: do(key, fn). Under the lock, the first caller (leader) registers a _Flight; followers wait on flight.done and re-raise flight.error or return flight.result. The leader runs fn(), stores the result or the BaseException (and re-raises it), then in finally removes the key and sets done.

tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.in_.text: Tells whether an operation for that key is running right now.
tools/single_flight.py::SingleFlight.in_.tech: Returns key in self._flights under the lock.

tools/single_flight.py::_Flight.text: Keeps track of one slow operation that is currently running: whether it has finished, and its result or error.
tools/single_flight.py::_Flight.tech: Slotted holder with done (threading.Event), result and error; internal to SingleFlight.

tools/single_flight.py::_Flight.__init__.text: Starts a new 'not finished yet' record.
tools/single_flight.py::_Flight.__init__.tech: Creates an unset Event and sets result and error to None.
